text:
A thread 🧵 

First-half analysis: 

England started with confidence
England came into this game knowing that Spain's possession-based football would test their defensive organisation.
However, Thomas Tuchel's side did not simply sit back and allow Spain to dictate proceedings.
England pressed aggressively, competed in midfield and looked dangerous whenever they moved forward.
Jude Bellingham offered quality between the lines.
Declan Rice provided midfield protection and physicality.
Anthony Gordon stretched Spain's defensive line.
Morgan Rogers offered energy and direct attacking movement.
Harry Kane remained a constant threat.
England eventually got their breakthrough when Pau Cubarsí fouled Kane in the penalty area. The England captain converted from the spot in the 45th minute.

Half-time: Spain 0–1 England.

Second-half analysis: 

England punished Spain..
This was where England showed their attacking quality.
In the 53rd minute, Ezri Konsa headed home from a Declan Rice corner to make it 2–0.
Just four minutes later, Ben White finished brilliantly after receiving a pass from Jude Bellingham.
At 3–0, England looked completely in control.
They were clinical, aggressive and took advantage of Spain's defensive vulnerabilities.

The turning point: 

Elliot Anderson's red card♦️
The 63rd-minute dismissal of Elliot Anderson completely changed the complexion of the match.
England were reduced to ten men after Anderson brought down an opponent in the penalty area.
Mikel Oyarzabal converted the resulting penalty in the 65th minute.
Spain immediately gained momentum, and Nico Williams made it 3–2 in the 75th minute.
The final stages became a serious test of England's defensive discipline.
James Trafford produced an outstanding late double save, while Ben White made a crucial intervention to deny Lamine Yamal.
England held on.

Tactical verdict: Tuchel deserves credit
There are three major positives from this performance:
1. England's pressing
They did not allow Spain to enjoy complete comfort in possession. England were proactive rather than simply reactive.
2. Attacking efficiency
Three goals against Spain in Madrid is a significant achievement. England converted their opportunities and punished defensive mistakes.
3. Mental strength
Going down to ten men against a technically gifted Spanish side and protecting a one-goal advantage requires serious concentration and organisation.
The biggest concern, however, is how quickly England lost control after Anderson's dismissal. Their defensive structure became vulnerable, and Spain nearly completed the comeback.

text:
🎙️🇪🇸 LUIS DE LA FUENTE ON PEDRI'S REPEATED BENCHING, ELLIOT ANDERSON'S PERFORMANCE AND ENGLAND'S DOMINANCE!

Q: Why do you keep leaving Pedri on the bench despite his quality and importance to Barcelona?

Luis de la Fuente:

"Pedri is an exceptional footballer. Nobody questions his technical ability, intelligence or importance to Spanish football. But playing for Spain is not just about individual reputation. Every selection is based on what I believe the team needs for a particular opponent.

Against England, I wanted a midfield with physical strength, defensive balance and the ability to make forward runs. That is why I selected Martín Zubimendi, Fabián Ruiz and Mikel Merino.

I understand why people are asking questions. Pedri is a player who can control the rhythm of a match, create opportunities and make difficult situations look simple. But being on the bench does not mean he has lost my confidence. He remains an important player for Spain.

Q: What is your assessment of Elliot Anderson?

Anderson has shown why England trust him in important matches. His energy, aggression and ability to compete in midfield have been noticeable. Alongside Declan Rice, he has helped England disrupt Spain's rhythm.

However, his red card following the challenge on Lamine Yamal was a costly moment. At this level, players must understand when to challenge and when to stay composed. His performance will naturally attract attention, but discipline is just as important as ability.

Q: What about Jude Bellingham and Harry Kane?

Bellingham has brought intensity and personality to England's midfield. His involvement in the attacking moves and ability to arrive in dangerous positions make him extremely difficult to control.

Harry Kane has once again demonstrated his experience. He took responsibility from the penalty spot and gave England the breakthrough just before half-time. That is what you expect from a world-class striker.

Declan Rice has also been influential, providing protection and helping England compete physically in midfield. Ben White and Ezri Konsa deserve credit for their contributions at the back.

Q: Spain have Lamine Yamal, Fabián Ruiz and Martín Zubimendi. What went wrong?

Lamine Yamal has continued to show his quality. He has been one of Spain's biggest attacking threats, and winning the penalty after Anderson's challenge was an important moment.

Fabián Ruiz and Zubimendi have tried to provide control, while Mikel Merino offers a different attacking dimension. But we need more consistency across the team.

Pau Cubarsí will also have to learn from the penalty incident involving Harry Kane. These small mistakes can change the direction of a major match.

The players must take responsibility, improve their decisions and understand that possession alone does not win football matches.

Q: Will Pedri return to the starting XI?

Pedri knows what I expect from him. He has the quality to influence matches, and there will be opportunities for him. My responsibility is to select the team that gives Spain the best balance.

I do not select players because of their club reputation or public popularity. I select them because of what the team needs."

🔥 THE BIG QUESTION: Is Luis de la Fuente right to keep Pedri on the bench, or should Spain build their midfield around the Barcelona star?

My take is that Elon Musk should keep his options open, but he shouldn’t rush into moving Tesla’s operations because of a political disagreement.

Florida may offer a business-friendly environment, but relocating a major factory is a massive decision involving workers, infrastructure, suppliers, costs and long-term investment.

At the same time, Governor Gina Hinojosa should understand that states compete for businesses, jobs and investment. If Texas creates an environment that makes companies feel unwelcome, other states will be ready to benefit.

Ultimately, this should be about economic growth, not political ego. Elon should choose the state that offers Tesla the strongest long-term future, while both governors should focus on creating jobs and attracting investment rather than trading political shots.

text:
Tim McGraw was 11 when he learned that baseball star Tug McGraw was his biological father. Tug refused to acknowledge him for years, then offered college support on the condition that Tim stop contacting him and his family.

Tim grew up in Louisiana using his stepfather's surname. While searching his mother's closet, he found a birth certificate naming Tug as his father, a player whose baseball card already hung on Tim's wall.

His mother arranged a meeting in Houston. Tug was friendly but told the boy to think of him as a friend, not a father. Tim continued writing afterward, but the messages went unanswered.

Near the end of high school, Tim needed help with college. He says Tug's representatives offered financial support through an agreement requiring Tim to end all contact. Tim agreed to consider it only if they met one last time.

At dinner in Houston, Tim told Tug he would sign the agreement and disappear from his life, but first asked: "Do you think you're my dad?" Tug answered, "Yes, I believe I am," and dropped the agreement.

Recognition did not instantly create a close relationship. Tim says another year passed before they began spending time together. He later visited Tug in Philadelphia and formed relationships with his half-siblings.

When Tug developed brain cancer in 2003, Tim helped arrange treatment and supported him through his final months. Tug died at Tim's cabin outside Nashville on January 5, 2004, with Tim and other relatives beside him.

Tim later said he waited beside his dying father for an apology that never came. In his 2026 Tim Ferriss interview, he said he never hated Tug, despite the years his father refused to claim him.

text:
When Virtual Worlds Begin to Replace Reality

Watching the current hype surrounding GTA 6, I find myself looking at it from a completely different perspective than I would have years ago.

Rockstar is taking Vice City beyond the screen and bringing its fictional world into real Miami. Blimps over beaches, themed decorations, advertising campaigns — the real city is becoming part of the game's universe.

Impressive marketing. But it also raises a much bigger question.

I know this world from the inside.

For years, I was deeply immersed in Rockstar's games. GTA and Red Dead Redemption weren't just occasional entertainment. I could spend weeks in those virtual worlds, anticipating releases, exploring, progressing, and becoming emotionally attached to environments that existed entirely on a screen.

At the time, it all seemed perfectly normal.

Eventually, however, my relationship with technology and gaming began to change. I developed a sensitivity to electromagnetic fields (EMF), which became one of the main reasons I gradually stepped away from gaming.

For me, the effects went beyond ordinary screen fatigue. I experienced physical reactions and periods of feeling unwell. I also noticed changes in my inner state and in a personal connection that is important to me. Long gaming sessions and powerful electronic equipment were no longer something I could comfortably accommodate in my life.

This forced me to reconsider not only gaming itself, but also the amount of time, attention, and emotional energy I had invested in virtual environments.

And gradually, something else became apparent.

The attraction wasn't simply about playing a game. It was about immersion — the atmosphere, the stimulation, the anticipation, the emotional experiences, and the familiar cycle of entering another world that temporarily became the center of your attention.

There is nothing inherently wrong with enjoying fictional worlds. Stories, films, books, and games can all enrich our lives. The question is what happens when an artificial experience begins to occupy more space than the life we are actually living.

How much of our attention do we give away? How much of our emotional energy becomes attached to something designed by someone else? And how easily can we confuse the feeling of experiencing something with actually living it?

A virtual world may offer enormous freedom within its boundaries, but those boundaries are designed by someone else. Its rules, rewards, progression, and incentives are all predetermined.

You can explore an entire fictional universe and still remain inside a system you never created.

A prison within a prison.

I'm not suggesting that everyone who plays video games is trapped, or that enjoying GTA means losing touch with reality. Everyone has a different relationship with entertainment. There is a difference between occasionally enjoying a game and allowing an artificial environment to dominate your attention.

But having experienced deep immersion myself, I recognize the attraction and the mechanisms that make it so compelling.

It took me several years to reach a point where I no longer felt the need to return. Today, I value things differently. Nature, genuine human connections, consciousness, discovery, and the experience of being present in the real world have taken on an entirely different meaning.

Perhaps the most interesting part of stepping away is that you don't necessarily have to stop appreciating those fictional universes. You simply stop needing to live inside them.

So, while millions of people are counting down to the next GTA release, I find myself asking a different question:

If reality already offers us an entire universe to explore, why do we sometimes feel such a strong need to escape into a world designed by someone else?

Perhaps true freedom doesn't begin when another virtual world opens its doors.

Perhaps it begins when we rediscover the world beyond them.

#Bitcoin - Weekly Market Commentary

I was not supposed to share my weekly market commentary here on X today, but given what happened in the Bitcoin market last week, I believe this post is needed.

What Happened

The last week marked the sixth week in a row of downward price action on Bitcoin, and it was the most aggressive one out of the six weeks. The week opened at $75,000 and dropped around 17% to 62k. If you have followed me for a while, you know I have been warning about a move down since 87k. I told you to be prepared to buy lower if the market allowed it, and told you the lowest level I expected was 68k, because that is where the MA200 Weekly sits, an indicator that offers a lot of strength to the market. I expected a strong bounce there, but that was not the case. We went almost 10% below 68k, and only at 62k did we finally see some market strength. The sell pressure witnessed over the past few weeks is beyond absurd, and no level or indicator offered any type of strength whatsoever until 62k.

Why It Happened

The reason for this move down remains unclear, and we can only guess. Binance was hacked for $6 billion a few weeks ago and needed to find funds to pay back its customers. Did Binance sell to the market to cover it, and now that it makes profits from user fees, it restarts buying? No one knows for sure, and CZ has come out and said Binance did not sell during this move. There is also the idea that institutions are raising funds to buy the Anthropic IPO. But if that were the case, why would they do it in such a desperate way, selling during a weekend when there is little to no orderbook liquidity and price is easy to move? Unless this institution is dumb and decided to lose money with a poor exit price, I believe this is not the case. Some will argue about the safety of the crypto space and the macroeconomic events, but tell me, if the crypto space is in danger, isn’t the whole financial system, including the banking system in danger as well? And since when do markets react to an incoming rate hike on a weekend, when the stock market had already priced it in during the week? I can’t tell who is behind this move down, but regardless of who it was, in my opinion its only purpose was to hunt the downside liquidity before we resume higher.

My Plan

In August I bought Bitcoin at 60-64k and called the bear market bottom at 57k. I told you the bull market was starting and higher was next. We ended up rallying to 87k where I told you to be prepared to buy lower. We placed orders at 72-76k and those orders were filled over these last few weeks. My average spot buying price on Bitcoin is 68k, exactly the same level as the MA200 Weekly, and I am happy to hold through this. I remain extremely bullish and I expect higher prices next. Due to how extended this move down was, my $93,000 target is cancelled and I now expect $97,000 or higher in the short term, by Q1 2027. The deeper the flush, the more liquidity is built above, and the stronger the move higher will be. That is why I raised my target.

I know a few believe my bullish bias is wrong. My bullish bias can only be wrong if the bottom is not in at 57k, and for that, you first need to see the market accept prices under 64k. The last market reaction below 64k resulted in a 7% pump. Acceptance below 64k would confirm the MA200 Weekly is lost and put my bullish bias at risk, but even then, we still have a very strong support holding since February in the 60-64k region, and the market would need to break below it to invalidate my bullish bias. Only then could 52-54k be tested before the bull market starts. For now, $57,000 is the bottom until proven otherwise.

I am seeing way too many people waiting for lower prices to finally start buying. They missed the move from 57k to 87k, and now that they have a good opportunity to redeem themselves, they prefer to wait for lower prices yet again. My question to these people is: do you think it’s worth waiting for a possible 20% dump to finally buy? In my opinion, even if the bears are right here, the risk to reward clearly favors the bulls. Over the coming days, I will be releasing liquidity from my reserves and I will be buying more Bitcoin while it’s cheap.

Why I Am So Bullish

Two weeks ago I told you a Democratic win of the House and the Senate would be bearish short term but very bullish mid to long term. The Democrats now have the power to force Trump into exiting the war with Iran, something they want so they can have the reputation of peacemakers for the next election. Lower oil prices bring inflation down, the Fed stops hiking, the labor market weakens and the Fed starts cutting. Lower rates mean more money in the financial system, the devaluation of FIAT currencies and the appreciation of all assets priced against them, especially risk assets such as Bitcoin and Stocks. As if this was not enough, Bitcoin is trading below the MA200 Weekly, and throughout its history this has always been a great opportunity to buy at prices that were never seen again. We also have the market in extreme fear, at levels only seen during local bottoms, and the Daily RSI is showing one of its weakest readings ever, which has always marked local bottoms as well. Bears are wrong, higher is the way, the only way.

Weekly Calendar

On Monday, Fed Chairman Warsh speaks on the state of the economy. On Tuesday, NVDA reports earnings after the close, and the market is uncertain about what to expect. If NVDA beats, the noise about the AI trade being over ends and the SPX and NDX will start to bounce higher. I expect Bitcoin to follow the indexes after the NVDA report.

She was gifted to Diddy like a party favor right after he broke up with J.Lo. She was 23. Decades later, Piers Morgan asked if Diddy ever had sex with her. She froze, then whispered: "Not to my knowledge. Honestly, I'm questioning a lot of things right now." Her name is Superhead.

Karrine Steffans was born on a tiny island in the US Virgin Islands to a mother who would strip her naked and beat her until she lost consciousness. By 10, she'd been moved to Florida to live in poverty. By 13, she'd been raped. By 16, she was living on the streets. At 17, she moved in with rapper Kool G Rap - a man twice her age who offered her the first roof she'd ever had that didn't come with her mother's fists. He beat her so severely she ended up in the hospital with cracked ribs. When she was three months pregnant with his child, he threw her out and sent her to a homeless shelter. She gave birth to her son Naim at 19, alone, with nothing. Every person who was supposed to protect her had destroyed her instead.

By 21, Karrine was in Los Angeles with a toddler and no money. The only people interested in her were hip-hop executives who looked at her and saw a product, not a person. She started appearing in music videos - Jay-Z, R. Kelly, LL Cool J, Mystikal. She was beautiful, she was broken, and that combination made her extremely useful to powerful men who collected women the way other people collect watches. Jadakiss put her in a song called "Blood Pressure" and gave her the nickname "Superhead" - and just like that, everything she'd survived, everything she was, got reduced to a single word. The industry didn't just exploit her body. It branded her soul.

In 2001, right after Diddy's breakup with Jennifer Lopez, an anonymous record executive literally "gifted" Karrine to him - not introduced, gifted, like a bottle of Hennessy you send to somebody's table. "No one asked me if I wanted to go," she said years later. "They talked about me like I wasn't there. I was property to cart around." She became Irv Gotti's showpiece - whenever he wanted to impress someone, he would send them to her. She was passed between executives, rappers, and producers like an industry party favor nobody was supposed to talk about. When Piers Morgan asked decades later if she ever had a sexual relationship with Diddy, she said no at first - then something shifted in her face. "Well, not to my knowledge. I'm questioning a lot of things right now." Asked if Diddy ever took advantage of her while she was intoxicated: "I don't know. Given what we know now, I can't be sure." His former bodyguard Gene Deal confirmed the fear she'd been carrying for twenty years: "Puff says, 'Yo Gene, watch the door. Don't let nobody come to the door.'"

In 2005, Karrine published "Confessions of a Video Vixen" - a tell-all that named every name, exposed every room, and detonated like a nuclear bomb across hip-hop. It became a New York Times bestseller, sold nearly 200,000 copies, and put her on Oprah's couch. She went on to write seven books total. But the men she exposed didn't disappear - they got furious. At a party after the book dropped, Diddy spent the entire night glaring at her from across the room. She couldn't stop wondering what he was so afraid she might remember. "From Cosby to Combs, Weinstein to Epstein, and everything in between," she later said. "They're all different tentacles of the same beast."

The fame didn't save her from the pattern. She married actor Darius McCrary - Eddie Winslow from Family Matters - in 2009. Bobby Brown personally warned him before the wedding. "Bobby tried to warn me," McCrary later admitted. The marriage lasted two years. Then she married actor Columbus Short in 2015 and within a year was filing a restraining order. She suffered a miscarriage due to chronic anemia. By 2018, she formally killed the name the world knew - retired "Karrine Steffans" and "Superhead" forever, and began going by her birth name, Elisabeth Ovesen. She said the woman who'd been passed around like property didn't exist anymore. Not a single cell of her remained.

But in July 2025, she found herself sitting across from Piers Morgan, realizing that the night she'd always remembered as harmless - the night a record executive gifted her to a man who had just been convicted of transporting people for prostitution - might have been something far worse than she'd allowed herself to believe for over two decades.

Can a woman ever truly escape a name that an entire industry carved into her identity before she was old enough to understand what it would cost her?

Before accepting this story as true, we should ask a simple question: where is the evidence?

The post presents lengthy quotes supposedly from Elon Musk and Byron Donalds, yet no video, official transcript, news interview, press release, or verified social media post has been provided to support them. When a claim relies on direct quotations, the burden is on the person sharing them to show where they came from.

Independent fact-checkers have already found that similar quotes attributed to Elon Musk about Texas Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa were fabricated and could not be traced to any authentic source. The fact that Florida politicians have invited Tesla to consider relocating does not automatically make every viral quote about the issue genuine.

The statement also makes serious accusations that Gina Hinojosa is acting on orders from Barack Obama, Kamala Harris, and Democratic leaders to 'take down' Elon Musk. Extraordinary claims require extraordinary evidence. No evidence has been presented to support those allegations.

A reasonable discussion is whether Texas, Florida, or any other state offers the best environment for business investment. That is a legitimate debate. However, spreading unverified quotes and unsupported conspiracy theories does not strengthen an argument; it weakens it.

Facts should come before politics. If Elon Musk and Byron Donalds actually made these statements, there should be verifiable recordings, transcripts, or official posts. Until those sources are produced, the quotes should be treated as unverified and likely false rather than accepted as fact.

Having a hard time understanding #2. Jobs open at struggling programs, and Wisconsin is a great job by any measure. It’s a Big Ten program with Big Ten money operating with a healthy balance sheet, a proud tradition, one of the best college towns in the country, and a top academic school. On top of the added state subsidies, UW's donor base just substantially raised its football spending , and the school just opened the new $285M Kellner Center. The cupboard isn’t bare either: the Badgers are headed to a bowl, and the defense proved its talented enough to hold USC to 7 on a good night. 

For Eck specifically, it’s an obvious fit. He was born in La Crosse, walked on at UW, played on the ‘98 Rose Bowl team, and started coaching under Alvarez. He’s an offensive line coach who wins by running the ball, and that’s Wisconsin football.

So what job is beating him? FSU? The balance sheet is heavily leveraged, they’re paying a ~$50M buyout, and they’re coming off two terrible seasons with tons of donor fatigue. Eck has also never coached in Florida or the Deep South. 

USC? If Riley goes, that may be the toughest competition. USC will outspend everyone, but it’s a win-now job with an impatient fan base. Not surprisingly, Eck’s brand of football also meshes a lot better with Badger history than with USC’s. Wisconsin offers him home, his alma mater, and a bit more patience than a brand like USC.  

Colorado? The Lovo connection notwithstanding, it’s not happening.

Big picture, I just wouldn’t be dismissive of how good a job UW-Madison is right now. I think coaches will be very eager to interview for the opening.

text:
LIVERPOOL FC EVENING DEBRIEFING: LIVERPOOL WEIGH UP €55M ARAUJO DEAL AS FITNESS CONCERNS LINGER

The Spanish newspaper Marca reports that Liverpool are seriously considering taking up their €55m option to sign Ronald Araujo permanently next summer, and that Barcelona could not block the move if the option is exercised and the player agrees. There has still been no official word on his fitness, a week before Manchester United visit Anfield.

In Sunday night's Nations League games, Jeremy Jacquet played the full match and Bradley Barcola started as France beat Turkiye 2-1, while Rio Ngumoha and Victor Muñoz both stayed on the bench as England won 3-2 in Spain.

LIVERPOOL HOLD THE CARDS ON ARAUJO

Marca's Luis F. Rojo reported on Sunday morning that Liverpool's sporting department is seriously considering triggering the €55m purchase option in Ronald Araujo's season-long loan, with a view to signing him permanently next summer. The paper says the option can only be formally exercised at the end of the season, so a permanent move in January looks off. It adds that if Liverpool exercise the option and the player agrees, Barcelona could not block the move and could only try to persuade him to turn the offer down. It also says Barcelona are not planning for his return.

That fits with what Fabrizio Romano said on his YouTube channel: that Liverpool are not deciding anything now, "November, December or probably even January", and that they are very happy with Araujo's performances. He added that salary would also need to be negotiated if Liverpool decide to make the move permanent.

Araujo, 27, has played at right-back and centre-back since arriving in August. Liverpool have not commented. Credibility: Medium.

FITNESS WATCH

Neither Liverpool nor the Uruguayan federation had commented on Ronald Araujo's condition by Sunday night, two days after the Uruguayan newspaper El Observador reported that he finished the 2-1 win over Argentina in Buenos Aires walking with difficulty. Uruguay play the Dominican Republic in Maldonado on Tuesday night.

Liverpool have also issued no fresh update on Dominik Szoboszlai, who played the full game in Georgia on Saturday after nearly pulling out in the warm-up. He said afterwards: "Now the treatment starts all over again. I have to be ready again by Tuesday." Hungary host Northern Ireland in Budapest on Tuesday at 7.45pm UK time.

JACQUET PLAYS FULL MATCH AS FRANCE TOP THEIR GROUP

Jeremy Jacquet played the full 90 minutes at centre-back as France beat Turkiye 2-1 at the Stade Atlantique in Bordeaux to finish top of Nations League Group A1 and reach the quarter-finals. Ouest-France's player ratings headline said he impressed, and Foot Mercato gave him 5.5 out of 10, praising his solidity and his work in the air, although it said Arda Güler's movement caused him problems.

Bradley Barcola started on the left of France's attack and was replaced by Eli Junior Kroupi after 63 minutes. Foot Mercato gave him five out of 10, saying he was busy down the left but wasteful with his final touch. France went ahead through an Emirhan Topçu own goal from a corner early in the second half, Kroupi made it 2-0 from Rayan Cherki's pass, and Abdülkerim Bardakci pulled one back in injury time.

BENCH DUTY IN MADRID

Rio Ngumoha and Victor Muñoz were both unused substitutes as England beat Spain 3-2 at the Metropolitano, ending the world champions' 43-match unbeaten run and finishing top of Group A3. Harry Kane, Ezri Konsa and Ben White put England 3-0 up before Elliot Anderson was sent off, and Mikel Oyarzabal and Nico Williams replied for Spain.

MONDAY'S REDS ON DUTY

Florian Wirtz's Germany host Cody Gakpo's Netherlands in Berlin, and Kostas Tsimikas's Greece host Serbia in Volos, both at 7.45pm UK time. Trey Nyoni's England Under-21s face France in Bristol at 7.30pm.

TRANSFER TALK

The website Turkish Football claims Fenerbahce have an advantage in the race for Virgil van Dijk, whose Liverpool contract expires next summer, because of his friendship with their defender Nathan Aké. No established Liverpool reporter has backed it up. Credibility: Low.

text:
OK, this right here should just about wrap up this debate.

The skill level and difficulty of competition in the NCAA finals are as high as it gets in collegiate wrestling. You’re talking about the two best wrestlers at each weight facing each other for a national championship. The only comparable dual would be two teams consisting entirely of NCAA finalists.

Over the last 25 NCAA Championships, 250 finals have produced 530 takedowns, averaging 2.12 per match.

Furthermore, 60% of those finals featured 2+ takedowns, compared to just 30% in the Nebraska–Oklahoma State dual, where 7 of 10 matches had one takedown or fewer.

That’s TWICE the rate of multiple-takedown matches against the highest level of competition college wrestling has to offer.

So while skill level can certainly contribute to fewer takedowns, you cannot reasonably argue that the lack of takedowns in that dual was simply because the wrestlers were so highly skilled.

The last 25 NCAA Championships provide 250 examples of why that explanation alone doesn’t hold up.

text:
"Mr Inbetween"  Created, written and starred in by Scott Ryan of Australia.

I know I'm kinda late to the party since the last episode of this FX TV series was made in 2020, but . . .

For anyone looing for discerning viewing excellence, it is so worth the watch.   It rings particularly true for me these days by its stark contrast with the latest darling of the viewing public "Heart of the Beast."

My decidedly and irredeemably negative reviews ot the Beast have stirred up a shitstorm of negative commentary on me, many referring to my presumed lack of testicles -- some of my review reviewers apparently having exhausted their jr. high level vocabularies and being forced to revert to questioning my manhood, or lack thereof.  

But comparison of the two productions is quite appropriate.  Not that Mr. Inbetween is a dog story (although there is a tragic dog story subplot contained).  But Mr Inbetween is everything "Beast" is not. 

It is both action and character driven, with the emphasis on character.  And the characters, in addition to being beautifully drawn, are like the rest of the production, refreshingly real.  Scott Ryan, and whoever else was involved in casting, deftly avoided the Hollywood habit of making sure that every character is both incredibly attractive by traditional American Madison Avenue standards, and perfectly matched to their character's role in the production.  A protagonist like Pitt is shown to be somewhat tormented by an exaggerated 5 o'clock shadow and a few grey hairs but not quite enough to cover up his boyish Thelma and Louise good looks.  Villains in Hollywood are either faceless, as are enemy soldiers in the Beast (because god forbid Hollywood should offend some indentifiable viewing demographic like the Muslims), or are sneeringly obvious.  Not a turban or hijab in sight.

And par for the course with Hollywood, there are no complexities in the way Beast characters are written or portrayed.  Pitt may be tormented by his wartime experiences, but there is nothing in his character that hints at regret, second thoughts, or God forbid hesitation to act that might be misinterpreted as cowardice or unconfronted fear.  As for Odin, the perfectly telegenic German Shepherd, not enough that he is a combat vet dog, he has to have a prosthetic leg, titanium teeth (courtesy of an enemy combatant we are informed that Pitt then "shot in the head"), and phony scars drawn on his dog face.  I would not be at all surprised to learn that makeup artists had dyed parts of his fur to create the perfect mix of ferocity and cuddleness.  And despite the prosthetic leg, Odin remains tough enough to kill several wild wolves in the same encounter with no more than a minor superficial wound on on of his three remaining real legs.  No lingering effects of canine PTSD there.

The characters in Mr Inbetween are all ordinary looking peoples with lots of conflicting character attributes.  Ray Shoesmith (Scott Ryan's title character) is in many ways the opposite what Hollywood would cast an indomitable hitman to look like, but we learn through his actions, statements and attitudes that he's every bit as indomitable as a hitman needs to be in all circumstances.  At the same time, his more human and humane attributes, like his love for his incredibly well played preteen daughter, are seamlessly interwoven with his brutaliity.  We don't have to be served up lessons like "violence is bad" by having him strike his daughter or some equally trite incident.  His love interests (which are sparingly woven into the various plots) are refreshingly ordinary by Hollywood standards – not unattractive mind you, but real.  Normal weight, non-supermodel looks, butall the same, attractive and fuckable.  You won't find the smudged up supermodel posing as a barista, automechanic or some such nonsense.  And other characters, even those with minor or brief appearances, are amazingly drawn and portrayed – testimony to great writing, great directing and great acting.  Ray's best friend Gary is one great example, but by no means the only one.  And Ray's court-ordered attendance at anger management classesis, woven into e=several episodes, is not to be missed.

Oh and just so you know, spoiler alert, the dog does die this case, and his death appropriately and brtutally avenged by Ray, and not by some hackneyed description like "shot in the  head."

There are three seasons to Mr.InBetween, all equally good.  I recommend binge watching from season 1 through season 3.  Each episode is about 20 minutes.  It's just amazing entertaining thought-provoking theater.

There is a way to see all these episodes for free, but out of respect and deference to Scott Ryan I urge you to pay.  I think Amazon prime runs about $20 for each  season.

If you have any taste at all for incredibly high quality theatrical production, I can't recommend Mr InBetween enough.  Google search will quickly reveal I am not alone in my praise of Mr. InBetween or Scott Ryan,  Worth 100 times whatever the Beast apparntly cost to produce.

True to form, Scott Ryan apparently declined offers to create a Season 4, believing he had adequately filled out his main character's story arc.

text:
WORLD NEWS REPORT — NOVEMBER 15, 2026
Global Headlines | Politics • War • Economy • Health • Climate • Technology
THE BIG PICTURE
A dramatic American election, renewed Middle Eastern military escalation, persistent inflation, a nationwide aviation breakdown and a worsening African health emergency dominate international developments. Governments face a common challenge: protecting public safety and economic stability while navigating political divisions.

1. UNITED STATES — DEMOCRATS WIN CONGRESS
Democrats captured both the House of Representatives and Senate in the November 3 midterm elections, delivering a major setback to President Donald Trump.

Voter dissatisfaction with prices, the Iran war and government accountability contributed to Republican losses, including in traditionally conservative states.
The new congressional majorities take office in January 2027. They could increase oversight of the administration, challenge legislation and influence federal spending. However, divided government could also produce legislative deadlock.

Outlook: Congressional leadership, budget negotiations and the administration's response will shape American politics throughout 2027.

2. AMERICAN AVIATION — NATIONAL SYSTEM FAILURE

A November 13 Federal Aviation Administration communications failure caused an extraordinary nationwide ground stop.

By November 15, more than 2,300 flights had been canceled and approximately 7,700 delayed that day alone. Investigators identified serious router and network problems involving facilities in Arkansas and Texas.
Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said investigators had found no evidence of sabotage or cyberattack, but the ultimate technical cause remained uncertain.

The administration is seeking $50 billion for modernization. Democratic lawmakers question the request because substantial previously approved funding remains unspent.

Implications: Aging infrastructure has become an urgent transportation, economic and national-security concern.

3. MIDDLE EAST — IRAN, YEMEN AND GAZA

Iran's Revolutionary Guards claimed drone attacks against American military facilities in Bahrain. Bahrain reported intercepting Iranian attacks.

Meanwhile, Saudi-backed Yemeni forces withdrew from positions near the strategically important Bab el-Mandeb Strait, strengthening the position of Iran-aligned Houthi forces.
In Gaza, Hamas confirmed that senior commander Samir Abu Younis was killed in an Israeli strike on November 14. Despite the October 2025 ceasefire, violence continues.

The unresolved conflict threatens civilians, regional shipping, energy markets and diplomatic efforts. Claims about some military strikes remain independently unverified.

Outlook: Iranian diplomatic contacts with Oman offer a possible channel for negotiations, but no breakthrough is assured.

4. UKRAINE — DIFFICULT PEACE QUESTIONS

President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said American officials had floated the possibility of Ukraine surrendering the Donbas region in exchange for NATO membership.

This is a reported proposal, not an agreed settlement.
Ukraine's position emphasizes sovereignty and security guarantees. Russian territorial demands and European concerns about rewarding aggression complicate negotiations.

The war continues to affect European security, defense spending, reconstruction costs and international relations.

Central question: Can negotiators establish a durable peace without creating incentives for future territorial conquest?

5. GLOBAL ECONOMY — INFLATION REMAINS STUBBORN

American policymakers disagree about how the Federal Reserve should respond to inflation.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent argues against excessive interest-rate increases driven by temporary energy disruptions. Federal Reserve officials warn that inflation has spread beyond oil into services and other economic sectors.
The Fed's December 8–9 meeting will be closely watched.

Oil prices remain sensitive to Middle Eastern security. Brent crude settled at $95.84 per barrel on November 13.

Implications: Interest-rate decisions influence mortgages, savings, businesses, government borrowing and global investment.

6. AFRICA — EBOLA EMERGENCY

Africa's public-health authorities warn that the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo remains uncontrolled.

Official figures reported more than 11,200 infections and 5,500 deaths since the outbreak was declared in May.
Health officials identify insufficient resources, insecurity, weak contact tracing and delayed financial support as major obstacles.

These figures reflect reported government data and may change as surveillance improves.

Priority: Strengthening treatment, community engagement, surveillance and protection for medical personnel.

7. ASIA — MYANMAR'S POLITICAL FUTURE

At their Manila summit, Southeast Asian leaders maintained restrictions on Myanmar's full political representation while opening a conditional path toward restoring participation.

Myanmar has experienced civil war since its military overthrew the elected government in February 2021.
Regional governments disagree over how much diplomatic engagement might encourage reform without legitimizing military rule.

ASEAN requires meaningful progress toward reducing violence and implementing its peace framework.

8. CLIMATE — COP31 FACES DIVISIONS

United Nations climate negotiations in Turkey face serious disagreements about transitioning away from fossil fuels.

Countries dependent on petroleum resist binding restrictions, while climate-vulnerable nations seek stronger commitments and financing.
UN climate chief Simon Stiell has urged negotiators to overcome delays and reach meaningful agreements.

Outlook: The credibility of the summit will depend on concrete policies, financing and implementation—not declarations alone.

9. TECHNOLOGY — AI AND SPACE INDUSTRY

Artificial intelligence investment continues reshaping productivity, cybersecurity, employment and financial markets.

A coalition of organizations has sued major AI developers seeking restrictions on advanced systems. The allegations remain subject to judicial review.
Separately, a United Launch Alliance Vulcan rocket failed following its November 15 launch, destroying 40 Amazon Leo communications satellites.

The cause remains under investigation.

CONCLUSION — THE WORLD AT A CROSSROADS

Five developments deserve particular attention: America's political transition, Middle Eastern escalation, Ukraine's security negotiations, persistent inflation and the Congo health emergency.

Across these stories, the most consequential decisions concern accountability, human life, international cooperation and long-term stability.
The defining question is whether governments can turn immediate crises into lasting solutions rather than allow today's emergencies to become tomorrow's disasters.

text:
What are the job requirements for Indiana Secretary of State? Does Beau Bayh meet the requirements for this position? Use right leaning sources.

GROK says:

Legal requirements for Indiana Secretary of State are minimal and primarily derived from the state Constitution and Indiana Code.

Core Qualifications

Under Article 6, Section 1 of the Indiana Constitution, the Secretary is elected statewide for a four-year term. The only explicit constitutional limit is that no person may serve more than eight years in any 12-year period. The Constitution does not impose additional age, residency duration, or other specific eligibility criteria for this office (unlike the Governor, who must be at least 30 upon taking office, a U.S. citizen for five years, and a state resident for five years).⁠
Law.justia

Statutory requirements (primarily Indiana Code 3-8-1) include:

Being a registered voter in Indiana by the relevant filing deadline.⁠
Ballotpedia

Not being disqualified under IC 3-8-1-5 (examples of disqualifiers: certain felony convictions, having offered a bribe/threat/reward to procure election, having been previously removed from office, or other listed      factors). Active-duty military service can also affect eligibility in some contexts.

Filing required paperwork, such as a statement of economic interest.

There is no constitutional or clear primary statutory minimum age of 30 specifically for Secretary of State. Secondary sources (including some Wikipedia entries) sometimes list a 30-year age requirement “on the day they take the oath,” but this does not appear in the Constitution or standard candidate guides and appears to confuse the office with the Governor’s requirements. Council of State Governments data lists a practical minimum around 18 tied to voter eligibility.⁠
Bookofthestates⁠
Wikipedia

Candidates are nominated at party conventions (not the primary ballot) for this office.

Does Beau Bayh Meet the Requirements?

Yes, based on available public information, he meets the formal legal qualifications.

Age: 
Born November 8, 1995, in Indianapolis. He is 31 as of late 2026 and will be 31 when taking office (January 1, 2027). This satisfies any plausible age threshold, including the sometimes-cited 30-year figure.

Registered voter: 
He has been registered to vote in Indiana since age 18 (around the 2014 primary) and has voted in the state (often by mail or early while living elsewhere).⁠
Indianacapitalchronicle

Residency/citizenship: 
Born in Indiana. While he spent much of his childhood and early adulthood outside the state (family moved to the D.C. area after his father entered the U.S. Senate in 1998; he attended St. Albans, Harvard, served in the Marines, and completed Harvard Law), he maintained Indiana voting registration and ties. He returned full-time around 2024 (after law school and Marine service) to work as an attorney in Indianapolis. No fixed multi-year continuous residency is required for this office under the Constitution (unlike the      Governor’s five-year rule).

Other: 
Marine Corps veteran (honorably discharged as a captain), attorney (Indiana-licensed), no reported felony convictions or other disqualifiers. Election authorities accepted his candidacy; he won the Democratic nomination at the 2026 state      convention and the November 3, 2026 general election.

Right-Leaning Perspectives and Context

Right-leaning coverage (e.g., Washington Examiner) has highlighted Beau Bayh’s limited full-time residence in Indiana for much of his adult life, his elite East Coast prep-school/Harvard background, “nepo baby” status as the son of former Governor/Senator Evan Bayh and grandson of Senator Birch Bayh, and questions about whether he is a “real Hoosier.” These are political and optics critiques focused on authenticity, experience, and family dynasty rather than formal legal eligibility. They do not assert that he fails the constitutional or statutory requirements to hold the office.⁠
Washingtonexaminer

In short, the formal bar is low, and Beau Bayh clears it. Debates about his suitability center on experience, residency time, and political background rather than disqualifying legal shortfalls. For the most authoritative details, consult the Indiana Election Division’s candidate guides or the state code.

text:
Lyndon B. Johnson was America's 37th Vice President, and he went from the most powerful man in the Senate to one of the most frustrated men in Washington.

In World War II, as a young congressman, he got himself sent to the Pacific as an observer. In June 1942 he flew along on a bombing mission over New Guinea. His plane developed engine trouble and turned back before reaching the target. Douglas MacArthur gave him the Silver Star anyway, one of the highest combat decorations in the military. Nobody else on that plane got one. Johnson wore the ribbon for the rest of his life, and historians have argued about it ever since.

By the late 1950s he was Senate Majority Leader, famous for "the Johnson Treatment," where he'd tower over a senator, grab his lapels, and lean in until the man agreed with him.

In 1960 he wanted to be President, and Texas even changed its election law so he could run for vice president and his Senate seat at the same time. He won both. John F. Kennedy beat him for the nomination and then offered him the number two spot. Robert Kennedy hated the idea and tried to talk Johnson out of taking it.

The vice presidency was miserable for him. When he tried to keep running the Senate Democratic caucus, senators voted him down. Kennedy's young aides mocked him behind his back. He had almost no power.

So Kennedy gave him the space program. Johnson pushed hard for the goal of putting a man on the moon.

On a 1961 trip to Pakistan, he met a poor camel driver named Bashir Ahmad on the roadside and casually invited him to visit America. Bashir took him up on it. He flew to the U.S., toured the country, and visited Johnson's Texas ranch.

On November 22, 1963, Johnson was two cars behind Kennedy in Dallas. When the shots rang out, a Secret Service agent shoved him to the floor and threw his body over him.

Hours later, aboard Air Force One, a federal judge named Sarah Hughes swore him in, with Jacqueline Kennedy standing next to him in her bloodstained suit. Hughes is still the only woman to administer the presidential oath.

💊 Novel CRISPR therapy is poised to gain first FDA approval to alter genes inside the body

A pioneering therapy that edits genes inside a recipient’s body continues to be effective four years after treatment, according to data released by its developer, Intellia Therapeutics.

The therapy, named lonvoguran ziclumeran (lonvo-z), was designed to treat one form of a genetic condition that can cause episodes of painful and potentially dangerous swelling in the throat and other parts of the body. Lonvo-z deploys the CRISPR–Cas9 gene-editing system to disable the gene that produces prekallikrein, a protein made in the liver that promotes blood-vessel leakage.

❗️ Intellia, headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts, has applied for approval of lonvo-z by the U.S. FDA, which is expected to issue a decision by 10 March. 

If approved, the therapy will become the world’s first CRISPR medicine to be delivered directly inside the body, or in vivo. Currently, the only CRISPR therapy approved by the FDA is performed on cells that have been removed from the body and are subsequently re-infused.

"For people with the condition, a type of hereditary angioedema, the gene-editing approach could offer relief from a lifetime of juggling medications to prevent and treat swelling attacks,” — says Jonathan Bernstein, a hereditary-angioedema specialist at the University of Cincinnati in Ohio and an investigator on a lonvo-z trial.

text:
Saturday 14 November 2026 Homeless Outreach in Downtown Syracuse

It was a cold and wet day in the North Country – Saturday 14 November 2026, especially where I live on Fort Drum New York. The mission was to load up everything I had in storage from donations and things acquired on my own for the homeless over a period of a few months. There were some people who came to me who donated scarves, gloves, jackets, cash (which I used to purchase canned goods), socks, personal hygiene items like deodorant and baby wipes. For those who offered these items to those in need on the streets, I thank you very much for your contribution as it was put to good use. I am sure the Lord will bless you in many ways for your efforts and goodwill.

On my way down highway Route 81 South through the Tug Hill region (a place known for random lake effect snow) from Watertown down to Syracuse, I came across the first snow that I have witnessed for the season, as it was pouring down along the route and filling up the trees and the ground. Driving through it, I wondered how people survive on the streets during the winter months? On my way into the city, I picked up fellow Evangelist and Lay Dominican Mr. Jeramyah Baxtron, OP who often volunteers to walk with me through the city to evangelize, share the gospel message, share Christ’s love, and to assist the homeless with their needs as Christ commanded. He also used to live in the area and often gives me tours around the city as to where to find homeless and those suffering from addictions, as he is very knowledgeable of the area and has a long history with the place.

Once we saddled up, we moved into the area of East Onondaga St. by the Immaculate Conception Cathedral where we parked the truck to begin our mission. We had an excess number of supplies that we could not carry in our ruck sacks over our backs, so we left the remaining in the back of the truck. The plan was to find people in need where they are, whether under bridges or on the sides of buildings getting warm away from the rain, and then to come back to this location and drop whatever remaining items we have, as there were a group of people waiting in the cold and rain for the Catholic Charities to open up for supplies. 

When we set out on foot through Columbus Circle, we immediately came across those in need. We talked with a woman named Candy for a moment about her situation and needs before providing her food and water. I mentioned how I liked the name “Candy,” as when I was in infantry basic training long ago on Fort Benning, my unit was called one five-O “Candyland” as that name always left a lasting impression on me. We also had a young man named Joseph come up to us who seemed very sick and needed some food and water. After we provided them and a few others with socks and additional supplies, including rosaries and Saint Paul Street Evangelization information brochures on “Salvation,” Jeramyah led us the group in prayer to Christ to provide for their needs both physically and spiritually. From there, we moved through the circle North on State Street under the bridge where we figured we would find some people hunkering down getting warm. Unfortunately, it was empty. So, we kept moving along State Street.

About a mile down the road, we turned around and hit North Salinas St. and back tracked into the downtown area looking and searching into alleyways, sides of buildings, and park benches for those in need. After some time being unsuccessful, we eventually came across a gentleman named Scott who was getting warm underneath the side of a building along the road. Scott told us that he was in prison for 45 years and that he is one of the main advocates in this area for the homeless, as he was also in the news, and acts as their representative at times to other organizations. Scott also is granted the opportunity to sleep in the Church at certain hours to get warmth and rest and is very grateful for this. Before prison, Scott had told me that he was deeply involved in Satanism and the occult, but turned to Christ during his period of incarceration.

Jeramyah and I offered him some food to which he was receptive but told us that he had gloves and everything else he needed (he seemed more concern about us giving what we had left to other people in need). As Scott began an intimate discussion with Jeramyah about occult ties and past satanism, I saw Joseph once again and began talking with him. Shortly after, a man we met many months ago whom we helped to clean the wounds on his legs and feet, where a woman approached us screaming at a different time, came up to us asking for some support. Right after this, three other men approached us in need, which is great because I was starting to think there was nobody around to receive aid (which would have been I good thing I suppose, especially in the cold rain).

During this interaction, I spoke with a man named Rob who was pushing a shopping cart with cans and bottles past our group. He was with his son named Charles who had a very large cyst growing on his left eye. I assumed he got hit in the face and offered to treat it, but after getting the story of what his condition was, Charles was still in high spirits. He told me that it gets to a point where the doctors must remove it, then it grows back again. His father Rob is very religious and positive, as he looked up to the sky with his hand raised and said, “This place is just a training ground for Heaven.” I agreed. Speaking of cysts, I wish I had some holy water from Lourdes France in that moment because I have heard of its healing properties. My wife was given some water from Lourdes from one of our Church parishioners named Anne Seegebarth who helped me and my children enter the Church during our RCIA (introduction instruction into the Catholic Church) classes a few years ago. Anne is passed away now (God bless her soul) and had a tremendous amount of faith. The same water she had given my wife, took my wife’s cyst (she also had many others along her head that disappeared after the water was applied) away on top of her head shortly after its application (Anne passed away shortly after given my wife the water and was gone when my wife applied it). Her cyst which kept growing over her head (after being removed, but coming back more numerous) and causing her pain and headaches for many years was becoming an increasing problem for her until the water removed it (by faith). My wife said after she applied the water, she lost some of her hair and bubbling on her scalp formed. Then when the bubbling went away, the cyst was gone and her hair grow back over like nothing ever happened. So, if you know anyone who went to Lourde’s and has water from there, please send it my way as I will try to apply it on people who have the faith to receive it in the streets when we come across them. 

Many of those who are homeless are suffering from ailments and often go without medical checkups and treatments. 

Once we wrapped up this interaction, we passed out some religious material and some money to provide for their needs, reminding them that it came from Lord Jesus Christ. A homeless person Jeramyah knew personally from the past also came up to us and asked for a smoke after this occurred. I asked him what his name was and if he wanted to know about Christ, to which the man given me a mean look and replied, “My name is Jasmine. No.” Jeramyah asked the man if he remembered him, to which he did. The man then walked away in silence. Please pray for his conversion, as this person has had a very tragic background with sexual abuse, mental illness, and transgenderism. 

We then made our way on foot with our rucksacks still on our back across Columbus Circle to the Oncenter. Along the way, we came across an elderly man named Tom who had his luggage next to him. We asked him if he needed anything like food or water, to which he agreed. He also accepted a rosary and was very receptive to the message of Christ Jesus and the gospel. He mentioned that he too would pass some of these things out to those in need when he finds them. He also agreed to pray with us and did the sign of the cross with us. Before we left, he gave me a hug and thanked us. Please pray for Tom’s protection. 

Moving along the streets past the Oncenter, we came across two women sitting down in front of a building staying out of the rain. One of them, Alexis, was responsive to us when we asked if they needed anything. The other, an older lady seemed very aggressive and demanded that we take Alexis with us. The angry woman did not want any of our help. Alexis wanted some food, feminine hygiene products, and some religious materials, and appeared upset or frightened by the woman. She also had wounds on her leg that needed to be treated, so I told her to come with us down the streets by the side steps of the Oncenter where we could treat her leg. She agreed. This also made the other woman happy; on our way out, I reminded the angry woman of what Christ said – “To love your neighbor as yourself.” She smiled at me in response and said nothing.

Once further down the road, Alexis rolled up her right leg pant to reveal a long dirty bandage going down her calf, to which she revealed many bloodied and potentially infected/unclean open wounds. Jeramyah and I proceeded to treat it with band aids and Neosporin. I asked Alexis if I could disinfect it with peroxide, but she refused. She also refused for me to wash it with my soapy water bottle but only accepted the band aids and Neosporin. During this application, Alexis began to turn aggressive towards us saying “I am not a baby or a child.” Then she proceeded to say things like, “Zombies gotta feed, it’s time to feed,” along with other things like “My avatar is getting hungry. I am from the layer, what do you know about that?” As I redirected her, she kept going on about food. She then proceeded to say, “Everyone is going to be on meth.” After she mentioned Subway food, we offered her a meal to calm her down. She rolled up her pant leg before we could finish patching her up, then she said, “Take all of this crap you gave me I don’t want it.” We stuffed the original provisions we given her into our ruck sacks and began to walk with her. As we walked, she became increasingly aggressive – speaking of coming from a “layer” and “avatars.” Jeramyah and I began to redirect her with words about faith, Christ, and what kinds of toppings she would get on her sub. This seemed to calm her down.

When we walked past the Cathedral, she mentioned Christ being Allah. We reminded Alexis that Christ Jesus was not Allah, but God and Divine – the Second Person of the Holy Trinity, something Jeramyah knows all about as he too was a former Muslim. She then continued on about her avatar and coming from the layer and wanting to feed. Once we got to Subway, Jeramyah and I saw Eric walking down the street and invited him in with Alexis. We paid for Eric and Alexis’ subs and food, which seemed to make them happy as they had a place to get warm for a while and fill their stomachs. On the way out, we reminded them of who bought their meal – Lord Jesus Christ and they thanked us. 

At times, Alexis seemed there and responsive, then suddenly, it would appear that she would check out and say perverse things. She also mentioned how she wanted to go home. Please pray for Alexis to overcome addiction, mental health problems, and diabolic attacks from evil spirits associated with addiction (which is very common today).

After this, we headed back to the supply point (my truck) by the cathedral. We noticed more homeless individuals congregating out in the circle waiting for the charities to open up in the cold. As we approached, we yelled out loud reminding them of our supply drop by the corner of the charities building and they all came over. We dumped our entire supply of food, water, clothes, and hygiene products for them to grab and for whoever may come across in need. Jeramyah and I agreed that it’s better this stuff goes to people in need now before the real cold hits, rather than sitting in a corner collecting dust. The people were very grateful and also received holy rosaries from our Blessed Mother Mary and also information tracts on the Salvation of Christ Jesus through His one and only Church founded upon the apostles – The Roman Catholic Church, who are the successors of the Levitical Priesthood of the Old Testament. Before we departed the area, the group allowed me to pray over them invoking Christ for their spiritual protection and physical needs, all in the name of Jesus. I even got a chance to use my Cohen Levitical Priesthood (Old Testament priesthood before the Apostles) hand signal during the prayer, which also felt very right and good. 

Please pray for these people to always be in the presence of Christ no matter what situation they are in and for their minds, hearts, and physical needs to always be wrought in the Holy Trinity, in the Name of Jesus – Amen!

text:
Love the Motherland—Respect Its Mothers

For centuries, rulers demanded love for the motherland. But what happened to its mothers?

Genghis Khan’s conquests shattered families. Hitler’s regime murdered millions. Mussolini’s wars brought suffering. Stalin’s purges, Mao’s campaigns, and repression under the Kim dynasty cost countless lives.

Power also wounded women inside royal courts. Ancient chronicles describe Empress Lü Zhi’s brutal mutilation of Consort Qi. Foot-binding restricted generations of Chinese women; European witch hunts killed many accused women. The fictional Empresses in the Palace dramatizes women forced into rivalry for imperial favor.

Jiang Qing helped persecute others during Mao’s Cultural Revolution, then stood trial after his death. She bore responsibility, but Mao’s leadership responsibility cannot be erased.

Today, Ukrainian mothers love their homeland while Russia’s invasion kills civilians and separates families. Patriotism cannot justify denying another nation’s mothers safety.

We must beware political “Trojan horses” who praise liberty while seeking unchecked power. Questions about Bao Xiaoyu require evidence, not unverified accusations. Power concentrated under Putin, Xi Jinping, and Kim Jong-un warrants scrutiny.

What mother wants her child imprisoned for speaking freely? What child wants their mother denied education, work, property, or independence?

Constitutional democracy offers a different vision: equal citizenship, independent courts, accountable government, and protections against abuse. Across constitutional democracies, women have become presidents and prime ministers—not possessions of powerful men.

A free motherland honors its mothers as full human beings. Love of country and freedom belong together.

Government of the people, by the people, for the people.

God bless every mother.

text:
A Louisiana Romance 
Romance found me most often in the dance halls of South Louisiana. Down here, music isn’t something you hear—it’s something that breathes through the floorboards, humming in the heartbeat of every accordion and fiddle. It’s the language of longing, spoken in waltzes and two-steps, whispered in the sway of bodies moving close. 
I danced with women I knew well and women I had just met, spinning beneath lights that glimmered like fireflies caught in summer dusk. The air was alive with laughter, the scent of gumbo curling through the room, and the soft swish of skirts tracing the rhythm like poetry. Some nights were just steps and songs—but others felt like sparks, like the universe had hidden a little magic on the dance floor just for me. 
One night, the magic didn’t just flicker—it blazed. She walked in like a melody the band had been waiting to play, her presence turning heads without effort. Her smile was gentle, but her eyes—Lord, her eyes—held a rhythm all their own, a secret cadence that pulled me in before I even asked her name. When I offered my hand, hers slid into mine as if it had always belonged there. 
We moved together like the music had written us into its story. The accordion sang, the fiddle cried, and somewhere between the two, the world outside those walls fell away. It was just her laughter, soft and bright, and the warmth of her touch anchoring me in a moment I never wanted to end. Every turn brought her closer, every step a promise I didn’t know I was making. 
When the song faded, we didn’t let go. The hall buzzed around us, but for a breath, it felt like we were the only two souls in South Louisiana. Then she smiled—a smile that felt like sunrise breaking over the bayou—and said, “Same time next Saturday?” 
I nodded, though my heart was already racing ahead to every Saturday after that. Because love doesn’t always arrive with grand gestures or perfect timing. Sometimes it slips in on the back of a melody, under the glow of string lights, and asks you to dance—not just for tonight, but for all the nights to come………

text:
*Why is 'Abhishekam' (ceremonial bathing) performed for a deity's idol?*
There are profound spiritual, scientific, and social reasons behind performing 'Abhishekam'—the ceremonial bathing of a deity's idol—in temples and homes. Below are the key reasons for this practice, which is carried out using *Panchamritam* (a mixture of five sacred substances) and holy water, accompanied by the chanting of Vedic mantras.

☘️🌻🌻🌻🌻🌹🌻🌻🌻🌻☘️

1. Spiritual Reasons (Devotion and Purification)
Offering Hospitality (*Shodashopachara*): In Indian tradition, we regard the deity as the most exalted guest visiting our home. Just as one would offer water for a guest to wash their feet and make arrangements for them to bathe, *Abhishekam* (bathing) serves as a central component of the *Shodashopachara Puja*—the sixteen-step ritual of offering hospitality to the Divine.

Preserving the Energy of *Prana-pratishtha*: According to *Agama Shastra* (scriptures governing temple rituals), when *Prana-pratishtha* (consecration) is performed, divine energy is invoked within the idol. To ensure that this energy does not diminish due to the constant influx of devotees and rituals, *Abhishekam* is performed alongside the chanting of Vedic mantras, keeping the idol perpetually vibrant and spiritually charged.

Purifying the Mind: The act of cleansing the deity's idol serves as a symbolic reminder for us to wash away the ego, anger, and impurities within our own minds, leading us toward a state of inner purity.
2. Scientific Reasons (Energy and Preservation of Idols)
Energy Absorption: The primary idols (mula-virat) in temples are crafted from specific black stone (*krishna-shila*) or a five-metal alloy (*panchaloha*). Through the sound waves of Vedic chants and the *abhishekam* (ritual bathing) performed with various substances, positive energy becomes embedded within these materials. Devotees can access this energy either by consuming the *theertham* (consecrated liquid) offered after the *abhishekam* or by standing within the *garbhagudi* (sanctum sanctorum).

Preservation and Durability of Idols: The substances used during *abhishekam* help ancient idols remain intact and well-preserved for centuries.
Sesame oil and ghee: These prevent cracks in stone idols, retain moisture, and protect the stone from wear and tear.
Turmeric, *kumkum* (vermilion), and sandalwood: These contain natural anti-bacterial properties that protect the idol from the accumulation of germs or microbes.
Milk, yogurt, and honey: These impart a natural luster and smoothness to the stone.
Medicinal Properties (*Theertham*): Ingredients used in the *abhishekam*such as milk, yogurt, honey, coconut water, turmeric, *tulasi* (holy basil), and *bilva* leaves—absorb the mineral properties of the idol, transforming into a potent, sacred medicine. Ayurveda suggests that consuming this *theertham* helps boost the body's immunity.
3. Gratitude Towards Nature
Every substance used in an *abhishekam* (ritual bathing of a deity)—such as milk, yogurt, ghee, honey, fruit juices, and water—is a gift from nature. The *abhishekam* serves as a testament to a spirit of gratitude, expressing the sentiment: "O Lord, we offer back to You the very treasures of nature that You have bestowed upon us."
Substances Used in *Panchamrita Abhishekam* and Their Benefits
According to the *shastras* (scriptures), each substance used in an *abhishekam* yields a specific, unique benefit:

Pure Water: Mental peace and liberation from hardships.

Milk: Longevity and the blessing of progeny.

Yogurt: Good health, strength, and familial well-being.

Ghee: Prosperity and the attainment of *moksha* (liberation).

Honey: Sweetness of speech, radiance, and charm.

Sugar: Removal of sorrow and the attainment of joy.

Coconut Water: Abundance of all forms of wealth and the fulfillment of desires.

Sandalwood Paste: The grace of Goddess Lakshmi, along with fame and prestige.

*Vibhuti* (Sacred Ash): Wisdom and liberation from sins.

text:
(Mat 26:59-61 NIV)  The chief priests and the whole Sanhedrin were looking for false evidence against Jesus so that they could put him to death. {60} But they did not find any, though many false witnesses came forward. Finally two came forward {61} and declared, "This fellow said, 'I am able to destroy the temple of God and rebuild it in three days.'"

a. Now the chief priests, the elders, and all the council: This nighttime trial was illegal according to the Sanhedrin’s own laws and regulations. According to Jewish law, all criminal trials must begin and end in the daylight. Therefore, though the decision to condemn Jesus was already made, they conducted a second trial in daylight (Luke 22:66-71), because they knew the first one – the real trial – had no legal standing.

i. This was only one of many illegalities made in the trial of Jesus. According to Jewish law, only decisions made in the official meeting place were valid. The first trial was held at the home of Caiaphas, the high priest.

· According to Jewish law, criminal cases could not be tried during the Passover season.

· According to Jewish law, only an acquittal could be issued on the day of the trial. Guilty verdicts had to wait one night to allow for feelings of mercy to rise.

· According to Jewish law, all evidence had to be guaranteed by two witnesses, who were separately examined and could not have contact with each other.

· According to Jewish law, false witness was punishable by death. Nothing was done to the many false witnesses in Jesus’ trial.

· According to Jewish law, a trial always began by bringing forth evidence for the innocence of the accused, before the evidence of guilt was offered. This was not the practice here.

ii. “These were the Sanhedrin’s own rules, and it is abundantly clear that, in their eagerness to get rid of Jesus, they broke their own rules.” (Barclay)

iii. “Neither in the annals of the historian nor in the realm of fiction is there anything that can equal the degradation of the unholy trial, the base devices to find a charge to prefer against the Prisoner, the illegal tricks to secure a verdict of guilty which would ensure a death penalty.” (Morgan)

b. The council sought false testimony against Jesus to put Him to death, but found none: This is a remarkable testimony to the life and integrity of Jesus. For having lived such a public life and performed such a public ministry, it was difficult to find even false testimony against Him.

c. This fellow said, “I am able to destroy the temple of God and to build it in three days”: After all the false witnesses had their say, Jesus was finally charged with threatening to destroy the temple (as in a modern-day bomb threat). Clearly, Jesus said “Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up” (John 2:19). But this glorious prophecy of His resurrection was twisted into a terrorist threat. John 2:21 makes it clear that He was speaking of the temple of His body.

text:
Zul 2026: Festival of a Thousand Butter Lamps on December 3

Zul is one of the most important holidays in the Kalmyk calendar. In 2026 it falls on Thursday, December 3, according to the lunar calendar used at the Golden Abode of Buddha Shakyamuni in Elista. The day is an official public holiday in the Republic of Kalmykia and is widely observed by Kalmyk communities in Russia and in the diaspora.

The name Zul comes from the Kalmyk word for a butter lamp or oil lamp. Lighting lamps is the central act of the holiday. The festival combines two meanings. It is the traditional Kalmyk winter New Year, when every person symbolically adds one year to their age. At the same time it commemorates the parinirvana of Je Tsongkhapa, the founder of the Gelug school of Tibetan Buddhism, which Kalmyks have followed for centuries. The Buddhist observance is also known as Zul Khural or the Festival of a Thousand Lamps.

In the weeks before Zul, the Central Khurul in Elista holds a series of life-extending rituals called Nasn utdullhgn. In 2026 these take place on the weekends of November 14-15, 21-22, and 28-29, from 9:00 AM to 11:30 AM. Devotees join the monks in prayers to Buddha Amitayus, White Tara, and Ushnishavijaya for long life, the removal of obstacles, and the strengthening of vital energy. These services prepare the community for the main holiday.

On the day of Zul itself, families light special lamps known as “boats of life.” Small boat-shaped forms are made from dough. Into each boat are placed wicks of grass or straw equal to a person’s age, plus one or two extra strands as a request for additional years. The wicks are soaked in clarified butter and lit when the first stars appear in the evening. The lamps are allowed to burn out on their own. This ritual, called nasn avakh or us avah, is performed in homes and is the most distinctive family custom of the holiday. Many families also light a second lamp with nine wicks, a number considered auspicious.

At the temples, monks conduct special prayers dedicated to Tsongkhapa and light hundreds or thousands of butter lamps. Families bring offerings and receive blessings. In homes, people prepare traditional Kalmyk tea (jomba) and bake bortsg biscuits. Fresh tea and some biscuits are placed on the household altar as offerings to the deities and ancestors before anyone eats. On this day people are encouraged to perform good deeds, offer well-wishes, and avoid harmful actions.

In the diaspora, Zul is also marked with community gatherings. In 2026 a concert dedicated to the holiday is scheduled for December 5 in Moscow, featuring Kalmyk singers, dancers, and traditional music. Kalmyk families in the United States and elsewhere often light lamps at home or attend local temple services on or near the date announced by the Central Khurul.

Zul remains a living bridge between the older nomadic calendar and Buddhist practice. It is both a day of collective renewal, when the whole people grows one year older together, and a day of spiritual remembrance. The light of the butter lamps symbolizes the warmth and hope that carry families through the winter months.
