text:
Andrew Lapin, Jewish Telegraphic Agency
Steven Van Zandt is worried about the Jews.
“There is that pre-Holocaust vibe,” the Rock and Roll Hall of Famer told the Jewish Telegraphic Agency recently about what he sees on social media, where he is a prolific user. “They spread lies around year after year after year, and if you say something often enough, people start to believe it.
“And that’s what happened that led to the Holocaust in the first place, and that’s what’s going on now.”
For a man equally beloved for his longtime work with Bruce Springsteen in the E Street Band and his role as Silvio on HBO’s “The Sopranos,” such a detour might seem unusual. But Van Zandt is looking to make his own mark in the world of Holocaust education, via his education initiative TeachRock, which since 2013 has provided K-12 lesson plans on a range of subjects built around popular music.
Titled “Jewish Heritage and the Holocaust: Exploring an Enduring Culture Through Music,” the initiative’s four-day lesson plan, launched this week, includes the onset of antisemitism in prewar Europe, survivor testimony and Jewish values. Anchoring the lessons are rock songs from the likes of KISS, the half-Jewish glam metal band, beloved Jewish folk singer Leonard Cohen and contemporary New York pop band Lawrence, which is fronted by two Jewish siblings.
It’s a departure from the somber tone of most Holocaust education programs, a space that the Jewish community has heavily invested in despite mounting questions about the effectiveness of such lessons in curbing antisemitism. Other contemporary Holocaust learning initiatives have employed video games, artificial intelligence and similarly novel approaches as educators struggle to adapt to a near future without living survivors to share their testimonies.
For Van Zandt, the lessons aren’t just teaching about the Holocaust, but also about highlighting positive Jewish influence in the world of popular culture. He rattled off a list of Jewish artists he admires, including Bob Dylan and the pop songwriting team Lieber and Stoller.
“I have a lot of gratitude for what they have contributed to my life, just in terms of enjoyment,” he said. “Show business doesn’t exist without the Jewish contributions.”
The guitarist founded TeachRock in 2013 alongside other big names from the world of music and the arts, including Springsteen, U2 frontman Bono, Jackson Browne and the director Martin Scorsese. On Thursday, the organization piloted its new Holocaust education lesson plan to 50 high school students at the Florida Holocaust Museum in St. Petersburg, timed to the state’s Holocaust Education Week. Florida’s Holocaust education task force is promoting the material to districts across the state.

“We always want to be educating in a way that feels like you’re not being taught. And I think this captures that,” Michael Igel, a contributing author on the TeachRock lesson plan who also chairs the statewide task force, told JTA.

For Igel, a descendant of survivors, the project fits neatly into his own efforts to bring Holocaust education into unconventional spaces. He’s planning future courses that incorporate food and theater.

“It’s still standards-based Holocaust education. But it’s being delivered to students in these different portals,” he said.

It was through Igel’s promotion of such nontraditional methods that he was approached by a member of TeachRock’s leadership council a year ago. TeachRock had recently been looking to offer lessons on Jewish heritage, and saw an opportunity to broach the subject of the Holocaust through Igel.
A huge E Street Band fan, Igel laughed as he recalled how the council member asked him if he had ever heard of Van Zandt.
The first of the curriculum’s four days opens with students listening to “Rock and Roll All Nite,” the 1975 hit by rock band KISS, before segueing into Jewish life in prewar Europe and the rise of antisemitism.
Igel noted the unique nature of the lesson. “When Gene Simmons with his tongue out is the first thing you see, you’re wondering, ‘What the heck happened to Holocaust education?’” he said.

text:
SURGERY PARTNERS $SGRY TOOK $25 OVER A $28 PROPOSAL:

The Momentum Len5 is watching Surgery Partners (SGRY) at $26.95, +$0.37 / +1.39% on Friday.

Surgery Partners, the Brentwood, Tennessee operator of surgery centers and surgical hospitals in 30 states, is #26 there and not a fit, because most of its six-month gain came in two sessions, each on an offer for the whole company. On November 9 it announced a higher cash price from its buyer, HealthSpan Partners, an affiliate of the nonprofit hospital system Bon Secours Mercy Health, after a committee of its directors turned down an unnamed party's $28.00 a share. Friday's close is above the most HealthSpan has agreed to pay. Bloomberg reported that the unnamed party is UnitedHealth Group (UNH) at $407.46, +$2.33 / +0.58% on Friday. Shareholders outside Bain Capital, the private investment firm that owns about 39%, vote separately on the deal, and that vote has no date.

- Momentum Len5: NOT A FIT, #26. Momentum wants gains built over one, three and six months; Surgery Partners is up 85.2%, 77.4% and 88.3% over those spans, and two sessions made most of the gain. It would fit the Momentum Len5 if the shares kept climbing on the company's own results, with no offer behind the price.
- Quality Len5: NOT A FIT. Quality wants a profit with debt under the owners' stake, the money shareholders have in the business; Surgery Partners lost $72.0M in the nine months to September 30 and owed $3.06B of long-term debt against a $1.66B stake. A profitable year with debt under that stake would bring it into view for the Quality Len5.
- Quality-Value and Deep-Value and Special-Situations Len5es: NOT A FIT. Both want a profitable business at a discount; Surgery Partners lost $77.9M in 2025, and offers for the company now set its price. Several profitable years at a low price against that profit would bring it into view for both.
- Hypergrowth Len5: NOT A FIT. Hypergrowth wants sales multiplying; revenue at the facilities Surgery Partners ran in both periods rose 6.0% in July-September from a year earlier. Sales doubling year after year would bring it into view for the Hypergrowth Len5.
- Income Len5: NOT A FIT. Income wants cash paid to owners; Surgery Partners pays no dividend. A declared dividend that profit covers would bring it into view for the Income Len5.

The six-month gain, in dollars a share:
- Six months to Friday, from the May 13 close of $14.31: +$12.64.
- October 26, the first session after the HealthSpan agreement, from $15.75: +$7.50.
- November 9, the day the higher price was announced, from $23.20: +$3.25.
- Every other session of those six months, together: +$1.89.
Friday's close is the highest since November 12, 2024.

HealthSpan's higher price came six days after the $28.00 proposal.
- October 23: Surgery Partners agrees to be bought for $23.50 a share in cash.
- November 3: an unnamed party proposes $28.00 a share in cash, in a proposal that is not binding, and updates it on November 8.
- November 9: HealthSpan's price becomes $25.00. If shareholders have approved the deal and it has not closed by March 1, 2027, HealthSpan adds payments at 10% a year on the $25.00, up to $1.61 a share if closing takes until October 23, 2027, the agreement's last day.
The committee said the $28.00 proposal "would be expected to take materially longer to close" or "may not close", and cited "the regulatory risk and complexity" of a deal with that party. Surgery Partners expects the HealthSpan deal to close in the first quarter of 2027.

Friday's close is above every price HealthSpan has agreed to and under the proposal the committee refused.
- HealthSpan, if the deal closes by March 1, 2027: $25.00, $1.95 under Friday's close.
- HealthSpan at most: $26.61, $0.34 under.
- The refused proposal: $28.00, $1.05 above.
Our read: buyers at $26.95 expect an offer higher than any Surgery Partners has accepted.

Bloomberg named UnitedHealth as the party behind the $28.00; Surgery Partners has named no one. UnitedHealth's Optum unit bought SCA Health, another operator of surgery centers, in 2017, so a purchase of Surgery Partners would put two such operators under one owner. UnitedHealth is on none of the Momentum, Quality-Value, Deep-Value and Special-Situations, Hypergrowth or Income Len5es; at about 20 times the profit it forecasts for 2026 on its own adjusted measure, its price is no discount.

The October 23 agreement needs two approvals: a majority of all shares, and a majority of the votes cast by holders other than Bain Capital's funds, directors and top officers. Bain Capital's funds have agreed to vote for the deal and will keep their stake in the company, taking no cash. In January 2025 Bain Capital proposed $25.75 a share for the shares it did not own, and a committee of Surgery Partners's directors turned that down in June 2025. HealthSpan's $25.00 is $0.75 under it. By Friday Surgery Partners had set no date for the vote.

Surgery Partners is on the Momentum Len5 because of two offer days, and Friday's buyers paid more than the signed deal pays on any timetable. No binding offer above $26.61 has been made public. If none comes and the deal closes by March 1, 2027, holders outside Bain Capital receive $25.00 a share.

text:
Elon Musk lost a $56 billion pay package to a man who owned 9 Tesla shares. A judge voided the deal, then ordered Tesla to pay that man's lawyers $345 million, after they asked for $5.6 billion.

Then Delaware's Supreme Court gave it all back. By then the package was worth $139 billion. The man with 9 shares got $1.

In the video below, Musk walks on stage right after shareholders voted for his pay a second time: "Hot damn, I love you guys."

In 2018 Tesla's board offered Musk options on 304 million shares, about 9% of the company, if Tesla hit a set of huge targets. It hit every one.

Richard Tornetta, a former heavy metal drummer with 9 shares, sued that same year.

In January 2024 a Delaware judge struck the deal down and called it "unfathomable."

His lawyers asked for $5.6 billion in fees. The judge called that a windfall and gave them $345 million.

In June 2024 shareholders voted for the package again. In December the judge rejected it again.

Musk moved Tesla's legal home from Delaware to Texas.

On December 19, 2025, the Delaware Supreme Court reversed it, unanimously. Throwing the deal out, it said, left Musk "uncompensated for his time and efforts over a period of six years." The lawyers' fee was cut by about 80%. Damages: $1.

Musk said he was "vindicated."

9 shares froze the biggest paycheck in history for 7 years. The final bill for the man who started it: $1.

Did the system protect shareholders, or did 9 shares nearly cost Musk $139 billion?

BRANIFF HISTORY TODAY - On this day, Wednesday, November 15, 1978, Braniff International inaugurated new nonstop service between Denver and Houston and between Chicago and San Antonio. The new service further enhanced Braniff's direct through-plane and/or connecting service between each of the city pairs and also enhanced flights between the Southwest and both the Rocky Mountains and the Upper Midwest.

Prior to the inauguration of nonstop service, Braniff service between Houston Intercontinental Airport and Denver Stapleton International Airport was only offered via connection service through Dallas/Ft. Worth Regional Airport. However, the addition of a single roundtrip every day except Monday and Tuesday, gave Braniff passengers a highly convenient alternative to the seven daily and two except Saturday connecting flights through DFW. Braniff Flight 175 originated at Denver and departed for Houston later in the evening and arrived before midnight. The flight terminated at Houston but did not offer continuing through-plane service beyond there.

Between Chicago O'Hare International Airport and San Antonio International Airport, Braniff began offering a single roundtrip each day except Monday and Tuesday. The late evening departure offered highly-discounted Night Coach fares in addition to standard First Class pricing. Flight 329 departed Chicago late in the evening and arrived in San Antonio just before midnight. The flight originated in Chicago and terminated at San Antonio, offering no additional through-plane service. The new nonstop enhanced the choices for Braniff passengers between the two cities that had only been offered four daily one-stop flights; one one-stop flight each day but Saturday and five daily connecting flights through Dallas/Ft. Worth.

Trevor Rogers is the #2 pitcher on the market behind only Tarik Skubal — and he's the most volatile one.

text:
An Objective Story Catalyst accelerates the shared conflict. Threat concerns signs of danger and the characters’ assessment of their vulnerability. Its presence can make a stalled negotiation suddenly worth pursuing.

Catherine’s captivity offers one illustration. The possibility that she will be killed gives Lecter leverage. Chilton arranges a deal with Senator Martin that offers Lecter a prison transfer for help identifying the killer. Lecter is flown to Memphis to meet her. The danger advances the negotiations by changing the concessions officials will make to obtain his cooperation.

Faster movement can bring further trouble: Lecter later escapes from his temporary confinement in Memphis. A Catalyst can move the story forward without making the characters safer.

If your Objective Story Catalyst is Threat, who recognizes which danger, and what do they agree to because of it? They might grant access or accept a proposal they previously resisted. Show how that perceived vulnerability changes their next move. If you have not identified what accelerates your shared conflict, Dramatica can help you find its Catalyst.

text:
Sri Devi Maayi Amma – The mysterious Avadhuta of Kanyakumari and Salem

There lived an extraordinary woman on the shores of Kanyakumari. Nobody knew where she had come from, who her parents were, what her real name was, or how old she actually was.
She did not give spiritual lectures. She did not ask people to worship her. She did not care about clothes, money, comfort, or what society thought of her.

Sometimes she wandered along the seashore without clothes, surrounded by stray dogs. Sometimes she sat quietly on the rocks, looking out at the ocean. At other times, she behaved in ways that ordinary people could not understand.

People called her Maayi Amma, Mayamma, or Devi Mayamma.

To some, she appeared to be an eccentric old woman. To others, she was a great Siddha Yogini, an Avadhuta who had gone beyond ordinary worldly attachments.

Her devotees came to believe that she was none other than Parashakti herself, walking among human beings in the simplest possible form.

He saw himself as a wandering ascetic, sitting beneath a banyan tree in a forest.

Suddenly, Maayi Amma appeared before him, enormous in form.

She asked him for something to eat.
He had only two grains of parched rice, which he offered to her.

She then told him that his real hunger was of a different kind.

She asked him to close his eyes and pressed the centre of his forehead with her thumb.

Sri M described being overwhelmed by an ocean of bliss, losing awareness of his body.

Even after waking, the feeling continued.

He understood this experience in the context of Shaktipat, the transmission of spiritual energy through a Guru's grace.

🙏 Jai Gurudatta 🙏

text:
Truth is Tarik Skubal won’t sign with the Padres: #Padres 

It's not that he _won't_ — it's that the Padres probably _can't_ win a bidding war for him. And Skubal has better options.

Here's the real breakdown:

1. The Price Is Insane
- MLB Trade Rumors projection: *9 years, $425M* — would break Yamamoto's $325M record for a pitcher
- That's *$47M+ AAV*. Skubal is expected to beat the current $43.3M AAV record too.
- Padres franchise record is Tatis at $340M total. They've only ever given $30M AAV to ONE guy: Machado.

2. The Padres Are Already Locked In
- Machado + Tatis Jr. + Bogaerts are owed a *combined $686M through 2034*
- Padres finished 2026 at ∼$224M actual payroll, ∼$269M luxury tax number. They're projected at ∼$193M for 2027 _before_ adding anyone.
- Skubal alone would blow them past the luxury tax — and they still need 3-4 MORE starters after him.

That's the killer argument: *Do you want 1 Skubal, or 2-3 good starters like Rogers + King + someone else?* For a team with only Musgrove and Vasquez returning, 1 ace doesn't fix the rotation.

3. The Competition Is Brutal
Skubal is meeting with *6 teams* — Padres are one, but:
- *Dodgers:* He "would love" to return. He went 5-2, 2.61 ERA there, fit the clubhouse, and lives 25 min from their spring training in Arizona (he's from Kingman, AZ). Dodgers GM said "if we want him, we can have him."
- *Mets:* Jon Heyman says they're "probably the favorite." Steve Cohen can outbid anyone, and they desperately need a true ace.

USA Today basically said it: Whatever the Dodgers want, they always get.

4. New Owners Said "Live Within Our Means"
Feliciano & Jones said they want to win, but also: _"We're going to live within our means... with the long-term health of the team in mind."_

That's not "we're about to give a pitcher $425M" language.

*Bottom line:*
Padres _have_ expressed interest (Jon Morosi reported it) and they _are_ meeting with him. But interest ≠ offer. Unless new ownership is willing to go to $300M+ payroll, Skubal is using San Diego as leverage to get the Dodgers or Mets to pay up.

That's exactly why Rogers at 3/$64M makes way more sense for San Diego.

GREENE COUNTY SHERIFF'S SERGEANT DEVIN JAMES KILLED IN A PATROL CRASH WHILE ASSISTING A PURSUIT

Sergeant Devin James of the Greene County, North Carolina, Sheriff's Office was killed on November 12, 2026, while assisting Farmville police with a vehicle pursuit.

Around 8:20 p.m., the chase crossed into Greene County on Highway 258 North.

Sergeant James was racing to back up a fellow deputy who had caught up with the suspect when he lost control of his patrol car near Highway 13 and suffered fatal injuries.

He had served the Greene County Sheriff's Office for five years, since November 2021.

His sheriff's office said he was always available and ready to serve at a moment's notice, often coming out for events and critical incidents on his own.

They said he was proud of his Sheriff's Office, and his Sheriff's Office was proud of him.

That is the kind of deputy every community hopes it has. He didn't wait to be asked. He just showed up, and he lost his life trying to get there to help.

The North Carolina State Highway Patrol is investigating.

The North Carolina Police Benevolent Association has started a memorial fund for his parents.

Flags across North Carolina flew at half-staff today in his honor.

Please keep his family and the Greene County Sheriff's Office in your prayers.

Rest in peace, Devin.

You were the best America has to offer, and you always will be 🇺🇸

text:
For 31 years, the leaders of China, the United States, and Russia have shared photographs.

On November 19, they will finally share a negotiating table of their own.

And it will happen in China.

Following announcements by the United States and Russia over the weekend, China's Foreign Ministry announced at 9 am Beijing time on November 16 that Chinese President Xi Jinping would hold a trilateral summit with Russian President Vladimir Putin and US President @realDonaldTrump in south China's city of Shenzhen (深圳) on November 19.

I spent some time going through the historical records of meetings between the leaders of these three countries.

And one thing stood out to me:
This appears to be the first dedicated trilateral summit between the heads of state of China, the United States, and Russia in history.

And the historical journey leading to this moment is fascinating.

The earliest event attended simultaneously by the presidents of China, the United States, and Russia appears to date back to May, 1995.

Russia held commemorations in Moscow marking the 50th anniversary of victory in WWII. Chinese President Jiang Zemin (江泽民), US President Bill Clinton, and Russian President Boris Yeltsin attended the military parade in Red Square.

In October of the same year, the three leaders gathered again in New York to commemorate the 50th anniversary of the founding of the United Nations (top right).

Since then, with the development of international multilateral diplomatic mechanisms, the leaders of China, the United States, and Russia have had increasingly frequent opportunities to appear together on the world stage.

In 1998, Russia officially joined APEC. However, then-President Yeltsin did not personally attend Russia's first two APEC Economic Leaders' Meetings, instead sending his premiers to represent the country.

On November 15-16, 2000 (exactly 26 years ago!), Chinese President Jiang Zemin, US President @BillClinton, and Russian President Vladimir Putin all attended the eighth APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting held in Brunei (bottom left). 

In October of the following year, the ninth meeting was held in Shanghai (上海), bringing together Jiang, George W. Bush, and Putin (bottom right). I was still in middle school at the time, and I remember watching Jiang deliver a speech in English on live television.

In 2014, China hosted the APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting for the second time, with Xi, @BarackObama, and Vladimir Putin in attendance (top left).

The upcoming APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting, scheduled for November 18-19 in Shenzhen, will mark the third time China has hosted the event.

Since the establishment of the G20 leaders' summit mechanism in 2008, the leaders of China, the United States, and Russia have had even more opportunities to cross paths on the international stage.

Yet one particularly intriguing fact stands out:

Over the past three decades, the leaders of China, the United States, and Russia have appeared together in numerous group photographs, but they have never actually sat down at a negotiating table specifically set for a trilateral meeting.

And the September 2000 summit of the five permanent members of the UN Security Council in New York was a five-party meeting, rather than a dedicated trilateral meeting between China, the United States, and Russia.

On November 19, that changes.

Why does this matter?

Here is how I see it:
Diplomacy: bring adversaries together.
Ideas: challenge the logic of inevitable confrontation.
Strategy: maintain relations without choosing sides.
Institutions: turn a historic meeting into lasting dialogue.

The summit's first significance is what it reveals about China's diplomatic convening power. Bringing friends together is easy. Bringing adversaries to the same table is an entirely different matter.

The influence of a great power should be measured not only by whom it can deter, but also by whom it can bring together.

Second, the summit offers an opportunity to challenge some of the most deeply entrenched and flawed assumptions in international relations.

China has long advocated a balanced approach to justice and interests (正确义利观), a vision that fundamentally challenges traditional thinking in IR. In my view, conventional notions such as the primacy of national interests, the security dilemma, and the clash of civilizations are increasingly ill-suited to today's international landscape and serve only to generate unnecessary suspicion, hostility and conflict. This is not a new argument for me.

During my time studying in the Department of Government at Cornell, I repeatedly questioned some of the fundamental assumptions underlying mainstream international relations theory. Yet I often encountered considerable resistance from a few professors and their overzealous TAs who seemed more committed to defending established intellectual paradigms than to examining their limitations.

And I have always wondered:
What happens when a theory designed to explain conflict becomes a prescription for producing it?

One of the great tragedies of American foreign policy, in my view, is that some of its intellectual architects have become so invested in theories of competition and confrontation that they struggle to imagine a world organized around cooperation and mutual benefit.

This summit will provide an important opportunity and a global platform for China to promote its vision of a new type of international relations. Whether China can encourage the world's major powers to move beyond some of their differences and seek common ground will be one of the most important aspects of this meeting to watch.

New ideas about IR are not ultimately judged by how persuasive they sound in academic journals, but by whether they can help make the world a more peaceful place.

Third, China does not need to undermine its relationship with one major power to demonstrate the strength of its relationship with another. 

Does a stronger China-Russia relationship necessarily mean a weaker China-US relationship?

Does improving relations with Washington require Beijing to distance itself from Moscow?

Why should China have to choose?

Washington and Moscow may both hope that China will play a role in addressing certain issues, but whether Beijing will accept the agenda they seek to set remains to be seen.

Fourth, perhaps the most consequential question is what happens after November 19.

Will Shenzhen be remembered as a one-off diplomatic event, or as the beginning of a new mechanism preventing bloc confrontation in international politics?

If the three countries can build on this meeting to establish more stable channels of communication, or even gradually institutionalize regular trilateral summits, its historical significance could extend far beyond that of a single APEC summit.

Some have drawn comparisons between this meeting and the Cairo, Tehran, Yalta, and Potsdam conferences. I do not share that view. The differences in national interests, strategic disagreements, and levels of mutual trust among the three countries mean that establishing such a mechanism will be anything but easy.

Moreover, no mechanism for dialogue among major powers should imply that a handful of powerful countries have the right to determine the fate of others. Its true value should lie in reducing the risk of confrontation, not in dividing the world into spheres of influence.

The world is not short of great-power competition. What it lacks are mechanisms to prevent that competition from spiraling out of control. 

November 19 will give us another historic photograph.

What happens afterward will determine its place in history.

text:
Quiet Diplomacy with the US: The Geopolitical Cost of Strategic Silence

Introduction

🌟 The editorial argues that India's excessive diplomatic silence towards American unilateralism may undermine its credibility as a champion of a rules-based international order. It advocates principled, calibrated diplomacy rather than unconditional accommodation of powerful nations.

Main Body

🌟 Quiet Diplomacy versus Public Silence: India's preference for behind-the-scenes negotiations may offer short-term advantages but risks weakening its international moral authority.

🌟 Historical Diplomatic Legacy: India condemned colonial interventions in Indonesia and Indochina in 1946 and the US invasion of Iraq in 2003, demonstrating its commitment to international norms.

🌟 Erosion of Normative Consistency: The article highlights India's restrained responses to several controversial international developments, including the Ukraine conflict, Hong Kong, Iran and other instances of alleged unilateral action.

🌟 Strategic Accommodation: Excessive caution towards Washington may protect immediate bilateral interests but weaken India's ability to influence global diplomatic narratives.

🌟 China's Geopolitical Opportunity: India's silence can create diplomatic space for Beijing to emerge as an alternative partner for countries facing American pressure.

🌟 International Norms and Institutions: Consistent criticism of violations helps strengthen international law, institutional accountability and multilateral cooperation.

🌟 India's Global Leverage: Its economic scale, military capabilities and strategic position give India considerable potential to influence international opinion.

Challenges

🌟 Managing strategic dependence on the US.

🌟 Balancing national interests with normative commitments.

🌟 Preventing diplomatic criticism from damaging bilateral cooperation.

🌟 Countering geopolitical polarisation and great-power pressure.

Constructive Criticism

🌟 Silence may be interpreted as tacit acceptance of unilateralism.

🌟 Selective application of principles weakens diplomatic credibility.

🌟 Excessive accommodation creates normative inconsistency.

🌟 Moral leadership requires consistent positions, not occasional declarations.

Way Forward

🌟 Adopt principled and calibrated public diplomacy.

🌟 Strengthen strategic autonomy and multi-alignment.

🌟 Uphold international law consistently across geopolitical conflicts.

🌟 Use multilateral platforms to build diplomatic coalitions.

🌟 Combine discreet negotiations with transparent articulation of national positions.

Highlighted Keywords

Strategic Autonomy | Normative Consistency | Rules-Based Order | Quiet Diplomacy | Normative Power | Multilateralism | Geopolitical Leverage

Conclusion

🌟 India's diplomatic strength must rest not merely on strategic accommodation but on the courage to defend principles, even when powerful partners are uncomfortable.

text:
CATHERINE PEREZ-SHAKDAM , Jerusalem Post
Genghis Khan understood a weakness in human nature that Western diplomacy seems determined to ignore: a man who believes himself trapped may fight ferociously, but offer him a path to safety and he may abandon every advantage that kept him alive.
The Mongol nerge began as a hunting technique. Horsemen spread across the steppe, tightened their formation, and drove the quarry into a narrowing enclosure.
In war, their successors sometimes left a deliberate opening. Soldiers who fled through it lost the protection of their formations and became easier to pursue.
At the Battle of Mohi in 1241, Batu Khan’s forces used this principle against the Hungarians.
The escape route belonged to the hunters.
The danger is that each participant can pursue its own interest while the final arrangement leaves Iran better placed to threaten its adversaries.
On November 9, US President Donald Trump met Qatar’s prime minister amid discussions over Iran, sanctions, and the Strait of Hormuz. Tehran has demanded relief from American restrictions and access to frozen assets in connection with restoring maritime traffic.
The next day, Iranian Security Chief Mohsen Rezaei insisted that direct talks were not underway. No multibillion-dollar asset-release agreement has been concluded.
Yet the logic of the bargaining is already unsettling. Iran helps make an essential waterway unsafe; its neighbors and trading partners suffer; and Washington is asked to consider economic relief as part of restoring the passage.
This is an excellent way to teach a coercive regime that disruption pays.
The strait is no marginal bargaining chip. Interference there affects tanker insurance, freight costs, energy prices, and governments far beyond the Gulf. Tehran need not defeat the US or Israel in conventional battle. It can impose enough expense to make an imperfect settlement look merciful.
Enter Doha.
Qatar hosts Al Udeid, a major American air base, while maintaining diplomatic ties with Iran and longstanding political contacts with Hamas. Its rulers have turned proximity to Washington’s adversaries into influence in Washington itself.
The more difficult the crisis, the more valuable the messenger who can reach the man responsible.
Of course, Qatar has its own vulnerabilities. Iran struck its Ras Laffan energy facilities in March. Doha is not immune to Tehran’s violence, and its interest in avoiding further attacks is understandable.
But vulnerability does not absolve a mediator from scrutiny of the terms it brokers.
On November 6, Al Jazeera reported that an Iranian parliamentary official described preferential passage for vessels associated with China, India, Iraq, and Qatar. It said Qatari ships could pass without fees, a privilege linked to Doha’s diplomatic role.
The exemptions were limited, and the seas remained dangerous. Still, Iran treated access to international shipping lanes as a favor to distribute according to political usefulness.
It is an extraordinary presumption. Tehran threatens commerce, then presents its restoration as a concession for which it deserves something in return.
Qatar's relationship with Hamas makes the mediating role even more delicate. Doha funded civilian salaries, fuel, and humanitarian needs in Gaza under arrangements often coordinated with Israel and supported by Washington.
That does not prove the money paid for Hamas’s weapons. But the political consequences of sustaining a Hamas-run administration deserve examination, particularly while Hamas received military support from Iran.
There are also direct financial-enforcement concerns.
In October 2023, the US Treasury sanctioned Muhammad Ahmad Abd al-Dayim Nasrallah, a Qatar-based Hamas operative who, it said, had close ties to Iranian elements and helped move tens of millions of dollars to Hamas, including its armed wing.
That finding does not establish Qatari government authorization; it demands serious oversight, not diplomatic inattentiveness. It is an extraordinary presumption. Tehran threatens commerce, then presents its restoration as a concession for which it deserves something in return.

text:
What if your application could improve its own prompts based on how well it performs?

DSPy is an open-source framework from Stanford NLP.

DSPy stands for Declarative Self-improving Python. Its philosophy is to move away from manually maintaining brittle prompts and towards programming language models using modular, composable Python components.

Here's how it approaches the problem.

1. Define the task, not the prompt.

DSPy uses something called Signatures to describe what a model should receive and what it should produce.

For example, you can define a task as:

Input: question, context

Output: answer

You don't have to manually write every instruction that goes into the final prompt. DSPy handles the formatting and execution.

2. Build modular AI programs.

DSPy provides modules such as:

• Predict: Generate outputs from a defined task.

• ChainOfThought: Encourage step-by-step reasoning.

• ReAct: Build agents that reason and interact with tools.

• Retrieve: Integrate information retrieval into your pipeline.

These components can be composed into larger systems, including RAG pipelines and agents.

3. Give it a way to measure success.

You provide a dataset and a metric that measures whether the program is doing a good job.

The metric could measure answer accuracy, retrieval quality, factual correctness or even a combination of business-specific criteria.

DSPy uses that feedback to optimize the program.

4. Let optimizers improve the application.

DSPy comes with several optimization algorithms.

• BootstrapFewShot generates useful examples from successful executions.

• MIPROv2 searches for better combinations of instructions and examples.

• GEPA uses reflective feedback from an LLM to identify failures and evolve instructions.

• BootstrapFinetune can use successful executions to prepare data for fine-tuning model weights.

The result is an optimized program that you can save and reuse.

The pros

• Reduces dependence on manually written and maintained prompts.

• Works with different language models rather than locking you into one provider.

• Supports optimization of multi-step pipelines, not just individual prompts.

• Provides multiple optimization strategies, from few-shot learning to reflective prompt evolution and fine-tuning.

• Open source, with an Apache 2.0 license.

The cons

• There's a learning curve. You need to understand signatures, modules, metrics, datasets and optimizers.

• Optimization requires additional LLM calls, which means additional inference costs and execution time.

• Your results depend heavily on the quality of your evaluation metric and training data. A poorly designed metric can optimize the wrong behaviour.

• Optimized prompts can overfit your training and validation examples. You still need an independent test set.

• It doesn't eliminate the need for observability, production monitoring, error handling or human evaluation.

What about paid alternatives?

DSPy operates in a slightly different category from many commercial tools, but there are overlapping products worth knowing:

• LangSmith: Prompt development, evaluations, tracing and observability, particularly useful in LangChain and LangGraph ecosystems.

• Braintrust: LLM evaluations, experimentation, datasets and production monitoring.

• Vellum: Visual workflow development, prompt experimentation, evaluations and deployment.

• PromptLayer: Prompt management, versioning, evaluation and collaboration.

These platforms offer managed experiences and team workflows. DSPy focuses more directly on programming and algorithmically optimizing LLM applications.

And remember, DSPy being free doesn't mean your LLM usage is free. You still pay for the underlying model calls and compute.

My take:

Prompt engineering is useful when you're building your first prototype.

But when you're building a production RAG system or an AI agent, manually changing instructions and hoping for better results isn't a particularly scalable engineering process.

DSPy brings a more systematic approach: define the task, measure the outcome, optimize the program and evaluate it again.

It's worth exploring if you're serious about building reliable LLM applications.

text:
👶🏻👶🏽👶🏿 Newborn Day 22 to 28, Infant Week 4 Phonics: Feel, Sense, Know
No false expectations. These phonics lessons are God's new model of education, built on three words: intuition, algorithm, and mathematics. Week by week, we guide you to teach your baby by what they can and can't do yet, in body and mind, at each stage of development.
🩺 Development stages follow the American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP) and the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC). General education only; follow your pediatrician's advice for your own baby.
🎵 Songs by David Holland White Jr.
💻 Claude AI from Anthropic writes code on the fly to build this manuscript, its Word layout, and its lesson videos.
🚀 Phonics images and phonic audio created with Grok AI.

🎬 Two Videos This Week
Video 1 is the phonics lesson: FEEL, SENSE, and KNOW, each broken into its phonograms (letters that stand for sounds), with phonic audio created with Grok AI. 
Video 2 is this week's Guardian Angel song, sung by Guardian Angel Ara, the baby music and lullabies that carry the same three words into your baby's day.

At 22 to 28 days old, your one-month-old cannot understand what feel, sense, or know mean, and most babies do not give true social smiles until around six weeks. Your baby cannot hold the head steady yet. None of that is behind schedule. It is right on time.

💡 Part 1: Intuition
No false expectations: your baby cannot explain a feeling. But feel, sense, and know are the beginning of intuition itself, one of the two words God gave David as this curriculum's foundation. A child who trusts what they sense can work with AI as a partner, because people bring the knowing.

Here is what your baby can do. Your baby knows your smell and your voice, lifts the head briefly during tummy time, brings the hands near the face, and watches your face closely. Your baby feels your touch and calms when you hold them. This week's lesson is built on that closeness.

👩 Three Ways to Teach It
Young children learn best when one lesson reaches them in different ways. Each way below is chosen for your baby's stage this week: a strong sense of touch and smell, a close interest in your face, and short times awake and alert.

The first way is touch. Lay your hand gently on your baby's chest and say feel. Move it to the cheek and say sense. Bring your baby close to your own chest and say know.

The second way is the close face. During tummy time, lie down on the floor facing your baby, at eye level, and say each word slowly while your baby works to lift the head toward you.

The third way is the song. Sing FEEL, SENSE, and KNOW on a low, warm note, and hold KNOW the longest. A low, warm voice is one of the most calming sounds a baby can hear.

👀 What Your Baby Senses
At one month, your baby watches faces closely, especially the eyes and hairline, and may follow your face a short way to each side. Your baby hears well, startles at loud noises, and quiets to your voice. Touch, warmth, and the smell of mom are deeply comforting.

🧠 What the Psychologist Knows
Researchers have shown that even young babies expect a response. When a parent's face goes blank and still, babies try to win the parent back, then get upset. When the parent responds again, the baby recovers. Babies learn from that repair, not from a perfect parent.

📝 Journal This Week
Record the numbers from the one-month checkup. Write down what calms your baby best: a touch, a song, a way of holding. Note one moment when you just knew what your baby needed. That knowing is intuition, and it is growing in you.

🎵 Keep Singing
At one month, your baby knows your songs. Use the same baby music or lullaby at the same moments each day, at bath time or bedtime. Phonic songs and nursery rhymes repeated in a routine help your baby feel safe and know what comes next.

🙏 Known Before Birth
Before your baby was a heartbeat, God knew this child. Now, one month in, you are coming to know your child too. You know the hungry cry from the tired cry. You know the face that means a burp is coming. You are learning your baby by heart.

This is the first lesson of intuition: knowing without being told. You did not read it in a book. You learned it by watching, feeling, and listening, day and night. This is God's plan: a parent who knows, raising a child who feels known.

✋ The Power of Touch
Touch is how your baby first learns that the world is safe. Gentle holding, stroking, and skin-to-skin contact help calm your baby's heart rate and breathing. Babies who are held often are not spoiled; they are learning that someone is near.

Infant massage is a lovely way to use touch. Choose a time when your baby is calm and awake, not right after a feeding. Warm the room, use your hands and a little plain plant oil if you like, and use slow, gentle strokes on the legs, arms, back, and chest.

Watch your baby the whole time. Bright eyes and relaxed hands mean keep going. Turning away, fussing, or stiffening means stop for today. Massage is not about finishing; it is a conversation through your hands, the same way songs are a conversation through your voice.

😶 What the Still-Face Research Teaches
In the still-face experiment, developed by psychologist Edward Tronick, a parent plays with a baby, then suddenly keeps a blank, unmoving face. Babies first try to bring the parent back with smiles and sounds, then become upset. When the parent responds again, they settle.

The deeper lesson is about repair. Researchers found that in everyday play, parents and babies are often out of sync. That is normal. What builds trust is reconnecting after a miss. You do not have to read every cue perfectly. You just keep coming back.

Your phone can become a still face without your meaning it to. When you are feeding or playing, put the screen away when you can and look at your baby. Your face, your voice, and your attention are the lesson, and they cannot be replaced.

👩 Postpartum Anxiety
Not every postpartum struggle looks like sadness. Some mothers feel constant worry, racing thoughts, a tight chest, or trouble sleeping even when the baby sleeps. Some have sudden scary thoughts about the baby getting hurt. This is postpartum anxiety, and it is common and treatable.

Having a frightening thought does not make you a bad mother. Tell your doctor, your pediatrician, or the maternal mental health hotline listed in Week 1. If you ever feel you might harm yourself or your baby, call 911 or 988 right away. Help is there.

Your own full postpartum visit should happen by 12 weeks after birth. Ask your doctor when you can return to exercise. Gentle walks with the stroller are usually a good start, along with pelvic floor exercises if your doctor recommends them.

👨 Dad Going Back to Work
Many fathers go back to work around now. If your job is covered, the federal Family and Medical Leave Act allows eligible workers up to 12 weeks of unpaid, job-protected leave in the first year after a birth. Some employers and states offer paid leave too.

When you are back at work, keep a daily job that is yours: the evening bath, the bedtime song, or the first morning diaper. Babies know their father by voice, touch, and routine. Ten focused minutes a day matters more than a whole distracted evening.

👵 Grandparents and Helpers
Grandparents and caregivers are part of your baby's village. Ask everyone who cares for your baby to be up to date on whooping cough and flu shots, to wash hands, and to follow your safe sleep rules, even if the rules have changed since they raised their own children.

Older relatives often know songs and nursery rhymes from their own childhood. Ask them to sing to your baby. Kids music passed down through a family carries love from one generation to the next, the same way faith is passed down.

🎶 Songs That Mark the Day
Babies feel safer when the day has a pattern. Choose one lullaby for bedtime, one song for bath time, and one for diaper changes. Sing them at the same moments every day. Soon your baby will start to calm at the first notes, because your baby knows what comes next.

Baby music and phonic songs work the same way. When a song always comes before sleep, it becomes a signal. That is the beginning of algorithm in your baby's mind: when this happens, that comes next. Repetition in love is how a child learns to know.

🏠 Feel, Sense, Know
This week's phonics words, FEEL, SENSE, and KNOW, are the heart of the whole series. They lead to the two words God gave David as the foundation of this vocabulary phase: intuition and algorithm. Feeling, sensing, and knowing are the beginning of intuition itself.

You are living these words this month. You feel your baby's weight in your arms. You sense the change before the cry. You know your baby. A child raised by parents who feel, sense, and know is ready to learn alongside an AI partner like Claude, with wisdom leading the way.

📝 Journal This Week
Write the numbers from the one-month visit and the shots your baby received. Describe your baby at one month in three words. Record the songs you chose for bedtime and bath time. Write one prayer of thanks for the first month God has given you together.

🕊️ A Prayer for the First Month
Lord, before You formed our child in the womb, You knew this child (Jeremiah 1:5, CPDV). Thank You for one month of life, growth, and love. Teach our hands to comfort, our hearts to sense, and our minds to know what our baby needs. Keep our child healthy and our home in Your peace. Amen.

🔁 Part 2: Algorithm
No false expectations: your one-month-old will not learn rules. But this month your baby has lived inside your routines: feeding, changing, sleeping, waking. Those routines are algorithms. Your baby has felt them repeat about thirty times, and repetition is how patterns become trust.

This is an intuition lesson, and it is the heart of the whole series. Feeling, sensing, and knowing come before words, and they lead to the two words God gave David as this curriculum's foundation: intuition and algorithm. Your baby is already living the first of them.

FEEL has two phonograms (letters that stand for sounds): f and eel. Say f, a soft blow, then eel, the long e of "see" ending with the tongue lifted for l. Join them: feel. Say it while your hand rests on your baby's chest.

SENSE has two: s and ense. Say s, a soft hiss, then ense, the short e of "bed," then n, then another soft hiss. Join them: sense. Say it slowly, like you are noticing something.

KNOW has two: kn and ow. In kn, the k stays quiet, so you hear only n. Then ow, the long o in "go." Join them: know. Rest on this word a moment longer than the others.

Keep each session to a minute or two. Say the words while you hold your baby close, so the sound and the feeling arrive at the same time. In this lesson the touch matters as much as the words.

🔗 Building on Last Week
For three weeks your baby has heard patterns: a beat, actions, and shapes. This week turns inward, to what is felt before it can be named. That order is on purpose. A baby feels safe first, then notices, then knows. When the algorithm words come back in later weeks, they will land on a child who first felt them in your arms. One month of lessons is a real milestone. Celebrate it.

🚨 When to Call Your Pediatrician
Call if your baby feeds poorly or very slowly, seems very floppy or very stiff, moves one side much less than the other, does not react to loud sounds, does not look at faces, or has a fever of 100.4°F (38°C) or higher. Early questions lead to early help.

👣 Tummy Time at One Month
Your baby may now lift the head briefly and turn it from side to side during tummy time. Aim for a few short sessions after naps and diaper changes. A rolled-up towel under the chest can make it easier. Stop when your baby gets tired and fussy.

🍭 Pacifiers at One Month
For breastfed babies, the American Academy of Pediatrics suggests waiting until breastfeeding is going well, usually around three to four weeks, before offering a pacifier. Many families are at that point now. Formula-fed babies can use a pacifier sooner.

Offering a pacifier at naps and bedtime is linked with a lower risk of SIDS. Use a one-piece pacifier made for babies, keep it clean, never tie it around your baby's neck or to clothing with a long cord, and never dip it in honey or sugar.

💉 Comfort for Shots
Shots are quick, but you can make them easier. Hold your baby close during the shot if the clinic allows it. Breastfeeding during or right after a shot, offering a pacifier, or a few drops of sugar water given by the nurse can all lower your baby's pain.

After shots, some babies are fussy or sleepy, or have a little redness where the shot was given. Ask your pediatrician what to watch for and whether any medicine is needed. Call for a high fever, crying that will not stop for three hours or more, or any reaction that worries you.

🏠 Home Safety at One Month
Babies can wiggle and push off surfaces sooner than parents expect. Keep one hand on your baby on a changing table, bed, or couch. Never set a car seat or bouncer on a table or counter. The floor is the safest place to put your baby down if you must step away.

Keep your home and car smoke-free. Smoke around a baby raises the risk of SIDS, ear infections, and breathing problems, and smoke left on clothes and furniture is harmful too. Test your smoke and carbon monoxide alarms this week.

🔢 Part 3: Mathematics
No false expectations: your baby will not count to four. But four weeks is the first full month, and the one-month checkup measures weight, length, and head size. Numbers tell the story of growth. In God's new model, children meet numbers as friendly, familiar things from the very start.

FEEL has 2 phonograms (letters that stand for sounds), SENSE has 2, and KNOW has 2. Six sounds, three words. Over four weeks your baby has now heard 12 words and 29 phonogram sounds from you, again and again, in your voice.

At one month, many formula-fed babies take up to about 4 ounces at a feeding, and breastfed babies often feed 8 to 12 times a day. Many babies are about 1 to 1.5 inches longer than at birth. Write the checkup numbers down so you can watch the growth line rise.

🎂 One Month Old
Four weeks ago you met your baby face to face. Today your baby is one month old. The newborn fog is starting to lift: your baby is awake a little longer, looks at you a little harder, and knows your voice, your smell, and your arms.

Your baby is also starting to know you through feeling. Touch was the first sense to develop in the womb, and it is still your baby's strongest. Every time you hold, stroke, and rock your baby, you are teaching love before words. This is God's plan for knowing.

“Before I formed you in the womb, I knew you. And before you went forth from the womb, I sanctified you. And I made you a prophet to the nations.” (Jeremiah 1:5, CPDV)

🩺 The One-Month Checkup
Most babies see the pediatrician around one month. Expect weight, length, and head size on the growth chart, a full physical exam, a hip check, and questions about feeding, sleep, and stools. Many babies get the second hepatitis B shot at one or two months.

Your pediatrician will likely ask how you are feeling too. Answer honestly; it is part of your baby's care. Bring your questions written down, because tired parents forget. This visit is also a good time to ask about vitamin D and safe sleep.

🍼 Feeding at One Month
Breastfed babies usually still feed about 8 to 12 times a day. By the end of the first month, many formula-fed babies take up to about 4 ounces every three to four hours. Your baby, your pediatrician, and the growth chart guide the amounts.

🏥 Inside the One-Month Visit
At this visit, your pediatrician checks your baby from head to toe. Expect a look at the soft spots, eyes, ears, mouth, heart, lungs, belly, hips, and skin. The doctor also checks reflexes and muscle tone, the way your baby's body feels when held.

Many babies are about a pound or two above birth weight by now, but every baby grows at their own pace. Your pediatrician cares most about the curve, how your baby is tracking over time, more than any single number on any single day.

The second dose of the hepatitis B vaccine is often given between one and two months. The rest of your baby's two-month shots come next month. Ask for a printed copy of your baby's vaccine record and keep it with your important papers.

🌱 What Many Babies Do at One Month
By the end of the first month, many babies lift the head briefly during tummy time, bring their hands near their mouth, and move both arms and both legs about equally. They watch faces with interest and quiet when picked up or spoken to.

Your baby still keeps the hands in loose fists much of the time, and the newborn reflexes are still strong. Every baby develops at their own pace. If you have a feeling that something is not right, tell your pediatrician. A parent's concern is always worth a conversation.

🧸 Three Games for This Stage
These games fit your baby's stage this week. Your baby cannot play back yet, so each game is a gentle sharing of touch, voice, and face.

Soft and Smooth: touch your baby's hand with a soft cloth, then with your smooth palm, saying feel each time. Two textures, one word.

Face to Face: during supervised tummy time, put your face at your baby's eye level and say know. When your baby lifts the head even a little, cheer softly.

Cuddle and Name: hold your baby skin to skin, breathe slowly together, and whisper sense on each long breath out. Calm is part of the lesson.

Watch your baby's face during these games. A soft, steady gaze means your baby is taking it in. Yawning, looking away, or hiccups can mean your baby has had enough for now. A one-month-old tires quickly, and stopping early is part of good teaching.

🔜 Next Week
In Week 5, your baby's movements become smoother, and the eyes can follow a face moving slowly from side to side. The phonics lesson moves on to BECOME, IMAGINE, and CREATE.

🕊️ A Prayer for Week 4
Lord, we taste and see that You are sweet (Psalm 33:9, CPDV (34:8 KJV)). Thank You for one month of feeling, sensing, and knowing our child. Let our baby feel Your love through our hands, sense Your peace in our home, and one day know You by name. Amen.

A socialist republic is a sovereign nation that operates under a republican form of government and maintains a socialist economic and political system.

Key Characteristics
• Republican Governance: The country lacks a monarch and is organized as a public matter (res publica), where leaders are chosen by representatives or the populace.
• Socialist Economy: Major means of production, resources, and key industries are publicly, collectively, or state-owned rather than privately controlled.
• Constitutional Commitment: The state’s foundational laws explicitly pledge allegiance to socialist principles or the transition toward socialism.

Political Structures
• Marxist–Leninist Models: Many historical and current socialist republics (such as the former Soviet republics or modern one-party states) feature a dominant communist or Marxist-Leninist party guiding the state apparatus.
• Democratic & Multi-Party Models: Some nations incorporate constitutional references to socialism or democratic socialism while operating within multi-party parliamentary frameworks.

Examples
• Current Examples: Countries such as the Socialist Republic of Vietnam formally designate themselves as socialist republics.
• Historical Examples: The Soviet Union (Union of Soviet Socialist Republics) and its constituent republics (such as the Socialist Republic of Croatia or Socialist Republic of Slovenia).

A socialist state, socialist republic, or socialist country is a sovereign state constitutionally dedicated to the establishment of socialism. This article is about states that refer to themselves as socialist states, and not specifically about communist states that refer to themselves as socialist states. It includes information on liberal democratic states with constitutional references to socialism as well as other state formations that have referred to themselves as socialist.

Constitutional references to socialism
See also: Liberal democratic constitutions with references to socialism
A number of countries that make references to socialism in their constitutions are not communist states. In most cases, these are constitutional references to the building of a socialist society and political principles that have little to no bearing on the structure and guidance of these country's machinery of government and economic system. The preamble to the 1976 Constitution of Portugal states that the Portuguese state has, as one of its goals, opening "the way to socialist society".[1] Another broad example is that of Slovenia, which defines itself as a "state governed by the rule of law and a social state".[2] Algeria, the Congo, India, and Sri Lanka have directly used the term socialist in their official constitution and name. Croatia, Hungary, and Poland directly denounce "Communism" in their founding documents in reference to their past regimes.[i]

In these cases, the intended meaning of socialism can vary widely and sometimes the constitutional references to socialism are left over from a previous period in the country's history. In the case of many Middle Eastern states, the term socialism was often used in reference to an Arab socialist/nationalist philosophy adopted by specific regimes, such as that of Gamal Abdel Nasser and that of the various Ba'ath parties. Examples of countries directly using the term socialist in their names include the Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka and the Socialist Republic of Vietnam, while a number of countries make references to socialism in their constitutions, but not in their names. These include India[3] and Portugal. In addition, countries such as Belarus, Colombia, France, Russia, and Spain use the varied term social state, leaving a more ambiguous meaning. In the constitutions of Croatia, Hungary, and Poland, direct condemnation is made to the respective past socialist regimes.[4] The autonomous region of Rojava, which operates under the principles of democratic confederalism, has been described as a socialist state.[5]

text:
Elon Musk offered $97.4 billion for OpenAI. Sam Altman answered in one line:

"no thank you but we will buy twitter for $9.74 billion if you want"

Exactly one tenth of the offer. Musk replied with one word. "Swindler."

The two started OpenAI together in 2015 as a nonprofit. Musk left the board in 2018 and has been fighting Altman ever since, including in court.

The bid landed in February 2025, right when OpenAI was trying to turn itself into a for-profit company. A few days later OpenAI's board rejected it unanimously. Altman's own guess was that Musk was "probably just trying to slow us down."

I don't think either of them expected a sale. Musk's offer made OpenAI's restructuring harder and more expensive. Altman's reply turned a serious legal move into a meme the whole internet shared.

Still, it's wild to watch two of the richest men in tech fight like this over a company they started together.

Who won this round, Musk or Altman?

text:
DAILY SCRIPTURE

THE BIRTHING OF A NATION
FAITH • FAMILY • FREEDOM

MONDAY, NOVEMBER 16, 2026

🔥 38 YEARS WAITING — ONE ENCOUNTER WITH JESUS!

John 5:8 (NLT)
“Jesus told him, ‘Stand up, pick up your mat, and walk!’”

Imagine waiting 38 years for your circumstances to change.

At the pool of Bethesda lay a man who had been sick for nearly four decades.

Day after day, he watched others move forward while he remained in the same condition.

Then one day, Jesus approached him and asked an extraordinary question:

“WOULD YOU LIKE TO GET WELL?”

Instead of answering directly, the man explained why he couldn’t get into the pool.

He had no one to help him.

But Jesus wasn’t asking him to explain why he had remained there.

JESUS WAS ABOUT TO DO WHAT THE MAN COULD NEVER DO FOR HIMSELF!

With one command, Jesus told him to stand, pick up his mat, and walk.

And immediately, the man was healed!

Church, there is a powerful lesson here.

Sometimes we become so accustomed to our struggles that we begin believing nothing will ever change.

We allow yesterday’s disappointments to shape tomorrow’s expectations.

But Jesus is not limited by how long we have been struggling.

38 YEARS OF SUFFERING DID NOT PLACE THIS MAN BEYOND THE POWER OF CHRIST!

Yet the story doesn’t end with his healing.

Later, Jesus found him in the temple and warned him to turn away from sin.

Why?

Because Jesus came to accomplish something greater than physical healing.

HE CAME TO SAVE OUR SOULS!

Through His death and resurrection, Jesus offers forgiveness, new life, and freedom from the bondage of sin.

Not every struggle disappears immediately, but no circumstance is beyond His knowledge or compassion.

DON’T LET THE LENGTH OF YOUR STRUGGLE CONVINCE YOU THAT GOD HAS FORGOTTEN YOU.

And don’t become so focused on changing your circumstances that you forget to surrender your heart to Jesus.

🎯 TODAY’S MISSION

Read John 5:1–15.

Ask yourself:

Have I allowed past disappointments to weaken my faith or keep me from obeying God’s Word?

Bring that struggle before Jesus today, and take one step of obedience.

🙏 PRAYER

Heavenly Father, forgive us for allowing fear, disappointment, and unbelief to hold us back. Strengthen our faith and teach us to trust Your Word. Lord Jesus, heal what is broken within us, lead us into genuine repentance, and help us walk in obedience to You. In Your mighty name, Amen.

FAITH • FAMILY • FREEDOM

text:
" human salvation depended on participating in the religious order"

Example 1: Dhruva achieves his divine vision and supreme status of Dhruva Lok through intense tapasya and single-minded bhakti to Sriman Narayana, guided by a Dwadashakshari given by Narada Maharishi, rather than by joining a monastic or religious order.

Sriman Narayana appears directly to the 5-year-old prince in the forest of Madhuvana because of his sincerity, purity of intent, and determination, bypassing any requirement of ritual hierarchy or social religious orders.

Dhruva returns to society, rules righteously as a king, and fulfills his worldly responsibilities before attaining his eternal celestial abode.

Example 2: Prahlada Charitram
Prahlada attains the direct protection and grace of Sriman Narayana despite being born in an Asura clan that strictly opposed Vedic traditions and religious institutions. Guided by the teachings he heard from Narada Maharishi while still in his mother's womb, the young boy practices unwavering internal devotion (smaranam and kirtanam) without performing any formal rituals or joining an ashram. Sriman Narayana manifests directly from a pillar as Lord Narasimha to save him, proving that pure faith transcends lineage and institutional participation.

Example 3: Kannappa Nayanar
Kannappa, a hunter from the forest, attains supreme union with Shiva despite not knowing any Agamic rituals, Sanskrit mantras, or temple priesthood. Driven by pure, selfless love, he offers water carried in his mouth, wild flowers from his hair, and cooked meat to the Shiva Lingam at Srikalahasti, and eventually plucks out his own eyes to stop Shiva's eyes from bleeding. Shiva appears directly to restore his sight and grant him eternal liberation, proving that innocent, uncompromising devotion outweighs formal religious orthodoxy.

Example 4: Sabari in the Ramayana
Sabari attains moksha not through Vedic scholarship or formal religious orders, but through patient service and pure love for Sri Rama. Following the simple instructions of her guru, Matanga Maharishi, she devotedly awaited Sri Ram in her hermitage, gathering forest berries every day. Sri Rama visited her humble dwelling personally, accepted the offering with joy, and Sri Rama didn't offer her Moksha as Sri Rama did to Jatayu; it was the gurubhakti itself that elevated her to Moksha.
She enters the yogagni through the power of her own tapas and gurubhakti, ascending directly to the eternal realms of her gurus without needing any external institutional rites.

They all prove that moksha does not require institutional priesthood or Vedic ritualism, not that Hinduism embraces materialistic atheism. They serve as pratyaksha pramana, proving an exception to your universal rule. Within the Sanatana tradition, moksha was never monopolised by an institutional order or clerical hierarchy.

You are conflating two completely different philosophical categories under a single English word: Atheism.

There is a fundamental distinction between Nirishvaravada (non-theism / denial of Ishvara) and Nastikatva (rejection of the Vedas, karma, and the atman).

Carvaka was rejected not merely for denying a creator God, but for Brahman-and-Atman denial that is Dehatmavada, as they were claiming consciousness is just a byproduct of matter and Pramana-samkoca that is rejecting inference, anumana, as a valid means of knowledge.

Meanwhile, orthodox Astika schools, specifically Purva Mimamsa as articulated by Jaimini and Kumarila Bhatta and Classical Samkhya as articulated by Kapila Muni, explicitly reject Ishvara while remaining pillars of Vedic orthodoxy. By equating "Atheism" exclusively with Carvaka, you are committing equivocation on the term atheism.

If "being fiercely attacked and called baseless by other Hindu schools" disqualifies a darshana from being part of Hinduism. Advaita Vedanta and Dvaita Vedanta would both be disqualified. Look, since Madhvacharya’s Mayavadakhandana calls Advaita a disguised Buddhism (pracchanna bauddha) and dangerous to Moksham. At the same time, Advaitins dismiss Dvaita as mere dualistic ignorance (avidya). Internal polemical warfare or vadakatha is the lifeblood of the Shad-darshana tradition, not proof of exclusion.

Hence, your claim that a school cannot be part of Hinduism if other Hindu, Buddhist, and Jain schools fiercely argued against it and found it "baseless or dangerous" falls flat.

Madhavaacharya’s Sarva-darsana-samgraha opens its very first chapter with Carvaka, and Jayarasi Bhatta’s Tattvopaplavasimha survives as a masterpiece of skeptical epistemology. Numerous early Nyaya, Samkhya, and Mimamsa sutras and commentaries also perished to time and climate. Therefore, textual loss is a historical accident. This is never a referendum on philosophical legitimacy.

Materialistic Carvaka was indeed a minority nastika school, not mainstream bhakti. But reducing the entire non-theistic and anti-institutional spectrum of Hindu thought to a modern invention erases both Mimamsa/Samkhya philosophy and the core lesson of the Puranas.
author: rb_eswar
authorBio: I'm R Bagavatheeswara Sharma.

text:
I am tired of this “Atheism is also a part of Hinduism” nonsense. 

The Buddhists, Jains, and Hindus were fiercely arguing with each other and rarely agreed on anything. But when it came to the purely materialist Cārvākas, even they all could agree that their philosophy was baseless, arrogant, and dangerous. Cārvāka was a very unpopular school both among the masses and among the intelligentsia that they waned out of existence and none of their original texts even survive. How can this happen if atheism is an integral part of Hinduism? 

Across every premodern civilization, materialistic atheism : i.e. a worldview that denies gods, spirits, cosmic justice, and popular devotion in all forms, were met with widespread hostility, suspicion, and rejection from the general public. For the vast majority of people in antiquity and the medieval world, the universe was an enchanted, morally ordered place where human survival depended on maintaining harmony with unseen forces, and human salvation depended on participating in the religious order. Rejecting this supernatural entirely, was rarely seen as an enlightened philosophical stance; instead, the masses viewed it as arrogant, reckless, and socially dangerous. In societies bound together by shared sacred rituals and shared world-views, a person who refused to honour these higher powers and authority, was suspected of inviting collective misfortune.

In classical Greece and Rome, public piety (Greek : Eusebia, Latin : pietas) was the bedrock of citizenship, and figures who denied the existence of the gods or mocked state cults faced exile, social ruin, or even execution for impiety. Even philosophical schools that refused to accommodate traditional myths and religious practices, such as Epicureanism, struggled to gain mass popularity and were routinely caricatured by the public as morally corrupt and hedonistic. Later, across medieval Christendom and the Islamic world, monotheistic orthodoxy left virtually no room for materialist unbelief. Denying the soul, divine judgment, or the afterlife was equated with moral nihilism, ensuring that strict materialism remained a despised and unallowed position to be held at least openly. In premodern China, refusal to participate in ancestor worship and other religious practices was a despised position to hold either. 

Across every continent, premodern societies consistently demanded cosmic accountability and sacred devotion, leaving strict materialistic atheism universally scorned by the masses.

I don’t have any problem with atheists and all other grades of lightly religious people (even I am a fallen person by the standards of my tradition). But, rewriting history to justify and cope with the novelty of your position that became viable to hold (and even popular) only in the era of modernity, is not just intellectually dishonest but also a sign of the insecurity of your worldview. Just say that you are atheist or just culturally Hindu. Don’t try to rewrite history and graft yourself awkwardly into the antiquity of Hinduism just for gaining social capital for your position.

I genuinely appreciate your honesty and your clear devotion to Jesus and the authority of Scripture. We both want to take God’s Word at face value rather than rewriting it. Where we differ is simply in letting the first-century audience and the rest of the New Testament define how those prophecies are fulfilled.
When we look closely at the three passages you mentioned, they actually point away from a future geopolitical restoration of the modern state of Israel:
1. Matthew 23:39 and the Judgment of Jerusalem
Jesus spoke those words right after pronouncing seven woes on the religious leaders and declaring that all the righteous blood shed on earth would come upon that generation (Matthew 23:36). In the very next verse, He announces that their house—the temple—is left desolate, and in the following chapter, He tells His disciples that this generation would not pass away until all these things took place. The "seeing Him" in judgment happened in AD 70 when Jerusalem and the Old Covenant system fell, vindicating Him as Lord—not thousands of years later to a secular nation-state.
2. Zechariah 14 and Apocalyptic Imagery
In Old Testament prophetic idiom, God "standing on the Mount of Olives" and splitting the mountain is standard apocalyptic language for divine judgment and covenantal upheaval—just like Micah 1:3–4 describes the Lord coming down to tread on the high places and melt the mountains when judging Samaria and Jerusalem. Notice that Zechariah 14 also describes the Feast of Tabernacles and animal sacrifices continuing—things the book of Hebrews explicitly tells us were shadows that became obsolete once Christ offered His final sacrifice. Taking Zechariah 14 as a literal future blueprint actually puts us back under Old Covenant shadows.
3. Romans 11 and "All Israel"
Paul’s entire argument in Romans 9–11 begins with a crucial definition: not all who are descended from physical Israel belong to true Israel (Romans 9:6). Throughout chapter 11, Paul explains that God never rejected His people—demonstrated by the first-century Jewish remnant, including Paul himself, who trusted in Christ. The olive tree in Romans 11 is not a modern geopolitical nation; it is the covenant community rooted in Christ, where unbelieving natural branches were broken off and believing Gentiles were grafted in. "All Israel" being saved is the full number of both Jews and Gentiles united in the Messiah through faith, not a separate ethnic track.
4. Our "Jewish Savior"
Jesus certainly came into the world through the lineage of David according to the flesh, and we are forever grateful for that heritage. Yet Paul reminds us in 2 Corinthians 5:16 that while we once regarded Christ according to the flesh, we regard Him that way no longer. In the New Creation, He is the resurrected Last Adam—the head of one new humanity where ethnic distinctions no longer confer special covenant status (Galatians 3:28; Ephesians 2:14–15).
Loving Jewish people—just like loving every neighbor—is a clear command of Christ. We just don't need to attach a dispensational political expectation to it to be faithful to the gospel.

André’s reply treats the gestures as neutral once the official vocabulary is correct. The problem is that the vocabulary does not change what the gestures do.

Solomon bowed before Bathsheba in 1 Kings 2:19. That is a son showing ordinary honor to his living mother in a specific court setting. It is not a recurring liturgical act directed to a statue, accompanied by incense, a crown, and language that entrusts one’s life to her maternal intercession. 

The two acts are not the same category. One is a one-time human courtesy. The other is a patterned religious practice that places a created person in the role of regular mediator.
Exodus 25:18–20 describes the cherubim on the mercy seat. 

They are part of the tabernacle furniture under direct divine instruction, they receive no prayers, and they are not treated as objects that can be petitioned. The second commandment still prohibits making and bowing to carved images as objects of religious devotion. 

The later practice of crowning statues, offering incense before them, and directing trust toward the figure represented is not what the tabernacle cherubim were for. The early church did not treat images that way. The shift comes centuries later.

The claim that incense and bowing do not automatically equal worship is true in the abstract. In the concrete case the Pope is not performing a generic gesture near an image. He is performing a sequence—crowning, incense, bowing, and entrusting his life to her—that matches the functional pattern the Old Testament and the apostles rejected: giving to a creature the petition and mediating role that belong to God alone. 

The technical distinction between latria and hyperdulia is real inside Catholic manuals. It does not erase the fact that the practice places Mary in a position the New Testament never assigns her.

The early church did not crown statues of Mary, did not offer incense before them, and did not teach believers to entrust their lives to her intercession. Those practices appear after the fourth century, once large numbers of people who already had mother-goddess habits entered the churches. 

The names were adjusted. The functional role stayed. André’s examples do not reverse that sequence. They show that ordinary honor and specific temple furniture existed. They do not show that the later Marian system was the pattern the apostles left.
