I saw the discussion under your post and i belive what You said it's truth , but It’s also true that some people either pretend to have illnesses or actually have them yet use them as an excuse to avoid moving forward, and a mental health condition—which cannot be verified in the same way as a physical illness—can be viewed with suspicion, especially when it is as severe as what you describe. That makes it harder for those who are genuinely struggling like yourself to be taken seriously. And i'm sorry for that . 

But one of the most frustrating aspects of talking to some poeple in such a state is that they often seem to have lost all hope of improvement or change; every time a suggestion is offered, it is met with a reason why that advice wouldn’t work. That said, I can understand why someone might feel this way and since it’s impossible to definitively prove to someone that there is, in fact, a path toward something better, You just have to have faith.

Ultimately, the only person who can change your mental state is you. With that in mind, I’d like to offer a few pieces of advice.

The only way to move past something like this is to understand why you feel or think the way you do—the thoughts or feelings that prevent you from living a normal life. You must either bravely accept these things (if they cannot be changed, like something traumatic in your past) or come to realize that your current perspective on them is not the right one. This requires a sincere, introspective effort. No one just has anxiety for the sake of having anxiety, as if it were purely instinctive, like fear; it happens because of a cognitive process. Behind your anxiety, there is a train of thoughts that leads you to feel anxious.

All this could be part of two therapies that can help you: Mindfulness-Based Cognitive Therapy (MBCT) and Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT).

In the first one, meditation is also used—not the mystical Buddhist kind, it's secular. It’s just sitting in a comfortable position, though not so comfortable that you fall asleep, and trying to focus on your breathing. Inevitably, you’re going to start thinking about other things, but every time that happens, the idea is not to pay attention to those thoughts and just let them pass by as if you were observing them from a distance. Every time you realize you got distracted, bring your focus back to your breathing without ruminating on the thoughts you had. You should do this even if you don't do the rest.

A second effective strategy is to confront what makes you uncomfortable. Think of it like a horror game: at first, when you can’t see what’s attacking you or what the enemies look like, it’s terrifying. But if you play every day, whatever scared you initially begins to lose its impact. This should be done gradually: set small, manageable goals, then challenge yourself with slightly larger tasks in small increments. For example, try going to the cinema once a week—or anywhere else you enjoy—just to get out of the house. Once you feel ready for the next step, you could combine that weekly cinema trip with a stop at a shop to buy a treat. Keep going like this, and little by little, your anxieties will lose their intensity and their power over you.

Also another therapy that could help you is Interpersonal and Social Rhythm Therapy (IPSRT). It’s basically about structuring your life around daily habits to give your life a routine, which helps you both physically and mentally, especially with your sleep. It can consist of simple things like taking a shower, getting out of bed and eating in the kitchen instead of your bedroom, playing with a pet, etc.

There is also another therapy called Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT).

You should read about these therapies. I hope you get better. God bless you, praying for you.

A socialist republic is a sovereign nation that operates under a republican form of government and maintains a socialist economic and political system.

Key Characteristics
• Republican Governance: The country lacks a monarch and is organized as a public matter (res publica), where leaders are chosen by representatives or the populace.
• Socialist Economy: Major means of production, resources, and key industries are publicly, collectively, or state-owned rather than privately controlled.
• Constitutional Commitment: The state’s foundational laws explicitly pledge allegiance to socialist principles or the transition toward socialism.

Political Structures
• Marxist–Leninist Models: Many historical and current socialist republics (such as the former Soviet republics or modern one-party states) feature a dominant communist or Marxist-Leninist party guiding the state apparatus.
• Democratic & Multi-Party Models: Some nations incorporate constitutional references to socialism or democratic socialism while operating within multi-party parliamentary frameworks.

Examples
• Current Examples: Countries such as the Socialist Republic of Vietnam formally designate themselves as socialist republics.
• Historical Examples: The Soviet Union (Union of Soviet Socialist Republics) and its constituent republics (such as the Socialist Republic of Croatia or Socialist Republic of Slovenia).

A socialist state, socialist republic, or socialist country is a sovereign state constitutionally dedicated to the establishment of socialism. This article is about states that refer to themselves as socialist states, and not specifically about communist states that refer to themselves as socialist states. It includes information on liberal democratic states with constitutional references to socialism as well as other state formations that have referred to themselves as socialist.

Constitutional references to socialism
See also: Liberal democratic constitutions with references to socialism
A number of countries that make references to socialism in their constitutions are not communist states. In most cases, these are constitutional references to the building of a socialist society and political principles that have little to no bearing on the structure and guidance of these country's machinery of government and economic system. The preamble to the 1976 Constitution of Portugal states that the Portuguese state has, as one of its goals, opening "the way to socialist society".[1] Another broad example is that of Slovenia, which defines itself as a "state governed by the rule of law and a social state".[2] Algeria, the Congo, India, and Sri Lanka have directly used the term socialist in their official constitution and name. Croatia, Hungary, and Poland directly denounce "Communism" in their founding documents in reference to their past regimes.[i]

In these cases, the intended meaning of socialism can vary widely and sometimes the constitutional references to socialism are left over from a previous period in the country's history. In the case of many Middle Eastern states, the term socialism was often used in reference to an Arab socialist/nationalist philosophy adopted by specific regimes, such as that of Gamal Abdel Nasser and that of the various Ba'ath parties. Examples of countries directly using the term socialist in their names include the Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka and the Socialist Republic of Vietnam, while a number of countries make references to socialism in their constitutions, but not in their names. These include India[3] and Portugal. In addition, countries such as Belarus, Colombia, France, Russia, and Spain use the varied term social state, leaving a more ambiguous meaning. In the constitutions of Croatia, Hungary, and Poland, direct condemnation is made to the respective past socialist regimes.[4] The autonomous region of Rojava, which operates under the principles of democratic confederalism, has been described as a socialist state.[5]

From its very inception, this state has served as an instrument and mechanism of colonial occupation by Punjabi imperialism and its ruthless military against historical nations, plunging Sindh into the abyss of the worst national subjugation and humiliation while continuously orchestrating conspiracies to plunder, exploit, and eradicate it. From the One Unit scheme to the 1973 Constitution, from conspiracies to erase the Sindhi language and history to the systematic, artificial alteration of Sindh’s demography, and from the seizure of its river, resources, islands, and millions of acres of land by Punjabi imperialism and its military, Sindh has perpetually been treated as a conquered territory and a goose laying golden eggs.
The reality is that due to Punjab being a landlocked region, coupled with its burgeoning population and massive military might, it seeks to establish its occupation, political tyranny, and imperialist hegemony over all historical nations of this region, including Sindh, to obliterate their national existence. The ongoing plunder of Sindh’s resources, lands, islands, coastal belt, the Karoonjhar mountains, and our sole lifeline, the Indus River, alongside the emerging state conspiracies and machinations to dismember Sindh’s historical unity under various administrative pretexts, are not coincidental events; rather, they are integral parts of this systematic and deep-seated conspiracy of Punjabi imperialism. This conspiracy aims to reduce the Sindhi nation to a minority on its own soil and wipe Sindh’s historical existence off the face of the earth.
When a nation is robbed of its water, when decisions regarding its land, coastline, and resources are made without the consent of the people of Sindh, when its demographic balance is distorted through the settlement of outsiders, and when plots are hatched to extinguish its language, history, and culture, then remaining within such a state means signing one's own death warrant against one's national existence and territorial unity. The right over Sindh’s resources, the authority to decide the fate of its land and water, and the protection of its language, history, and national identity, these are not rights bestowed as charity by any government; they are the fundamental and birthrights of the Sindhi nation.
Therefore, it is the clear, unequivocal, and historical stance of Sindh’s national movement (JSMM) that Sindh’s continuation within Pakistan is a death warrant against the existence of the Sindhi nation.
This state is neither the guarantor of our national identity nor the protector of the survival of our future generations. The so-called constitution, assemblies, and federal institutions are merely tools to legitimize Punjabi supremacy, through which the plunder of Sindh’s resources is sanctioned. The assurances of reforms and provincial autonomy offered by state-sponsored intellectuals and opportunist politicians are merely tactics to waste time and lull the nation into a slumber of negligence, enabling the enemy (Punjabi imperialism and its deceitful military) to fully execute its imperialist designs and anti-Sindh conspiracies. Dividing Sindh under any pretext or disenfranchising it from its resources is a direct assault by Punjabi imperialism on the existence of the Sindhi nation and the future of its coming generations.
The path of our struggle is one of national consciousness, organized strength, historical reasoning, and mass resistance, a path that, in accordance with the principles of modern national concepts, safeguards the historical unity of Sindh while recognizing the dignity, security, and shared rights of every resident of Sindh and every community living within it. History testifies that nations survive only when they recognize their history, defend the unity of their homeland, fight for their freedom, and possess the resolve and courage to offer sacrifices before history for their national survival, security, and territorial integrity.
O honorable sons and conscious daughters of Sindh! History demands a decision from us, and we have only two paths before us: either accept the slavery of this oppressive Punjabi colonial system and await our national demise, or unite under the philosophy of our great leader Sain G.M. Syed and the banner of national liberation, become the true heirs of Raja Dahir, Dodo Soomro, and Darya Khan, shatter the chains of slavery of this unnatural state, and strive for the establishment of our free and sovereign homeland, "Sindhudesh."
Our survival, our dignity, and the secure future of our coming generations lie solely in the complete unity of Sindh, our historical right over our resources, and complete national independence. The time has come for every Sindhi to realize their historical responsibility and answer this call of the national movement, for freedom is life, and slavery is worse than death!
In conclusion, on behalf of the Jeay Sindh Muttahida Mahaz (JSMM) and the valiant youth of Sindh, we send this clear and unequivocal message to the entire Sindhi nation: we are making practical efforts to awaken, arouse, and focus onto a single center that sleeping lion of Sindh’s political consciousness, national spirit, and historical strength, which has been the guardian of its motherland for thousands of years. Our objective is to ignite a blazing fire of national awakening across all of Sindh and kindle such flames of resistance whose heat will not only thwart the anti-Sindh conspiracies, resource plunder, and schemes to dismember the homeland orchestrated by Punjabi imperialism but will also inflict a historic defeat upon Punjabi imperialism on this soil.
Therefore, our message to the entire Sindhi nation is: do not become disheartened, anxious, or hopeless under any circumstances; we, the rightful heirs and masters of Sindh, stand firmly in the field with our national responsibilities. History is witness that when the Sindhi nation rises for its national freedom and survival, no imperialist power can stand in its way. Let us come together to become part of this fearless political struggle and resolute national resistance, and guarantee a secure future for our coming generations and the freedom of our homeland, Sindhudesh!

text:
The Druze: The Moral Minority the West Has Forgotten

Dany A. Khalek
Secretary-General, Neo Lebanese Party

Western travelers, orientalists and even poets once wrote about the Druze with admiration; Robert Browning dedicated a whole play to them in 1843. Yet ask a Westerner today about the Middle East and you will hear about oil, wars, militias and refugees, rarely about the Druze. That forgetting is a loss, because the Druze may be the clearest proof that the region's story does not have to be written in blood and extremism.
The Druze are not newcomers to this land. Their faith took shape a thousand years ago, but the people who embraced it are far older: an indigenous people of the Eastern Mediterranean whose roots in these mountains go back thousands of years, long before the Arab conquest. Today they live in Mount Lebanon, Jabal al-Bashan (Suwayda), the Galilee and the Carmel, a small community of around a million people surrounded by empires, regimes and movements that tried to absorb them, convert them or wipe them out. They survived not by expanding, but by holding on to something rarer than land: a strict moral code.

At the heart of Druze life are values that need no translation: truthfulness, protecting one's brother, honoring women, keeping one's word and respecting the land. The Druze do not seek converts and do not preach to others. They do not export ideology, and they have never asked anyone to live as they do. In a region where religion is too often used as a weapon, the Druze treat faith as a private discipline, not a political project.

My grandfather used to tell me about the rules Druze fighters lived by in times of war. Laying traps for the enemy was strictly forbidden; it was not worthy of men. If you want to fight, he would say, step out and face your enemy. A Druze fighter was not allowed to eat before his prisoner had eaten. And there was one disgrace the community would never forgive: a Druze fighter taking a woman captive, even a woman of the enemy. These were not laws written in a book. They were a code of honor, passed from grandfather to grandson, and they still shape how the Druze see the world.

That discipline shows in daily life. Druze villages are known for their tight family bonds, their sense of shame toward wrongdoing, and an honor culture that pushes people to resolve problems inside the community before they ever reach a courtroom. In the Druze diaspora, from Australia to the Americas, you will often hear the same proud remark: you rarely find a Druze in prison. Whether or not a statistic exists to measure it, the saying itself tells you what the community expects of its own.

Women hold a respected place in Druze society. Monogamy is the rule, and men are forbidden from taking a second wife. Women can become religious initiates, and education is a priority for girls as much as for boys. In a region where many Western readers assume the worst about how women are treated, the Druze offer a different picture.

Perhaps most striking is the Druze relationship with the state. Wherever they live, the Druze have a long tradition of loyalty to the country that protects them. In Israel, Druze men serve in the army and rise to its highest ranks, side by side with Jewish soldiers, in a bond often called a "covenant of blood." This is not opportunism. It is a principle: the Druze stand with those who respect their existence and their dignity.

And this is exactly why the Druze are under attack today. In July 2025, the Druze of Suwayda faced a campaign of massacres by forces linked to the new Syrian regime and jihadist militias. Their crime was simple: they refused to surrender their identity, their weapons and their right to govern their own affairs. The world looked away. Israel did not.

The West often asks where its natural partners in the Middle East are. They are not hard to find. They are the communities that believe in human dignity, coexistence and the rule of law, communities that do not dream of conquering anyone, but only of living freely on their own land. The Druze are one of them.

Supporting the Druze is not charity. It is an investment in the kind of Middle East the West claims it wants: tolerant, stable and free from the grip of political Islam. The free world has much to gain by building bridges with the Druze.
-

text:
🚨🚨FAKE NEWS ALERT – Afghan Proxy Propaganda

This is not analysis. This is classic Afghan proxy psychological warfare.

The account @burhan_uddin_0 is an Afghanistan-based digital operative that routinely pushes anti-Pakistan Army narratives, celebrates “Afghan forces” striking Pakistani posts, and frames every Pakistani institutional action as illegitimate. 

Its sole job is to undermine Pakistan’s economic outreach and security institutions. The tweet is pure disinformation.

The Facts

Army Chief promoting minerals is not a scandal it is policy.

Field Marshal Asim Munir addressed the Pakistan Minerals Investment Forum 2026 and clearly stated Pakistan’s goal become a competitive destination for long-term mineral investment, develop the full value chain (not just raw exports), and provide maximum security to mines, investors, workers and projects. 

This is public, official, and aligned with the Special Investment Facilitation Council (SIFC) mandate. Calling legitimate economic diplomacy marketing in uniform is deliberate framing by a hostile account.

FDI has fallen to an all-time low during his tenure is false.

Absolute FDI numbers have never hit an all-time low under the current tenure. Historical lows occurred years earlier (including periods with net outflows). 

Recent data shows fluctuation some years higher, some lower but the claim of an all-time low is fabricated. 

What is chronically low is Pakistan’s investment-to-GDP ratio (hovering near 13%) and FDI as a share of GDP (around 0.4–0.5%). That is a structural, multi-decade problem, not a sudden collapse invented to fit a political attack on one individual.

The no investor trusts the regime line is propaganda, not evidence
China remains the largest source of FDI. Power and financial sectors continue to attract significant inflows. Security guarantees for mining projects are being publicly offered precisely because investors care about risk. 

Low absolute numbers relative to potential do not equal “no investor trusts the country.” That is narrative warfare, not economics.
Bottom Line

An Afghan account that posts videos of Afghan forces targeting Pakistani posts and frames Pakistan’s military leadership as illegitimate is not a neutral observer of Pakistan’s investment climate. 

It is running a coordinated information operation. The numbers it selectively highlights are either outdated, distorted, or presented without context to manufacture the appearance of economic collapse.

Pakistan’s mineral potential is real. The effort to attract long-term investment is real. The attempt by this account to sabotage that effort with false “all-time low” claims is also real and it is disinformation.

Do not amplify Afghan proxy narratives.

text:
After World War II in 1948, the British military administration offered control of the ruined Volkswagen factory in Wolfsburg, Germany, to the Ford Motor Company Free Press, practically for free...

In 1945, the factory built to make Hitler's people's car lies half in ruins, and the British Army is in charge of it. Following WWII, the British Army controlled the heavily damaged Volkswagen factory in Wolfsburg, Germany. 

Sir William Rootes, head of the British Rootes Group, inspected it and predicted it would fail within two years. The car, he reportedly said, was too ugly and too noisy for the average buyer. A British report concluded that building it commercially would be a completely uneconomic enterprise. 

British authorities offered the plant and the Volkswagen Beetle design to various international carmakers—including Ford—essentially for free. 

In March 1948, the British even offered the company to Ford free of charge. Henry Ford II travelled to Germany to look at it. His chairman, Ernest Breech, is reported to have told him the offer was not worth a damn. Ford declined the offer. Under British supervision and later German leadership (led by Heinz Nordhoff), the Volkswagen Beetle went on to become one of the best-selling and most enduring automobiles in history.

🇸🇩⚔️🔄 BREAKING: RSF Commander Quits Militia, Joins Sudan Army and Blames UAE for War

A field commander of Sudan's paramilitary Rapid Support Forces has announced his defection to the Sudanese army, Sudan Tribune reported.
Ahmed Hasab Al-Rasoul, who led the RSF's first group in Saraf Omra in North Darfur, made the announcement in a video statement on Sunday.
He said he was officially leaving the militia and "returning to the national fold" by joining the armed forces.
Hasab Al-Rasoul claimed the RSF has no national cause or clear goal and is driven by outside powers.
He accused the United Arab Emirates of planning and funding the conflict and bringing in foreign mercenaries.
He also described RSF chief Mohamed Hamdan Dagalo and his brother Abdel Rahim as tools of a foreign plot against Sudan.
The commander blamed favouritism, tribalism and racism inside the RSF ranks, along with a lack of unified leadership.
He urged other fighters to follow him and take advantage of the government's amnesty offer.
His exit follows a series of defections by RSF field commanders and fighters in recent months.
Sudan's war between the army and the RSF has caused one of the world's worst humanitarian crises.

text:
Dmytro Kuleba, Former Minister of Foreign Affairs of Ukraine:

During the 2022 negotiations, russia demanded that Ukraine surrender all its long-range weapons, put its missiles into storage, and allow the russian army to enter Ukraine.

The russians proposed allowing us to maintain an army of 50,000 troops. We wanted 250,000.

It was capitulation with makeup on. Now we are seeing the same demands: abandoning NATO membership, limiting the size of our army, and lifting sanctions.

Kuleba in an interview with Ukrainska Pravda:

When I met with Lavrov in Antalya, he said he had no authority to make decisions. I took out my phone and suggested that we call our presidents right then and there to obtain that authority.

The russians spread a story about “scruffy” Boris Johnson, who supposedly came to Zelenskyy and told him: “Fight to the last Ukrainian.” They played this narrative brilliantly.

When Zelenskyy stayed in Kyiv at the beginning of the invasion, the entire chain of command understood: we were going to fight. The president personally ordered some officials who were already on their way out to turn around and return to Kyiv.

Ukraine had its strongest negotiating position in September–October 2022. We could have initiated negotiations, but society believed that one more push would allow us to drive the russians out.

There was no political opportunity to begin negotiations. And I believe that, ultimately, nothing would have come of them anyway.

Putin models himself after Stalin. In November 2021, russia demanded that the United States roll NATO back to its 1997 borders.

Some people who knew Putin and had negotiated with him tried to convince me that everything came down to money: a billion here, a billion there. But Europe will not be able to buy him off.

Finland has the charismatic Stubb, who knows Putin, understands Trump, and plays golf with him. But Norway is more important to Ukraine because it has real leverage: money, weapons, and F-16s.

We are now criticizing Trump for pressuring us over strikes on russian oil refineries. But the Biden administration also tried to restrain us.

I suggest that we stop constantly telling Europeans that Ukraine is Europe’s shield. Nobody buys that argument. Emotions are powerful, but they don’t last long. Then calculations begin.

Putin’s objective in a war with Europe is to create 24 hours of hesitation in Brussels. If the collective security mechanisms of the EU and NATO fail to respond during that time, individual countries will start calling Putin themselves and asking what he wants. Drone strikes against European facilities would be enough.

On his resignation:

In December 2023, I ranked among the three most trusted government officials. That was the beginning of the end.

For a long time, the president tried to maintain a balance between me, Andriy Yermak, and other players. Eventually, he grew tired of it. In August or September 2024, I was asked to leave, and the primary role in foreign policy was handed over to the head of the Presidential Office.

After my resignation, I was offered the opportunity to move to Harvard, live there, and teach. I declined. I want to live in Ukraine and be useful.

text:
I lived on the fourth floor of a small apartment building in Ohio.

The notes were always written in blue ink, folded twice, and pushed under my door.

I asked the building manager whether anyone had complained about me.

He checked the records and shook his head.

“No official complaints.”

I showed him the notes.

He read them, frowned, and asked me to leave the next one with him.

A few days later, another note appeared.

“Your visitors keep using my parking space.”

I lived alone. I barely had visitors.

This time, I decided to investigate.

I checked the hallway camera footage with the manager’s permission.

At 11:40 every night, an elderly man from apartment 4B walked down the hallway and slipped a note under my door.

I recognized him. His name was Mr. Patterson.

The manager explained that he had lived there for twenty years and had recently begun confusing apartment numbers after a minor renovation changed the hallway layout.

He wasn’t deliberately targeting me.

He genuinely believed my apartment was his old neighbor’s apartment.

The manager offered to speak with him.

But I had another idea.

I bought a small welcome mat, wrote my apartment number in large letters on it, and placed it directly outside my door.

Then I waited.

text:
On March 7, 2019, a court camera in Cleveland filmed a 24-year-old hear a judge sentence him to 43 years in prison for two home robberies. Nobody was killed. Nobody was shot.

He answered the judge with one obscene word, and the room exploded.

His name is Robert Howse. In September 2018 he was on parole after more than five years in prison for another home invasion. He was wearing a GPS ankle monitor. He said he owed $1,500 for drugs.

On September 12 he broke into the home of a 70-year-old woman and hid under her bed. When she found him, she locked herself in the bathroom and called 911.

Two days later, on September 14, in Gates Mills, Ohio, he was waiting in the barn of Joe Jurevicius, a former NFL receiver who won a Super Bowl with Tampa Bay. Jurevicius walked out after dinner to turn off the lights. Howse held him at gunpoint for more than 30 minutes and made him open his safe. To avoid leaving fingerprints, he put on Jurevicius's own Super Bowl gloves. Jurevicius offered him his Super Bowl ring. Howse turned it down.

Then he walked him toward the house, where his wife and kids were, and threatened to shoot him. Jurevicius ran inside, locked the door and hid with his family, holding a gun, until police came.

Howse pleaded guilty in January 2019.

In the video below, Judge Nancy McDonnell reads the sentence. 43 years. Howse curses at her. Deputies grab him and wrestle him out while he screams. His family starts shouting at the deputies. One woman insults the judge on her way out. The courtroom is cleared.

A man who walked out of prison on parole was back in a stranger's home within months. This time the judge made sure he wouldn't get another chance soon.

Was 43 years justice for a repeat offender who terrorized two families, or way too much for a robbery where nobody got hurt?

The value of Alphabet’s stake in the artificial intelligence start-up Anthropic has soared to around $US124 billion ($178 billion), making it one of the most lucrative bets in the company’s history.The Google parent disclosed in a filing on Thursday (Friday AEST) that the value of its investments in unidentified private companies totalled roughly $US124.3 billion as of June 30. Australian Mining

Global Commodity Rankings

Australia holds some of the world's largest reserves and is a leading producer of several key minerals.

#1 Producer: Iron Ore, Bauxite, Lithium, Rutile, and Zircon.

#1 Reserves: Iron Ore, Gold, Lead, Nickel, Rutile, Uranium, and Zinc.

#2 Producer: Gold, Alumina, and Manganese.

Key Mining Hubs & Major Projects

Western Australia: The nation's "engine room," producing 98% of Australia's iron ore and 60% of its gold. Major sites include the Pilbara (iron ore) and the Super Pit in Kalgoorlie (gold).

Queensland: A global leader in metallurgical coal (Bowen Basin) and silver/lead production (Cannington mine).

South Australia: Home to Olympic Dam, which contains the world's largest single uranium deposit and significant copper and gold reserves.

Major Players

The sector is dominated by several multinational giants and significant domestic players:

BHP: Often ranked as Australia's most valuable company; major interests in iron ore, copper, and coal.

Rio Tinto: A world leader in iron ore (Pilbara) and aluminum.

Fortescue (FMG): Primarily focused on iron ore and rapidly expanding into green energy.

Hancock Prospecting: Australia's largest private mining company, led by Gina Rinehart, the nation's wealthiest person.

South32: Spun out of BHP; manages a diversified portfolio including manganese, silver, and nickel.

2026 Trends & Developments

Critical Minerals Push: The government has introduced a $23 billion package to support domestic processing and manufacturing of critical minerals to reduce global reliance on single-country supply chains.

Uranium Rally: Prices exceeding US$100/lb have sparked renewed interest in Australian prospects like the Kalkaroo project.

M&A Activity: Major merger talks continue between giants like Rio Tinto and Glencore as they seek to consolidate copper exposure for the EV market.

Workforce Challenges: The Minerals Council of Australia is currently calling for migration reforms to address a significant "skills crunch" in the sector.

text:
The Private Citizen Builder of Civilization

In the years after the Civil War, America was a continental market waiting to be connected. Freight still crawled by canal or coastal steamer. Iron rails bent and broke. Kerosene lamps flickered and exploded. The price signals were clear to anyone watching the ledgers: speed and reliability paid.

Cornelius Vanderbilt had already read those signals on the Hudson. Starting as a teenage ferry operator, he watched passengers and cargo abandon slow sail for reliable steam. He scaled the insight, then pivoted. When railroads offered the next leap, he bought control of the Harlem, the Hudson River line, and the New York Central, knitting them into a continuous system from New York to Chicago. He replaced iron with steel, double-tracked main lines, and built the Grand Central Depot as a single terminal for the whole network. The result was not abstract monopoly; it was measurable: shorter travel times, lower rates on high-volume routes, and a physical backbone that let Chicago grain and Michigan timber reach eastern markets at commercial speed.

John D. Rockefeller watched the same expansion from Cleveland’s oil fields. Crude poured out of Pennsylvania, but refining was chaotic, wasteful, and dangerous. He standardized the process, integrated pipelines and tank cars, and drove the cost of reliable kerosene down until it displaced whale oil for ordinary households. By the early 1880s Standard Oil controlled roughly 90 percent of U.S. refining capacity. Critics called it a trust; customers called it light that did not explode and fuel that arrived on schedule.

Andrew Carnegie, the Scottish immigrant who had started as a bobbin boy, saw the railroad boom’s next bottleneck: iron rails that wore out too fast. He adopted the Bessemer process at the Edgar Thomson works outside Pittsburgh in 1875, then integrated iron ore, coal, limestone, and transport under one system. Steel rail prices fell from around $100 a ton in the early 1870s toward $18 by the 1890s. Carnegie Steel produced a quarter of America’s output; the metal went into bridges, elevators, and the first true skyscrapers. When he sold to J.P. Morgan in 1901, the transaction created the first billion-dollar corporation—not because of political favor, but because the market had already absorbed the cheaper, stronger material.

A century and a half later the signals had shifted, but the pattern was the same. Launching a kilogram to orbit still cost tens of thousands of dollars under government monopoly. Battery storage was laboratory-scale while intermittent renewables and, later, AI data centers demanded firm power. Broadband stopped at the edge of cities. Elon Musk, funded by the proceeds of earlier software ventures, treated those prices as invitations.

SpaceX began with the premise that reusable rockets could cut launch cost by an order of magnitude. After early failures, Falcon 9 achieved routine booster recovery; Starship later flew revenue missions carrying next-generation Starlink satellites. By the third quarter of 2026 the company reported $14.6 billion in revenue—up 161 percent year-over-year—with Starlink alone serving 13.6 million subscribers and an AI-compute business already larger than the connectivity segment. Reusability had turned space access from a sovereign privilege into a commercial utility.

Tesla applied the same logic to electrons and atoms. Electric vehicles were niche until manufacturing scale, vertical integration of battery chemistry, and software updates made them competitive on price and performance. Parallel energy-storage products followed the same curve. In the same 2026 quarter the company deployed 13.7 GWh of storage—Powerwalls for homes and Megapacks for utilities and data centers—while its Megapack factories in California, Texas, and Shanghai pushed toward 110 GWh of annual capacity. Demand ran ahead of supply; executives noted the systems were nearly sold out into the following year.

Duffy and other officials say they have ruled out a cyberattack or AI-related incident as the cause of the disruptions.

Democrats like Maryland's Chris Van Hollen have heard enough - telling ABC:: “I think he should be fired, and I chair the subcommittee that oversees the Department of Commerce that helped expose his involvement with the Epstein, and now we have this on top of what we already knew. ”

Federal safety investigators say they believe a steering system failure led to the crash of a tanker into a river cruise ship docked in New Orleans. text:
In 2021, Texas suffered the worst energy infrastructure failure in state history, following three severe winter storms in February. At least 246 people were killed as a result of the disruptions, which led to food, water, heat and electricity shortages.

If energy officials had had more time to prepare for the storms, for example by bringing in more trucks of natural gas to disrupted areas, damage from the event could have been mitigated. Unfortunately, weather forecasts beyond two weeks are notoriously unreliable, making for a tighter window for energy operators, farmers, and emergency response officials around the globe.

A new technique by a team including researchers at MIT significantly improves weather forecasting beyond two weeks. The researchers developed a machine-learning model that learns to correct errors in existing forecasting models to improve their output over the two-to-six-week time frame. When applied to a gold-standard forecasting model, it doubled forecasting accuracy over that time frame, placing first in a prominent international forecasting competition.

In a new paper in Nature, the researchers describe their approach and show how it enables forecasts that for the first time beat climatologic averages between two and six weeks.

“Not only does this do better on time averaged forecasts for this range, which is already very useful for farmers and members of the energy industry trying to match supply with demand, but it also improves predictions of extreme weather events, whether it’s flooding or cold spells or something else,” co-author and MIT Research Scientist Judah Cohen says. “It’s really important to predict both, but extreme events might be the most impactful part of this for society.” 

Joining Cohen on the paper are lead authors Hannah Guan, a Harvard College undergraduate; Soukayna Mouatadid, a University of Toronto postdoc; Genevieve Flaspohler SM ’18, PhD ’22; Paulo Orenstein, an associate professor at Brazil’s National Institute for Pure and Applied Mathematics; Jeremy Berman of the data company DTN; Jakob Schloer and Joshua Talib, researchers with the European Center for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts; and Alex Lu, Haiyu Dong, Jonathan Weyn, Zekun Ni, and Lester Mackey, all researchers at Microsoft.

Longer forecasts

In the 1970s, longtime MIT Professor Edward Lorenz came up with the idea of chaos theory to describe how tiny changes in initial weather conditions lead to completely different outcomes.

“He came up with this theoretical two-week limit where beyond that, we just can’t predict weather because the noise in the system grows so much that it overwhelms any signal you start with,” Cohen says. “That had a strong influence on the field that may have held people back from exploring forecasting beyond the two-week range. I never really believed that completely. In theory the atmosphere can create an infinite number of patterns, but it likes to fall into these favorite patterns over and over again. Once one thing happens, I think you can predict the domino that will fall after that, and the domino that will fall after that.”

Today, the best weather forecasts come from either dynamical models, which numerically simulate how the atmosphere and oceans evolve over time, or artificial intelligence models, which learn to make predictions from historical weather data. AI models have shown improvements in predicting weather at short ranges, but they’re even worse than dynamical models at longer time ranges.

Cohen, who is based in the MIT Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering, focuses on forecasting weather two to six weeks in advance, which is known as subseasonal forecasting. “That range is referred to as the ‘predictability desert,’ because in the short range you can capitalize on the initial conditions in the climate system and the atmosphere, and on the longer term you have these slow, varying boundary forces, like the super El Niño everyone’s focused on this winter,” Cohen says. “The subseasonal range can’t take advantage of either of those. In most cases forecasting in the subseasonal ranges is no different than going to a casino and rolling the dice.”

Cohen credits his co-author Lester Mackey, whom he has been collaborating with for more than a decade, with the initial idea of using machine learning to reduce errors in forecasting models.

“We built this wrapper — Lester calls it postprocessing,” Cohen says. “We know AI models have a lot of errors, so we thought maybe we can quantify those errors and remove them.”

While other forecasting systems do more simplistic error correction, the research team’s postprocessing layer uses AI to learn from a forecasting system’s mistakes based on historic data and shifts its forecasts. In that time range, forecasters use so-called probabilistic forecasts, where the likelihood of a range of possibilities if given.

“As more forecasts and data become available, our model adaptively improves its correction,” Cohen says.

To build the model, the researchers used MIT Engaging, a supercomputing cluster hosted by MIT’s Office of Research Computing and Data, but the resulting model does not require a supercomputer to run.

To put their model to the test, last year the research team submitted three models that included their post-processing layer to the European Center for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF), which is considered the best forecasting center in the world. Each season ECMWF holds forecasting competitions between models.

The submission that won first place combined ECMWF’s forecasting model with another, and then applied the postprocessing correction on top. That approach ended up doubling the original model’s predictive power in the subseasonal range. For the first time, the model offered an improvement over relying on climatologic averages.

“Up until now, no one had been able to show a model predicts weather better than long term averages for these subseasonal forecasts,” Cohen says. “They’ve pretty much all been worse than that — you could literally flip a coin and do better. People have questioned if it’s even worth investing in models at all for this time range. We consistently beat climatology averages with our models.”

The model also showed a statistically significant improvement in the ability to predict extreme weather.

“That’s one of the more important findings, because it’s so difficult to accomplish,” Cohen says. “When the ECMWF developed their own, non-AI, error-correction to their model, it got worse at predicting extreme weather. I think that’s because traditional error, or bias, correction is always trying to get to the mean, whereas extreme weather is on the fringe of probabilities.”

Preparing for disaster

In the Nature paper, the team showed their technique could be used to improve land forecasts in most regions across the globe. They also applied their bias correction technique to other models and showed it improved those as well, putting even lesser models on par with the ECMWF’s forecasts.

“What’s nice about our model is it’s an add-on wrapper,” Cohen explains. “We used it with the ECMWF’s dynamical model because that was considered the best, but it can be used with any model. It even improves models that are already bias corrected using another AI algorithm. So it shows a robust improvement. And it’s open source and low cost.”

Cohen says the meteorological office for the Republic of Kenya has already reached out about implementing the model to improve forecasting of the annual monsoon season to improve agricultural yields this winter. He hopes other groups will also use the model.

“This could help you decide when to fertilize around rain, when there’s a freeze coming to protect crops during winter harvests, or help you avoid droughts,” Cohen says. “It could also be useful for energy and emergency management. I’ve talked to energy officials who say, ‘If I’m told two days before that an ice storm’s coming, I don’t have enough time, but if I had two weeks, that could be enough to make adequate preparations.”

The work was supported, in part, by the U.S. National Science Foundation, the Carlos Chagas Filho Foundation for Research Support, and the European Union.

text:
On 18 January 2027, something quietly historic happens: a dollar that lives on a blockchain becomes a federally regulated part of the US financial system.

No new coin. No launch event. A law simply takes effect: the GENIUS Act, with its implementing rules now finalised by the OCC.

What it does in plain terms: it turns stablecoins from a grey area into a licensed product. Issuers serving the US must hold full 1:1 backing in safe, liquid assets, publish reserves monthly, redeem on request within two business days, and give holders priority if the issuer fails. No interest just for holding the coin.

The Comptroller compared it to the 1863 National Currency Act, which standardised America's patchwork of bank notes. Same principle, new rails: if private money circulates, it needs public rules.

What changes: trust and access. Expect digital dollar features inside apps you already use.

What doesn't: a stablecoin is not an FDIC-insured deposit, not a CBDC, and regulated doesn't mean risk-free.

For the diaspora, the promise is real. Houston to Lagos or London to Accra can still take days and cost several per cent. Stablecoins settle in minutes, including weekends. The catch is the last mile: turning digital dollars into naira or cedi still depends on local rules, exchanges and banks. The rails get faster. The friction moves to cashing out.

Before you touch any digital dollar, ask three questions: Who issues it? What backs it? How do I get my dollar back, and how fast? And read the "rewards" small print. If someone offers a return on a stablecoin, ask who is paying it and what risk you're taking to earn it.

Money has always changed form: shells, coins, paper, plastic, now code. The people who understood the new form early were rarely the ones left behind.
The question for 2027 isn't whether digital dollars reach your wallet. It's whether you'll understand them when they do.

(Education, not financial advice.)

The value of Alphabet’s stake in the artificial intelligence start-up Anthropic has soared to around $US124 billion ($178 billion), making it one of the most lucrative bets in the company’s history.The Google parent disclosed in a filing on Thursday (Friday AEST) that the value of its investments in unidentified private companies totalled roughly $US124.3 billion as of June 30. Earlier this year, it agreed to invest as much as $US40 billion more, consisting of $US10 billion upfront and a potential $US30 billion in additional funding tied to operational and financial milestones through 2030.Alphabet’s filing on Thursday showed the remaining commitment has fallen to $US20 billion as of June 30 from $US30 billion at the end of the first quarter, suggesting that Google invested another $US10 billion in the start-up last quarter. Rio Tinto dodges merger bullet

Rio Tinto has dodged two 'bullets' due to Glencore's rejection of a merger proposal: a possible BHP takeover bid and a dangerous acquisition. BHP looked closely at whether to bid for Rio Tinto if the latter announced a merger with Glencore. The two companies would make excellent merger partners; amongst others things, their staff and senior people have similar cultures, they are co-operating on future Australian iron ore projects and they are copper joint venture partners in Chile and the US. Meanwhile, there are significance cultural differences between Rio Tinto and Glencore; there is little doubt that Rio Tinto's CEO Simon Trott would have had doubts about a merger once he understood these cultural differences. (RMS)

News/Snapshot

Australian Mining

Global Commodity Rankings

Australia holds some of the world's largest reserves and is a leading producer of several key minerals.

#1 Producer: Iron Ore, Bauxite, Lithium, Rutile, and Zircon.

#1 Reserves: Iron Ore, Gold, Lead, Nickel, Rutile, Uranium, and Zinc.

#2 Producer: Gold, Alumina, and Manganese.

Key Mining Hubs & Major Projects

Western Australia: The nation's "engine room," producing 98% of Australia's iron ore and 60% of its gold. Major sites include the Pilbara (iron ore) and the Super Pit in Kalgoorlie (gold).

Queensland: A global leader in metallurgical coal (Bowen Basin) and silver/lead production (Cannington mine).

South Australia: Home to Olympic Dam, which contains the world's largest single uranium deposit and significant copper and gold reserves.

Major Players

The sector is dominated by several multinational giants and significant domestic players:

BHP: Often ranked as Australia's most valuable company; major interests in iron ore, copper, and coal.

Rio Tinto: A world leader in iron ore (Pilbara) and aluminum.

Fortescue (FMG): Primarily focused on iron ore and rapidly expanding into green energy.

Hancock Prospecting: Australia's largest private mining company, led by Gina Rinehart, the nation's wealthiest person.

South32: Spun out of BHP; manages a diversified portfolio including manganese, silver, and nickel.

2026 Trends & Developments

Critical Minerals Push: The government has introduced a $23 billion package to support domestic processing and manufacturing of critical minerals to reduce global reliance on single-country supply chains.

Uranium Rally: Prices exceeding US$100/lb have sparked renewed interest in Australian prospects like the Kalkaroo project.

M&A Activity: Major merger talks continue between giants like Rio Tinto and Glencore as they seek to consolidate copper exposure for the EV market.

Workforce Challenges: The Minerals Council of Australia is currently calling for migration reforms to address a significant "skills crunch" in the sector.

Alphabet’s stake in Anthropic expands

The value of Alphabet’s stake in the artificial intelligence start-up Anthropic has soared to around $US124 billion ($178 billion), making it one of the most lucrative bets in the company’s history.The Google parent disclosed in a filing on Thursday (Friday AEST) that the value of its investments in unidentified private companies totalled roughly $US124.3 billion as of June 30. The filing noted that this value is “primarily” driven by one investment, which is a reference to Alphabet’s stake in Anthropic, according to a person familiar with the matter, who asked not to be identified because the information is not public. The company said it recorded about $US77 billion in unrealised gains from its private investments in the second quarter, without providing further details in the filing. Google has emerged as one of Anthropic’s biggest backers over the past several years. The technology giant first invested $US3 billion in the start-up starting in 2023. Earlier this year, it agreed to invest as much as $US40 billion more, consisting of $US10 billion upfront and a potential $US30 billion in additional funding tied to operational and financial milestones through 2030.Alphabet’s filing on Thursday showed the remaining commitment has fallen to $US20 billion as of June 30 from $US30 billion at the end of the first quarter, suggesting that Google invested another $US10 billion in the start-up last quarter. Australian Mining

Global Commodity Rankings

Australia holds some of the world's largest reserves and is a leading producer of several key minerals.

#1 Producer: Iron Ore, Bauxite, Lithium, Rutile, and Zircon.

#1 Reserves: Iron Ore, Gold, Lead, Nickel, Rutile, Uranium, and Zinc.

#2 Producer: Gold, Alumina, and Manganese.

Key Mining Hubs & Major Projects

Western Australia: The nation's "engine room," producing 98% of Australia's iron ore and 60% of its gold. Major sites include the Pilbara (iron ore) and the Super Pit in Kalgoorlie (gold).

Queensland: A global leader in metallurgical coal (Bowen Basin) and silver/lead production (Cannington mine).

South Australia: Home to Olympic Dam, which contains the world's largest single uranium deposit and significant copper and gold reserves.

Major Players

The sector is dominated by several multinational giants and significant domestic players:

BHP: Often ranked as Australia's most valuable company; major interests in iron ore, copper, and coal.

Rio Tinto: A world leader in iron ore (Pilbara) and aluminum.

Fortescue (FMG): Primarily focused on iron ore and rapidly expanding into green energy.

Hancock Prospecting: Australia's largest private mining company, led by Gina Rinehart, the nation's wealthiest person.

South32: Spun out of BHP; manages a diversified portfolio including manganese, silver, and nickel.

2026 Trends & Developments

Critical Minerals Push: The government has introduced a $23 billion package to support domestic processing and manufacturing of critical minerals to reduce global reliance on single-country supply chains.

Uranium Rally: Prices exceeding US$100/lb have sparked renewed interest in Australian prospects like the Kalkaroo project.

M&A Activity: Major merger talks continue between giants like Rio Tinto and Glencore as they seek to consolidate copper exposure for the EV market.

Workforce Challenges: The Minerals Council of Australia is currently calling for migration reforms to address a significant "skills crunch" in the sector.

Nothing to offer? The list has been on the table since 2021.

text:
NIGERIANS HAVE BEEN CONDITIONED TO CELEBRATE THE VERY THINGS THAT SHOULD OFFEND THEM.

One of the greatest tragedies of our political experience is how years of poverty, mismanagement and political manipulation have lowered our expectations of government.

We have normalised begging, political handouts and patronage. Politicians distribute rice, cartons of Indomie and small amounts of money during elections, and we celebrate them for it.

Meanwhile, these are largely public resources being distributed by people entrusted with managing them.

IT IS OUR MONEY!

An entire mini-industry emerges during election season. Some secure contracts for campaign materials and advertisements; others queue for rice, noodles and whatever little is available. Politicians distribute a fraction of what belongs to the public, and we reward them with political loyalty.

A bag of rice will not last four years. Why should it determine four years of our future?

We have also confused political patronage with leadership. We celebrate politicians for the number of associates they have elevated into positions of power and wealth.

But even criminal organisations build networks, reward loyalists and position trusted associates strategically. That is not evidence of good leadership.

THE REAL MEASURE OF LEADERSHIP IS NOT HOW MANY PEOPLE YOU HAVE MADE WEALTHY THROUGH YOUR CONNECTIONS, BUT HOW MANY ORDINARY CITIZENS HAVE BENEFITED FROM YOUR GOVERNANCE.

Did you reduce poverty? Create employment? Improve education and healthcare? Make communities safer? Strengthen institutions? Make life more affordable?

These are the metrics that matter.

Look at Bola Ahmed Tinubu. He has been an influential political figure since 1999. That is more than 27 years of political influence. Beyond the political networks and individuals who have benefited from their association with him, what measurable improvements can ordinary Nigerians point to?

After more than three years as President, Nigerians deserve more than political explanations, campaign promises and macroeconomic figures.

Foreign reserves matter, but they do not automatically put food on anyone's table. Economic growth and financial stability must ultimately translate into better living conditions.

Likewise, student loans are not a complete solution to educational access if graduates leave university burdened with debt and face an economy that offers insufficient employment opportunities.

We should be investing in skills, vocational education, entrepreneurship, productive industries and sustainable employment.

A GOVERNMENT CANNOT CONTINUALLY CELEBRATE ECONOMIC STATISTICS WHILE IGNORING THE ECONOMIC REALITIES OF THE PEOPLE.

Our biggest problem is that we have become conditioned to seek opportunities through proximity to powerful individuals rather than through institutions that should work fairly for everyone.

We celebrate political godfathers because we hope to become beneficiaries of their patronage one day.

But a functioning country should not require you to know a minister, governor or political godfather to access opportunities.

The system should be stronger than the individual. Public office should be about public service, not personal empires.

This is the social contract: citizens have obligations to the state, but government equally has obligations to its citizens. Healthcare, education, security, infrastructure and an enabling economic environment are not acts of charity. They are fundamental responsibilities of governance.

I hope Nigerians begin to recognise how much we have normalised what should be unacceptable.

We must stop selling our long-term future for temporary election-season comfort.

We must stop confusing handouts with development, political connections with competence, and personal loyalty with leadership.

text:
Meet @trungfinity, The guy behind @AxieInfinity.

He co-founded @SkyMavisHQ, raised $152M from a16z, Paradigm and Accel in Oct 2021 at a $3B valuation, and watched $AXS fall from $164.9 to $0.68.

That's 99.6% gone.

Here's how it got there.

In Nov 2020, Axie had around 7,500 players. A year later it had 2.7M daily active users. In Aug 2021 alone, the game brought in $364M in revenue.

Most of the players were in the Philippines. Naavik counted 55% of them there.

A starter team of three Axies cost about $1,500, so guilds lent teams to "scholars" and took a cut of what they earned. One scholar told Rest of World he made about $2,000 in a month, nearly double his old job selling rice feed.

The pay came in $SLP. It peaked near $0.40 in July 2021. By November, Naavik found the typical player earned less than the Philippine minimum wage of $7.03 a day.

Today SLP trades at $0.0004. That's 99.9% down.

Then came the hack.

On March 23, 2022, attackers drained 173,600 ETH and 25.5M USDC from the @Ronin_Network bridge. About $620M.

The bridge needed 5 of 9 validator signatures. Sky Mavis ran 4 of them itself.

The fifth came from the Axie DAO. In November 2021, the DAO let Sky Mavis sign on its behalf during a traffic spike. Sky Mavis's own words: "This was discontinued in Dec 2021, but the allowlist access was not revoked."

How did the attackers get in? Two sources told The Block a senior engineer applied for a fake job and opened a PDF offer letter. The Sky Mavis postmortem says "one employee was compromised."

Nobody at Sky Mavis noticed for six days. Also from the postmortem: "We didn't have a proper tracking system for monitoring large outflows from the bridge."

They found out on March 29, when a user couldn't withdraw 5K ETH.

On April 14, the FBI named North Korea's Lazarus Group.

Now the part most people forgot.

Hours before Sky Mavis announced the hack and closed the bridge, almost $3M in AXS moved from Trung's wallet to @binance. A YouTuber named Asobs traced it. Sky Mavis confirmed the transfer to @Bloomberg.

His explanation? "The Founding Team chose to transfer it from my wallet to ensure that short-sellers, who track official Axie wallets, would not be able to front-run the news."

He called the insider trading claims "baseless and false." Sky Mavis says the founding team put its own funds into reimbursing users.

Sky Mavis announced a $150M round led by @binance to make users whole. It later said it raised only $11M of it, because its balance sheet covered the rest.

But Sky Mavis wouldn't confirm or deny which other wallets that made large transfers belonged to staff.

So whose other wallets moved before the freeze?

The bridge reopened on June 28, 2022, and users were made whole. The 56,000 ETH taken from the Axie DAO treasury was never refilled. US authorities seized about $30M, roughly 10% of the haul.

In April, @CoinDesk, citing @DappRadar, put Axie at around 5,500 daily users. Down from 2.7M.

In February, co-founder @Psycheout86 stepped down from his operating role. In August, Sky Mavis said Axie Classic, the game that started all of this, had its final competitive season and would be handed over to the community.

2.7M players. $620M stolen. 6 days before anyone noticed. Almost $3M moved hours before the freeze.

So where is it all now?

A 13-year-old American girl came home covered in bruises after being raped, and when her mother finally arrived from India, her first words were "You disgust me. I have found a husband for you."

Her name is Vilas. She was born in Los Angeles in 1969 to parents who had just joined the Hare Krishna movement. At 3 they put her in one of the movement's first boarding schools, sleeping on the floor next to 30 other kids. Teachers beat the children with paddles. When her older sister saw her bloodied back, she asked why Vilas couldn't behave better.

At 13, at a festival, a musician from the stage offered to show her a waterfall and raped her on a dirt road out of sight of hundreds of people. A woman saw the bruises on her face and told her father. He took her to a hospital in Maryland. Nobody raised an alarm. The punishment fell on her: a 4-month vow of silence, cooking in the temple kitchen from 4 AM to 8 PM every day.

Then her mother came back. A week later they flew to India. He was 25. She was 13. At the wedding in the temple courtyard, the guru asked who gives this child away. Her mother said, "Me, gladly." He was now her legal guardian. He told her he was doing her a favor, since she was "tainted."

About a year and a half later he said he was done with her and sent her back to the village alone. She was 15. The guest house clerk let himself into her room at 4 AM and raped her. Then she got malaria and lay in a 6-by-4-foot cell for weeks before anyone noticed she was missing. At 16 she landed in Washington, D.C. and slept on the streets.

Years later her mother called her on Mother's Day and asked if she knew why she had always hated her. "You are the product of rape."

Vilas now runs the Maryland Coalition to End Child Marriage.

The Atlantic reports on one of the Pentagon's biggest failures in the war with Iran, when the U.S. command knew about and had a ready-made Ukrainian solution against "Shahed" drones – cheap interceptors and an acoustic detection network – but deliberately ignored them.

The publication presents a timeline to demonstrate that the U.S. could have been better prepared to defend against Iranian drones by using Ukrainian experience.

 Summer 2025: Ukraine is actively deploying interceptors for "Shahed" drones from various manufacturers. They cost a few thousand dollars compared to multi-million dollar Patriot missiles. Together with a network of acoustic sensors – sometimes just smartphones on poles – they shoot down over 90% of the "Shahed" drones.

 Fall 2025: The U.S. Army in Europe, under the command of General Donaghy, begins training on these interceptors and deploys them in Romania and Poland.

 December 2025: The first report on Ukrainian experience is circulated among U.S. military personnel and allies. In February of the following year, the report with step-by-step instructions is sent to commanders of the U.S. Army in other regions.

 February 28: The start of the war with Iran. In response to U.S. and Israeli attacks, Iran launches over 2,000 "Shahed" drones across the region. On March 1, one of the "Shahed" drones penetrates the roof of a building at a U.S. military base in Kuwait, resulting in the deaths of six U.S. soldiers – the largest single loss for the U.S. in this war.

The Atlantic writes that there were two reasons why Americans decided to ignore Ukrainian experience.

1. Arrogance. "Why would we need that?" was the reaction in Washington when Zelensky offered his help on the sixth day of the war. Trump initially agreed, but on March 13, he refused, saying that "we know more about drones than anyone else."

2. Politics. After a dispute in the Oval Office in February 2025, a negative attitude towards Ukraine developed within the administration, treating it as a petitioner rather than an ally. Hegset "didn't even want to hear the word 'Ukraine'." Therefore, a previously planned agreement to purchase Ukrainian weapons was postponed with the message "know your place."

☝️ But the paradox, according to The Atlantic, is that as soon as the war with Iran began, the U.S.'s allies in the region began calling Zelensky, urgently requesting the sale of Ukrainian interceptors.

It was then that the then-Secretary of the Army, Driscoll, along with Eric Schmidt, transferred 13,000 Merops interceptors to the Middle East in a few days. But the result was only one "Shahed" shot down, because the U.S. and countries in the Gulf slowly agreed on the deployment of the technology, and most importantly, the interceptors were sent without the sensor network, i.e., without "eyes."

 The Atlantic writes that the Ukrainian system is effective not because of a single drone, but as a whole complex – sensors, DELTA, interceptors, and most importantly, trained crews. Therefore, it is not possible to simply copy one individual element.

The Atlantic also writes about the personnel consequences that occurred in the Pentagon and the U.S. Army later – essentially, a purge of the "Ukrainian lobby" began:
 General Donaghy, who, at his own discretion, sent hundreds of interceptors to the Middle East and asked Kyiv for more, was removed as part of a reduction in general officer positions;
 Cavoli left even earlier;
 Driscoll followed, and the experimental drone assault battalion formed in Italy was disbanded under the slogan "returning to basics."

 And one more symbolic detail – on the wall in Wiesbaden [the U.S. military command center in Europe, from where operations, including in Ukraine, were controlled], the portrait of Donaghy was simply replaced with a large black square.
