text:
**CHAPTER 10: THE SON WHO BROKE THE SILENCE — WHY MUHOOZI LACKS HIS DAD'S WIT**

Every African strongman eventually faces the same question:
Who comes after me?Museveni tried to answer that question through his family.
His son, #Muhoozi Kainerugaba, was rapidly promoted through the military ranks:
Major. Brigadier. Major General. Lieutenant General. General.
Then, in March 2024, Museveni appointed him Chief of Defence Forces — the highest military position in #Uganda .
On paper, it looked like a father rewarding a loyal son.
Inside the barracks, it was an earthquake.
Because two camps had become increasingly visible.
-CAMP A — THE OLD GUARD
Bush-war veterans such as Salim Saleh, Museveni's brother and a powerful general and businessman, alongside other Luwero-era commanders.
They believe Uganda's military establishment belongs to those who fought for it.They see Muhoozi as a prince who never experienced the same hardships in the bush.
-CAMP B — THE SFC GENERATION
Younger, well-paid and heavily armed officers whose careers depend heavily on Muhoozi.
They do not necessarily share the old generation's attachment to Luwero.
Their priority is the security establishment around State House.And Muhoozi made the situation worse by being loud.
His now-deleted tweets threatening to invade #Kenya  within two weeks, threatening opposition leader #Bobi Wine and joking about war were not merely embarrassing.They were revealing.They showed the world that Uganda's succession debate was increasingly being conducted through military influence and family politics rather than a transparent constitutional process.
A succession plan should be a constitutional arrangement.
Instead, critics increasingly saw a family WhatsApp group with guns.Even Museveni's Western allies were alarmed.
A CDF who tweets about invading neighbouring countries creates a diplomatic liability.

-WHY MUHOOZI CAN'T MANAGE UGANDA-

#Muhoozi is almost the opposite of his father in the political qualities that matter most.
#Museveni is patient. Muhoozi is impatient.
Museveni is quiet. Muhoozi tweets at 2 a.m.
Museveni deceives. Muhoozi announces.
Museveni divides his enemies quietly. Muhoozi risks uniting them publicly by threatening everyone at once — #Kenya , Bobi Wine, journalists and even his own generals.
Museveni would never tweet, "I will invade Kenya in two weeks."
He would invade Kenya, deny it for ten years and smile at a regional summit.
Muhoozi has his father's guns, his father's SFC and his father's name.
But does he have his father's brain, patience and ability to lie with a straight face while making people believe him?
That is the real question.
To manage Uganda, you need to manage the Buganda & other Kingdoms, the Catholic Church, the West, the military, oil companies, Rwanda, Tanzania, Kenya, the DRC, South Sudan and your own family.
All at the same time.
And you must do it while pretending that you are not managing anything.
Museveni can do that in his sleep.
Muhoozi cannot do it even while fully awake.
That is why even Museveni may recognise that his son is not yet ready for the political demands of the throne.
He loves his son.But a Knight is not a King.A Knight can attack.Only a King can rule.

**CHAPTER 11: ODREK RWABOGO — THE BISHOP WHO WANTS TO BE KING**

Now meet the man nobody talks about enough.
Odrek Rwabogo.Husband to Patience Museveni, Museveni's daughter. Son-in-law to the President. Father to Museveni's grandchildren.On paper, he is a businessman, pastor and Presidential Advisor on Special Duties.Quiet. Smiling. Always in a suit. Always quoting the https://t.co/hLZTYZ4qMd #Chess , he is the Bishop.
Bishops do not move like Knights.
They do not jump and shout.
They move diagonally, silently, across the whole board.
You may not notice them until they are already checking your King.
Why might Rwabogo be considered a potential succession figure?
Analysts and political insiders point to three reasons, as reported in Ugandan media and political circles.

1. HE IS THE CLEAN ALTERNATIVE
Muhoozi is loud, controversial and has alienated some Western observers through his tweets.
Rwabogo presents a different image.
Soft-spoken. Business-friendly. Religious. More acceptable to Western diplomats.
He can present himself as a modern Museveni without the military controversy.

2. HE HAS THE FAMILY CARD
He is not simply a political associate.
He is married to the President's daughter. His children are Museveni's https://t.co/GECgqOIVXd a political system where family connections matter, that is significant.
He can make the argument:
"I am family, but I am not the controversial son."

3. HE HAS BUILT HIS OWN NETWORK
While Muhoozi built his influence around the SFC, Rwabogo has developed business, church, youth and political networks.He has been touring, speaking and positioning himself as a new-generation leader.
And here is where the real rivalry begins.
Muhoozi sees himself as the rightful heir by blood.
The son. The CDF. The Prince.
Rwabogo sees himself as a potential heir by competence.
The son-in-law. The manager. The Bishop.Two princes.
One throne.

**CHAPTER 12: RWABOGO VS MUHOOZI — THE SUCCESSION BATTLE**

The rivalry is no longer merely about family gossip.
It is about succession.
Why now?
Because Museveni is ageing. Everyone can see the clock.
And the family is increasingly confronted with the question of who will occupy the throne when the King eventually leaves it.According to reports in Ugandan media and analyst circles in 2025–2026, the Rwabogo and Muhoozi camps have been clashing over three major issues.

1. WHO CONTROLS THE YOUTH?
Muhoozi has #PLU.
Rwabogo has church, business and youth networks.
Both have been associated with efforts to build political support across the country, holding rallies, giving out money and promising opportunities.
But is this really about campaigning for Uganda?
Or is it about campaigning for Museveni's blessing?

2. WHO CONTROLS THE NARRATIVE?
Muhoozi's supporters say:
"Rwabogo is just a son-in-law. He married into power."
Rwabogo's supporters counter:
"Muhoozi is reckless. He will destroy the family legacy with his tweets."
Both camps are reportedly briefing journalists and diplomats.
The family disagreement is increasingly becoming a media battle.

3. WHO DOES MUSEVENI TRUST?
This is the real beef.
Museveni has an incentive to keep both sides competing for his approval.He tells Muhoozi:"You are my son. You are the future."
He tells Rwabogo:"You are my son-in-law. You are mature. You are the future."
Is he promising both the same throne?
And do both men know that they may be competing for something their father-in-law has no intention of surrendering?That is the succession game.Not policy.
Not Uganda.Succession.

-WHY RWABOGO COULD BE DANGEROUS TO MUHOOZI-

This is the part that could worry Muhoozi's camp the most.
Rwabogo is potentially dangerous not because he is loud.
He is dangerous because he is quiet.
If Rwabogo ever became President, political analysts might expect him to deal with Muhoozi's independent military and political influence seriously.
Why?Because Rwabogo would understand a fundamental problem:
You cannot have two centres of power in Uganda.
You cannot have a President in State House and a former CDF or Prince operating with his own SFC loyalists, his own PLU and an independent power base inside the military establishment.A new President would have to consolidate control.
And the first major challenge could be Muhoozi himself.
Not necessarily by killing him.That would be politically disastrous.
A more calculated strategy would be to neutralise his influence.
Retire him. Give him an ambassadorial position in a distant country. Restructure his SFC networks. Cut off his PLU funding. Investigate or arrest commanders suspected of corruption.
Make him politically irrelevant.
Muhoozi would understand the danger.
That is why, in this succession scenario, Rwabogo could be a more serious rival than Bobi Wine.
Bobi Wine is an opposition politician.
Rwabogo is a potential replacement from inside the family.Rwabogo is a Bishop.
Bishops attack diagonally. You may not see the move until it is too late.
Muhoozi is a Knight.
He jumps around loudly. Everyone sees him coming.
In a contest between a quiet Bishop and a loud Knight, the Bishop may have the advantage because he has a plan while the Knight is busy making noise.
That is why this rivalry is more than gossip.
It is a potential cold war within the ruling family.
And Museveni?
He is sitting in the middle.
Perhaps he understands that as long as his son and son-in-law are competing against each other, neither can easily turn against him.
Master of deception.
Again.

**EPILOGUE: THE KING WILL NOT RETIRE — KINGS DON'T RETIRE**

Now we arrive at the real underground battle in Kampala.
It is neither  happening in Parliament nor on television.
It is happening in whispers at State House, in military barracks and around family dinner tables.

-THE SUCCESSION BATTLE.-
Muhoozi does not want to wait forever.
According to analysts, insiders and the pattern of his political positioning, one possible succession strategy is not a conventional coup.
It is something potentially more sophisticated.
He wants to become VICE PRESIDENT.
Why the Vice Presidency?
Because under Uganda's constitutional arrangements, if the President dies in office, the Vice President assumes the presidency, subject to the constitutional succession provisions.
No military https://t.co/Z3H94RTHbE immediate presidential https://t.co/E17VIDRdkB tanks rolling through Kampala.
Just the Constitution doing the work.
That is the chess move.
Not a gun. A chair.
Become Vice President. Wait. Let nature do what politics cannot.
Then inherit the kingdom through the constitutional route.
His Patriotic League of Uganda (PLU) is part of this wider political positioning.
PLU is not yet a conventional political party with an established electoral machinery capable of independently defeating the major opposition forces.
It is a political platform and pressure network.
Rallies. T-shirts. Tweets. Youth mobilisation.
Its message to Museveni is simple:
"Look, I have the crowd. I have the army. Give me the Vice Presidency."
But PLU would face a very different test in a competitive national election.
Against Bobi Wine, particularly in Kampala, Buganda and among younger voters, Muhoozi could face a formidable challenge.Muhoozi may struggle to win the ballot.
His stronger route could be succession.
That is why a coup may be his worst option.
And he knows it.

-WHY AN SFC COUP WOULD BE SUICIDE-

Imagine .Muhoozi ordering the SFC to take Kampala.
The State House&  radio stations.
And Announce:
"My father is old. I am now in charge."
What happens next?
The SFC is elite, well-armed and loyal to the presidential security structure.
It may number around 10,000–15,000 personnel at most, according to the estimates in this analysis.
The UPDF, meanwhile, is a much larger national military force, with more than 40,000 personnel, tanks, artillery, air assets and formations across the country.
The SFC might win the first six hours.
But what happens over the next six days?
The UPDF's sidelined and retired generals would not necessarily sit back and watch a son take over the kingdom they helped build in Luwero.
Networks associated with Salim Saleh, regional commanders and disgruntled officers could become important.
And what about the angry Pawns who believe their AMISOM allowances were withheld?
The result could be a confrontation between the two military structures.
SFC versus UPDF.
The son's army versus the father's army.
Family versus Revolution.
Real https://t.co/rVJaLCC8Z5 Kampala.
Brother killing brother.
That is a can of worms Muhoozi could struggle to close.
Even if he won the initial confrontation, he could end up ruling over ashes.
The West could sanction him. Kenya could close its border. Rwanda could exploit the instability. The #DRC  could face further regional uncertainty.
That is why the Vice Presidency route appears politically safer.
It is https://t.co/bhUkoHEqjq is constitutional.
It allows succession without having to win a war against the very military institution that helped build the kingdom.
But here is the tragedy.
His father may never give him the Vice Presidency.
And that brings us to the central question of this entire story.
Why can Museveni not simply retire?

**WHY MUSEVENI CANNOT RETIRE — "I AM NOT A PUBLIC SERVANT, I AM A FREEDOM FIGHTER"**

Museveni has been reported by Ugandan media as saying:
"I am not a public servant. I am a freedom fighter."
Pwahahahaha!
That one line captures the entire kingdom.
A public servant retires.
A public servant answers to the people. A public servant can be removed by the voters. A public servant receives a pension and goes home.
A freedom fighter?A freedom fighter never retires.
A freedom fighter can begin to see himself as the owner of the country he claims to have liberated.
A freedom fighter can begin to see himself as above the Constitution.
A freedom fighter becomes a King.
Museveni did not simply build a republic.
He built a political system around himself, his military networks and his family.
And now he is a prisoner of that very system.
Think about it from the perspective of a King.

1. IF HE RETIRES, WHO PROTECTS HIS FAMILY?

What happens to the networks surrounding his family, the allegations relating to DRC gold, the torture cases, corruption allegations and the interests accumulated during decades in power?
A retired president may become vulnerable to investigations, political revenge and legal challenges.
Retirement is not necessarily a peaceful option.

2. IF HE HANDS OVER TO MUHOOZI, THE OLD GUARD COULD REVOLT.

The old generals may resist. The West may be uncomfortable. Bobi Wine's supporters may reject the arrangement.Uganda could burn.

3. IF HE HANDS OVER TO RWABOGO, MUHOOZI AND THE SFC COULD RESIST.

The same fire, but from the other side of the family.

4. IF HE HANDS OVER TO AN OUTSIDER, HIS FAMILY COULD LOSE EVERYTHING.

The political protection. The security networks. The business interests. The influence surrounding the presidency.
There is no obviously safe exit.
No simple retirement home in Ntungamo.
No guaranteed quiet life as an elder statesman like #Nyerere.Because Museveni did not build a political system in which power can easily change hands without threatening the people who currently hold it.
And that is the tragedy.
"KINGS DON'T RETIRE. KINGS DIE ON THE THRONE"
This is why Museveni may remain President for as long as his health allows.
Not necessarily because he enjoys political power.
But because the system he built leaves him with very few reasons to trust the next person who occupies State House.
And that is exactly why #Paul Biya in #Cameroon offers an interesting comparison.
People laugh at Biya.
"93 and still President? hahaha!"
But Biya understands the same political chess.
He has been President since 1982. He has seen what can happen to African leaders who leave office.
Some face prosecution.Some go into exile.
Some lose their political protection & Wealth e.g Angolas's Dos Santos.
Some are removed by the very people they once trusted.
Biya stays because staying may appear safer than leaving.
He remains in Yaoundé, makes medical trips to Switzerland and continues holding on to power because the presidency is also his political insurance.
Museveni looks at Biya and sees a mirror.
Biya looks at Museveni and sees a brother.
Two ageing Kings.
Both in Zugzwang.
Both facing a future in which leaving the palace may be more dangerous than remaining inside it.
And Museveni knows the board better than anyone.
He knows Muhoozi wants the Vice Presidency.
He knows Rwabogo may want the throne.
He knows the West is looking for a new manager.
He knows the old generals may still have influence.
He knows the Pawns are angry about their AMISOM money.
So what does he do?
He does what every experienced King does when he has no safe move.
He delays.
He plays son against son-in-law.
He plays SFC against UPDF.
He plays West against East.
He promises Muhoozi "soon."
He promises Rwabogo "maybe."
He promises the West "reform."
He promises Uganda "stability."
He keeps everyone waiting.
Because as long as everyone is waiting for him to decide, he is still King.
The day he makes a definitive decision could be the day his political power begins to unravel.
So he delays.And delays.And delays.
Until his body eventually makes the decision for him.
In chess, this position has a name:-
ZUGZWANG + STALEMATE-
-Zugzwang is when every move available makes your position worse.
-Stalemate is when you cannot make a legal move at all, even though you are not in check.
Museveni is caught between the two.
He is in Zugzwang because every succession option carries enormous risks.
He is in stalemate because he cannot easily move without destabilising the system he has spent 40 years building.
And that is the irony.
Stalemate may be his best position.
If he moves, he risks losing.
If he does not move, he remains King.
He built the board.
Now the board owns him.
He came from a family whose history crossed the Rwanda-Uganda border. He was a refugee boy mentored by Nyerere, a student of African liberation movements, and a guerrilla fighter who took power after the ballot failed him.
He built an empire of soldiers, political networks, gold, regional wars and carefully managed alliances.
And now he sits in State House Entebbe, in his 80s, surrounded by the SFC, guarded by a military structure led by his son, watched by generals he has sidelined and slowly losing the unquestioning support of some of his old Western friends.
He cannot easily leave, because the system may turn against his family.
He cannot comfortably stay, because the system is increasingly strained from within.
He is not simply the President of Uganda.
He is the prisoner of the system he created.
He is not just a public servant.He is a freedom fighter.
He is a King.
AND KINGS DON'T RETIRE.

#DISCLAIMER
This is historical Geopolitical Chess moves analysis and opinion based on public records, UN reports, court rulings, memoirs and investigative journalism.
Allegations are identified as alleged or reported and should not be confused with court convictions. Political interpretations and succession scenarios are analysis, not established facts. Verify the sources at the end.

#SOURCES & FURTHER READING

1. Museveni, Y. Sowing the Mustard Seed (1997).
2. UN Panel of Experts on Illegal Exploitation of Natural Resources in the DRC — Reports S/2001/357 and S/2002/1146.
3. #International Court of Justice — Armed Activities on the Territory of the Congo (DRC v. Uganda), Judgment, 19 December 2005.
4. Human Rights Watch and Amnesty International — Uganda country reports.
5. Ugandan Parliament Hansard — Debates on UPDF AMISOM allowances (2015–2022) and constitutional amendments (2005, 2017).
6. Daily Monitor, The Observer and Nile Post — Investigative reports on delayed soldier pay, SFC, UPDF retirements, and the removal of presidential term and age limits.
7. #BBC  and #Reuters  — Muhoozi's appointment as CDF in March 2024, Kayihura's arrest in 2018, Garang's helicopter crash in 2005, and Paul Biya's presidency.
8. Ugandan media reports and analyst commentary on Odrek Rwabogo's political positioning (2022–2026) — presented as reported positioning, not a confirmed presidential candidacy.
9. #USA  State Department Human Rights Reports — Uganda, including corruption in the security sector.
10. #World Bank — Statement on suspension of new loans to Uganda, August 2023.
11. Ugandan media coverage of Museveni's reported statements on being a "freedom fighter" rather than a public servant.

Thanks for reading.

text:
South Florida has something that very few American regions can replicate. 🐚

It’s simultaneously a major U.S. business center and a gateway to Latin America, the Caribbean, and international capital.

For entrepreneurs and investors, that geographic position creates some fascinating advantages.

You can operate within the American legal and financial system while maintaining close commercial relationships with international markets.

You can meet investors from Brazil, business owners from Mexico, developers from Colombia, and executives from New York, sometimes all in the same week.

And for international families, Miami offers something particularly valuable: a place to establish a U.S. presence without completely disconnecting from their existing businesses and relationships abroad.

This matters for real estate.

Because housing demand isn’t driven exclusively by local salaries or local employment.

In an international city, demand can also come from global wealth, business expansion, second-home buyers, and families seeking geographic diversification.

That doesn’t make Miami immune to economic cycles.

But it does mean the city’s real estate market is influenced by a much broader set of economic forces than many people realize.

When you buy real estate in Miami, you’re not just investing in a local housing market. You’re participating in a city connected to capital, commerce, and opportunity across continents. 🤍

- The surge has reclaimed the 0.00692 area, so my 1h bias is bullish for a continuation attempt, but this remains a countertrend rebound: daily and weekly structure, as well as BTC, are bearish. I would not chase the vertical 15-minute candle.
- The reported 19.1x volume spike shows unusually intense activity, not proof of smart-money accumulation; the dashboard’s broader relative volume is elevated at 4.03x, while taker flow is near balanced and open interest has risen only modestly. That mix leaves a squeeze or fast profit-taking plausible.
- I’d consider a long only on a pullback into 0.00680–0.00665 that holds, followed by a clear 5–15-minute bullish market-structure shift, or a bullish engulfing/pin bar with renewed buying volume. If price loses that zone without reclaiming it, I’d stand aside rather than buy the impulse.
- For a confirmed entry, my first target is 0.00750, followed by 0.00848; take partials and watch how price reacts, since the higher-timeframe downtrend makes the second objective less certain. The next upside area is around 0.00878–0.00900 only if momentum and participation persist.
- The 0.00660 swing high and 0.00624 swing low are liquidity reference points, not ordinary support/resistance; a sweep of the low followed by a strong reclaim would offer a cleaner long trigger than chasing. Keep protection beyond the relevant structure invalidation, allowing for HUMA’s elevated volatility.
- My bullish expectation is invalidated by a 1h close below 0.00624, the stated structure-flip level; until then, I favor a controlled retest-and-continuation setup, not an assumption that one volume burst guarantees durable accumulation. Not investment advice; educational report only.

ANTHROPIC IPO PRIME PUBLIC ROUND CLOSES TOMORROW! ARE YOU STILL CONSIDERING GETTING EXPOSURE TO $ANT? 🧐

After weeks of covering Anthropic's upcoming IPO, we are now approaching one of the more important dates for anyone considering participating.

November 17, 08:00 UTC.

That's the scheduled deadline for Bitget IPO Prime's Public Round, assuming Anthropic proceeds with its anticipated November 19 listing.

And before that deadline arrives, I want to revisit one reason Anthropic has attracted so much investor attention.

LET'S TALK ABOUT ANTHROPIC'S BUSINESS GROWTH 🌱

According to its recent IPO filing, Anthropic generated about $33.2 billion in revenue in the first nine months of 2026, up 1,206% from the same period last year.

That's a substantial increase for a company founded just five years ago.

Much of the attention surrounding the company comes from Claude and its growing presence in enterprise AI through developer tools, coding assistants, and business applications.

But I would not look at revenue growth alone when evaluating the company.

Anthropic is also spending enormous amounts of money on computing infrastructure, and maintaining that growth will require continued investment.

For me, one angle to look at is whether the company can eventually turn its rapidly growing revenue into sustainable profits without increasing infrastructure spending at the same pace.

And given the selloff in tech stocks recently, investors will be paying close attention to that balance.

WHAT ABOUT THE DEMAND FOR ITS IPO? 🙋

Recent reports suggest that Anthropic's offering has attracted demand several times greater than the shares expected to be available (6x-7x oversubscribed).

That suggests institutional interest remains strong, but it does not mean Anthropic is guaranteed to pump significantly once trading begins.

A heavily subscribed IPO can still disappoint investors if the final valuation is too high or broader market conditions deteriorate.

That's why I would pay more attention to Anthropic's final offering price and valuation than assume the enthusiasm surrounding AI will continue after listing.

FOR THOSE CONSIDERING BITGET IPO PRIME 🔎

The Public Round remains open to eligible users, allowing commitments between $100 and $25,000 using USDT or USDGO.

A 5% underwriting service fee applies to the amount actually allocated, and allocations are calculated proportionally based on the available pool.

Participants will receive rANT, a tokenized asset linked to Anthropic, rather than direct ownership of the company's shares.

And if you are new to @Bitget, there's also a separate promotional campaign offering additional rANT rewards.

Eligible new users who registered from November 2 can qualify for 20 USDT worth of rANT after making a qualifying first deposit of at least 1,000 USDT and participating in the IPO subscription.

A higher reward tier offers 100 USDT worth of rANT for a qualifying first deposit of at least 30,000 USDT, with an additional 5 USDT available for eligible P2P deposits.

These rewards are subject to registration, a limited 100,000 USDT reward pool, and a fund-retention requirement extending 30 days after the IPO. The two main reward tiers cannot be combined.

SO, WOULD I STILL CONSIDER ANTHROPIC AT THIS STAGE? 💭

In my own opinion, given the negative sentiment and recent sell-off in the crypto market, the situation reminds me of what happened ahead of the SpaceX IPO five months ago.

I would not be surprised if some traders were already selling their crypto holdings a few days ago to free up capital for Anthropic. It may not make sense to everyone, but markets do not always need to make sense.

Sometimes, money simply moves from one opportunity to another, and right now, Anthropic seems to be getting a lot of attention despite everything happening in the broader market.

Of course, that does not mean the company will perform the same way SpaceX did. But considering the demand we have seen so far, I think it's still worth looking into before the Public Round closes.

For anyone who's planning to get exposure to Anthropic before the Public Round closes, here's the official campaign page: https://t.co/TDxg4gOIFs

Remember that November 19 remains an anticipated IPO date, and the subscription timeline may change.

rANT does not provide direct shareholder ownership, voting rights, or direct dividends. The token can trade below its reference offering price, and returns or allocations are not assured.

Make sure you understand the product terms and risks before committing capital. This is not financial advice.

My question for everyone following the Anthropic IPO is, are you more interested in its extraordinary revenue growth, or are you concerned that its valuation might already reflect years of future AI expansion?

SUPREME COURT OF THE UNITED STATES
AZADEH KHATIBI, ET AL. v. FELIX C. YIP, PRESIDENT
OF THE MEDICAL BOARD OF CALIFORNIA, ET AL.
ON PETITION FOR WRIT OF CERTIORARI TO THE UNITED
STATES COURT OF APPEALS FOR THE NINTH CIRCUIT
No. 25–1240. Decided November 16, 2026

The petition for a writ of certiorari is denied. JUSTICE
GORSUCH would grant the petition for a writ of certiorari.
JUSTICE THOMAS, with whom JUSTICE ALITO joins, dis-
senting from the denial of certiorari.
In 2022, California began requiring private instructors in
privately run and privately accredited continuing medical
education (CME) courses to discuss how so-called implicit
bias affects healthcare outcomes. The Ninth Circuit held
that First Amendment scrutiny did not apply to this com-
pelled-speech requirement because the breadth of Califor-
nia’s CME regulation renders the content of any CME
course government speech, not private speech. That logic
fundamentally misunderstands this Court’s precedents and
the Constitution. First Amendment protections do not give
way simply because a State heavily regulates speech.
I would have granted certiorari to clarify the government-
speech doctrine. At a minimum, the Ninth Circuit misap-
plied Shurtleff v. Boston, 596 U. S. 243 (2022), which in-
structs courts to identify government speech by considering
(1) “the history of the expression at issue,” (2) “the public’s
likely perception as to who (the government or a private
person) is speaking,” and (3) “the extent to which the gov-
ernment has actively shaped or controlled the expression.”
Id., at 252. The Ninth Circuit collapsed those distinct in-
quiries, focusing on the breadth of the government’s regu-
latory scheme at each step. More fundamentally, however,
Shurtleff is leading courts astray. I joined JUSTICE ALITO’s
2 KHATIBI v. YIP

THOMAS, J., dissenting

concurrence in Shurtleff, which warned that the majority’s
three-factor test could cause courts to conclude that exten-
sive government regulation transforms a private message
into government speech exempt from First Amendment
scrutiny. Id., at 263–266 (opinion concurring in judgment).
As the Ninth Circuit’s decision shows, those concerns were
prescient. This Court should reconsider whether the
Shurtleff test is the proper mode of analysis for identifying
government speech.
I
California-licensed physicians are required to complete
50 hours of approved CME every two years. Cal. Code
Regs., tit. 16, §1336(a) (2026). Credit-eligible CME courses
are often organized by private entities, certified by private
accreditors, and taught by private instructors. See
§§1337(a), 1337.5(a)(1); Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code Ann.
§2190.1(d)(3) (West Cum. Supp. 2026). The State does not
preapprove course content but reserves the right to audit
courses for compliance with its CME standards. Cal. Code
Regs., tit. 16, §1337.5(b).
The Medical Board of California “adopt[s] and adminis-
ter[s] [CME] standards,” few of which relate to course con-
tent. Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code Ann. §2190 (West 2019); see
Cal. Code Regs., tit. 16, §§1336–1339.5. In addition, the
State requires that CME courses broadly relate to the med-
ical profession. They must “serve to maintain, develop, or
increase the knowledge, skills, and professional perfor-
mance that a physician and surgeon uses to provide care, or
to improve the quality of care provided to patients.” Cal.
Bus. & Prof. Code Ann. §2190.1(a) (West Cum. Supp. 2026).
In 2019, however, the California Legislature added a re-
quirement that after January 1, 2022, all CME courses
must “contain curriculum that includes the understanding
of implicit bias.” §2190.1(d)(1). To satisfy that require-
ment, CME courses must contain “[e]xamples of how
Cite as: 610 U. S. ____ (2026) 3

THOMAS, J., dissenting

implicit bias affects perceptions and treatment decisions of
physicians and surgeons, leading to disparities in health
outcomes” or “[s]trategies to address how unintended biases
in decisionmaking may contribute to health care dispari-
ties.” §§2190.1(e)(1), (2).
Petitioners Dr. Azadeh Khatibi and Do No Harm do not
want to speak California’s preferred message on implicit
bias, and they challenged §2190.1(d) as compelling speech
in violation of the First Amendment. Dr. Khatibi, a Cali-
fornia-licensed ophthalmologist, creates and teaches CME
courses. First Amended Complaint in No. 2:23–cv–06195
(CD Cal.), ECF Doc. 26, ¶5 (First Amended Complaint).
She “disagrees that implicit bias is the primary factor driv-
ing disparities in healthcare” and does not want to devote
time to the subject during her courses. Id., ¶43. Do No
Harm is a nonprofit corporation. Id., ¶7. At least one of its
members teaches CME courses and believes that implicit
bias trainings “have not been shown to successfully reduce
barriers to healthcare, and instead risk infecting healthcare
decisions with divisive and discriminatory ideas.” Id., ¶61.
Yet, California’s implicit-bias-training requirement leaves
petitioners no choice but to discuss the topic in a way that
affirms the State’s view that implicit bias causes “dispari-
ties in health outcomes.” Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code Ann.
§2190.1(e)(1) (West Cum. Supp. 2026).
The District Court dismissed the complaint on the theory
that the implicit-bias-training requirement “constitutes
government speech,” Khatibi v. Hawkins, No. 2:23–cv–
06195 (CD Cal., May 2, 2024), p. 14, and the Ninth Circuit
affirmed. The Ninth Circuit held that all three Shurtleff
factors indicate that “CMEs eligible for Board credit consti-
tute government speech.” Khatibi v. Hawkins, 145 F. 4th
1139, 1146 (2025). At every step of the analysis, the Ninth
Circuit emphasized the breadth of the State’s regulation.
Considering history, the court noted that California “has
long regulated the practice of medicine as an exercise of the
4 KHATIBI v. YIP

THOMAS, J., dissenting

police power” and has “adopted, updated, and enforced
CME standards.” Id., at 1147–1148 (internal quotation
marks omitted). Considering the public’s likely perception
of the speaker in a CME course, the court reasoned that “li-
censees could attribute approved CMEs’ content to Califor-
nia” because “their profession is heavily regulated.” Id., at
1151. Considering the extent to which the government has
shaped the expression, the court cited “California’s extraor-
dinary control over accredited CMEs.” Id., at 1152. As
Judge VanDyke explained in his dissent from the denial of
rehearing en banc, the panel’s “approach boil[ed] down to a
single-factor analysis: does the government ‘heavily’ or ‘ac-
tively’ regulate CMEs?” Khatibi v. Hawkins, 164 F. 4th
1105, 1109 (CA9 2025).
II
A
In its blinkered application of the Shurtleff factors, the
Ninth Circuit lost sight of the core government-speech in-
quiry: whether the government is “speak[ing] for itself or
. . . regulat[ing] private expression.” Shurtleff, 596 U. S., at
252.
The government-speech doctrine occupies a narrow cor-
ner of our First Amendment jurisprudence. The First
Amendment protects the people’s right of free speech
against government interference; it does not prevent the
government from speaking for itself. Pleasant Grove City v.
Summum, 555 U. S. 460, 467 (2009). “But courts must be
very careful when a government claims that speech by one
or more private speakers is actually government speech.”
Shurtleff, 596 U. S., at 262 (ALITO, J., concurring in judg-
ment). “If private speech could be passed off as government
speech by simply affixing a government seal of approval,
government could . . . muffle the expression of disfavored
viewpoints,” Matal v. Tam, 582 U. S. 218, 235 (2017), or, as
Cite as: 610 U. S. ____ (2026) 5

THOMAS, J., dissenting

here, require private speakers to convey government mes-
sages without facing any constitutional scrutiny.
This Court has thus exercised “great caution” before char-
acterizing a message as government speech. Ibid. In Jo-
hanns v. Livestock Marketing Assn., 544 U. S. 550 (2005),
we held that government-sponsored beef ads constituted
government speech because the government determined
“the overarching message” of the ads, helped develop pro-
posals for the ads, reviewed every ad “for substance and for
wording,” and the Secretary of Agriculture “exercise[d] final
approval authority over every word used in every” ad. Id.,
at 561. In Summum, we held that the permanent display
of monuments in a public park was government speech be-
cause the City “effectively controlled the messages sent by
the monuments in the Park by exercising final approval au-
thority over their selection.” 555 U. S., at 473 (internal quo-
tation marks omitted). And, in Walker v. Texas Div., Sons
of Confederate Veterans, Inc., 576 U. S. 200 (2015), we held
that the messages on government-issued license plates,
over which the State “maintain[ed] direct control,” were
government speech. Id., at 208, 213.
Since Walker—which we have described as the “outer
boun[d] of the government-speech doctrine,” Matal, 582
U. S., at 238—we have been careful to distinguish between
government control over messages and government control
over the broader scheme through which the messages are
communicated. We held, for example, that trademarks are
private speech, notwithstanding the government’s substan-
tial involvement in the registration process. Id., at 239.
And, this Court held that flags flown outside of Boston’s
City Hall did not constitute government speech in part be-
cause the city regularly permitted private groups to freely
fly their own colors. Shurtleff, 596 U. S., at 255–259. In all
these cases, the controlling question was whether “the gov-
ernment intends to speak for itself or to regulate private
expression.” Id., at 252.
6 KHATIBI v. YIP

THOMAS, J., dissenting

Put in those simple terms, and in light of our precedents,
California’s attempt to require private individuals in pri-
vately accredited CME courses to run implicit-bias training
is an evident attempt “to regulate private expression.” Ibid.
The Ninth Circuit resisted that conclusion. It mechanically
analyzed the Shurtleff factors in isolation, without stepping
back to consider “the identity of the speaker,” which is “[t]he
ultimate question” in the government-speech inquiry. Id.,
at 263 (ALITO, J., concurring in judgment).
Even under the Shurtleff test, I doubt that California’s
implicit-bias-training requirement is government speech.
First, California has not historically used CME to com-
municate government messages. While the State requires
that CME courses generally relate to the practice of medi-
cine and occasionally requires that courses cover certain
subjects, California has not otherwise dictated the content
of courses. See Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code Ann. §2190.1 (West
Cum. Supp. 2026). Second, because California “relie[s] on
the participation of private parties in executing the CME
scheme,” Khatibi, 145 F. 4th, at 1151, the public is unlikely
to perceive a private instructor’s CME course as govern-
ment speech. As the Ninth Circuit acknowledged, Dr. Khat-
ibi “plausibly alleged facts suggesting that attendees treat
her as the person responsible for CME content.” Id., at
1150–1151. Third, while California extensively regulates
the medical field, licenses physicians, and sets the require-
ments for credit-eligible CME, there is little evidence that
California “shape[s] the messages” communicated in CME
courses. Cf. Shurtleff, 596 U. S., at 256 (emphasis added).
Despite its long recitation of California regulations, the
Ninth Circuit did not identify any state law that requires
private speakers in a CME course to express a particular
viewpoint—even on contestable medical issues. See Khat-
ibi, 145 F. 4th, at 1152–1157. The implicit-bias-training re-
quirement is a notable departure from that practice. It
should have been easy, then, for the courts below to
Cite as: 610 U. S. ____ (2026) 7

THOMAS, J., dissenting

conclude that California’s implicit-bias-training require-
ment regulates private speech.
More troubling than the Ninth Circuit’s misapplication of
the Shurtleff factors are the implications of the court’s de-
cision. On the Ninth Circuit’s view of government speech,
could California require a CME instructor to communicate
the State’s preferred message on the availability of abor-
tion? Cf. National Institute of Family and Life Advocates v.
Becerra, 585 U. S. 755, 766 (2018). Could the State require
a CME instructor to inform participants that for certain pa-
tients, gender-transition surgery is ethically required? Cf.
Chiles v. Salazar, 607 U. S. 627, 636, 639–640 (2026). What
of other professions whose members California licenses and
regulates? At the next statewide legal conference at which
lectures are offered for continuing legal education, could
California require a keynote speaker to oppose racial pref-
erences in law firm hiring? Applying the Ninth Circuit’s
logic, enough government regulation of the field would con-
vert the private speaker’s message in each of these hypo-
theticals into government speech unprotected by the First
Amendment. That result does not follow from this Court’s
precedents, and it certainly does not follow from the Consti-
tution.
B
If the Ninth Circuit’s decision is truly the kind of result
that Shurtleff ’s three-factor test countenances, we should
reconsider Shurtleff. Before Shurtleff, this Court had iden-
tified history, public perception, and government control as
“relevant” but not mandatory “considerations” for identify-
ing government speech. See Walker, 576 U. S., at 210.
When Shurtleff described those considerations as a three-
factor test, several Members of the Court—myself in-
cluded—warned that the test would be unworkable and ob-
scure the central inquiry in government-speech cases:
whether the government is speaking or regulating private
8 KHATIBI v. YIP

THOMAS, J., dissenting

speech. “[L]ike any factorized analysis,” the Shurtleff ma-
jority’s approach does not “provide a principled way of de-
ciding cases.” 596 U. S., at 266 (ALITO, J., concurring in
judgment). Worse, myopic focus on the history and scope of
government control over speech may give courts the false
impression that state regulation can convert private speech
into government speech. Id., at 264–265.
After only a few years, those concerns are materializing.
The Ninth

text:
gfermah

When users can rewrite an AI system's instructions, its reliability becomes a security problem.

In December 2023, Chevrolet of Watsonville, a car dealership in California, experienced an unusual problem with its AI-powered customer service chatbot.
A visitor named Chris Bakke discovered that he could influence the chatbot's behaviour by giving it new instructions.

He told it to agree with everything customers said, regardless of how unreasonable the request was, and to end its responses by claiming that the agreement was legally binding.
The chatbot accepted the instruction.

Bakke then offered $1 for a 2024 Chevrolet Tahoe, a vehicle valued at more than $76,000. 
The chatbot agreed to the proposed price and repeated that the offer was legally binding.

The exchange went viral, and other users began experimenting with the chatbot, getting it to perform unrelated tasks and recommend competing vehicles.

There is an important distinction here. No vehicle was actually sold for $1, and the chatbot's response did not create a binding sale. 
However, the incident exposed how easily a public-facing AI assistant could be manipulated into producing statements outside its intended role. The chatbot was subsequently taken offline.

The underlying problem is prompt injection.
Prompt injection happens when someone supplies instructions through an input channel that an AI system processes, attempting to override its intended behaviour or redirect its task.

The problem becomes more serious when an AI system is responsible for evaluating information or making decisions that affect other people.
Ultramint @ultramint_xyz built on Fermah's kernel addresses this risk directly in its Content Policy.

Section 7 prohibits users from embedding instructions, prompts or other content designed to manipulate or evade automated screening and resolution systems, including its AI Oracle.

This is an important restriction because market descriptions and supporting content are not always harmless text. They can contain instructions intended to influence how an automated system interprets information.

Consider how this could affect a prediction market.

Suppose someone creates a market about whether a particular company will release a product before a specified date.

The market description could contain additional instructions attempting to persuade an AI resolution system to ignore its normal evaluation process, favour a particular interpretation or produce a predetermined result.

If those instructions were treated as authoritative, the system could end up evaluating the creator's manipulation rather than the actual evidence surrounding the event.

Ultramint's policy explicitly prohibits this behaviour. 
It also prohibits attempts to bypass screening by disguising prohibited content through misspellings, encoding or other techniques.

There is another important layer in the policy.
Ultramint describes its market screening as a best-efforts process. 
Automated or manual checks may be applied before or after creation, but the platform does not guarantee that every prohibited market will be detected.

This distinction matters because screening is a protective layer, not proof that every market is safe. 
Creators remain responsible for ensuring their markets comply with the rules.

The Chevrolet incident shows why this matters beyond chatbots.
An AI system can produce a convincing response while operating outside the authority it was supposed to have.

For Ultramint, protecting the resolution process means preventing participants from using market content as an indirect way to manipulate the systems responsible for evaluating outcomes.

The goal is to keep the AI Oracle focused on evidence and the market's established resolution criteria, rather than instructions planted by someone who wants a particular result.

text:
gfermah

Some people don't predict an outcome. They know it before everyone else does.

The 2024 UK General Election exposed how damaging that information advantage can become in a betting market.

Before the election date was publicly announced, betting operators offered markets on when the election would take place. 
Behind the scenes, confidential discussions were already taking place about holding the election on July 4, 2024.

Then-Prime Minister Rishi Sunak announced the date on May 22.
What happened before that announcement eventually became a criminal case.

On October 23, 2026, the UK Gambling Commission confirmed that Anthony Lee, Laura Lee and Amy Hind had been sentenced for cheating offences connected to bets on the election date.

Anthony Lee was the Conservative Party's Director of Campaigning and had access to confidential discussions about the election. 
He used that information to place bets and passed it to his wife, Laura, who also placed bets using the information.

Amy Hind had previously worked for the Conservative Party and received confidential information about when the election would be called. 
She also used it to place bets.

The important detail is that these individuals were not simply making unusually accurate predictions. 
They had access to information that the wider betting market did not.

Fermah's Ultramint @ultramint_xyz addresses this through its Material Non-Public Information rules.

MNPI refers to information that has not been broadly released to the public but could influence someone's decision to enter, hold or exit a market position.

Section 3.3 of Ultramint's Terms of Service prohibits participants from trading while possessing relevant MNPI.

The rule covers more than the person who originally receives confidential information. 
It also prohibits tipping, which means communicating or making that information available to another person when there is reason to believe they may use it to trade.

This distinction is important.
Imagine an employee who learns about an upcoming government decision during a confidential meeting. 
They might never place a bet themselves, but passing the information to a friend who does can still create an unfair advantage.

Ultramint's rules address both sides of that arrangement. 
The person supplying the information and the recipient trading on it are covered.

The Content Policy adds another layer before a market even opens.

Ultramint prohibits creating markets whose outcomes depend on information that is not publicly available. 
This includes unannounced government decisions, regulatory outcomes, corporate announcements and other confidential developments.

The purpose is to avoid creating markets where participants are effectively rewarded for obtaining information that ordinary traders cannot reasonably access.

There is also an important distinction between public information and rumours. 
Ultramint's terms require information to be broadly released through generally available channels and for participants to have a reasonable opportunity to absorb it.

That prevents a private leak or an isolated message from automatically being treated as public knowledge.

The UK election betting case shows why these boundaries matter. 
A market can attract participants who believe they are competing through research and judgement, while others may already know the outcome through privileged access.

Ultramint cannot guarantee that every insider-trading attempt will be detected. However, its MNPI rules and listing restrictions establish clear standards for what information participants may use and what markets should be allowed.

A fair prediction market should reward informed judgement, not privileged access to confidential decisions.

text:
gfermah

A market becomes dangerous when the person betting on an outcome can also influence that outcome.

In October 2022, Mango Markets suffered an exploit involving the manipulation of its MNGO token price.

According to the US Securities and Exchange Commission's complaint, Avraham Eisenberg used two accounts he controlled to trade MNGO perpetual futures against himself. 
He then made large purchases of the relatively thinly traded MNGO token, artificially increasing its price.

The effect was significant. 
The value of his perpetual futures position rose by approximately 1,300%. Mango Markets allowed users to borrow against the value of their assets, so the inflated position gave Eisenberg the ability to borrow and withdraw approximately $116 million in crypto assets.
When the token price fell back towards its earlier levels, the platform was left with a substantial deficit.

The important lesson is that the reference price was not simply observing the market. 
Trading activity was being used to influence the very value on which the borrowing system depended.

Fermah's @fermah_xyz Ultramint @ultramint_xyz addresses a related problem through its rules against self-influenced outcomes.
Its Terms of Service prohibit participants from taking positions in markets whose real-world outcomes they can directly cause, influence or determine when their purpose or effect is to profit from bringing about that outcome.

This is different from ordinary market participation. 
Having a strong opinion, conducting research or taking a large position is not automatically prohibited. 
The concern is when someone has the ability to influence the outcome and uses that ability to extract value from the market.

Consider a market based on whether a particular event will happen by a stated deadline. 
If a participant can directly make that event happen, prevent it or control the information determining its outcome, their position creates a conflict that ordinary trading rules may not adequately address.

The platform's rules therefore look beyond the size of a position and consider the relationship between the participant and the event itself.
There is also a preventive layer at market creation.

Ultramint's Content Policy prohibits self-referential and circular markets. This includes markets whose outcomes depend on their own trading volume, participant numbers, implied probability, platform engagement or even their own resolution.

Why does that matter?

Imagine a market asking whether its own trading volume will exceed a certain figure. 
Participants could trade specifically to increase the volume that determines the answer. 
The market would no longer be measuring an independent event. 
Its activity would be helping create its own outcome.

The same problem applies to markets that resolve based on their own implied probability or platform engagement.
By prohibiting these structures, Ultramint separates the event being predicted from the market activity surrounding it.
This distinction matters for market integrity.

The Mango incident demonstrated how an actor could manipulate an underlying reference value and use that distortion to extract assets from a financial system.

Ultramint approaches the related risk from two directions. 
Its listing rules reject market structures that are inherently self-referential or directly manipulable, while its participant rules prohibit attempts to profit from outcomes a participant can influence.

Neither rule eliminates every form of manipulation. 
But together, they establish an important boundary between predicting an event and engineering the event to win a position.

A prediction market should measure uncertainty about the world, not reward someone for being able to manufacture the answer.

text:
Not Being Greedy Is My Treasure

"I treat not being greedy as my treasure."

This story is about 2,500 years old, and it's only a few lines long.

Source
It's from the Zuo Zhuan, under the fifteenth year of Duke Xiang of Lu. That's 558 BCE, in the state of Song. Zihan was Song's Minister of Works, one of the men who actually ran the state.

The story
A man in Song came across a piece of jade and brought it to Zihan as a gift. Zihan said no.

The man pushed back. "I showed it to a jade expert, and he said it's a real treasure. That's why I dared to offer it to you." In other words: don't worry, it's worth it.

Zihan's answer is the line Chinese readers still quote, 我以不贪为宝 (wǒ yǐ bù tān wéi bǎo): "You treat jade as your treasure. I treat not being greedy as mine. If you give it to me, we both lose our treasure. Better for each of us to keep our own."

He talks about honesty as something he owns and could lose, not as a rule he recites.

Then the man bowed his head to the ground and told him the truth. "I'm just a nobody carrying a precious jade. I can't even make it past my own village safely. I'm giving it to you so I can stay alive."

So this wasn't really a bribe. Holding on to the jade had become dangerous for him.

Zihan turned the jade down, but the story doesn't end there. He let the man stay in his own neighborhood and had a jade worker cut and polish the stone for him. Only after the man had become well off did he send him home.

The moral
Saying out loud what you value only counts if you still hold to it when real jade is on the table. But the second half is the part that stays with me. Zihan didn't stop at "I won't take it." He also worked out what would happen to the man once he'd said no.

A short comment
A ranking of values only binds you if you make it public. Zihan's refusal protected his own treasure, his integrity. What he did next protected the other man's life.

text:
It’s not just a golf course, NOW. It’s a public park for walking, running, swimming, fishing, biking, tennis, mini-golf, playgrounds, birding, sightseeing, festivals, picnics...

East Potomac Park covers approximately 327 to 330 acres on a man-made peninsula in Washington, D.C. East Potomac Park and Hains Point

Total Park Size: Roughly 327 to 330 acres (though some historical or broader regional sources cite up to 400 acres).

Hains Point: A 15-acre open green space at the southern tip of the park, where the Potomac and Anacostia rivers meet.

Golf Course Area: The East Potomac Golf Links occupies about 210 acres of the park.

Recreational Space: Nearly 275 acres are dedicated to general recreation, including walking/bike paths, a swimming pool, and tennis courts. Walking and biking loops around Hains Point

East Potomac Park and Hains Point offer golf, cycling, running, tennis, picnicking, swimming, fishing, and seasonal cherry blossom viewing, though the National Park Service does not publish exact weekend headcounts for the peninsula alone.

Things to Do and Enjoy 
Golf and Driving Range: The East Potomac Golf Links features 36 holes across three public courses (the 18-hole Blue Course and two 9-hole courses), plus a 100-stall Toptracer driving range. 

Historic Miniature Golf: Built in 1931, the Mini Golf Course at East Potomac Golf Links is the oldest continuously operating miniature golf course in the United States, featuring 18 D.C.-themed holes. 

Biking, Running, and Skating: A flat, paved perimeter loop along Ohio Drive (roughly 3 to 4.4 miles depending on the route) hugs the waterfront and is heavily used by cyclists, runners, walkers, and inline skaters.

Waterfront Picnicking and Playgrounds: At the southern tip, the Point Picnic Area offers four reservable group picnic groves, grassy lawns, playgrounds, and panoramic views where the Potomac River, Anacostia River, and Washington Channel meet. 

Tennis and Swimming: The northern end of the park houses the East Potomac Tennis Center, which offers 24 indoor and outdoor public courts, alongside an outdoor Olympic-size swimming pool open seasonally in the summer. 

Fishing, Birding, and Sightseeing: Visitors frequently fish off the seawalls, watch planes land at nearby Reagan National Airport, ride the seasonal Wharf Jitney ferry across the Washington Channel, and walk beneath thousands of blooming cherry trees each spring. 

Typical Weekend Crowd Levels: On standard weekends, the park draws steady crowds of thousands of local golfers, cyclists, runners, and picnicking families, peaking on Saturday afternoons. During major annual events—such as the National Cherry Blossom Festival in spring, the Credit Union Cherry Blossom Ten Mile Run, and the Marine Corps Marathon weekend attendance surges into the tens of thousands. 

Important Access Notice: Access to the park is currently subject to major disruption, as the National Park Service issued a directive to close all parkland and facilities south of Buckeye Drive—including Hains Point, the perimeter loop, and the golf courses—starting November 15, 2026, amid an active federal court battle over a proposed championship golf redevelopment.

The Joyful Mysteries of the Rosary: Monday November 16, 2026

A door stands open in a small house. Ordinary tasks wait on the table. Then a word arrives that the world cannot measure. God asks for room in a human life. Will we make space, or keep the door half shut?

The Annunciation opens the Joyful Mysteries. Mary hears, believes, and consents. The Word takes flesh in her womb. That same Child stirs Elizabeth's house to joy. He is born in poverty. He is offered in the Temple. He is found doing his Father's work. This is not a mood. This is God with us. We place our crowded hours, our hidden fears, and the people we carry into these mysteries. We ask for a yes that trusts God more than our plans. Pray the Joyful Mysteries with us today. Let each bead make room for the Lord who already seeks a home in us.

I pray for you today 🙏 @RCatholicPrayer

text:
Psalm 5
 A morning prayer asking for help Those who welcome the Word as the guest of their hearts will have abiding joy.

To my words give ear, O Lord, give heed to my groaning. Attend to the sound of my cries, my King and my God.

It is you whom I invoke, O Lord. In the morning you hear me; in the morning I offer you my prayer, watching and waiting.

You are no God who loves evil; no sinner is your guest. The boastful shall not stand their ground before your face.

You hate all who do evil: you destroy all who lie. The deceitful and bloodthirsty man the Lord detests.

But I through the greatness of your love have access to your house. I bow down before your holy temple, filled with awe.

Lead me, Lord, in your justice, because of those who lie in wait; make clear your way before me.

No truth can be found in their mouths, their heart is all mischief, their throat a wide-open grave, all honey their speech.

All those you protect shall be glad and ring out their joy. You shelter them; in you they rejoice, those who love your name.

It is you who bless the just man, Lord: you surround him with favor as with a shield.

Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit: — as it was in the beginning, is now, and will be for ever. Amen.

text:
Revelation 17:9 An exhortation preparing unto audience, by the same argument, with that of Christ: He that hath ears to hear, let him hear. Wherefore, for mine own part, I had rather read in this place, Let there be here a mind, etc. So the Angel passeth fully unto the second place of this description.
Revelation 17:9 Very children know what that seven hilled city is, which is so much spoken of, and whereof Virgil thus reporteth, And compasseth seven towers in one wall: that city it is, which when John wrote these things had rule over the kings of the earth: It was and is not, and yet it remaineth this day, but it is declining to destruction.
Revelation 17:9 This is the painting out of the beast by things present (as I said before) whereby S. John endeavored to describe the same, that he might both be known of the godly in that age, and be further observed and marked of posterity afterwards. This delineation hath one type, that is, his heads, but a double description or application of the type: one permanent from the nature of itself, the other changeable, by the working of men. The description permanent, is by the seven hills, in this verse, the other that fleeteth, is from the seven kings, verses 10, 11. And here it is worthy to be observed, that one type hath sometimes two or more applications, as seemeth good unto the holy Ghost to express either one thing by divers types, or divers things by one type. So I noted before, of the seven spirits, Rev. 1:4. Now this woman that sitteth upon seven hills, is the city of Rome, called in times past of the Greeks, … i. of seven tops or crests, and of Varro, septiceps, i. of her seven heads (as here) of seven heads, and of others, septicollis, i. standing upon seven hills.
Revelation 17:9 The beginning of these Kings or Emperors is almost the same with the beginning of the Church of Christ, which I showed before, Rev. 11:1. Namely from the year 35, after the passion of Christ, what time the Temple and Church of the Jews was overthrown. In which year it came to pass by the providence of God that that saying The beast was and is not, was fulfilled before that the destruction of the Jews immediately following came to pass. That was the year from the building of the city of Rome, 109, from which year S. John both numbered the Emperors which hitherto hath been, when he wrote these things, and foretelleth two others next to come: and that with this purpose, that when this particular prediction of foretelling of things to come, should take effect the truth of all other predictions in the Church might be the more confirmed. Which sign God of old mentioned this in the Law, Deut. 18, and Jeremiah confirmeth, Jer. 28:8.
Revelation 17:10 Whose names are these: the first, Servius Sulpicius Galba, who was the seventh Emperor of the people of Rome, the second Marcus Salvius Otho, the third Aulus Vitellius, the fourth, Titus Flavius Vespasianus, the fifth, Titus Vespasianus his son of his own name.
Revelation 17:10 Flavius Domitian son of the first Vespasian. For in the latter end of his days S. John wrote these things, as witnesseth Irenaus, Lib. 5 adversus hareses.
Revelation 17:10 Nerua. The Empire being now translated from the family of Flavius. This man reigned only one year, four months, and nine days, as the history writers do tell.
Revelation 17:11 This is spoken by the figure synecdoche, as much to say as that head of the beast which was and is not, because it is cut off, and Nerua in so short time extinguished. How many heads there were, so many beasts there seemed to be in one. See the like speech in Rev. 13.3
Revelation 17:11 Nerua Traianus, who himself in divers respects is called here the seventh and the eighth.
Revelation 17:11 Though in number and order of succession he be the eighth, yet he is reckoned together with one of these heads, because Nerua and he were one head. For this man obtained authority together with Nerua, and was Consul with him, when Nerua left his life.
Revelation 17:11 Namely, to molest with persecutions the Churches of Christ, as the histories do accord, and I have briefly noted, Rev. 2:10.
Revelation 17:12 The third place of this description as I said, verse 18, is a prophetical prediction of things to come which the beast should do, as in the words following S. John doth not obscurely signify, saying, which have not yet received the kingdom, etc. For there is an Antithesis or opposition between these kings, and those that went before. And first the persons are described, in this verse, then their deeds in the two verses following.
Revelation 17:12 That is, arising with their kingdoms out of the Roman beast: at such time as that political Empire began by the craft of the Popes greatly to fall.
Revelation 17:12 Namely, with the second beast whom we called before a false prophet, which beast, ascending out of the earth got unto himself all the authority and power of the first beast, and exerciseth the same before his face, as was said, Rev. 14:11, 12. For when the political Empire of the West began to bow downwards, there both arose those ten kings, and the second beast took the opportunity offered to usurp unto himself all the power of the former beast. These kings long ago, many have numbered and described to be ten and a great part of the events plainly testifieth the same in this our age.
Revelation 17:13 That is, by consent and agreement, that they may conspire with the beast, and depend upon his beck. Their story is divided into three parts, counsels, acts, and events. The counselors some of them consist in communicating of judgments and affections: and some in communicating of power, which they are said to have given unto this beast in this verse.
Revelation 17:14 With Christ and his Church, as the reason following doth declare, and here are mentioned the facts and the events which followed for Christ’s sake, and for the grace of God the Father towards those that are called, elected, and are his faithful ones in Christ.
Revelation 17:15 This is the other member of the narration as I said verse 7, belonging unto the harlot, showed in the vision, verse 3. In this history of the harlot, these 3 things are distinctly propounded, what is her magnificence in this verse, what is her fall, and by whom it shall happen unto her, in the two verses following: and lastly, who that harlot is, in the last verse. This place which by order of nature should have been the first, is therefore made the last, because it was more fit to be joined with the next Chap.
Revelation 17:15 That is, as unconstant and variable as the waters. Upon this foundation sitteth this harlot as Queen, a vain person upon that which is vain.
Revelation 17:16 The ten Kings as verse 12. The accomplishment of this fact and event, is daily increased in this our age by the singular providence and most mighty government of God. Wherefore the facts are propounded in this verse, and the cause of them in the verses following.
Revelation 17:17 A reason rendered from the chief efficient cause, which is the providence of God, by which alone S. John by inversion of order affirmeth to have come to pass, both that the Kings should execute upon the harlot, that which pleased God, and which he declared in the verse next beforegoing: and also that by one consent and counsel, they should give their kingdom unto the beast, etc., verses 13, 14. For as these being blinded have before depended upon the beck of the beast that lifteth up the harlot, so it is said that afterward it shall come to pass, that they shall turn back, and shall fall away from her when their hearts shall be turned into better state by the grace and mercy of God.
Revelation 17:18 That is, Rome that great City, or only City (as Justinian calleth it) the King and head whereof was then the Emperor, but now the Pope, since that the condition of the beast was changed.

Apostle and Evangelist Matthew
Commemorated on November 16
The Holy Apostle and Evangelist Matthew, was also named Levi (Mark 2:14; Luke 5:27); he was one of the Twelve Apostles (Mark 3:18; Luke 6:45; Acts 1:13), and was brother of the Apostle James Alphaeus (Mark 2:14). He was a publican, or tax-collector for Rome, in a time when the Jews were under the rule of the Roman Empire. He lived in the Galilean city of Capernaum. When Matthew heard the voice of Jesus Christ: “Come, follow Me” (Mt. 9:9), he left everything and followed the Savior. Christ and His disciples did not refuse Matthew’s invitation and they visited his house, where they shared table with the publican’s friends and acquaintances. Like the host, they were also publicans and known sinners. This event disturbed the pharisees and scribes a great deal.

Publicans who collected taxes from their countrymen did this with great profit for themselves. Usually greedy and cruel people, the Jews considered them pernicious betrayers of their country and religion. The word “publican” for the Jews had the connotation of “public sinner” and “idol-worshipper.” To even speak with a tax-collector was considered a sin, and to associate with one was defilement. But the Jewish teachers were not able to comprehend that the Lord had “come to call not the righteous, but sinners to repentance” (Mt. 9:13).

Matthew, acknowledging his sinfulness, repaid fourfold anyone he had cheated, and he distributed his remaining possessions to the poor, and he followed after Christ with the other apostles. Saint Matthew was attentive to the instructions of the Divine Teacher, he beheld His innumerable miracles, he went together with the Twelve Apostles preaching to “the lost sheep of the house of Israel” (Mt. 10:6). He was a witness to the suffering, death, and Resurrection of the Savior, and of His glorious Ascension into Heaven.

Having received the grace of the Holy Spirit, which descended upon the Apostles on the day of Pentecost, Saint Matthew preached in Palestine for several years. At the request of the Jewish converts at Jerusalem, the holy Apostle Matthew wrote his Gospel describing the earthly life of the Savior, before leaving to preach the Gospel in faraway lands.

In the order of the books of the New Testament, the Gospel of Matthew comes first. Palestine is said to be the place where the Gospel was written. Saint Matthew wrote in Aramaic, and then it was translated into Greek. The Aramaic text has not survived, but many of the linguistic and cultural-historical peculiarities of the Greek translation give indications of it.

The Apostle Matthew preached among people who were awaiting the Messiah. His Gospel manifests itself as a vivid proof that Jesus Christ is the Messiah foretold by the prophets, and that there would not be another (Mt. 11:3).

The preaching and deeds of the Savior are presented by the evangelist in three divisions, constituting three aspects of the service of the Messiah: as Prophet and Law-Giver (Ch. 5-7), Lord over the world both visible and invisible (Ch. 8-25), and finally as High Priest offered as Sacrifice for the sins of all mankind (Ch. 26-27).

The theological content of the Gospel, besides the Christological themes, includes also the teaching about the Kingdom of God and about the Church, which the Lord sets forth in parables about the inner preparation for entering into the Kingdom (Ch. 5-7), about the worthiness of servers of the Church in the world (Ch. 10-11), about the signs of the Kingdom and its growth in the souls of mankind (Ch. 13), about the humility and simplicity of the inheritors of the Kingdom (Mt. 18:1-35; 19 13-30; 20:1-16; 25-27; 23:1-28), and about the eschatological revelations of the Kingdom in the Second Coming of Christ within the daily spiritual life of the Church (Ch. 24-25).

The Kingdom of Heaven and the Church are closely interconnected in the spiritual experience of Christianity: the Church is the historical embodiment of the Kingdom of Heaven in the world, and the Kingdom of Heaven is the Church of Christ in its eschatological perfection (Mt. 16:18-19; 28:18-20).

The holy Apostle brought the Gospel of Christ to Syria, Media, Persia, Parthia, and finishing his preaching in Ethiopia with a martyr’s death. This land was inhabited by tribes of cannibals with primitive customs and beliefs. The holy Apostle Matthew converted some of the idol-worshippers to faith in Christ. He founded the Church and built a temple in the city of Mirmena, establishing there his companion Platon as bishop.

When the holy apostle was fervently entreating God for the conversion of the Ethiopians the Lord Himself appeared to him in the form of a youth. He gave him a staff, and commanded him to plant it at the doors of the church. The Lord said that a tree would grow from this staff and it would bear fruit, and from its roots would flow a stream of water. When the Ethiopians washed themselves in the water and ate the fruit, they lost their wild ways and became gentle and good.

When the holy apostle carried the staff towards the church, he was met by the wife and son of the ruler of the land, Fulvian, who were afflicted by unclean spirits. In the Name of Christ the holy apostle healed them. This miracle converted a number of the pagans to the Lord. But the ruler did not want his subjects to become Christians and cease worshiping the pagan gods. He accused the apostle of sorcery and gave orders to execute him.

They put Saint Matthew head downwards, piled up brushwood and ignited it. When the fire flared up, everyone then saw that the fire did not harm Saint Matthew. Then Fulvian gave orders to add more wood to the fire, and frenzied with boldness, he commanded to set up twelve idols around the fire. But the flames melted the idols and flared up toward Fulvian. The frightened Ethiopian turned to the saint with an entreaty for mercy, and by the prayer of the martyr the flame went out. The body of the holy apostle remained unharmed, and he departed to the Lord.

The ruler Fulvian deeply repented of his deed, but still he had doubts. By his command, they put the body of Saint Matthew into an iron coffin and threw it into the sea. In doing this Fulvian said that if the God of Matthew would preserve the body of the apostle in the water as He preserved him in the fire, then this would be proper reason to worship this One True God.

That night the Apostle Matthew appeared to Bishop Platon in a dream, and commanded him to go with clergy to the shore of the sea and to find his body there. The righteous Fulvian and his retinue went with the bishop to the shore of the sea. The coffin carried by the waves was taken to the church built by the apostle. Then Fulvian begged forgiveness of the holy Apostle Matthew, after which Bishop Platon baptized him, giving him the name Matthew in obedience to a command of God.

Soon Saint Fulvian-Matthew abdicated his rule and became a presbyter. Upon the death of Bishop Platon, the Apostle Matthew appeared to him and exhorted him to head the Ethiopian Church. Having become a bishop, Saint Fulvian-Matthew toiled at preaching the Word of God, continuing the work of his heavenly patron.

not any more    Europe has lifted far less tonnage to orbit than the US (driven overwhelmingly by SpaceX), and also trails China and Russia in recent years.⁠Elontimes

Recent years (payload mass to orbit)
Sources include Flight Atlas (drawing on Jonathan McDowell’s GCAT catalog) and Elon Times aggregations:

YearWorld totalUS (mostly SpaceX)ChinaRussiaEurope (Ariane + Vega etc.)2025~2,877–3,194 t~2,430 t (SpaceX ~2,330 t / ~81%)~313–328 t~64 t~15 t2026 YTD (mid-Nov)~2,300 tSpaceX ~1,876 t (~81%)~224 t~71 tPart of the ~72 t “rest of world”
In 2025, Europe’s contribution (ArianeGroup + Avio/Vega) was only about 15 tonnes—roughly 0.5% of the global total. SpaceX alone put up more than 150× that.⁠Flightatlas
All-time cumulative (Flight Atlas, by country of the launch vehicle, through late 2026)
United States: ~15,476 t

Russia + Soviet Union: ~12,598 t
China: ~2,213 t
France (almost entirely the European Ariane program): ~1,532 t
Italy (mainly Vega): ~32 t
Japan ~421 t, India ~135 t
Europe total is roughly 1,560+ tonnes all-time. That is respectable historically (especially for a multi-nation program focused on reliable GEO commercial launches) but a small fraction of the US or Russia/USSR totals, and China has already surpassed it in cumulative mass.⁠Flightatlas
Context
Europe has solid capability: Ariane 5 was a successful commercial workhorse for decades; Ariane 6 offers ~10–22 t to LEO (depending on configuration) with high reliability. Vega serves smaller payloads. Institutional programs (Galileo, science missions, etc.) continue.

The modern gap is driven by cadence and reusability, not single-rocket performance. Falcon 9 routinely flies 100+ times per year carrying ~15 t-class payloads (especially Starlink). Europe does a handful of launches annually. Starlink alone has accounted for the large majority of global mass to orbit in recent years.
Historical European launches were often high-value GEO satellites (lower mass per flight) or institutional missions rather than mass-market LEO constellations.
In short: Europe remains a capable space power with proven rockets and infrastructure, but it is not competitive in tonnage delivered with the US (SpaceX) or even China in the current era. The difference is orders of magnitude in recent years.

1. Broadcom ($AVGO)

Custom AI chips (ASICs) and high-speed networking chips. One of the most direct ways to benefit from AI data center spending beyond Nvidia.

The world's leading advanced-chip foundry. Many of the world's most important AI chips, including those designed by Nvidia, AMD, and Apple, are manufactured by TSMC. One of the strongest picks-and-shovels plays in the AI supply chain.

3. Rocket Lab ($RKLB)

Small-launch rockets, satellite manufacturing, and space systems. One of the few publicly traded pure-play space companies with meaningful revenue and a growing backlog. It offers exposure to an emerging commercial space supply chain.

4. Palantir ($PLTR)

Enterprise AI software platform. Already bringing AI into real-world government and large-enterprise operations. One of the more commercially established players in the AI application layer.

5. Micron Technology ($MU)

A key supplier of high-bandwidth memory (HBM). The AI boom is driving surging demand for advanced memory, making Micron a critical player in the AI hardware supply chain.
