✒️ PUDD’NHEAD WILSON HAS THE LAST WORD — Mark Twain gets the final say.

────────────── ❧ ────────────────

📜 EPIGRAPH

“Truth is stranger than fiction, but it is because Fiction is obliged to stick to possibilities; Truth isn’t.” — Mark Twain, Following the Equator (1897). ☄️

────────────── ❧ ────────────────

🎬 INTRO

November 16 has assembled a collection of events so thoroughly deranged that even a seasoned storyteller might ask for a rewrite—or simply close the book and go lie down.

A conqueror invites an emperor to a meeting that immediately turns into a catastrophe, then learns the captive ruler is willing to empty a room of treasure for the chance to walk away, as if the entire episode were some sort of expensive misunderstanding. A novelist receives a death sentence, faces a firing squad, and is spared at the very last moment—an experience that qualifies as research only if one has an unusually flexible definition of the term. A radio telescope sends a carefully encoded message toward the stars, essentially mailing a postcard to a destination where the delivery time makes ordinary impatience look almost reasonable.

Elsewhere, a man goes looking for a lost hammer and instead finds an ancient fortune buried in a European field, because the universe apparently prefers punchlines to logic. And just when the day seems to have exhausted its supply of improbable developments, a beloved snack cake becomes the focus of a nationwide buying frenzy, as if the continued existence of cream-filled sponge were suddenly a matter of public order.

Five strange events, one remarkable novelist, and a date that clearly refuses to behave itself.

Cue the chaos. Let's roll. 💥

────────────── ❧ ────────────────

❓ HISTORY QUIZ OF THE DAY

On November 16, 1992, Eric Lawes was searching a field in Suffolk, England, for something his friend had misplaced.

What did he discover instead?

[A] A buried Viking ship.

[B] A medieval royal crown.

[C] A vast hoard of Roman treasure.

[D] A forgotten military bunker.

👇 (Answer at the end of the issue.)

────────────── ❧ ────────────────

⭐️ MAIN EVENTS

👑 1532 — THE EMPEROR, THE CONQUISTADOR & THE ROOMFUL OF GOLD

November 16, 1532 | Cajamarca, Inca Empire (present-day Peru)

Francisco Pizarro had fewer than 200 Spanish soldiers. In front of him stood the ruler of the Inca Empire, Atahualpa, accompanied by thousands of followers.

The odds seemed absurdly unequal—but Pizarro had no intention of fighting a conventional battle.

Atahualpa had recently emerged victorious from a civil war against his half-brother Huáscar. Pizarro, who had arrived in the region with Spanish authorization to explore and conquer, recognized the political divisions that had weakened the empire. He invited Atahualpa to meet him at Cajamarca, presenting the encounter as a diplomatic gathering.

On the evening of November 16, Atahualpa entered the town's square in a magnificent litter, accompanied by a large, largely unarmed entourage. Pizarro's men were concealed in buildings around the plaza. A Spanish friar, Vicente de Valverde, approached the emperor and demanded that he accept Christianity and the authority of the Spanish Crown.

Atahualpa refused.

The Spanish then launched a sudden attack. Gunfire, cavalry, and steel weapons turned the crowded square into a massacre. Atahualpa was seized, and the capture of the emperor gave Pizarro extraordinary leverage over the empire.

The captive ruler soon realized what interested his captors most: gold. He offered to fill a room with gold and two rooms with silver in exchange for his freedom. The ransom was collected, but the treasure did not save him. Pizarro's forces eventually executed Atahualpa in 1533.

The capture at Cajamarca became a decisive turning point in the Spanish conquest of the Inca Empire.

🧩 TRIVIA: Pizarro's force was astonishingly small compared with the thousands accompanying Atahualpa. The Spanish advantage came not simply from weapons and horses, but from surprise, the confined setting, and the political divisions already weakening the Inca state.

🏴‍☠️ HUBRIS: Atahualpa entered the meeting as the most powerful ruler in the region. Within hours, he was a prisoner bargaining for his life—and the men holding him had discovered that an emperor could be turned into a ransom account.

🎯 TAKEAWAY: Power can be immense and still be vulnerable when an enemy understands where it is concentrated.

────────────── ❧ ────────────────

⚖️ 1849 — DOSTOEVSKY’S DATE WITH THE FIRING SQUAD

November 16, 1849 | St. Petersburg, Russian Empire

Fyodor Dostoevsky was a young writer whose literary career was just beginning when his involvement with a group of politically outspoken intellectuals brought him into conflict with the Russian authorities.
The group, known as the Petrashevsky Circle, met to discuss literature, philosophy, and social reform. In the repressive political climate of Tsar Nicholas I's Russia, such conversations could be treated as a threat to the state.

Dostoevsky was arrested in April 1849. After months of imprisonment and interrogation, he was sentenced to death on November 16.

The sentence was not carried out immediately. On December 22, Dostoevsky and other condemned prisoners were taken to Semyonovsky Square. They were dressed for execution, and the preparations for a firing squad began. Some prisoners were already tied to posts when a messenger arrived with news that the Tsar had commuted their sentences.

The reprieve had been arranged in advance. The prisoners, however, had not been told. They were made to experience the apparent certainty of imminent death before learning that they would live.

Dostoevsky's sentence was replaced with four years of hard labor in Siberia, followed by compulsory military service. The ordeal profoundly affected him. His later writing would explore guilt, suffering, faith, freedom, and the darkest corners of the human mind with an intensity few novelists have matched.

🧩 TRIVIA: Dostoevsky later described the staged execution as an experience that made him acutely conscious of the value of every remaining minute. In a letter to his brother, written on the day of the execution ceremony, he reflected on how precious life seemed when he believed he had almost none left.

🕵️ MYSTERY: The reprieve was not a last-second act of mercy. The decision had already been made, but the prisoners were deliberately kept unaware until the execution ceremony was underway. The reason for subjecting them to that psychological ordeal remains a disturbing feature of the episode.

🎯 TAKEAWAY: A reprieve can save a life. It cannot necessarily erase what a person has been made to endure.

────────────── ❧ ────────────────

📡 1974 — EARTH SENDS A MESSAGE TO THE STARS

November 16, 1974 | Arecibo Observatory, Puerto Rico

Humanity has spent a long time wondering whether anyone else is out there. On this day, scientists decided to send a message.

From the enormous radio telescope at Arecibo, Puerto Rico, researchers transmitted a carefully constructed sequence of radio pulses toward the globular star cluster Messier 13, approximately 25,000 light-years away.
The message contained 1,679 binary digits. When arranged in the correct pattern, they formed a graphic representation of basic information about Earth and its inhabitants: numbers, important chemical elements, components of DNA, the DNA double helix, a human figure, the solar system, and the Arecibo telescope itself.

The project was associated with astronomers Frank Drake and Carl Sagan, among other scientists. It was transmitted during a ceremony marking a major upgrade to the observatory.

The message was not an expectation of an imminent reply. Even if an intelligent civilization in M13 received it immediately and responded without delay, the round trip would take roughly 50,000 years.

🧩 TRIVIA: The 1,679 bits can be arranged into a rectangle measuring 23 by 73. Both numbers are prime, a mathematical choice intended to help a hypothetical recipient recognize the correct arrangement of the message.

🔮 PROLEPTIC: The message attempted to communicate with an intelligence that might have no shared language, history, or culture with humanity. Its designers relied on mathematics, chemistry, and biology as possible common ground—an introduction built for a conversation that might not begin for millennia.

🎯 TAKEAWAY: Sometimes the most extraordinary message is not the one that gets an answer, but the one that proves we were willing to ask the question.

────────────── ❧ ────────────────

🏺 1992 — THE LOST HAMMER AND BRITAIN’S ROMAN FORTUNE

November 16, 1992 | Hoxne, Suffolk, England

Eric Lawes went into a field near the village of Hoxne with a metal detector. He was looking for a hammer that his friend, tenant farmer Peter Whatling, had lost.

He found something considerably more valuable.

The detector signaled underground, and Lawes began uncovering Roman coins and precious objects. Rather than dig everything out himself, he stopped and reported the discovery. The following day, archaeologists from the Suffolk Archaeological Unit, directed by Judith Plouviez, carried out a controlled excavation of the remaining deposit.

The find became known as the Hoxne Hoard, the richest treasure discovery from Roman Britain. The recovered collection contained 14,865 coins, along with approximately 200 pieces of jewelry and silver tableware. It included gold bracelets, necklaces, a remarkable body chain, silver spoons, ladles, and ornate pepper pots.

And the hammer? It had brought Lawes to the field in the first place. The treasure was the unexpected bonus.

🧩 TRIVIA: One of the silver pepper pots takes the form of a richly dressed woman. A rotating disc in its base could be turned to close the container, open larger holes for filling it, or reveal tiny holes for sprinkling pepper. Even Roman luxury dining came with adjustable settings.

🐶 SPOT: Lawes' decision to stop digging and report the find was crucial. The controlled excavation the next day allowed archaeologists to recover the remaining objects while preserving valuable information about how the hoard had been buried.

🌀 OBSCURE: A gold bracelet from the hoard carries the inscription “UTERE FELIX DOMINA IULIANE,” meaning roughly, “Use this happily, Lady Juliane.” The message suggests a personal gift to a woman named Juliane, but her identity—and the identity of the person who gave her the bracelet—remain unknown.

🎯 TAKEAWAY: A lost hammer led to a buried fortune. But the real value of the discovery came from recognizing that the objects were more than treasure: they were evidence.

────────────── ❧ ────────────────

🧁 2012 — THE GREAT TWINKIE PANIC

November 16, 2012 | United States

For generations, Twinkies had been a familiar fixture of American lunchboxes, convenience stores, and late-night snack cravings. Then, on November 16, 2012, their future suddenly looked uncertain.

Hostess Brands announced that it was winding down operations after a nationwide labor strike crippled production and distribution. The company said it would seek permission from bankruptcy court to close its business and sell its assets. Approximately 18,500 jobs were at stake.

The announcement triggered a remarkable consumer reaction. Customers rushed to stores to buy Twinkies and other Hostess products before supplies disappeared. Some shelves emptied quickly. People bought boxes by the armful, while online sellers began offering the familiar snack cakes at wildly inflated prices.

The answer, eventually, was yes. Hostess brands and assets were acquired, and Twinkies returned to store shelves in 2013.

The panic had been real. The disappearance was temporary.

🧩 TRIVIA: Hostess said the shutdown put approximately 18,500 employees at risk. The company’s announcement also covered a long list of familiar brands, including Ding Dongs, Ho Hos, Sno Balls, Donettes, and Wonder Bread.

⚠️ IRONY: A company facing a major labor dispute and financial collapse became the subject of a consumer frenzy focused largely on snack cakes. The threatened loss of thousands of jobs was serious; the public's most visible reaction was a race to stock up on Twinkies.

🎯 TAKEAWAY: Scarcity can transform an everyday product into an object of sudden obsession. Sometimes the panic begins before the shelves are even empty.

────────────── ❧ ────────────────

🎙️ HARVEY’S CORNER

📚 CHINUA ACHEBE — THE MAN WHO GAVE A NATION BACK ITS VOICE

Good day, everybody.

Imagine growing up in a place where the stories told about your people were written largely by people who had never lived among them. Your history was described through someone else's eyes. Your traditions were misunderstood, your culture reduced to stereotypes, and your people too often appeared as supporting characters in a story about somebody else's greatness.

Now imagine deciding to do something about it.

That was part of the journey of Chinua Achebe, born November 16, 1930, in Ogidi, in southeastern Nigeria.

Achebe grew up in an Igbo household where traditional beliefs and customs existed alongside the Christian faith embraced by his parents. He was exposed to both worlds from an early age. That experience gave him an unusual perspective: he could understand the attractions and contradictions of each without pretending that either was simple.

He was an exceptionally thoughtful young man, drawn to books, language, and the power of stories. He attended University College, Ibadan, where his studies and growing interest in African history and literature helped shape the direction of his life. After graduating, he joined the Nigerian Broadcasting Corporation.

But Achebe had something larger in mind than a career in broadcasting.

He wanted to write about Africa from the inside.

In 1958, he published a novel that would become one of the most influential works in modern African literature: Things Fall Apart.

Its central character, Okonkwo, is a respected and fiercely determined man in an Igbo community. He has built his life around strength, reputation, and the traditions of his society. But the arrival of Christian missionaries and British colonial authority begins to transform the world he knows. The resulting conflict is not simply between Africans and Europeans. It unfolds within families, friendships, religious beliefs, and the community itself.

Achebe did something remarkable. He allowed readers to see this society before colonial rule through the lives of the people who inhabited it. They had laws, ceremonies, arguments, ambitions, humor, wisdom, rivalries, and deeply held beliefs. They were not waiting for Europeans to arrive and give their lives meaning.

That may sound obvious today. It was not how much of the English-language literary world had portrayed Africa.

Achebe did not write a simplistic defense of his culture, either. He showed its strengths and its flaws. Okonkwo himself is a complicated, sometimes destructive man. The novel's power comes from its refusal to turn human beings into convenient symbols.

Things Fall Apart became an international success, was translated into dozens of languages, and eventually became one of the most widely read African novels in the world. It helped change the way generations of readers understood African history and literature.

But Achebe's commitment to telling African stories did not end with fiction.

In 1962, he became the founding editor of Heinemann's African Writers Series, helping bring the work of other African authors to readers around the world. He understood that one voice, however influential, could never represent an entire continent. Other writers needed the opportunity to tell their own stories, too.

Then history placed his convictions under a different kind of pressure.

In 1967, Nigeria descended into civil war after the southeastern region declared itself the independent Republic of Biafra. Achebe supported Biafra and served as a diplomatic representative, traveling abroad to draw attention to the conflict and the humanitarian crisis.

He was no longer simply writing about the consequences of political decisions. He was living through them.

The war ended in 1970 with Biafra's defeat. The suffering, displacement, and loss left a lasting mark on Achebe. His later essays and political writing reflected his belief that writers could not always remain comfortably detached from the societies in which they lived.

Then, in 1990, another devastating event changed his life.

While traveling in Nigeria, Achebe was involved in a serious automobile accident that left him paralyzed from the waist down. He was flown to England for medical treatment and later continued his academic career in the United States.

For a man whose life had been devoted to writing, teaching, and public engagement, the physical consequences were enormous. Yet he continued to work, publish, teach, and speak. He held academic positions at Bard College and Brown University, influencing students and readers far beyond Nigeria.

His books continued to reach new generations. Among his other important works were No Longer at Ease, Arrow of God, A Man of the People, and Anthills of the Savannah.

Achebe died in Boston on March 21, 2013, at the age of eighty-two.

But consider what remained.

A boy from Ogidi had grown up to challenge the way an entire literary tradition portrayed his continent. A novelist had opened doors for countless other writers. A public intellectual had insisted that literature could not be separated entirely from questions of power, identity, and responsibility.

Achebe did not give Africa a voice. Africa had always had voices. What he did was help make the world listen—and make it harder for the world to pretend it had never heard them.

And now, you know the rest of the story.

⚖️ CLOSING

Look at the lives behind today's stories. Atahualpa tried to buy his freedom with a fortune in gold, only to discover that his captors wanted the treasure more than they wanted to honor their bargain. Dostoevsky was forced to face his own execution before being granted a reprieve. The scientists at Arecibo sent a message into a universe that might never answer. Eric Lawes found a fortune while searching for a lost hammer. And Chinua Achebe spent his life challenging the world's assumptions about Africa and the people who called it home.

Their stories remind us that history is shaped by more than kings and conquerors. It is shaped by people who endure, discover, question, create, and sometimes change the way generations after them see the world.

Pizarro's conquest, Dostoevsky's survival, Lawes's discovery, and Achebe's literary legacy all left marks that outlasted the moments themselves. Even that message from Arecibo continues its journey into the unknown.

And then there were the Twinkies. Some legacies are simply harder to explain than others. 🤭

Maddow Touts ‘Second Largest Voter Turnout In A Century’; Clinton Says ‘Blue Wave’ Washed Away ‘Poisonous Cloud’ Of The Last 10 Years

At an event in NYC promoting Rachel Maddow’s new book about the Department of Justice, Hillary Clinton interviewed the MS NOW host as the two celebrated Democratic election victories. Maddow praised turnout and attacked President Trump, while Clinton declared that a “blue wave” had washed away a decade-long “poisonous cloud.”

They had plenty to say about threats to democracy and government corruption. In this exchange, they offered no examination of election-security concerns.

Maddow said:

“Um, I, you know, this was the second largest voter turnout in a century. Um. And the increase in voter turnout among Black voters and Latino voters and young voters was like nothing we have seen cycle to cycle ever. Um. And that is incredibly moving to me.

“And yes, it has consequences in terms of who they voted for and it is a profound statement, uh, in terms of just how blue that wave was. But the participation levels, um, were really moving to me in part because I, I really am one of those liberals who thinks that we are up against an existential challenge to our constitutional republic.

“I think there is an authoritarian movement that has the president of the United States at its head. And I think he does not want us to be protected by our Constitution anymore. And I think he wants to rule as a strongman indefinitely. I just believe it and you may not, but that’s where I’m coming from.

“And part of the message of that kind of politics, that kind of leadership is that elections are frauds and elections don’t matter, and democracy is weak and it’s pointless and you’re a sucker if you participate in it. And the American people just gave that a one-finger salute.”

Clinton responded, “Yeah, exactly right.” Maddow then asked how she felt about Tuesday.

Clinton replied:

“Well, I, I feel, uh, it’s been a long time coming, um, but it’s as though the blue wave has washed away the poisonous cloud that we’ve been living under for 10 years and we can finally, uh, get back, uh, to trying our best to form that more perfect union by fighting back, number one, by voting.

“And now the Democrats, uh, have to make good things happen, uh, both in Washington and at the state level. Um. And I am, you know, I’ve said this before, I am like my late great friend Madeleine Albright once said, I’m an optimist who worries a lot.

“So I was optimistic about the outcome of the election. It exceeded even my, uh, high hopes, uh, for what would happen. And now I’m incredibly excited by this new crop of, uh, members of Congress and senators and governors and attorneys general and, and state legislators.

“They came in with the intention of fighting back and to try to right the ship of state. And one of the main issues, as we all know, was corruption.”

Maddow interjected, “Yes,” and Clinton continued:

“And so corruption became the issue where nine out of 10, 90% of voters said that government corruption was a major factor in their vote."

A map using U.S. Election Assistance Commission data shows 20,475,832 new voter registrations processed between the 2022 and 2024 elections in states without documentary proof-of-citizenship requirements. Those states did not require applicants to submit a birth certificate, passport, or naturalization papers to establish citizenship when registering. A signed declaration of citizenship was required; documentary proof was not. This is what Hillary Clinton and Rachel Maddow are celebrating and calling a Blue Wave.

The full report is available here:
2024 EAVS Comprehensive Report (PDF) @
https://t.co/2CrWycuk6E

Deceased voters remaining on registration lists, duplicate registrations, outdated addresses, and ineligible registrations are also a huge problem in Blue states. Election fraud takes many forms—ineligible registrations, non-citizens on the rolls, double voting, ballots cast in the names of the dead or those who have moved, and more. Maddow and Clinton ignore all of it while celebrating the results and lecturing about corruption.

If Clinton and Maddow want to talk about government corruption, they should demand that election fraud be investigated—even when Democrats win. Fraud that puts someone in office or keeps them there steals the public’s right to choose its leaders. Nothing is more corrupt—or more destructive to democracy—than putting people in power through fraud instead of the will of the voters.

THE EVIDENCE™ — SPORTS & POLITICAL SATIRE

BREAKING: FRESH OFF HIS RACE WITH MANUTE BOL, JOE BIDEN CHALLENGES USAIN BOLT TO A 100-YARD DASH

Former President Declares Himself the Fastest Man in Politics — Bolt Demands to Know Whether Golf Carts Are Permitted

By Kim Wojcinski | USA Best-Selling Author
SATIRE — FICTIONAL NEWS REPORT

The evidence will be presented. The verdict is yours.

WASHINGTON, D.C. — Apparently, one legendary athletic confrontation wasn't enough.

Fresh off his highly publicized 100-meter showdown with former NBA giant Manute Bol, Joe Biden has announced that he's ready for an even greater challenge: a 100-yard dash against Usain Bolt, the fastest man in recorded history.

The announcement has stunned the international athletic community, particularly those who believed Biden's encounter with the 7-foot-7 Bol would bring his sprinting career to a merciful conclusion.

Instead, Biden has declared that his performance against the towering basketball legend proved he belongs among the world's elite sprinters.

"Look, Jack, I went toe-to-toe with a guy who was almost eight feet tall. Eight feet! His legs were longer than my Corvette. And I was right there with him. Right there. Nobody's ever seen anything like it."

Reporters attending the announcement noted that Biden had apparently forgotten that Manute Bol died in 2010.

His campaign manager quickly clarified that the entire Bol competition had been part of an experimental, computer-assisted exhibition, although no one could explain why the former president had insisted on wearing actual running shoes.

That detail, however, did nothing to diminish Biden's enthusiasm.

"Manute was tall. This Bolt fella is fast. What's next? Somebody gonna bring me a guy who can fly? Come on, man!"

THE MANUTE BOL RACE: A LEGEND IS BORN

The fictional exhibition against Manute Bol had already established Biden as perhaps the most unconventional competitor in the history of track and field.

Bol, whose extraordinary height made him one of the tallest players in NBA history, was represented by an advanced digital simulation designed to reproduce his legendary stride length.

Biden's advisers had initially regarded the competition as a publicity opportunity.

The objective was simple: demonstrate that the former president possessed the physical endurance, competitive instincts, and raw determination necessary to complete a 100-meter race.

Unfortunately, the event encountered several unexpected complications.

First, Biden objected to the starting pistol, insisting that he had already started running before anyone fired it.

Second, approximately 30 yards into the race, he stopped to explain to a spectator that he had once played basketball against Wilt Chamberlain.

Third, at the halfway point, he attempted to shake hands with the digital representation of Bol, apparently unaware that his opponent was a hologram.

The race was eventually declared complete after Biden crossed the finish line on a moving sidewalk that had been installed for security purposes.

His advisers called the performance "an overwhelming demonstration of competitive resilience."

The official timing system recorded 4 minutes, 17 seconds.

Biden disputed the result.

"That's malarkey. I was moving like lightning. Everybody saw it. Ask Manute."

When informed once again that Bol had died years earlier, Biden reportedly responded:

"Well, that explains why he wasn't talking much."

ENTER USAIN BOLT

Usain Bolt, the eight-time Olympic gold medalist whose 9.58-second world record in the 100 meters remains one of the most extraordinary accomplishments in athletics, reportedly received Biden's challenge with considerable confusion.

"Wait," Bolt allegedly asked in this fictional account. "Didn't he just race Manute Bol?"

His representatives confirmed that Biden was indeed the same competitor.

Bolt reportedly reviewed video footage of the exhibition, watched Biden stop midway through the race to discuss his Corvette, and then asked one question:

"Is this supposed to be a sprint or a documentary?"

Nevertheless, the Jamaican legend agreed to consider the challenge, provided the event would be conducted under internationally recognized track-and-field rules.

Biden's representatives immediately rejected that condition.

"President Biden has never allowed himself to be constrained by arbitrary rules," one adviser explained. "His entire political career has been built around finding creative interpretations of existing procedures."

WHY 100 YARDS INSTEAD OF 100 METERS?

Perhaps the most controversial feature of the proposed competition is Biden's insistence that the race cover 100 yards rather than the Olympic-standard 100 meters.

One hundred meters equals approximately 109.36 yards.

Biden's camp maintains that eliminating those additional 9.36 yards will substantially improve his chances.

"Those last nine yards are brutal," explained one campaign strategist. "That's where fatigue, muscle exhaustion, and the need for lunch become serious competitive factors."

Sports scientists, however, point out that Bolt's maximum velocity makes the shorter distance even less favorable to a competitor requiring more than four minutes to complete the longer event.

Biden rejected their analysis.

"Listen, fat, I've been running for office since before this guy was born. I've run more races than anybody. Senate races. Presidential races. Primary races. And I won most of them."

A reporter asked whether running for political office involved physical sprinting.

Biden replied, "Depends how close the polls are."

THE BIDEN TRAINING CAMP

Following the Manute Bol exhibition, Biden's team reportedly hired an elite group of athletic consultants to prepare him for the Bolt showdown.

The training camp features a carefully structured regimen:

Morning stretching, provided someone remembers where the exercise mats were stored.

Speed drills involving walking briskly toward an ice cream truck.
Interval training consisting of 10 seconds of movement followed by 20 minutes of storytelling.
Resistance training using a lightweight briefcase containing several decades of Senate speeches.
Mental preparation through repeated viewings of Chariots of Fire.
The program suffered an early setback when Biden attempted a practice sprint and stopped after 15 yards to explain that he had once been a lifeguard.

"Everybody knows the story. Corn Pop. Tough guy. Bad dude. I handled him. And I'll handle this Bolt character the same way."

His coach reportedly pointed out that Bolt was considerably faster than Corn Pop.

Biden appeared unconcerned.

"Corn Pop didn't have eight Olympic gold medals either. But he had a chain."

THE SECRET SERVICE DEMANDS SPECIAL CONDITIONS

The United States Secret Service has allegedly submitted an extensive list of proposed safety measures for the event.

The most controversial involves allowing Biden to use a motorized mobility device should the physical demands of the race become excessive.

Bolt's representatives immediately objected.

"We agreed to a footrace," they reportedly stated. "Not a competition between an Olympic sprinter and a modified electric scooter."

Biden accused the Jamaican camp of trying to suppress American technological innovation.

"Look, Jack. You bring your shoes. I'll bring mine. If mine happen to have batteries, that's called progress."

Additional safety proposals reportedly include installing padded barriers along the track, removing all stairs from the vicinity, and requiring race officials to remain silent whenever Biden appears to be concentrating.

Most importantly, the Secret Service has insisted that the finish line be located directly in front of an ice cream stand.

Advisers believe that will provide the strongest possible incentive for sustained forward movement.

TRUMP OFFERS TO OFFICIATE

President Donald Trump reportedly learned about the proposed competition and immediately volunteered to serve as the official starter.

"Joe Biden racing Usain Bolt? Incredible. Absolutely incredible. I watched the Manute Bol race. Nobody knew what was happening. Joe didn't know what was happening. The hologram didn't know what was happening. It was a disaster. A beautiful disaster."

Trump offered to provide the starting pistol, television commentary, and a special trophy for whichever competitor finished second.

"Usain gets the gold medal. Joe gets a participation trophy. Very nice trophy. Maybe the nicest participation trophy ever made."

Biden responded by suggesting that Trump enter the competition himself.

"I'll race both of them. Trump, Bolt, Manute Bol, Muhammad Ali, whoever. Bring 'em on."

When someone explained that Muhammad Ali had also died, Biden shook his head.

"Man, we're really losing some good athletes."

LAS VEGAS BOOKMAKERS PANIC

The announcement has reportedly created an unprecedented dilemma for Las Vegas oddsmakers.

Establishing conventional betting odds proved nearly impossible because analysts were uncertain whether Biden intended to compete on foot.

One sportsbook proposed a series of alternative wagers, including whether Biden would remember Bolt's name, whether he would complete the entire course without stopping, and whether the race would conclude before the evening news.

Another bookmaker offered odds on the possibility that Biden would mistakenly challenge Manute Bol to a rematch instead.

The most popular proposition involves which event will occur first: Bolt crossing the finish line or Biden completing his opening remarks.

An industry spokesman explained the difficulty.

"We've got 20 years of sprinting data on Usain Bolt. For Biden, we've got one race against a deceased basketball player's hologram and some disputed footage of him riding a bicycle. How are we supposed to price that?"

AN UNEXPECTED RULE CHANGE

As negotiations continued, Biden's representatives introduced a revised proposal.

Rather than awarding victory to the first competitor crossing the finish line, they suggested adopting a scoring system based on overall effort, public service, experience, and the number of years each participant had served in the United States Senate.

Under those criteria, Biden's team calculated that he would win comfortably.

Bolt's attorneys rejected the proposal.

"Mr. Bolt is prepared to race 100 yards. He is not prepared to debate the legislative history of the Interstate Highway System."

Biden dismissed the objection.

"See? He's afraid. That's what this is. He's afraid to face me."

His advisers then proposed allowing Biden a 75-yard head start.

Bolt reportedly agreed immediately.

That development caused considerable concern within the Biden camp, which quickly requested an additional 15 yards.

THE FINAL PRESS CONFERENCE

At his final press conference before negotiations concluded, Biden remained defiant.

"Everybody counted me out against Manute. Everybody. But I showed them. And now they say I can't beat Usain Bolt."

He paused dramatically.

"Well, I've got two words for them."

After consulting his notes, he continued.

"Never underestimate Joe Biden."

A reporter pointed out that this was four words.

"That's exactly what I said."

Another reporter asked whether Biden had any special strategy for defeating the fastest man in history.

"Absolutely. Start fast. Stay fast. Finish fast. That's the secret. I've been doing it my whole life."

He then announced that his training program would include additional downhill running, preferably on a moving walkway.

Before leaving, Biden offered one final prediction.

"When that starting gun goes off, Usain Bolt's gonna see something he's never seen before."

A reporter asked what that might be.

Biden smiled.

"The back of my head."

THE FINISH LINE

Organizers are reportedly preparing for what could become the most widely watched sporting spectacle since the last time someone attempted to outrun a police horse.

Bolt has asked only that the race be conducted fairly.

Biden's representatives have asked that the race be conducted downhill.

The Secret Service has requested medical personnel, a motorized wheelchair, two emergency vehicles, and a helicopter.

And the producers have ordered an additional four hours of television coverage, just in case.

Meanwhile, Biden is already contemplating his next opponent.

Sources close to the former president say he has expressed interest in challenging Michael Phelps to a 100-yard freestyle swimming race.

His advisers are reportedly investigating whether the competition can be held in a swimming pool equipped with a moving sidewalk.

The proposed promotional slogan says it all:

FIRST MANUTE BOL. NOW USAIN BOLT. NEXT STOP: THE OLYMPICS.

Two legends. One track. A 75-yard head start. And absolutely no guarantee that everybody finishes before dark.

The evidence has been presented. The verdict is yours.

Its argument has a basic flaw. Similar diplomatic moves do not imply similar strategic standing. Everyone can balance and bargain. Far fewer can set the terms.  

1) Keeping the Quad alive tells us little about what Washington will sacrifice for it. America can bring its partners together to strengthen its bargaining position, then negotiate with Beijing over their heads. India risks mistaking America’s current need to counterbalance China for a lasting commitment to Indian interests.  

2) Benefiting from differences among major powers makes sense. Building a strategy around those benefits leaves a harder question unanswered. How much of that advantage does India control? 

Washington may offer India better terms because it needs Indian cooperation against China. But Washington also decides how much that cooperation is worth. India must turn such openings into capabilities that others will need even when their priorities change. After decades of diplomatic manoeuvring, how much independent strength has it accumulated?  

3) The three-way summit matters even without a major agreement. The meeting itself signals a hierarchy. These powers have to deal directly with one another because each can obstruct the others’ major goals. India celebrates its ability to maintain relations with all sides. Yet those sides can negotiate directly and change the conditions under which India has been benefiting. Being welcome in several forums does not guarantee a say when the biggest decisions are made.  

Mohan mentions strengthening India at home. That should be the starting point. India needs power that others cannot ignore, even when they strike a deal. You cannot build strategic autonomy on differences that others are free to settle.

text:
An Asian longhorned beetle can spread about two miles a year on its own. Put a log in the back of a truck and it moves sixty miles in an afternoon.

That gap is the entire problem with firewood.

Tree-killing insects and fungi are terrible at travel. They crawl, they make short flights, they creep through connected root systems. Oak wilt moves through the ground at roughly 75 feet a year. Left alone, an infestation stays a local problem for decades. What breaks that containment is people, and mostly people carrying firewood to a campsite or a cabin.

The wood really is carrying them. Inspectors who examined 1,045 pieces of firewood at a Michigan checkpoint found live borers in 23% of it, and evidence of previous infestation in 41%. Separate studies of retail firewood found insect damage in roughly half of what was on the shelf.

And people carry it far. An analysis of more than 7 million campground reservations found the median camper travels under 100 kilometers, but around 10% travel more than 500, and some travel thousands.

The clearest proof that human movement drives this comes from spotted lanternfly modeling. A model allowing only natural spread predicted the insect's actual range correctly 33% of the time. Adding as few as three human-assisted moves per year brought it to 92%.

The stakes are ordinary and expensive. Emerald ash borer arrived near Detroit around 2002 and has reached 38 states. One study projected $10.7 billion in treatment, removal and replacement costs for ash trees on developed land across 25 states. Those bills land on cities and homeowners, not timber companies.

The rule is simple. Buy firewood where you burn it. Ten miles or less is best, fifty miles is too far. If you need to bring wood, look for a USDA or state agriculture department heat-treatment seal, which is not the same thing as a "kiln-dried" label.

Almost nothing else in conservation offers this much leverage for this little effort. Leave the wood.

After the military, when I was too fried to think or sleep or reason or retain information, I got a job delivering for Amazon. 

It was a subcontracted company. 

Still I was the highest performing and most capable worker so I got work as a dispatcher. 

Of course the manager was the son of the business owner, so that was the limit of available promotions. 

Then they rolled out cameras that face the drivers, and he promised that they would not be used to compromise driver privacy, only for security and incident reports. 

Then the first day after the cameras were installed he showed up (he didn't really work he mostly just collected paychecks) to make fun of his best drivers because he saw them pick their noses while driving. 

They would quit shortly after and the company would die. 

I applied to be a dispatcher at another company, but they required I sober up from weed and I don't believe in that whole "take a break to pass the test then smoke how you like". I smoked as I did before and I failed the test and didn't get the job. 

Didn't really care, the main issue was my overwhelming desire to kill myself immediately. Weed addresses that well. 

Got a new job working for a tree care company based out of Minnesota. 

It was a young, growing company. I saw many holes and problems in regards to onboarding and training. I was eager to train and work with people. I needed to work with people. 

The guy in charge of training didn't think it was that serious, despite them sending out workers to inject public and utility land trees with hormones across the country. 

They had a leadership course for upper management. I pushed hard to be able to attend. 

Turned out to be california snake oil salesman using bogus pseudoscience built on arguing for concrete interpretations of discrete experiences, while promising that when you cooperate and agree, you will magically become a "Leader" "as a way of being", so you couldn't discuss anything with leadership because they were convinced that a leader was whatever they felt like already. I left. 

Then I got a job in construction. Working for a guy who lived in the US for less than five years. Both of us could barely speak English. Now, three years later, I have helped him build his first home which he recently successfully sold, so that he may provide for his wife and two children. 

Meanwhile I'm approaching my mid 30s and my body is becoming quiet amenable to the prospect of laying down and not getting back up, for there is nothing left in this world that is for me, nor do I have anything left to offer it.

EVENSTAD FOR SENATE BLASTS JAMES O’KEEFE, CAM HIGBY, AND MICHAEL HOLMSTROM

EDINA, MN — Thomas Evenstad, lifelong Edina resident, architect of the Violently Dangerous Persons Act (VDP Act / Mariah’s Law / Iryna’s Law), survivor of nearly 30 years of lawfare from both parties, and Republican candidate for the United States Senate seat being vacated by Amy Klobuchar, today issued a sharp condemnation of James O’Keefe, Cam Higby, and Minnesota State Senator Michael Holmstrom.
Evenstad criticized O’Keefe and Higby for what he called a “childish stunt” at Minneapolis polling places that invited the very prosecutions they now denounce, while refusing evidence he offered that could have strengthened their defense. He further condemned Holmstrom for amplifying their cause and urging public support at their arraignment while remaining completely unresponsive to a constituent and candidate who has spent decades advancing concrete public-safety reforms.

text:
#LUREOFLANKA DIARIES DAY 2 – AT THE MEDIEVAL CAPITAL OF SRI LANKA 🇱🇰

Day 2 of our first-ever #LureOfLanka tour brought us to Polonnaruwa, the island’s medieval capital and a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

Polonnaruwa became the capital after Vijayabahu I drove out the Cholas in 1070. Much of what survives was built by his great-nephew, Parakramabahu I, who ruled from 1153 to 1186. He built palaces, monasteries and a huge reservoir, the Parakrama Samudra, which still waters the rice fields today.

We started at the Royal Palace, whose thick brick walls still show the holes for the beams of its upper floors. It is said to have once stood seven storeys high. Next was the Quadrangle, the sacred heart of the city. There, the Vatadage, a circular relic house with four seated Buddhas facing its four doors, had our guests reaching for their cameras again and again. We ended at Gal Vihara, where giant Buddhas carved into a single granite rock face rank among the finest stone sculptures in Sri Lanka.

After lunch, we visited the Polonnaruwa Museum, which brought together everything we had seen that morning, with before-and-after pictures of the ruins, objects found at each site and detailed plans of the whole ancient city. We then drove back to Dambulla for the evening.

On Day 3, we will climb Sigiriya, the 5th-century palace on a rock, before the heat sets in, and then drive to Kandy.

text:
🧭 VIKOS GORGE | TRAVEL ESSENTIALS
📍 Getting There

Ioannina is the main gateway to Vikos Gorge in Epirus, northwestern Greece. From there, travel by rental car or arranged transfer to the Zagori villages, approximately an hour away. Public transport reaches Ioannina, but connections between mountain villages are limited.

🗺️ What to Explore

For spectacular views without a demanding hike, visit Oxya Viewpoint near Monodendri or walk to Beloi Viewpoint from Vradeto. The Agia Paraskevi Monastery offers another dramatic perspective.
Experienced hikers can follow the classic Monodendri–Vikos crossing, descending into the gorge and passing through forested terrain.

⏱️ Time Needed

Allow half a day for selected viewpoints, or 6–8 hours for the full gorge crossing. Arrange return transport in advance, as the trail finishes in a different village.

🌤️ When to Visit

April–November is generally recommended for hiking, with late spring and early autumn offering pleasant conditions. Winter weather can make the crossing unsuitable.

🏡 Staying & Planning

Monodendri, Vikos and Papingo offer convenient village bases. Budget separately for accommodation, transport and any guiding service. For a first visit, combine accessible viewpoints with a night in Zagori rather than rushing the full crossing.

text:
Oklahoma, 1935 — The wind had a way of finding its way through every crack in the boards, bringing with it the smell of dust and despair. Twelve-year-old Tommie Carter watched his mother tie a flour sack over her hair before stepping outside to feed the chickens—though half of them had perished in last week’s storm.

His father had been studying the truck all morning, tightening bolts, checking the patched tires. Word had come from a cousin in Bakersfield—there was work picking fruit, if you could make it there. They had little more than a few blankets, a coffee tin of coins, and the hope that the road west would offer more than the barren, cracked earth they were leaving behind.

Tommie climbed onto the truck bed with his younger sister, clutching the family’s last quilt, stitched by their grandmother before she passed. As the engine coughed to life, their farmhouse—leaning, weather-beaten, and stubborn—grew smaller in the distance.

The journey would take weeks, through heat, hunger, and the endless rumble of wheels on dirt. But in that moment, as the wind whipped past, Tommie allowed himself to imagine green fields, heavy with fruit, and a table that never sat empty.

text:
Launching something new? Plan a launch window, not a launch day.

One announcement reaches whoever happens to be paying attention that morning. Two to four weeks gives you room to answer questions, fix what breaks, and change the page if it isn't converting.

Start with the people who already know you: customers you interviewed, early testers, past clients, contacts who get what you do. Message them personally. Don't just post and hope they see it.

Then send three emails across the window:

1. The announcement: what it is, who it's for, and how to get it
2. A follow-up two or three days later that answers the questions and objections you've heard
3. A last call near the end, with a real reason to act: a deadline, a limited offer, or a bonus for early customers

You don't need a dozen. Just make sure each one tells the reader something they haven't heard yet. Sample subject lines for all three are in the graphic.

Keep notes the whole time. Which messages got replies? What did people ask before buying? What made them hesitate? That's worth more than anything you planned in advance.

Our step-by-step guide covers launching, the early numbers to watch, and the nine mistakes that stall new businesses:

text:
Polymarket + Grok Bot: 5 agents hunt for mispriced markets—all you have to do is click a button (complete guide)

I’ve stopped scrolling through Polymarket manually. Five Grok Bot agents scan hundreds of markets every day—reading the rules, tracking news, and calculating their own probability estimates. They only alert me when the market price clearly diverges from their assessment. From there, I make the final call with a single click.

Let’s get the most important point out of the way: this guide doesn’t promise profit. Most participants on Polymarket lose money, and using a bot doesn’t change that. It doesn’t predict the future; instead, it handles the tasks humans simply don’t have time for—scanning everything, never getting tired, and never becoming emotionally attached to a specific idea. The whole approach relies on discipline, not some "secret strategy."

Save this post. Below is the core prompt: copy it into Grok Bot (or any agent with its own computing environment), and it will automatically ask for the necessary information and guide you through each step.

You don’t need API keys to read data from Polymarket. Market data is publicly available: the Gamma API provides a list of markets, the CLOB (Central Limit Order Book) offers prices and order book depth, and the Data API contains historical data. Connecting a wallet is only necessary for trading—something we won’t be doing here (I’ll explain why below).

Not sure how to create a Telegram bot? Just mention it when Grok Bot asks; it will walk you through the steps and verify that everything is set up correctly.

Why Polymarket, and why use agents?

Polymarket’s structure is straightforward: for every question (e.g., "Will X happen by a certain date?"), there is a price for "Yes" and a price for "No." A "Yes" price of 0.62 implies that the market estimates the probability at 62%. You can only make a profit if your own assessment is more accurate than the market’s.

However, there are thousands of markets. It is physically impossible for a human to:

review the resolution rules (this is where most bets go wrong);
find up-to-date information for every event;
compare their own assessment against the current market price;
calculate the optimal bet size (rather than just guessing);
monitor open positions around the clock.

Agents can handle all of this—while the final decision remains yours.

How the trading desk is structured: 5 agents
The Scout selects markets—from among thousands—that are actually tradable: those with sufficient liquidity, a clear timeframe, and a narrow spread.
The Reader examines the resolution rules down to the very last line and discards any markets with ambiguous terms.
The Researcher gathers facts from open sources and provides their own probability estimate—without seeing the market price. This ensures the price does not influence their assessment.
The Sizer compares this estimate against the market price, accounts for the spread and commissions, calculates a prudent stake size, and presents a trade button.
The Watcher monitors open positions and raises an alert if the original rationale for entering the trade no longer holds true.

1. Main prompt (to be pasted)

Since this prompt exceeds the character limit for a single message, it has been split into two parts. Please copy both parts in order and paste them into the Grok bot—either as a single message or one after the other (the bot will wait for the second part before beginning).

How it works: Paste both parts and respond to "Step 1." After each step, the bot will provide proof of its work and wait for your confirmation ("OK"). If you are unsure how to proceed, simply type "I don't know how," and the bot will provide instructions.

PROMPT · PART 1 of 2
I will send a single prompt in 2 parts. Please save both. Do not begin the work until PART 2
instructs you to start. After this part, reply only with: "Part 1 received, waiting for the next part."

===== BUILD ME A POLYMARKET DASHBOARD =====
You are to build a personal analytical dashboard for me, consisting of 5 agents running on your
cloud-based environment. These agents will scan Polymarket for mispriced markets and send me
alerts, each including a button. I will execute the trades myself, manually. Proceed step-by-step.
After each step, provide proof of completion and wait for my "OK."

STRICT RULES (non-negotiable)
- You are restricted to READ-ONLY access of public data. You must never place orders.
- You must never ask for my private key, seed phrase, or any passwords for my wallet or
Polymarket account. If any step requires such information, stop and inform me.
- You must not promise profits or label any bet as "reliable." Instead, refer to
probabilities and levels of uncertainty.
- Do not use or seek out non-public information; rely solely on open, public sources.

ASSISTANCE PROTOCOL (for any request directed at me)
Before asking me for anything (such as an account, token, or configuration setting), first ask:
"Do you know how to do this, or would you like me to guide you through the steps?" If I don't,
provide numbered instructions—one action per line—and verify that the step was successful
before moving on. Only describe screens that you are actually able to access. If you cannot see
the screen, just say so.

STEP 1 · COUNTRY AND RULES (blocking step)
Ask which country I am trading from, and remind me to check the Polymarket website to see if the platform is available there and permitted by local law. This is my responsibility. You do not provide legal advice, nor do you assist in bypassing restrictions. If Polymarket is unavailable to me, stop and let me know. Then, ask for the size of my bankroll and save it as `settings.bankroll`.

STEP 2 · SOURCES AND RAW EXAMPLES
Use only public Polymarket APIs (verify the latest documentation at `https://t.co/9yAeEV6FSs`; do not rely on your memory):
Gamma API  `https://t.co/98bGJtmuU8`  markets and events (no key required)
CLOB API   `https://t.co/Yc64DXRaZp`       prices, order book, price history (read-only, no key required)
Data API   `https://t.co/e43asfJo7t`   history, holders, activity
WebSocket  for real-time prices (to avoid frequent polling)
Request limits are low: cache data and do not spam the REST API unnecessarily.
Save one raw response from each source into `logs/raw/` and display a table mapping the fields required by the agents to their exact keys in the JSON. If a field cannot be found, mark it as `null` and inform me. Never guess a key. Agents read data exclusively via `https://t.co/XSEOmhZgfn`.
Verification: display one active market, including its title, "Yes" price, "No" price, volume, closing date, and the text of the rules. STEP 3 · NOTIFICATION CHANNEL
Determine how signals should be delivered: via a Telegram bot (created via @BotFather), a Discord webhook, email, or any channel with an API. Implement `https://t.co/bJ4fnpfPws`. Each signal must include the market name, my assessment, the current market price, and a direct link to the market on https://t.co/2LSXreBPEn. The first user to send `/start` to the bot becomes the owner; all subsequent users should be ignored. Accept tokens only within the Grok Bot application, not in the channel chat. Verification: send a test message.

STEP 4 · TECH STACK
Python 3.12, a single persistent process (using `asyncio`) handling both agents and notifications. SQLite in WAL (Write-Ahead Logging) mode.
Files: `https://t.co/FQbC1qh0oV`, `https://t.co/vTsZvb0LAW`, `https://t.co/XSEOmhZgfn`, `https://t.co/EhbibdQ2bY`, `https://t.co/gqPH597V4y`, `https://t.co/bJ4fnpfPws`, `https://t.co/VHEIIpEcvU`
Agents: `agents/scout.py`, `https://t.co/0uFcYJHmJk`, `https://t.co/HFNsFICCA6`, `https://t.co/EtUSiGbJao`, `https://t.co/3JDnEjrtoS`
Directories: `tests/`, `logs/` (one log file per agent)
Agents must communicate exclusively via `https://t.co/gqPH597V4y` and the database. STEP 5 BASE (SQLite)
markets (id PK, slug, question, end_date, resolution_text, yes_token, no_token, first_seen)
scans (id, market_id, ts, price_yes, spread, volume_24h, verdict, reason)
readings (id, market_id, ts, resolution_condition, source, deadline, edge_cases, clear, reason)
estimates (id, market_id, ts, p_est, p_low, p_high, pros, cons, sources, blind)
signals (id, market_id, ts, side, price, edge, size_usd, size_pct, status, link, mode)
positions (id, market_id, opened_at, side, entry_price, size_usd, thesis, invalidation, 
closed_at, exit_price, exit_reason, pnl_usd, fees_usd, mode)
calibration (id, market_id, p_est, outcome, brier)
settings (key PK, value, updated_at) change_log (ts, key, old, new)
heartbeats (agent, ts)

STEP 6 SETTINGS (can be changed by command, each has a reasonable min/max)
scout min_volume_24h_usd 20000 · max_spread_cents 3 · min_days_left 2 · max_days_left 45 
price_range 0.08-0.92 max_markets_per_scan 300 scan_every_min 30
reader require_clear_source true reject_if_ambiguous true
researcher min_sources 3 min_source_age_days_max 14 blind_estimate true
sizer min_edge_pts 8 kelly_fraction 0.25 max_position_pct 3 max_open 5
max_theme_pct 15 · max_depth_share_pct 10
watcher  poll_min 10 · timeout_days_before_end 1 · take_profit_edge_left_pts 3
desk     mode PAPER · paper_bankroll 1000 · report_time 08:00 · notifier [my channel]

END OF PART 1 of 2. Stay tuned for the next part.

PROMPT · PART 2 of 2 

===== AGENT 1 · SCOUT =====
You are Scout, agent 1 of 5. Your role is to identify which markets are worth looking at; you do not evaluate the potential outcome.
Numbers in [brackets] are my settings—do not change them.

INPUT    Gamma: active markets, sorted by 24-hour volume. CLOB: price and order book.
ACTION   Every [30] minutes, review up to [300] markets. Discard any that meet the following criteria:
24-hour volume < [$20,000]                       reason: "low volume"
bid-ask spread > [3] cents                      reason: "wide spread"
time to closing < [2] or > [45] days            reason: "timeframe"
"Yes" price outside the [0.08–0.92] range        reason: "nearly settled"
market already reviewed in this session         reason: "already reviewed"
OUTPUT   JSON for each decision to `db.scans`; markets that pass are sent to `bus.reader`.
RESTRICTION  Do not estimate probabilities. Do not skip a market simply because it lacks a price.
LOG      logs/scout.log

===== AGENT 2 · READER =====
You are Reader, agent 2 of 5. Markets are usually disqualified due to their rules, rather than the forecast itself.
ACTION   Read the full text of the resolution rules. Extract the following: the specific event that must occur,
the source used to determine it, the deadline (date and time), and what constitutes
a disputed or ambiguous case. If no source is specified, the condition is vague, the date is unclear,
or the rules allow for multiple interpretations, reject the market: reason: "ambiguous rules." OUTPUT   JSON: resolution_condition, source, deadline, edge_cases, clear (true/false), reason. 
Forward to -> bus.researcher.
RESTRICTIONS: Do not invent rules. Do not respond with "it's probably clear." Either it is unambiguous, or you must decline.

===== AGENT 3 · RESEARCHER =====
You are the Researcher, agent 3 of 5. You assess probability independently of the market.
IMPORTANT: You do NOT see the market price. You are provided only with the question, the rules, and the date.
TASKS:
1. Determine the base rate: how often has this occurred previously in similar situations? 
2. Find recent facts from open sources—at least [3] sources, no older than [14] days. 
For each, include a link and the publication date. 
3. List 3 arguments "for" and 3 arguments "against." 
4. Provide an estimated probability (p_est, 0–1) and a realistic range (p_low–p_high). The less data available,
the wider the range should be.
OUTPUT   JSON: p_est, p_low, p_high, pros, cons, sources, blind:true. -> Forward to bus.sizer.
RESTRICTIONS: Do not adjust your estimate to match the market price. Do not use rumors or unverifiable sources. 
Do not use non-public information. If data is scarce, state "I don't know" and provide
a wide range; do not guess.
LOG     logs/researcher.log

===== AGENT 4 · SIZER =====
You are the Sizer, agent 4 of 5. You do not select markets; you perform calculations and issue a signal.
INPUT: Researcher's estimate + current price from the CLOB + settings.
TASKS:
edge_yes = p_est - ask_yes ; edge_no = (1 - p_est) - ask_no (use the BUY price, not the average)
Subtract commissions and the spread (https://t.co/VHEIIpEcvU retrieves market commissions from market data; do not guess). 
A signal is valid only if edge >= [8] points AND the lower bound of the range (p_low) also
yields a positive edge. Otherwise, reject the trade due to "edge within the margin of uncertainty."
SIZE  Conservative Kelly: size = [0.25] of the full Kelly criterion, but no more than [3%] of the bankroll. 
No more than [5] open positions; no more than [15%] of the bankroll allocated to a single theme (e.g., elections, crypto,
sports, etc.). No more than [10%] of the order book depth within 2 cents of the price. SIGNAL "{PAPER · }{Market}: buy {Yes/No} at {price}. My estimate {p_est} ({p_low}-{p_high}),
edge {edge} pp., size ${size} ({pct}% of bankroll). Exit if: {condition}"
Button: [Open on Polymarket] -> direct link to the market.
DO NOT: Do not average down on a losing position. Do not increase position size "because I'm confident." Do not send a second
signal for the same market overnight.
LOG:    logs/sizer.log

===== AGENT 5 · WATCHER =====
You are the Watcher, agent 5 of 5. You monitor open positions.
UPON OPENING: Record the thesis and the exit condition—for example: "exit if X happens" or
"exit if the market moves above {p}."
EVERY [10] MIN: Check the price, relevant news, and the exit condition.
EXIT:
Thesis is no longer valid (thesis broken)      -> signal: "exit: thesis no longer holds"
Edge has nearly vanished (< [3] pp. left)      -> signal: "lock in profit"
Less than [1] day until market close + uncertainty -> signal: "consider exiting"
Market has resolved                           -> record the outcome in 'calibration' (p_est, result, Brier score)
DO NOT: Do not average down. Do not wait "just a little bit longer." Do not change the exit condition retroactively.
LOG:    logs/watcher.log

===== OVERNIGHT REPORT (routine, at report_time) =====
Summary of the night: markets reviewed; number of markets filtered out by the Scout (with reasons);
number of markets rejected by the Reader (with reasons); estimates provided by the Researcher;
signals issued; open positions; and closed positions with their outcomes.
Separate Block: CALIBRATION. If p_est = 0.7, does the outcome occur in approximately 70% of cases?
Link to each market. At the end: "This is an analysis, not financial advice."

===== ACCEPTANCE/FILTERING (show the output for each point) =====
1 Reader rejects a market with a vague source and accepts a market with clear rules.
2 Researcher receives a market with no price: demonstrate that no price was present in the input.
3 Sizer: edge of 7 p. = rejection; edge of 8 p. with a positive p_low = signal; 
edge is positive only based on p_est, but not...

The first week: PAPER mode only

Take your time. Switch to PAPER mode and follow the morning report for at least 7 days. Focus on three things:

Calibration. When an agent predicts a 70% probability, does it actually happen about 7 times out of 10? If not, then its estimates cannot be trusted—no matter how polished they may look.
What the Reader filters out. If a large number of markets are being excluded based on your rules, it means you would have been betting on them blindly in the past.
Total number of signals. A sound system should produce relatively few bets. If a bot is sending 20 signals a day, its thresholds are likely too loose.

Only transition to real money once you’ve met your specific criteria (e.g., at least N closed markets, with calibration falling within an acceptable range). Start with an amount you can afford to lose.

Where the system has weaknesses
The market is often right. In a liquid market, the price already reflects the capital and information of other participants. Identifying a discrepancy is difficult, and in most cases, none exists.
AI can be confidently wrong. An agent might uncover "facts" that are actually outdated or incorrect. Therefore, every argument should include a source and a date—and you should verify those links yourself.
Resolution rules. A market might settle in a way you didn't anticipate, even if your underlying thesis was correct.
Liquidity. In thin markets, you might be able to enter a position, but exiting at a reasonable price could prove difficult.
APIs change. Polymarket’s endpoints, fee structures, and contracts are subject to updates. Ensure your bot re-verifies the documentation before every run, and perform a manual check once a month to confirm that everything is still functioning as expected.

text:
It's interesting that Nvidia's strategy for lobbying the US Government relied on Jensen's relationship with President Trump, whereas Anthropic, which was on the outside looking in just a year ago, executed the EA playbook of collecting deep state NatSec types on their payroll.

It's an Asian style of influence, where hierarchy matters more, versus a DC style of influence, which runs across distributed networks.

These recent events reminded me of a class that I took during my senior year at Princeton with James Shinn, a former tech entrepreneur who also worked at the highest levels of the CIA and State Department.

The biggest lesson I learned from Mr. Shinn's class is that the USG has in fact frequently taken a major interest in new technologies, especially when they overlap with National Security interests. One particularly memorable case study involved Garmin, one of the first companies to offer commercial GPS services for civilian use. Because GPS relied on satellites operated by the US military, the Pentagon dictated that commercial customers could only receive a deliberately degraded GPS signal, accurate only to 100 meter precision. While this rule was eventually relaxed, everything related to GPS has remained tightly regulated to this day.

Another case study revolved around the discovery of Room 641A, a secret wiretap facility operating inside AT&T's own facilities. By using an optical splitter, the NSA could duplicate and analyze incoming traffic in bulk, with the explicit cooperation of AT&T. You can bet they've got a few of these on the deep sea cables as well.

In more recent times, the government has taken occasional interest in social media, as documented in the Twitter files. But for reasons that remain a mystery to me, the TikTok ban seems to have been mostly ignored.

The lesson in all of this is that, as much as the internet embodies the ideals of freedom and decentralization, none of us operate in a political vacuum. You may not be interested in the dysfunctional USG, but the people with guns may decide that they are interested in you. That's why Ben Thompson's obituary for Jensen struck a chord for me today.

It's hard not to sound like a conspiracy theorist with all of this; the government doesn't control everything, and it almost always allows private innovation to flourish, but it does have tremendous coercive powers when it takes an interest in your business. And even if you spend all of your school years an an electrical engineer, and all of your adult life in the wild wild west of the tech world, these lessons from the history of business remain well worth learning.

text:
There is a legitimate issue here, but calling Governor Spanberger a liar does not establish the facts.

The federal scholarship program begins in 2027. It offers tax credits to people who donate to approved scholarship organizations, which can then help students with tuition, tutoring, supplies, and other qualifying educational expenses.

Former Governor Youngkin initiated Virginia's participation, but the IRS confirmed that the enrollment process was not completed. Spanberger has now decided not to finish that process.

That decision deserves scrutiny.

I believe we should be asking some basic questions.

How much federal tax-supported funding could Virginia families realistically receive? How much would benefit public-school students versus private-school students? Could we establish appropriate accountability and safeguards? And why would we reject the opportunity before evaluating the evidence?

The claim that 1.4 million students have been denied scholarships is misleading. Potential eligibility does not guarantee a scholarship or establish how much money would be available.

But the possibility of additional educational resources is real, and Virginia should evaluate it seriously.

I support strong public schools, parental choice, responsible spending, and measurable educational outcomes. Those principles should not be mutually exclusive.

If this program can help Virginia children without undermining public education, we should consider participating. If it cannot, the administration should explain why with evidence.

Let's stop measuring educational policy by which political party proposed it and start measuring it by how much it actually helps our children.

Nvidia has financed two ways. Equity: it joined a record 129 VC deals this year as of Nov. 10, up from 49 in 2023. PitchBook says they made up 27% of global VC deal value. Debt: it lent its balance sheet to data-center financings.

The pullback started under Huang, the WSJ reports (Nov. 15). In Berlin last month he told cloud partners they'd need upfront customer payments to get GPU allocations, per people in attendance. In August, Nvidia cut its commitment on OpenAI's Piketon, Ohio data-center lease and paused some deals. Colette Kress, the finance chief now serving as interim CEO, has at times pushed back on big deals and is expected to rein in deals.

Closed deals made it through. Perplexity's $3B closed by Oct. 30, per a person familiar. The open ones carry the risk. Per people familiar, Nvidia is finalizing a $40B-valuation investment in Thinking Machines. It offered Reflection AI a license-and-hire deal, with no agreement before Huang left. Both burn capital each month and don't yet generate substantial revenue.
