AI Overview
Distinguishing a true prophet from a false prophet involves evaluating their character, message accuracy, and overall impact on people.
True Prophet
• Divine Alignment: Their message completely matches established scripture and core spiritual truths.
• Accurate Predictions: Their spoken visions and prophecies come true.
• Godly Character: They show humility, honesty, and moral goodness instead of seeking fame or money.
• Calls to Repentance: They confront sin and urge people to turn back to God rather than comforting bad behavior.
• Good Fruit: Their ministry builds up the community and produces lasting spiritual growth.
False Prophet
• Self-Serving Motives: They look for personal wealth, power, or praise.
• Contradictory Teachings: Their words go against foundational scripture and sound doctrine.
• Failed Predictions: Their specific claims and timelines fail to happen.
• Tickling Ears: They flatter listeners, ignore sin, and offer false comfort to make people feel comfortable in wrongdoing.
• Deception: They use manipulation, fake signs, or twisted words to lead followers astray.

What is a prophetess in the Bible?
what does the bible say?
A prophetess is a female prophet. The role and responsibility of prophets and prophetesses is to speak forth the word of God. The Greek origin of the English term prophet, prophetes, reveals this meaning: pro means "forth or before," and phetes means "to say or to speak." Thus, prophets and prophetesses are to say whatever message God has given them before the person or people for whom the message is intended. Prophets and prophetesses sometimes foretold future events, but most often they forthtold, proclaiming God’s truth, warning people of judgment, and calling them to repentance. Throughout history, God has used His Spirit to relay messages to female prophetesses, who were responsible to speak forth His Word to the people.

from the old testament
Sometimes, the message of a prophetess was a comforting encouragement (Haggai 1:13). Sometimes, it was a convicting warning (Jonah 3:2).
From time to time, it was a prediction of far-off future events (Zechariah 2:10–12).
A prophet or prophetess was responsible to share exactly what the Lord had given them (Deuteronomy 18:18). Samuel was taught to share the message in full, even if it was an uncomfortable truth that might not be well received (1 Samuel 3:17–18). When Jeremiah tried to stop sharing God's messages, he said, "If I say, 'I will not mention him, or speak any more in his name,' there is in my heart as it were a burning fire shut up in my bones, and I am weary with holding it in, and I cannot" (Jeremiah 20:9). Thus, prophets and prophetesses bore great responsibility in relaying God's Word to its intended audience.
God declared, "And it shall come to pass afterward, that I will pour out my Spirit on all flesh; your sons and your daughters shall prophesy, your old men shall dream dreams, and your young men shall see visions. Even on the male and female servants in those days I will pour out my Spirit" (Joel 2:28–29). In this statement, God specifically mentioned daughters who prophesy and His Spirit being poured out on female servants.
The first woman to be identified as a prophetess in Scripture is Moses's sister, Miriam, in Exodus 15:20. Her words were recorded in Scripture as she led the women in worship after God's miraculous rescue at the Red Sea.
The female judge who ruled over the Israelites, Deborah, was introduced first as "a prophetess," then "wife of Lappidoth," and finally in her role as "judging Israel at that time," perhaps implying that her primary role and legacy was as a prophetess who spoke the Word of the Lord (Judges 4:4). Many of those words are recorded in Judges 4. Judges 5 is exclusively the Holy Spirit's inspired words spoken by Deborah and Barak.
When Judah's King Josiah read a recently found copy of the Torah and realized the extent of his people's sin, he asked his advisors to "Go, inquire of the LORD for me" (2 Kings 22:13; 2 Chronicles 34:21). The prophets Jeremiah and Zephaniah were both contemporary and local, yet these men sought the insight of the female prophetess Huldah to discern God's will for the king and the nation (2 Kings 22:14; 2 Chronicles 34:22). Her response is recorded in Scripture and was confirmed as coming true within the lifetime of those who heard it.
The prophet Isaiah's wife is also identified as a prophetess in her own right, although no words of hers are recorded in Scripture (Isaiah 8:3).
Unfortunately, there have been false prophets and prophetesses as well. Nehemiah 6:14 mentions the prophetess Noadiah, who tried to use fear to prevent Nehemiah from following God's will. Ezekiel recorded about Jerusalem, "And her prophets have smeared whitewash for them, seeing false visions and divining lies for them, saying, 'Thus says the Lord GOD,' when the LORD has not spoken" (Ezekiel 22:28).
from the new testament
Elizabeth, the mother of John the Baptist, "was filled with the Holy Spirit, and she exclaimed with a loud cry, 'Blessed are you among women, and blessed is the fruit of your womb! And why is this granted to me that the mother of my Lord should come to me? For behold, when the sound of your greeting came to my ears, the baby in my womb leaped for joy. And blessed is she who believed that there would be a fulfillment of what was spoken to her from the Lord'" (Luke 1:41–45). Elizabeth spoke forth God's message to her cousin Mary through the power of the Holy Spirit, thus fulfilling the role of prophetess.
When Jesus was brought to the temple for His circumcision, His parents encountered Anna, a prophetess. "She did not depart from the temple, worshiping with fasting and prayer night and day. And coming up at that very hour she began to give thanks to God and to speak of him to all who were waiting for the redemption of Jerusalem" (Luke 2:37–38). This woman faithfully spoke God's Word about Jesus being the Messiah every day as she devoted the last years of her life to serving in the temple.
On the Day of Pentecost, when the Holy Spirit came upon male and female followers of Jesus, "they were all filled with the Holy Spirit and began to speak in other tongues as the Spirit gave them utterance" (Acts 2:4). Peter explained this phenomenon to the crowds in Jerusalem as one of the ways God's promise in Joel 2:28–29 was being fulfilled. He said, "And in the last days it shall be, God declares, that I will pour out my Spirit on all flesh, and your sons and your daughters shall prophesy, and your young men shall see visions, and your old men shall dream dreams; even on my male servants and female servants in those days I will pour out my Spirit, and they shall prophesy" (Acts 2:17–18).
While Paul was visiting Caesarea, Philip the evangelist's four unmarried daughters prophesied (Acts 21:8–9).
In the church in Corinth, women were regularly prophesying before the congregation, which is why Paul addressed customs of how to do that properly within their cultural context (1 Corinthians 11:5–6).
implications for today
From looking at the prophetesses in the Bible, we can learn the importance of faithfully communicating God's truth. Just as prophetesses like Miriam, Deborah, and Anna spoke forth God's Word, we, too, are called to share the truth of who He is and how He calls us to live. This can be done through teaching, encouraging, or even warning others, much like the various roles prophetesses played. By embracing this responsibility, we honor the legacy of these women and ensure that God's message continues to reach those who need it. In our daily lives, this means being attentive to God's guidance, knowing His Word, and being courageous in our communication. We can be consistent in sharing His love and wisdom with those around us, knowing that the Spirit can speak through anyone, regardless of gender, age, or status.

Some have suggested that the surviving texts may include some fragments or remnants of the Sibylline Books with a legendary provenance from the Cumaean Sibyl, which had been kept in temples in Rome. The original oracular books, kept in Rome, were accidentally destroyed in a fire in 83 BC, which resulted in an attempt in 76 BC to recollect them when the Roman senate sent envoys throughout the world to discover copies. This official copy existed until at least AD 405, but little is known of their contents.

That the use of the Sibylline Oracles was not always exclusive to Christians is shown by an extract from Book III concerning the Tower of Babel as quoted by the Jewish historian Flavius Josephus, in the late 1st century AD.[3]

The Christian apologist Athenagoras of Athens, writing A Plea for the Christians to Marcus Aurelius in c. 176 AD, quoted the same section of the extant Oracles verbatim, in the midst of a lengthy series of classical and pagan references including Homer and Hesiod, and stated several times that all these works should already be familiar to the Roman Emperor.

Varro enumerated ten Sibyls: Persian, Libyan, Delphic, Cimmerian, Erythrean, Samian, Cumean, Hellospontian, Phrygian, and Tiburtine. The list omits the Hebrew, Chaldean, and Egyptian Sibyls.[4] The Suda repeats this list but identifies the Persian Sibyl with the Hebrew.[4][5]

The Sibyls themselves, and the so-called Sibylline oracles, were often referred to by other early Church fathers; Theophilus, Bishop of Antioch (c. 180), Clement of Alexandria (c. 200), Lactantius (c. 305), and Augustine (c. 400), all knew various versions of the pseudo-Sibylline collections, quoted them or referred to them in paraphrase as Lactantius:

"The Erythraean Sibyl" in the beginning of her song, which she commenced by the help of the Most High God, proclaims the Son of God as leader and commander of all in these verses:

All-nourishing Creator, who in all
Sweet breath implanted, and made God the guide of all.

Some fragmentary verses that do not appear in the collections that survive are only known because they were quoted by a Church Father. Justin Martyr (c. 150), if he is truly the author of the Exhortation to the Greeks, gives such a circumstantial account of the Cumaean Sibyl that the Address is quoted here at the Cumaean Sibyl's entry. The Catholic Encyclopedia states, "Through the decline and disappearance of paganism, however, interest in them gradually diminished and they ceased to be widely read or circulated, though they were known and used during the Middle Ages in both the East and the West." [Need edition] Thus, a student may find echoes of their imagery and style in much early medieval literature.

These books, in spite of their pagan content, have sometimes been described as part of the Pseudepigrapha. They do not appear in the canonical lists of any Church.

AI Overview
Distinguishing a true prophet from a false prophet involves evaluating their character, message accuracy, and overall impact on people.
True Prophet
• Divine Alignment: Their message completely matches established scripture and core spiritual truths.
• Accurate Predictions: Their spoken visions and prophecies come true.
• Godly Character: They show humility, honesty, and moral goodness instead of seeking fame or money.
• Calls to Repentance: They confront sin and urge people to turn back to God rather than comforting bad behavior.
• Good Fruit: Their ministry builds up the community and produces lasting spiritual growth.
False Prophet
• Self-Serving Motives: They look for personal wealth, power, or praise.
• Contradictory Teachings: Their words go against foundational scripture and sound doctrine.
• Failed Predictions: Their specific claims and timelines fail to happen.
• Tickling Ears: They flatter listeners, ignore sin, and offer false comfort to make people feel comfortable in wrongdoing.
• Deception: They use manipulation, fake signs, or twisted words to lead followers astray.

What is a prophetess in the Bible?
what does the bible say?
A prophetess is a female prophet. The role and responsibility of prophets and prophetesses is to speak forth the word of God. The Greek origin of the English term prophet, prophetes, reveals this meaning: pro means "forth or before," and phetes means "to say or to speak." Thus, prophets and prophetesses are to say whatever message God has given them before the person or people for whom the message is intended. Prophets and prophetesses sometimes foretold future events, but most often they forthtold, proclaiming God’s truth, warning people of judgment, and calling them to repentance. Throughout history, God has used His Spirit to relay messages to female prophetesses, who were responsible to speak forth His Word to the people.

from the old testament
Sometimes, the message of a prophetess was a comforting encouragement (Haggai 1:13). Sometimes, it was a convicting warning (Jonah 3:2).
From time to time, it was a prediction of far-off future events (Zechariah 2:10–12).
A prophet or prophetess was responsible to share exactly what the Lord had given them (Deuteronomy 18:18). Samuel was taught to share the message in full, even if it was an uncomfortable truth that might not be well received (1 Samuel 3:17–18). When Jeremiah tried to stop sharing God's messages, he said, "If I say, 'I will not mention him, or speak any more in his name,' there is in my heart as it were a burning fire shut up in my bones, and I am weary with holding it in, and I cannot" (Jeremiah 20:9). Thus, prophets and prophetesses bore great responsibility in relaying God's Word to its intended audience.
God declared, "And it shall come to pass afterward, that I will pour out my Spirit on all flesh; your sons and your daughters shall prophesy, your old men shall dream dreams, and your young men shall see visions. Even on the male and female servants in those days I will pour out my Spirit" (Joel 2:28–29). In this statement, God specifically mentioned daughters who prophesy and His Spirit being poured out on female servants.
The first woman to be identified as a prophetess in Scripture is Moses's sister, Miriam, in Exodus 15:20. Her words were recorded in Scripture as she led the women in worship after God's miraculous rescue at the Red Sea.
The female judge who ruled over the Israelites, Deborah, was introduced first as "a prophetess," then "wife of Lappidoth," and finally in her role as "judging Israel at that time," perhaps implying that her primary role and legacy was as a prophetess who spoke the Word of the Lord (Judges 4:4). Many of those words are recorded in Judges 4. Judges 5 is exclusively the Holy Spirit's inspired words spoken by Deborah and Barak.
When Judah's King Josiah read a recently found copy of the Torah and realized the extent of his people's sin, he asked his advisors to "Go, inquire of the LORD for me" (2 Kings 22:13; 2 Chronicles 34:21). The prophets Jeremiah and Zephaniah were both contemporary and local, yet these men sought the insight of the female prophetess Huldah to discern God's will for the king and the nation (2 Kings 22:14; 2 Chronicles 34:22). Her response is recorded in Scripture and was confirmed as coming true within the lifetime of those who heard it.
The prophet Isaiah's wife is also identified as a prophetess in her own right, although no words of hers are recorded in Scripture (Isaiah 8:3).
Unfortunately, there have been false prophets and prophetesses as well. Nehemiah 6:14 mentions the prophetess Noadiah, who tried to use fear to prevent Nehemiah from following God's will. Ezekiel recorded about Jerusalem, "And her prophets have smeared whitewash for them, seeing false visions and divining lies for them, saying, 'Thus says the Lord GOD,' when the LORD has not spoken" (Ezekiel 22:28).
from the new testament
Elizabeth, the mother of John the Baptist, "was filled with the Holy Spirit, and she exclaimed with a loud cry, 'Blessed are you among women, and blessed is the fruit of your womb! And why is this granted to me that the mother of my Lord should come to me? For behold, when the sound of your greeting came to my ears, the baby in my womb leaped for joy. And blessed is she who believed that there would be a fulfillment of what was spoken to her from the Lord'" (Luke 1:41–45). Elizabeth spoke forth God's message to her cousin Mary through the power of the Holy Spirit, thus fulfilling the role of prophetess.
When Jesus was brought to the temple for His circumcision, His parents encountered Anna, a prophetess. "She did not depart from the temple, worshiping with fasting and prayer night and day. And coming up at that very hour she began to give thanks to God and to speak of him to all who were waiting for the redemption of Jerusalem" (Luke 2:37–38). This woman faithfully spoke God's Word about Jesus being the Messiah every day as she devoted the last years of her life to serving in the temple.
On the Day of Pentecost, when the Holy Spirit came upon male and female followers of Jesus, "they were all filled with the Holy Spirit and began to speak in other tongues as the Spirit gave them utterance" (Acts 2:4). Peter explained this phenomenon to the crowds in Jerusalem as one of the ways God's promise in Joel 2:28–29 was being fulfilled. He said, "And in the last days it shall be, God declares, that I will pour out my Spirit on all flesh, and your sons and your daughters shall prophesy, and your young men shall see visions, and your old men shall dream dreams; even on my male servants and female servants in those days I will pour out my Spirit, and they shall prophesy" (Acts 2:17–18).
While Paul was visiting Caesarea, Philip the evangelist's four unmarried daughters prophesied (Acts 21:8–9).
In the church in Corinth, women were regularly prophesying before the congregation, which is why Paul addressed customs of how to do that properly within their cultural context (1 Corinthians 11:5–6).
implications for today
From looking at the prophetesses in the Bible, we can learn the importance of faithfully communicating God's truth. Just as prophetesses like Miriam, Deborah, and Anna spoke forth God's Word, we, too, are called to share the truth of who He is and how He calls us to live. This can be done through teaching, encouraging, or even warning others, much like the various roles prophetesses played. By embracing this responsibility, we honor the legacy of these women and ensure that God's message continues to reach those who need it. In our daily lives, this means being attentive to God's guidance, knowing His Word, and being courageous in our communication. We can be consistent in sharing His love and wisdom with those around us, knowing that the Spirit can speak through anyone, regardless of gender, age, or status.

I simply couldn't cry for him.

4

The rolling sound began again. This time, I distinctly heard it stop outside our door.

An eerie female voice called out.

"Is anyone in here?"

Everyone in the wardrobe went rigid, barely daring to breathe.

"Hee-hee-hee. I see you. I see you."

"Stop hiding. Stop hiding."

Beside me, Vivian stiffened. Nancy raised a finger and shook it, warning us not to move.

The comments offered advice too.

[She's bluffing. Don't open the wardrobe!]

[This boss is clever. She even knows how to bait them.]

[No. Pick someone to send out as cannon fodder. Once the bottle woman kills someone in a room, she won't come back to it.]

The bottle woman rolled inside. Vivian and Mum exchanged a look, then shoved me out.

Nancy didn't react in time. By the time she tried to catch me, it was too late.

I stumbled to the doorway, face-to-face with the bottle woman.

A beautiful woman's head grew from an elegant vase.

Creamy skin, a face like a flower. So familiar.

Our eyes met. My tears spilled over.

"Big Sister, what happened to you?"

5

The screen filled with question marks.

[????]

[Is the girl scared stupid? Why's she calling her that?]

[She's done for. The bottle woman's going to be angry. Hope the newcomer doesn't die too horribly.]

[She tears people's limbs off alive. If this girl keeps that up, she'll get worse. Three seconds of silence for her.]

At the sight of my tears, the bottle woman jolted. In a blink, she grew a body and changed her clothes.

The vase became a fitted qipao. Neatly dressed, she looked almost ethereal.

Producing an osmanthus cake from nowhere, she popped it into my mouth and coaxed me gently.

"Oh, you little terror. What are you doing back here? I'm working. Don't cry."

"You're breaking your big sister's heart."

"Did I frighten you?"

"Be good. I didn't mean to. Have something nice to eat and cheer up."

The bottle woman before me was none other than my eldest senior sister, who'd raised me before I went home.

My birth parents hadn't found me until I was seventeen. Before that, I'd grown up at Qingyun Temple.

For as long as I could remember, my eldest senior sister and second senior brother had been with me.

She flew kites with me, bought me snacks and a phone, taught me to read, and made pastries for me.

But to see her like this, her whole body curled inside that tiny vase... I felt a hurt I couldn't describe.

The viewers were stunned.

[Wait. The bottle woman really is her senior sister?]

[Does the newcomer have some innate charm skill? Otherwise, how could a player know a boss?]

[I don't believe it. The bottle woman actually spared her.]

[Am I the only one noticing that the bottle woman took human form for a player?]

Seeing someone familiar brought all my misery bursting out. Tears pattered down my face.

text:
Congress Demands 181 Seats: Will SP Agree to 100–120 Seats?

Talks between the Samajwadi Party (SP) and Congress over seat-sharing for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections are gaining momentum. In the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, both parties benefited significantly from their alliance. Together, they won 43 out of 80 Lok Sabha seats in Uttar Pradesh. Now, both parties are preparing to contest the 2027 Assembly elections together.

Congress has demanded 181 out of the 403 Assembly seats. This is around 45% of the total seats. On the other hand, some SP leaders have suggested giving Congress around 50–60 seats, or a maximum of 65.

But the big question is: What formula will both parties follow to divide the seats?

Based on the 2024 Lok Sabha seat-sharing arrangement, it does not seem easy for SP to agree to Congress's demand for 181 seats.

In the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, SP contested 62 out of 80 seats in Uttar Pradesh, while Congress contested 17. One seat was given to their alliance partner, Trinamool Congress (TMC).

Based on this arrangement, SP contested 77.5% of the total seats, while Congress contested 21.25%.

If the same formula is applied to the 403 Assembly seats, SP would get around 312 seats and Congress would get 86 seats. The remaining seat could be kept for alliance partners.

Now, let's look at their election performance.
SP won 37 out of the 62 seats it contested, giving it a strike rate of 59.68%. Congress won 6 out of 17 seats, with a strike rate of 35.29%.
Out of the alliance's total 43 winning seats, SP contributed around 86%, while Congress contributed around 14%.

If this winning-seat ratio is applied to the 403 Assembly seats, SP would get around 347 seats and Congress would get 56.

However, if we compare the actual strike rates of both parties and apply that ratio to the 403 Assembly seats, SP would get around 253 seats and Congress around 150.

This means the 2024 Lok Sabha results give us three different seat-sharing estimates:
Based on seats contested: Congress gets around 86 seats.
Based on seats won: Congress gets around 56 seats.Based on the strike-rate ratio: Congress gets around 150 seats.

But are the political conditions in 2024 and 2027 the same? The answer is no.

Since 2024, several new issues and political equations have emerged in Uttar Pradesh.
The opposition's questions over the SIR process have given Congress a new political issue to raise. Rahul Gandhi's growing political activity and Congress's increased presence have strengthened the party's political claims. This could benefit the alliance in the 2027 Assembly elections.

On the other hand, the alleged misappropriation of donation money at the Ram Temple in Ayodhya could create an uncomfortable situation for the BJP's Hindutva politics. The opposition may raise this issue by linking it to religious faith and transparency.

If a section of upper-caste voters unhappy with the BJP shifts towards Congress, the alliance could benefit. It may be relatively difficult for these voters to shift directly towards SP because the party's main social base is built around its PDA strategy. In this situation, Congress could play an important role within the alliance by attracting upper-caste voters.

Therefore, SP should also consider giving Congress between 100 and 120 seats.

SP needs to understand that alliances are not formed only on the basis of previous election results. Future political possibilities, organisational strength and changing social equations also matter.

Congress may also be willing to accept a respectable seat-sharing arrangement. However, there is still a significant gap between its demand for 181 seats and the possible offer from SP.

Ultimately, the biggest challenge for both parties is not just the number of seats, but finding an agreement that balances their political ambitions with their chances of winning the election.

"Scripture offers zero exceptions for art or pedagogy—it commands us to 1) make no images and 2) bow down to none."
Simply NOT TRUE. The Command is in 2 parts, interdependent: 1)No images 2)[that you] worship.
The Tabernacle AND Temple were full of images: Pomegranates embroidered on the curtains, Golden lampstand looking like pomegranates, Bronze oxen holding up the large "bronze sea" (laver, for ceremonial washing), and in the Holy of Holies HUGE statues of the bowing angels to the invisible Mercy Seat above the Ark (images on the Ark in the Tabernacle, and above it, overshadowing it in the Temple).  There were probably other decorative images too, we're not told about.  

Key issue: NONE were to be worshipped. The making and existence of the images...was not, in itself, wrong.  When Moses's bronze serpent--which Jesus called a type for Himself--came to be worshipped in the Temple--good King Hezekiah rightfully destroyed it.  That story shows us idolatry MUST involve worship, it's not merely the making of or presence of an image....it's making an image TO WORSHIP.

Only in Islam....are images themselves deemed to be wrong.  According to 2CV, and, contemporary usage (and instructions, directly from God) images themselves are not the issue, it is images-to-worship, that is: Idols.

Also we have the complication that God Himself, Father, Son & Holy Spirit, is SPIRIT.  A spirit, by definition...is a being without form, therefore it cannot be imaged.  In the incarnation though, Jesus's human nature....was (& is) a form, since He is human.  Therefore it's possible to make an image of Jesus....  
Following the 2 part definition then, IF an image of Jesus's nature is not worshipped (and I do think Romanist/EO veneration....does cross the line into worship) that image is acceptable.  It can easily become an idol however...so it should not be placed in front of a Church....in a place to be ostensively worshipped. 
For teaching purposes though, and for art...it does NOT break the 2nd Commandment.

MIT is launching a new strategic initiative today: MIT for America, which seeks to strengthen STEM education nationally, at many levels of learning. 

Addressing a critical national need, the initiative ranges across STEM fields and will engage students from kindergarten through community college, preparing them to live and work in a world increasingly shaped by science and technology. MIT for America’s programs will develop new opportunities for student achievement in mathematics, hands-on design and fabrication, and constructive engagement with artificial intelligence. 

President Sally Kornbluth made the announcement today in a letter to the Institute community.

“A natural extension of the Institute’s long record of national service, MIT for America is grounded in our deep belief in potential over pedigree, of the transformative power of learning by doing and in the open sharing of knowledge,” Kornbluth wrote.

The initiative represents an Institute-wide effort to address the national challenge of improving STEM education and helping it adapt to shifting societal needs. MIT for America will leverage the Institute’s longstanding strengths to develop new programs and expand existing projects, while amplifying MIT’s impact on national education.

MIT for America’s faculty leaders emphasize that the initiative will support programs that can be scaled up and that provide direct, face-to-face guidance for learners and educators. 

“The goal is to provide programs that are both scalable and high-touch, and make an impact across the country,” says Professor Eric Klopfer, a faculty co-director of MIT for America and director of the Scheller Teacher Education Program and the Education Arcade at MIT. “All our programs take advantage of things we are well-positioned to do at MIT, and can be distributed around the country. That’s our guiding light.” 

Cynthia Breazeal, faculty co-director of MIT for America, professor of media arts and sciences, and the Benesse Professor of Research in Education, says the initiative “is about bringing high-quality access to STEM and AI education, from kindergarten to community college, across the United States. We live in an innovation-driven world, and it’s important to have an education that gives you access to it, whether that’s so you can be a fully engaged citizen or have the opportunity for economic mobility.”

Breazeal adds: “Talent is everywhere. We think opportunity should be, too.” 

The initiative is addressing large-scale needs in STEM education. Only 29 percent of U.S. students in grades 9-12 build circuits, and only 6 percent of students enroll in computer science classes, even though about 60 percent of high schools offer such courses. MIT for America intends to substantially help communities across the country build the bandwidth needed to further develop STEM knowledge and workplace skills. 

“This effort is about really rolling up sleeves and getting out there and engaging communities, and helping to build capacity across the United States,” Breazeal adds.

MIT for America features programs addressing three high-priority areas:

Mathematical thinking and problem solving: Work here builds on an existing program, the MIT for America Calculus Project, launched a year ago, in which MIT students and alumni volunteer to help provide calculus tutoring to students in school districts across the country. 

Living, learning, and working with AI: This area addresses multiple issues revolving around AI, including teacher education that helps instructors integrate AI into classroom learning in productive ways, and programs that enhance AI skills and STEM education in technical-vocational schools and community colleges. The MIT RAISE program (Responsible AI for Social Empowerment and Education) is a leader in this domain. 

Designing, making, and innovating: MIT for America plans to build out programs that encourage hands-on learning, design work, use of fab labs and makerspaces, and experiential learning, sometimes deploying tools such as national design challenges. 

“Across the U.S., we want to unlock opportunities and experiences where students are,” says Claudia Urrea, head of MIT for America and head of the MIT pK-12 Initiative. “We want to find people who have not had the opportunity to discover their talent.”

In the first case, the MIT for America Calculus Project provides a ready model of outreach with growth potential. About half of U.S. school districts offer calculus, but many of those districts may be under-resourced. The MIT for America Calculus Project has been growing in partnership with an increasing number of school districts, while MIT undergraduates and alumni have enjoyed participating in the program.  

“People have been really excited about the MIT for America Calculus Project, seeing both the impact that it has, and its model, which I think has resonated,” Klopfer says. “That’s really representative of what other programs could look like.”

In the second topic area, MIT for America can leverage burgeoning efforts such as MIT RAISE. The program helps educate teachers and engage students about implementing AI in ways that can complement the developing skills of students, enabling them to use AI in productive ways.

“RAISE is about providing materials and training for teachers that helps them have conversations and productive activities around AI,” Klopfer says. “It’s about understanding how AI works and discussing what the values are in your school. It has to be active, involving the students. If you try to force things, about AI one way or the other, that will fail.”

In an outgrowth of RAISE, MIT also launched a related program, Pathways for AI Training and Hiring (PATH), on Oct. 1. Starting with a partnership with Georgia State University, PATH aims to bring AI training to two-year and four-year colleges, to help students gain AI skills useful for workplaces. 

“RAISE has had a lot of success with scaling already,” Breazeal says, noting that about 1 million students were involved with RAISE’s Day of AI event earlier this year. “At MIT, we want to empower youth voices to shape the future. It’s an excellent example of our ability to do that.”

And in the third topic area, MIT for America can help produce substantial growth in programs aimed at hands-on learning. That may include more projects such as MIT’s Regenerative Futures Challenge, a global program stemming from MIT’s pK-12 Initiative, which give students the opportunity to create climate and sustainability solutions. Additionally, the Fab Foundation, which grew out of MIT’s Center for Bits and Atoms Fab Lab program, offers tools and curriculum to learners at 300 fab labs across the U.S.

“It’s about coming together in places where there are people who can work together, mentor each other, and learn by example,” Klopfer says. “That’s the kind of thing we want to be creating at scale. We want to build on that.”

All told, MIT for America represents a vigorous all-campus effort to enhance education through sustained outreach and knowledge-sharing. At MIT, partners in creating the initiative include the MIT Media Lab; MIT RAISE; the MIT pK-12 Initiative; the Office of the Vice President for Resource Development; and the Office of Innovation and Strategy.

The leaders of MIT for America presented an overview of the program in September at MIT’s Alumni Leadership Conference, and they say alumni activity around the new initiative will be another key to its success. 

“We really appreciate the support and engagement of our alumni,” Breazeal says. “We know they care about K-12 education and access to community colleges.” More broadly, she adds, “We do think this message will resonate with people all across the country.”

“I look forward to watching these programs flourish, evolve, and grow,” Kornbluth wrote to the community.

text:
Maddow To Clinton: Investigate FBI Over Seizing Voting Machines... So They Stop ‘That Kind Of Stuff’

Hillary Clinton interviewed Rachel Maddow in New York City about Maddow’s new Department of Justice book one week after the midterm elections. Their conversation aired on The Rachel Maddow Show. Maddow reportedly earns $25 million a year for this kind of stuff.

Apparently, Clinton’s decades as first lady, senator, and secretary of state were preparation for a lesson on Washington, D.C., from Rachel Maddow.

Clinton began:

“One thing that didn’t happen in this election, the dog that didn’t bark, thank goodness, um, was our fear about massive disruption of the elections, of undermining, uh, voters’ right to have their vote cast and their vote counted.And I go to, uh, the book where you write about what happened in 2020, where again, Bill Barr claimed mail-in fraud with no evidence, none, and basically said, I don’t need evidence. I, I have common sense. And then he ordered, um, fraud investigations, which led to the head of the election crimes, uh, branch 

Now for the last two years, this administration and this Justice Department have done a lot. They’ve seized ballots, they have threatened state election officials. So it’s not for the lack of trying that they were, you know, attempting to intimidate both voters and election officials, but why didn’t it work this time?”

Clinton then offered an answer to her own question:

“You know, we had really good lawyers who were defending elections and we had, you know, voters turning out en masse. Um. And do you worry that there’s gonna be any shenanigans between the certification of the winners and the winners being seated, uh, in, uh, the weeks ahead?”

Collecting ballots as evidence does not establish voter intimidation. Clinton presented that conclusion without establishing it in this exchange.

Maddow singled out the FBI’s collection of 2020 election ballots from Fulton County, Georgia:

“There should be an investigation there. We need to know what happened there.”

She continued:

“It’s not normal for the FBI to go seize ballots. It’s not normal for the FBI to go to Puerto Rico and seize their voting machines. It’s not normal for the staff at the Homeland Security Cyber Security Agency, CISA, which they’ve gutted, to be told to obtain a voting machine and learn how to hack it and then say nothing about it publicly, but report what they’ve done and how they did it to the White House.”

Maddow’s idea of what’s “normal” doesn’t decide what the FBI can lawfully investigate. Election records should not be off-limits just because Democrats object.

Then came the warning:

“If that’s the stuff you’ve been doing, you need to know you’re gonna have to answer for it and you’re never gonna get away with it.”

But her clearest statement was about what she wanted those investigations to accomplish:

“The investigations of what they’ve already done, I think, are just important so that they stop doing that kind of stuff.”

So that they stop doing that kind of stuff.” Among the actions Maddow wants investigated are the FBI’s collection of Fulton County ballots and voting machines in Puerto Rico. She portrays those actions as election interference and wants it to end.

Investigating possible election crimes is part of government accountability, too.

Clinton and Maddow cannot turn an investigation into election interference simply by calling it that. The demand should be to follow the evidence—not to stop looking.

Hillary Clinton cited Rachel Maddow’s own book while interviewing her. A former secretary of state and a cable host sat together reinforcing each other’s arguments about election fraud while talking about government accountability.

Our media is hopeless.

Judge Edwards took the bond request under advisement and asked the attorneys to obtain additional information concerning Starr's medical treatment in custody.

text:
Below is a list of some of the national, international, global and local observances for November 16, 2026:

Odd Socks Day (United Kingdom and British Overseas Territories) opens Anti-Bullying Week by encouraging people to wear mismatched socks as a low-cost, visible celebration of individuality; it was created in 2017 by children’s presenter Andy Day and the Anti-Bullying Alliance. In 2026 the week runs November 16–20 under the theme “Break the Silence,” and more than five million children participated in the prior year’s observance.

National Fast Food Day celebrates the convenience, cultural footprint, and sheer volume of quick-service meals that reshaped American eating habits, tracing back to White Castle’s 1921 assembly-line nickel burgers in Wichita. Merriam-Webster first entered the term “fast food” in 1951, and Americans now consume roughly 50 billion burgers a year—enough, stacked end to end, to circle the Earth more than thirty times.

National Button Day honors both the practical fastener and the organized hobby of button collecting, formalized when the National Button Society formed in 1938 after Depression-era radio and hobby-show interest. In 2001 Guinness World Records certified Dalton Stevens of South Carolina as holding the largest collection: 439,900 unique buttons with no duplicates, earning him the lasting nickname “the Button King.”

Have a Party With Your Bear Day invites children and adults to stage imaginary parties with stuffed bears, treating the toys as full guests and sparking elaborate pretend play. The date aligns with the November 16, 1902, Washington Post cartoon by Clifford Berryman that showed President Theodore Roosevelt refusing to shoot a tethered black bear; that image directly inspired Morris Michtom’s first commercial “Teddy’s Bear.”

International Day for Tolerance, proclaimed by the UN General Assembly in 1996, promotes active respect and appreciation of cultural diversity rather than mere indifference, rooted in UNESCO’s 1995 Declaration of Principles on Tolerance. The same calendar date also marks the 1945 signing of UNESCO’s constitution in London, linking the observance to the organization’s founding mission of building peace in the minds of people.

International Check Your Wipers Day (also observed as National Check Your Wipers Day in North America) reminds drivers to inspect and replace windshield wipers before winter travel, launched in 2021 by Michelin and National Day Calendar and expanded internationally the following year. A Michelin survey found that 92 percent of drivers agree worn blades impair visibility, yet 90 percent do not regularly check them and more than half do not know the proper inspection method.

National Indiana Day offers an unofficial November celebration of the Hoosier State—the 19th admitted to the Union—highlighting its crossroads geography, basketball culture, and the Indianapolis 500. The official statutory Indiana Day remains December 11 (the 1816 admission anniversary), and the origin of the nickname “Hoosier” is still unexplained despite centuries of use.

Clarinet Day (also called World Clarinet Day) celebrates the single-reed woodwind whose modern form was refined around 1700 in Germany by Johann Christoph Denner from the earlier chalumeau. The instrument’s chameleon range lets it voice the duck in Prokofiev’s Peter and the Wolf, anchor Benny Goodman’s jazz, and appear in over a dozen specialized sizes from the tiny E-flat to the contrabass.

National Press Day (India) commemorates the 1966 establishment of the Press Council of India and underscores the role of free, ethical journalism in a democracy. The Council was created specifically to preserve press freedom while setting standards of responsibility, and the date is marked each year with seminars on media ethics and recognition of journalistic excellence.

National Slobber Appreciation Day raises awareness of the natural drooling of certain large-breed dogs (especially Newfoundlands) so that owners understand the trait rather than surrender pets over unexpected mess. It was started in 2012 by a Newfoundland enthusiast to turn a common complaint into a point of breed education and acceptance.

American Education Week begins on this Monday and runs through November 22, 2026 (the week preceding Thanksgiving), focusing national attention on the work of public schools, teachers, and support staff. The observance dates to 1921 and was jointly launched by the National Education Association and the American Legion to strengthen community support for education after World War I.

National Geography Awareness Week also starts today and continues through November 20, 2026 (the third full week of November), promoting geographic literacy across classrooms and communities. Organized for decades by the National Geographic Society and partners, the week highlights how spatial thinking shapes everything from climate adaptation to everyday navigation.

text:
Scout Motors tops 212,000 reservations for upcoming trucks and SUVs

Volkswagen-backed Scout Motors has received approximately 212,000 reservations for its upcoming Terra pickup and Traveler SUV, and CEO Scott Keogh says the total could exceed 400,000 before customer production begins. The reservation mix is notable: about 87% are for extended-range electric vehicles (EREVs), while roughly 75% are for the Traveler SUV. Scout plans to launch its EREV models ahead of the all-electric versions.

The company’s $2 billion South Carolina plant is about 85% complete, with production expected to begin in 2027 and customer deliveries scheduled for 2028. Both vehicles are expected to start below $60,000 before incentives, with EREV versions targeting more than 500 miles of range. The early demand and strong preference for range-extender technology offer automakers and dealers a useful signal about how shoppers are weighing electrification, range confidence, and price.

The Architect’s Challenge: Achieving Expressive Texture Without Compromising Performance
Modern architecture demands material honesty. You’re designing homes that celebrate natural wood, not hide it behind flat facades. Yet selecting between textured profiles means navigating competing demands: visual richness, structural integrity, weather exposure, and long-term maintenance.

Architects working in the contemporary space know the tension well. A design that relies on expressive wood textures to create warmth and visual interest must also withstand Texas weather-intense sun, humidity swings, and occasional freeze-thaw cycles. Choosing the wrong profile compromises either aesthetics or durability. Choosing poorly sourced material undermines both.

We understand this challenge because we work with firms like Lake|Flato and Page every project. These practices treat wood texture as a design language, not an afterthought. That means your supplier must deliver consistent, high-quality material in the exact profile your design demands, backed by real performance data and sourcing transparency.
The right material choice elevates a home from nice to distinctive. Poor material choice creates callbacks, warranty disputes, and damaged client relationships.

What Sets Fluted Wall Paneling and Comb-Profile Siding Apart

Fluted wall paneling features parallel, evenly-spaced grooves running vertically across the board face. These grooves create shadow lines that deepen with angle and light, generating visual texture without raised edges. The profile sits flat to the substrate, making it a natural choice for accent walls, interior-exterior transitions, and areas where you want dramatic effect without structural complication.
Comb-profile siding uses alternating raised ridges and grooves-like a comb’s teeth. This profile delivers more aggressive shadow play and pronounced tactile texture. The raised portions create genuine three-dimensionality, which can catch water and debris more readily but also provides superior visual drama at distance.

The practical difference matters: fluted paneling sits proud of the substrate by minimal amounts, simplifying flashing and trim. Comb-profile siding’s raised ridges require more thoughtful flashing details, especially at penetrations and transitions. Neither approach is wrong; the choice depends on your design intent and site conditions.

We stock both profiles in the same premium species-clear and vertical grain Western Red Cedar, hemlock, Douglas fir, and cypress-so your selection reflects pure design preference, not material availability.

Material Quality and Species Selection: Where Our Inventory Leads

Species choice determines how texture reads in real light. Fluted patterns in tight-grain Douglas fir or hemlock emphasize linearity; the same profile in wide-grain Southern Yellow Pine creates visual complexity as growth rings interact with the grooves.
Clear and vertical grain cedar brings warmth and tonal consistency that lets texture dominate the visual story. We prioritize vertical grain specifically because it minimizes movement and cupping-critical for fluted or comb profiles where profile integrity directly affects shadow quality. Horizontal grain cedar tends to distort over time, softening the designed texture into an uncontrolled appearance.

Hemlock offers similar stability with cooler undertones. Douglas fir delivers durability plus the visual pop that contemporary designs often demand. Cypress provides unmatched rot resistance in areas exposed to ground contact or constant moisture.

For projects requiring maximum durability without traditional softwood grain patterns, our inventory includes thermally modified ash, pine, and poplar-materials engineered to resist cupping and movement while accepting fluted or comb profiles that maintain crisp lines across decades.

We also stock hardwood alternatives: Ipe, Cumaru, Garapa, and Massaranduba. These deliver dimensional stability and natural resistance that eliminates finish concerns, though their density requires precision milling to achieve true fluted clarity. Tigerwood bridges the gap-harder than traditional softwoods yet machinable enough for detailed profiles.

Your species selection should reflect exposure, maintenance philosophy, and the specific visual character your design demands. We help you match intention to material.

Durability and Weather Resistance: A Head-to-Head Comparison

Fluted paneling’s minimal profile variance means water drains predictably. Grooves funnel moisture downward without pooling in ridges. This translates to simpler finishing strategies and lower maintenance burden. Paint or stain adheres more uniformly because you’re coating flat surfaces plus vertical wall areas, not complex three-dimensional geometry.
Comb-profile siding’s raised ridges create horizontal ledges where moisture can collect momentarily before draining. Quality installation with proper flashing mitigates this risk, but the profile demands more rigorous detailing at roof lines, window heads, and horizontal transitions. The tradeoff: comb profiles handle freeze-thaw cycles well because the raised ridges allow expansion and contraction without buckling the overall plane.

Both profiles perform well in Texas climate when specified correctly. Cypress and cedar naturally resist moisture damage. Douglas fir and hemlock require proper finish systems-we recommend exterior-grade primers and two-coat paint systems for maximum durability. Thermally modified materials eliminate finish concerns almost entirely; the thermal treatment changes wood structure at the cellular level, essentially rendering the material rot and cupping resistant without surface coatings.

WUI (Wildland Urban Interface) Class A fire-rated options exist for both profiles if your project sits in high-risk areas around Austin Hill Country or similar zones. These materials meet stringent fire ratings without sacrificing the texture-rich aesthetic your design requires.

Aesthetic Impact and Design Flexibility: Creating Distinctive Exteriors

Fluted paneling works brilliantly for continuous wall expression, feature walls, and large uninterrupted surfaces. The repeating groove pattern reads as intentional rhythm from distance; up close, it invites tactile engagement. Contemporary homes often leverage fluted walls to create visual lightness-the parallel lines recede, making substantial walls feel less massive.
Comb-profile siding delivers presence. It reads aggressively from twenty feet away, making modest elevations feel architecturally significant. This profile suits accent applications, feature areas, and homes where you want wood to dominate the visual narrative.

The interplay between profile and lighting is crucial. South and west-facing fluted walls in morning light read completely different from east or north exposures. Comb profiles amplify this variation-morning and evening light creates shadow patterns that shift across the elevation. We’ve worked with architects who deliberately specify comb profiles on specific elevations precisely because the light-responsive texture reinforces the home’s connection to its site and time of day.
Color and grain consistency interact with profile selection too. Wide-variation stain palettes pair well with comb profiles (the ridges absorb color variation naturally). High-clarity natural finishes or paint colors demand vertical grain material and tight milling tolerances, where fluted profiles maximize the payoff.

Sustainability and FSC Certification: Our Commitment to Responsible Sourcing

Contemporary architecture demands material integrity at every level-including sourcing. We supply FSC certified wood products across our full inventory: clear and vertical grain cedar, hemlock, Douglas fir, cypress, and all hardwood species.

FSC certification ensures responsible forest management, fair labor practices, and community benefit. For architects seeking LEED credits or simply designing with material honesty, FSC verification matters. We maintain full chain-of-custody documentation; you receive our certified material with sourcing transparency your clients deserve.
Thermally modified products add another sustainability dimension: these materials extend wood life through thermal treatment rather than chemical processing, reducing finish maintenance across the home’s lifespan. Less maintenance means fewer surface coatings, which benefits both durability and environmental impact.

Composite alternatives-TimberTech, Trex, and Fiberon products-eliminate wood entirely while delivering texture analogous to fluted or comb profiles. These materials suit architects prioritizing zero maintenance and maximum longevity, though they carry different environmental considerations than solid wood. We stock leading brands so your specification reflects authentic design choice, not material limitation.

Installation Considerations and Long-Term Maintenance Requirements

Fluted paneling installation is straightforward: boards attach to standard framing with fastener placement between grooves (fasteners remain hidden). Flashing at transitions requires attention but follows conventional practices. The profile’s simplicity means installers making their first fluted installation still achieve professional results.

Comb-profile siding demands more precision. The raised ridges create potential water intrusion points at fastener holes; quality installation uses stainless steel fasteners and sealant protocols. Flashing complexity increases at roof lines and penetrations because the profile’s three-dimensionality requires customized trim details. Working with installers experienced in textured profiles prevents costly callbacks.
Both profiles benefit from annual inspection: debris accumulation in fluted grooves typically clears with rain, but roof gutters and eaves demand seasonal cleaning. Comb profiles require slightly more attention at horizontal transitions where wind-driven rain might find purchase in ridge-and-valley geometry.

Finish maintenance depends on material selection. Solid wood requires recoating every 5–7 years for painted finishes, longer for stain. Thermally modified materials extend this interval to 10+ years. Hardwoods like Ipe demand minimal maintenance but require professional refinishing if color change occurs. Composite materials require virtually no maintenance beyond occasional cleaning.

We provide detailed maintenance guides for every species and profile combination we supply. Your specification should include these requirements in project documentation so clients understand the material’s care needs upfront.

Why US Lumber Brokers Is Your Definitive Partner for Texture-Rich Designs

You’re designing homes that demand more than standard lumber suppliers provide. We’ve built our business specifically to serve architects and builders pursuing contemporary wood-forward design. Our inventory depth-clear and vertical grain softwoods, premium hardwoods, thermally modified products, fire-rated materials, and leading composite brands-means your specification encounters zero availability friction.

Beyond inventory, we understand the distinction between fluted and comb profiles as design language, not commodity products. We stock both in multiple species, mill custom profiles on request, and provide sourcing transparency through FSC certification and chain-of-custody documentation. When you specify US Lumber Brokers, your material arrives exactly as designed-consistent, high-quality, and backed by suppliers who understand architectural intent.
Our Texas roots matter too. We work with the same architects and builders across Austin, Dallas, Houston, and Hill Country. We know the climate challenges these projects face. We understand the site-specific variations that influence species and profile selection. When you need material advice that reflects genuine regional expertise, not generic industry recommendations, we provide that grounded perspective.

Start your next project with a material consultation. Bring your design intent, site exposure, and maintenance philosophy. We’ll recommend the exact profile, species, and sourcing approach that transforms your textured wood vision into a home that performs beautifully for decades.

Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

What’s the practical difference between fluted wall paneling and comb-profile siding for our Texas climate?

We find that fluted paneling offers deeper, more dramatic shadow lines that photograph exceptionally well for contemporary designs, while comb-profile siding provides a subtler linear texture that weathers more evenly in our intense sun. Both profiles perform well in Texas heat, but fluted designs can trap slightly more moisture in the grooves, so we always recommend specifying species with natural rot resistance like Western Red Cedar or Cypress for those applications. The choice really depends on whether your design calls for bold architectural expression or refined understatement.
Do we stock fluted and comb-profile options in the wood species architects typically specify?
We maintain inventory in vertical grain Western Red Cedar, Douglas Fir, and Hemlock in both profiles, and we can source additional species like Cypress and thermally modified options through our manufacturing relationships. Since we manufacture some of our own products, we also work with architects to create custom profile specifications when a project demands something beyond our standard offerings. Our FSC-certified inventory ensures you’re specifying responsibly sourced material regardless of profile.

Which textured profile requires less maintenance in the long run?
Comb-profile siding generally demands fewer maintenance visits because its shallower grooves shed debris more easily and dry faster after rain, making it ideal for clients who prefer a low-touch approach. Fluted paneling creates that striking architectural impact, but the deeper channels benefit from more frequent cleaning and inspection to prevent moisture accumulation, particularly in shaded exposures. We recommend discussing maintenance expectations with your builders early, as this often influences which profile makes the most sense for specific project locations.

text:
Elon Musk lost a $56 billion pay package to a man who owned 9 Tesla shares. A judge voided the deal, then ordered Tesla to pay that man's lawyers $345 million, after they asked for $5.6 billion.

Then Delaware's Supreme Court gave it all back. By then the package was worth $139 billion. The man with 9 shares got $1.

In the video below, Musk walks on stage right after shareholders voted for his pay a second time: "Hot damn, I love you guys."

In 2018 Tesla's board offered Musk options on 304 million shares, about 9% of the company, if Tesla hit a set of huge targets. It hit every one.

Richard Tornetta, a former heavy metal drummer with 9 shares, sued that same year.

In January 2024 a Delaware judge struck the deal down and called it "unfathomable."

His lawyers asked for $5.6 billion in fees. The judge called that a windfall and gave them $345 million.

In June 2024 shareholders voted for the package again. In December the judge rejected it again.

Musk moved Tesla's legal home from Delaware to Texas.

On December 19, 2025, the Delaware Supreme Court reversed it, unanimously. Throwing the deal out, it said, left Musk "uncompensated for his time and efforts over a period of six years." The lawyers' fee was cut by about 80%. Damages: $1.

Musk said he was "vindicated."

9 shares froze the biggest paycheck in history for 7 years. The final bill for the man who started it: $1.

Did the system protect shareholders, or did 9 shares nearly cost Musk $139 billion?

text:
In an astonishingly dramatic few days, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, leader of the AI revolution, was forced to resign amid a shocking and tawdry sex scandal. And every time it looks like the story has peaked, something even weirder happens. Republican Sen. John Kennedy of Louisiana described the situation as “an intergalactic freak show.” 
 
You can read the juicy bits elsewhere. I’ll discuss second-order effects, and what comes next. 
 
For starters, the markets quivered but didn’t collapse, at least not yet. 
 
Huang was supposedly the most important player in the economy - take a seat, Kevin Warsh, Donald Trump, and whoever is running Iran - so it’s comforting his resignation didn’t blow up everything. 
 
On Thursday, neither the Nasdaq Composite nor the S&P 500 moved much on the news; both fell less than 0.4%. But things got a little spicier Friday, as the story evolved. Both Dell and Super Micro Computer were tied to shipments of AI servers to China, added to the pressure on the AI trade. Nasdaq traded broadly lower. 
 
The good news is that history says companies can thrive without their iconic founder/CEOs. Apple did fine under Tim Cook. Microsoft is two CEOs past Bill Gates and trading near all-time highs. Warren Buffett handed the reins to Greg Abel, and the stock continues to outperform. An Nvidia CEO change seemed unthinkable last week, but no one expected Democratic senators in Texas, Mississippi, and Kansas, either.  
 
Who’s next? For now, CFO Colette Kress is in charge. CEO candidates abound;  Tim Cook is Donald Trump’s choice. How about Eric Schmidt, who once ran Google? Or Rene Haas, CEO of ARM? Some people think the right choice is AMD CEO Lisa Su, who just happens to be Jensen’s first cousin once removed. And there are other family options: Jensen’s kids, Spencer and Madison, both Nvidia execs? There are some Republican senators looking for work. Just saying. 
 
This soap opera will drag on for months or longer. Expect Congressional hearings, national security assessments, and self-reflection on the Street about the wisdom of concentrated control. Bloomberg noted that pricing on Nvidia credit default swaps has soared, suggesting bond market worries. Nvidia sits at the center of a web of deals involving AI companies investing in each other; some implications have yet to be sniffed out. And what will his wife, his kids, and his paramours do? Eventually, all will be revealed. But not just yet.

I don’t want to take sides on this, but I think what he is really trying to say is that the entire transfer culture, which was driven by programs like Bosco and Mater Dei, has created a toxic environment where everyone feels forced to compete at that level. Now we’re seeing that same mentality spread into Texas, where schools are chasing national rankings and recognition and it also create toxic environments out there.

I genuinely believe there are a lot of good coaches, administrators, and parents who hate what this system has become. But they also feel they have no choice but to participate because otherwise, they simply cannot compete. And at the end of the day, so much of this comes back to one thing: Fame

Personally, I think private and public schools should compete separately, and all public schools should operate under the same rules. No loopholes, no special programs like agricultural classes being used to get around transfer restrictions, and no unfair advantages.

And I can say this because I was part of this whole mess myself. Looking back, I genuinely believe I made some mistakes. I bought into the system, the hype, and the idea that this was what you had to do to give your kid the best opportunity. But after everything I’ve experienced and learned, I see things very differently today.

Kids should be kids. They should enjoy high school, build friendships, represent their communities, and create memories that last a lifetime. High school football should be about much more than rankings, transfers, exposure, and chasing stars.

But there is another side to this conversation that we cannot ignore. I happen to live in a beautiful community with great schools. What about the kid growing up in a dangerous neighborhood with a struggling school system? What about the family that sees transferring as an opportunity to give their child a better education, a safer environment, and a chance at a better life? We cannot simply take that opportunity away either. That’s what makes this issue so complicated.

However, one thing I can say with 100% confidence, based on my own experience, is that this obsession with the Trinity League being the best path to college football is complete nonsense.

How do I know? Because I’ve personally met with50+ college coaches, traveled across the country, and experienced the football culture in Texas firsthand. You would be surprised how many college coaches laugh when they hear parents talk about how their kids play in the Trinity League to get recruited.

They don’t care. They care about your film, your physical tools, your development, your academics, and how you perform against the competition in front of you.

I can name several players playing in Division 2 through Division 5 high school programs around here who are nationally ranked and receiving major college offers. Just like in Texas in D3 Would some of those same players would struggle to compete in trinity? Yet they’re the ones getting recruited. That alone should tell parents something about how the system actually works. Play where you would look good vs others. Because you need to get notice first to get there. 

And this is why I think it’s so important for parents like me to speak up. Put your ego aside. Admit when you made mistakes. Share what you’ve learned so other families don’t fall into the same trap.

I am not embarrassed to say that I bought into some of this nonsense myself. I wish my own path as a teenager would of been a different experience, it influence my thinking with all of that. 

The most important thing should be finding a good school, getting an education, building relationships and a network, enjoying your high school years, and eventually earning a college degree. If you’re fortunate enough to have the physical tools, talent, and work ethic to play college football, then absolutely pursue that dream. But football should be an opportunity, not something that takes over your entire childhood.

🧭 SOUTH TARAWA | TRAVEL ESSENTIALS
📍 Getting There

Fly into Bonriki International Airport (TRW), with connections via Nadi, Fiji, or regional services operated by Nauru Airlines. Flights are limited, so confirm schedules before arranging accommodation.

🚌 Getting Around

Local minibuses travel along the main road connecting Bonriki, Bairiki and Betio. They are inexpensive, while hotel-arranged rental cars offer greater flexibility for exploring the causeways.

🗺️ What to Explore

Start in Betio, where coastal guns and bunkers recall the 1943 Battle of Tarawa. Continue through Bairiki's government district and along the lagoon shoreline. For a quieter island experience, consider a boat excursion to North Tarawa, subject to tides and weather.

⏱️ Time Needed & Accommodation

Allow 1–2 days for South Tarawa's main sights, with an additional day for North Tarawa. Accommodation consists mainly of modest hotels and guesthouses; advance reservations are advisable.

🌤️ When to Visit & Costs

Conditions are warm year-round, with rainfall varying considerably. May–October is generally less rainy, though weather remains unpredictable.

The Australian dollar is used locally. Confirm current airfares, accommodation rates and boat arrangements before departure.

text:
THE NEXT SPACE ECONOMY | 6 SPACE & CONNECTIVITY STOCKS TO WATCH
The next major opportunity in the space economy may not come from the biggest aerospace companies. It could come from businesses building the infrastructure behind satellite communications, Earth observation, and next-generation global connectivity.

United Airlines CEO Scott Kirby recently highlighted Starlink as a competitive advantage, noting that the airline is already seeing customers move from competitors. While the evidence remains largely anecdotal, it highlights an important trend: satellite connectivity is becoming increasingly valuable in commercial markets.

Here are 6 companies worth watching:

1. $ASTS — AST SpaceMobile
Building a space-based cellular broadband network designed to connect directly with standard smartphones. Its direct-to-device technology could expand mobile coverage beyond traditional terrestrial networks. Commercial execution, satellite deployment, and funding requirements remain important factors to monitor.

2. $PL — Planet Labs
Operates a large Earth-imaging satellite constellation, providing geospatial intelligence and frequently updated satellite imagery. Its data has potential applications across defense, agriculture, infrastructure, and logistics.

3. $LUNR — Intuitive Machines
Focused on lunar exploration, space infrastructure, and communications services. Its exposure to NASA programs and the developing lunar economy creates significant long-term opportunities, alongside substantial execution and contract risks.

4. $RDW — Redwire
Provides critical space infrastructure, avionics, solar power systems, and other technologies supporting commercial and government space missions. Growing investment in orbital infrastructure could create additional demand for its capabilities.

5. $BKSY — BlackSky
Develops real-time geospatial intelligence and satellite-based monitoring capabilities for defense, intelligence, and commercial customers. Its analytics platform could benefit from increasing demand for timely, actionable intelligence.

6. $GOGO — Gogo
A provider of in-flight connectivity for business aviation. Its expansion into low-Earth-orbit satellite connectivity through Gogo Galileo could create new opportunities to strengthen its aviation communications business.

THE BIGGER PICTURE

The space economy is evolving beyond rockets and satellite launches.

Some of the most important opportunities may emerge across:

Direct-to-device satellite connectivity

Earth observation and geospatial intelligence
Lunar infrastructure and communications
Orbital manufacturing and space systems
Defense and government satellite applications
In-flight and global broadband connectivity
These six companies offer exposure to different parts of this developing industry.

The potential is significant, but so are the risks. Capital requirements, execution, dilution, competition, regulatory approvals, and valuation all deserve close attention. A compelling industry trend does not automatically translate into a successful investment.

I'll continue tracking these names as the space and connectivity markets develop.

Research First. Discipline Always.

text:
The Ship and the Bed

I wrote Homer had autonomous ships at the top of the page, then spent the next hour trying to deserve the sentence.

The Phaeacian ships know where people want to go. They know cities and countries, cross the sea without an ordinary pilot, and carry Odysseus to Ithaca while he sleeps. There are still rowers, which spoiled the little picture I had already made of an empty vessel slipping through the dark. Somebody still has to do the work. I had removed them almost immediately, before I had even finished being impressed.

That seems worth keeping in the notes. The first thing I did with an ancient imagining was improve its resemblance to something I already understood.

There is a whole afternoon available down that road: ancient artificial intelligence, drugs concealed in myths, lost technologies waiting for us to recognize them. Some comparisons might be useful. But the poems have passed through too many mouths and centuries to behave like a report recovered from one particular morning in the Bronze Age. An old object, a familiar workshop, a god's invention and somebody's remembered war can occupy the same few lines. I keep wanting to pull out the oldest thread and call it the original cloth.

Even the hiss when the Cyclops is blinded needs care. The weapon is wood; the iron tool plunged into water belongs to the simile. There is practical knowledge in that comparison. Somebody knew the sound from a workshop, and now it makes the violence in the cave horribly audible. I don't need to turn the passage into a lost metallurgy paper to find that remarkable.

Still, the ships won't leave me alone. A vessel that understands an intention and supplies the route is close enough to my own work to make me lean forward. I have spent evenings watching little computational creatures find their way through worlds I built for them, usually discovering too late that I had rewarded something other than what I wanted. The Phaeacians seem to have solved the navigation problem rather elegantly. Tell the ship where. Go to sleep.

Then I remembered how much of the poem remains after the journey is over.

Odysseus can be delivered to the right shore and still have a great deal of getting home to do. His household has continued in his absence. His wife has lived through years he cannot give back to her, making decisions without knowing whether he will ever return. Now she has to decide whether to believe the man in front of her. His arrival gives her another uncertainty before it gives her anything back.

I drew a line under destination. It was beginning to look like the wrong end of the problem.

Earlier, the Lotus-Eaters offer a quieter danger than shipwreck. A person can remain alive and lose the wish to return. That troubles the neat little model in which a goal sits safely inside an agent while the world supplies obstacles outside it. What happens if the world changes the goal? Or changes the memories through which the goal made sense? I can check whether a creature reaches the square I marked. I have less idea what I would be checking if it could forget why that square had mattered.

The Sirens complicate this further. They offer knowledge, including knowledge of Troy. I recognize the temptation more readily than I would like. There is always another connection to follow, another answer that might make the whole arrangement clear. Odysseus has himself tied down before he listens. His earlier decision survives the desires of the man who hears the song. I keep circling that: which version of a person gets to decide?

Yet keeping everything would be no solution either. The poem ends with the danger of further vengeance; the dead leave relatives, and victory provides fresh reasons to kill. A settlement has to interrupt that continuation. Memory can keep the journey alive and keep the violence alive. I can't make a rule for it without first asking whose memory, of what, and what they intend to do next.

By now the ship has become the easy part, which is unfair to anyone who has ever built a ship.

What stays with me is Penelope's test. Odysseus made their bed around a rooted olive tree. When she speaks of moving it, his response reaches into something they know together. A face can be altered, a convincing story assembled, but here is knowledge with a history behind it: the making of a room, the work of his hands, a marriage that happened somewhere particular.

I had started to label these things as recognition mechanisms. Scar. Shared secret. Evidence of identity. The labels are useful, but I notice how quickly the room disappears when I put them on. The tree becomes a password. Penelope becomes the person checking it. Once again I have made the old thing easier to fit inside my work, and smaller in the process.

Perhaps this is what I want to investigate next. I know how to give a creature a destination. I can put something in its way and measure whether it gets there. But the bed belongs to two people. Whatever I put in that square, it cannot answer for the person waiting at the other end.

At the bottom of the page I drew the ship again. This time I put the rowers in. Beside it I left space for the house.
