FREE SPORTS PICKS - MONDAY, NOVEMBER 16, 2026

MONDAY NIGHT FOOTBALL, NBA, COLLEGE BASKETBALL AND NHL FREE PICKS!

Monday’s PicksDepot betting card features 20 free selections from professional sports handicappers. The headliner is Los Angeles Chargers at Baltimore Ravens on Monday Night Football, where handicappers are divided on both the point spread and the total.

Today’s NBA selections include Chicago-Cleveland, Memphis-Washington and Houston-Miami. College basketball offers three early-season opportunities, while the NHL card features Montreal-New York and Vancouver-Utah.

Every selection is credited to the individual handicapper who released it, with the published line, betting analysis and important matchup considerations. Several handicappers disagree on the same games, making line shopping particularly important. Prices can change before game time.

NFL FREE PICKS - MONDAY NIGHT FOOTBALL

LOS ANGELES CHARGERS AT BALTIMORE RAVENS - 8:15 PM ET

Baltimore’s quarterback situation dominates tonight’s matchup. Newly acquired Jacoby Brissett is expected to make his Ravens debut after the offense struggled badly without Lamar Jackson. Baltimore has scored 13 or fewer points in four consecutive games, but the Chargers have also struggled defensively, allowing 44 points to Houston in their previous contest.

Los Angeles counters with Justin Herbert, whose finger imaging reportedly came back negative. The Chargers have experienced serious pass-protection problems, however, and Herbert faces another difficult assignment against a Baltimore defense looking to recover its earlier form.

The free-pick board includes opposing selections on Baltimore -4.5 and Los Angeles +4.5 or +5, along with Over 38.5 and Unders at 39 and 39.5.

HUNTER PRICE - CHARGERS/RAVENS OVER 38.5 (-110)

Price backs a higher-scoring game despite both offenses experiencing recent difficulties. The total reflects Baltimore’s offensive collapse without Jackson, but the arrival of Brissett introduces a different quarterback profile and the possibility of more consistent passing production.

The Ravens still have Derrick Henry, Zay Flowers and Mark Andrews available as established offensive weapons. Meanwhile, the Chargers’ defense has allowed substantial production in recent games. This wager needs only 39 combined points, a relatively modest threshold if Brissett can stabilize Baltimore’s passing game and Herbert generates enough offense for Los Angeles.

DUSTIN HAWKINS - CHARGERS/RAVENS UNDER 39.5 (-115)

Hawkins takes the opposite approach, backing the Under at 39.5. Baltimore’s quarterback transition does not guarantee an immediate offensive improvement, especially against an opponent that can pressure the passer and force difficult third-down situations.

The Chargers’ offensive line has struggled to protect Herbert, while Baltimore’s offense has repeatedly failed to produce sustained scoring drives. If both teams emphasize field position, avoid unnecessary risks and settle for field goals rather than touchdowns, the scoring could remain below 40 points. The extra point compared with Under 38.5 provides meaningful protection.

BRODY VAUGHN - LOS ANGELES CHARGERS +4.5 (-108) AT BALTIMORE

Vaughn backs Los Angeles as a road underdog, getting more than a field goal against a Baltimore team still adjusting to its quarterback situation. The Ravens may benefit from Brissett’s experience, but installing a new starter creates uncertainty regarding offensive timing and execution.

Herbert gives the Chargers an established quarterback capable of keeping a game competitive, even when pass protection becomes a problem. The wager does not require Los Angeles to win outright. A Ravens victory by four points or fewer would still cash the Chargers +4.5.

MAX CHASE - LOS ANGELES CHARGERS +4.5 (-108) AT BALTIMORE

Chase joins Vaughn on Los Angeles at the same spread and price. Baltimore enters having lost four consecutive games, with its offensive struggles making it difficult to assume the Ravens can create substantial separation.

The Chargers’ defensive problems are a concern, particularly against Henry and Baltimore’s rushing attack, but the betting question is whether the Ravens deserve to be favored by more than four points while introducing a new quarterback.

Los Angeles needs to protect Herbert, avoid turnovers that create short fields and remain competitive into the fourth quarter. A one-possession game would give the underdog a realistic opportunity to cover.

COLE FAXON - CHARGERS/RAVENS UNDER 39.5 (-115)

Faxon also expects a relatively low-scoring Monday night game. Baltimore has averaged just 14.6 points across its previous five contests, according to the offensive numbers published with the matchup, and has failed to reach 14 points in four straight games.

Brissett’s arrival could improve the offense, but the Ravens still need to establish passing-game chemistry. On the other side, Herbert has absorbed considerable pressure behind a struggling offensive line.

Both teams have reasons to avoid unnecessary turnovers and protect field position. The Under 39.5 wins with 39 or fewer combined points and offers a better scoring threshold than Under 39.

BOBBY CONN - BALTIMORE RAVENS -4.5 (-110) VS. LOS ANGELES CHARGERS

Conn backs Baltimore to win by at least five points at home. The Ravens have struggled offensively, but replacing rookie Joe Fagnano with veteran Brissett could improve decision-making and give the offense a more dependable passing presence.

Baltimore still possesses dangerous skill-position personnel. Henry can force defenses to commit additional resources against the run, potentially creating opportunities for Flowers and Andrews.

The Chargers have allowed 27.4 points per game this season and are coming off a difficult defensive performance against Houston. Conn’s selection depends on Baltimore taking advantage of those weaknesses while preventing Herbert from keeping Los Angeles within one possession.

TIMOTHY BLACK - LOS ANGELES CHARGERS +5 (-110) AT BALTIMORE

Black backs Los Angeles with five points, obtaining a slightly larger cushion than the handicappers holding +4.5.

That half-point difference matters. A five-point Baltimore victory would push Chargers +5 but lose at +4.5. In a game with a relatively low total, every point becomes more valuable because fewer scoring possessions can make it difficult for either team to build a comfortable margin.

Herbert’s ability to generate scoring opportunities despite protection issues is critical. Baltimore’s recent offensive difficulties also strengthen the case that the Ravens could win without necessarily covering a spread of this size.

BLACK WIDOW - BALTIMORE RAVENS -4.5 (-110) VS. LOS ANGELES CHARGERS

Black Widow joins Conn on the Baltimore favorite, publishing the selection as a free Wiseguy play. The handicapper is taking the position that the Ravens’ home-field advantage, established offensive personnel and quarterback adjustment will be sufficient to overcome their recent struggles.

Baltimore’s defense also has an opportunity against a Chargers offensive line that has allowed substantial quarterback pressure. If the Ravens can disrupt Herbert and generate favorable field position, they could create the separation needed to cover.

The principal risk is another inefficient Baltimore offensive performance. Even a Ravens victory may not be enough if the game remains within four points.

STEVE JANUS - CHARGERS/RAVENS OVER 38.5 (-110)

Janus backs the Over at 38.5, joining Hunter Price on the same selection. The wager reflects the possibility that Baltimore’s recent offensive struggles have depressed the total beyond what the current matchup deserves.

Brissett is a veteran quarterback taking over an offense with established rushing and receiving options. Los Angeles also has the ability to generate offense through Herbert, even if its protection is inconsistent.

The Ravens have allowed substantial scoring during their recent losing streak, and the Chargers surrendered 44 points to Houston last week. Either defense creating turnovers or short fields could help push the combined score beyond 38.5.

JIMMY BOYD - CHARGERS/RAVENS OVER 38.5 (-110)

Boyd offers one of the more detailed arguments for the Over. He believes the market is placing too much emphasis on Baltimore’s recent offensive results, which were produced during a difficult period of quarterback instability.

Fagnano threw for only 60 yards against Jacksonville, averaging 3.3 yards per attempt with two interceptions. Brissett brings substantially more NFL starting experience and previously demonstrated the ability to move the football through the air.

Boyd also emphasizes the defenses. Baltimore has allowed approximately 28 points per game over its previous five contests, including 33 against Jacksonville, 36 against Buffalo and 35 against Cincinnati. Los Angeles is allowing 27.4 points per game this season.

Herbert’s finger imaging was encouraging, and the Chargers have multiple receiving options even with uncertainty surrounding Ladd McConkey. Boyd believes 38.5 is too low considering the defensive vulnerabilities and Baltimore’s quarterback upgrade.

ANDREW GOLD - CHARGERS/RAVENS UNDER 39 (-108)

Gold completes the group of Under selections, targeting a total of 39 at slightly better odds than the handicappers taking Under 39.5.

Baltimore’s recent offensive production raises reasonable questions about whether a quarterback change can immediately solve its problems. Los Angeles has also struggled to protect Herbert, and another game featuring heavy pressure could limit sustained drives.

The scoring threshold is important. Under 39 wins with 38 or fewer combined points and pushes at exactly 39. That makes it less attractive numerically than Under 39.5, although Gold’s -108 price is slightly better than the -115 attached to the higher number.

The matchup presents a genuine disagreement among PicksDepot handicappers: some expect Brissett to improve Baltimore’s offense immediately, while others believe quarterback transitions and pass-protection problems will keep scoring limited.

COLLEGE BASKETBALL FREE PICKS

BRIAN BITLER - RICHMOND +13.5 (-116) AT VIRGINIA TECH - 7:00 PM ET

Bitler backs Richmond with nearly 14 points against unbeaten Virginia Tech. The Hokies enter 4-0 and recently defeated Mount St. Mary’s 82-62, but Richmond has demonstrated considerable offensive potential during its 3-1 start.

The Spiders scored 100 points against UNC Asheville and 107 against Southern Virginia. Dominick Stewart has emerged as an important offensive contributor and scored 25 points in Richmond’s 80-70 loss to Southern Illinois.

Virginia Tech has the stronger defensive profile and can create additional opportunities through turnovers. The Hokies forced 23 turnovers against Mount St. Mary’s, which represents an important concern for Richmond.

However, Bitler believes the spread is excessive for an early-season nonconference game against a capable offensive opponent. Virginia Tech could control the contest and win by double digits without covering 13.5.

ROCKY ATKINSON - MINNESOTA -33.5 (-109) VS. WESTERN ILLINOIS - 8:00 PM ET

Atkinson backs Minnesota to produce a decisive home victory against Western Illinois. The Golden Gophers enter 4-0, while Western Illinois is 1-3.

Minnesota recently defeated Southern University 91-61, shooting 60% from the field and connecting on 13 three-pointers. Isaac Asuma contributed 23 points, while the Gophers dominated the rebounding battle 40-21.

Atkinson cites a historical system involving substantial home favorites with strong three-point shooting facing opponents with weak perimeter shooting. He reports the qualifying situation has produced a 52-22 record, covering 70.3%, since 1998.

The challenge is the enormous spread. Minnesota must win by at least 34 points, which requires consistent offensive execution and defensive intensity even if the result is no longer in doubt. Atkinson recommends a smaller play rather than treating the historical record as a guarantee.

MATT SULLIVAN - ABILENE CHRISTIAN/MISSOURI STATE OVER 141.5 (-110) - 8:00 PM ET

Sullivan backs the Over in Abilene Christian’s visit to Missouri State. The Bears enter 3-0 after scoring 88, 79 and 89 points in their first three games. However, all three victories came against Division II competition, making the offensive results difficult to project directly against a Division I opponent.

Abilene Christian enters 1-2 and recently lost 76-71 to Stephen F. Austin. The Wildcats have shown they can contribute offensively but have also experienced defensive problems, allowing 94 points against Colorado and 81 against Lamar.

Missouri State’s offensive size and interior opportunities could create favorable scoring chances, while Abilene Christian needs to contribute enough to make the Over attainable.

The selection needs 142 combined points. With such an early-season matchup, shooting efficiency, turnovers and pace will be particularly important in determining whether the teams can clear that number.

NBA FREE PICKS

BRANDON LEE - CHICAGO BULLS +9.5 (-102) AT CLEVELAND CAVALIERS - 7:10 PM ET

Lee backs Chicago with a substantial cushion against Cleveland. The Bulls have shown signs of improvement after a difficult stretch, recently defeating Atlanta 125-117 in overtime and Minnesota 117-106.

Cleveland has its own personnel questions. Evan Mobley is listed out with a toe injury, removing an important defensive presence and rebounder from the Cavaliers’ frontcourt. Donovan Mitchell, James Harden and Jarrett Allen could provide Cleveland with additional offensive strength after missing the previous game, making final availability important.

The Bulls’ argument rests on recent improvement and the significant point spread. Chicago does not need to win outright; a defeat by nine points or fewer would cash.

The published -102 price is also attractive compared with standard -110 odds, although Cleveland’s offensive ceiling remains a serious concern for anyone backing the underdog.

INFO PLAYS - WASHINGTON WIZARDS +5.5 (-110) VS. MEMPHIS GRIZZLIES - 7:10 PM ET

Info Plays backs Washington despite the Wizards entering on a seven-game losing streak. Memphis has been the stronger team, starting 9-4 overall and winning its first six road games.

Washington is coming off a 147-119 defeat against Houston in which the Rockets dominated the middle quarters and controlled the rebounding battle. Alex Sarr has been a productive contributor for the Wizards, but Washington needs better overall defensive execution to remain competitive.

Memphis has demonstrated consistent road performance, making the Grizzlies a difficult opponent to oppose. However, Info Plays receives 5.5 points with the home team, creating room for Washington to lose a relatively competitive contest and still cover.

The Wizards must improve their transition defense, avoid allowing Memphis easy second-chance points and keep the game close through the third quarter. The published number is particularly important because some broader-market prices have been shorter.

MIKE LUNDIN - HOUSTON ROCKETS/MIAMI HEAT UNDER 231 (-110) - 7:40 PM ET

Lundin believes the total has been inflated by recent scoring performances from both teams. Houston enters on a four-game winning streak, while Miami has recovered from an 0-4 start to win seven of its previous nine games, including four consecutive victories.

Houston just defeated Washington 147-119, with Amen Thompson scoring 26 points and Kevin Durant and Tari Eason adding 25 apiece. That extraordinary offensive performance could encourage bettors to expect another high-scoring contest.

Lundin instead emphasizes Houston’s defensive identity, rebounding and ability to disrupt opposing offensive possessions. He also believes Miami has experienced periods of inconsistent half-court scoring, even during its recent improvement.

The Rockets’ physicality and control of the glass could help reduce second-chance scoring opportunities for Miami. The Heat must also defend more effectively than Washington did in Houston’s previous game.

Lundin expects the recent scoring surge to overstate the likelihood of another offensive explosion. The wager wins with 230 or fewer combined points and pushes at exactly 231.

NHL FREE PICKS

KENNY WALKER - MONTREAL CANADIENS ML -106 AT NEW YORK RANGERS - 7:37 PM ET

Walker backs Montreal in an Original Six matchup at Madison Square Garden. The Canadiens enter 12-4-4 and have been particularly effective away from home, compiling a 7-1-1 road record.

Montreal’s 12-game point streak ended Saturday in a 4-1 loss to Colorado, but the Canadiens remain among the stronger teams in the Eastern Conference. Cole Caufield has provided consistent goal scoring, while Nick Suzuki remains an important offensive contributor.

New York presents a substantial challenge. The Rangers have won five of their previous six games, own an 8-2 home record and have allowed only 2.30 goals per game at Madison Square Garden.

Walker’s selection comes down to Montreal’s impressive road performance and the relatively modest moneyline price. At -106, the Canadiens need to win outright, but bettors are not required to lay heavy favorite odds against a Rangers team playing well at home.

ROB VINCILETTI - UTAH MAMMOTH -1.5 GOALS (-145) VS. VANCOUVER CANUCKS - 9:37 PM ET

Vinciletti backs Utah on the puck line against struggling Vancouver. The Canucks enter 4-17-1, although they snapped a seven-game losing streak Sunday with a 6-3 victory over Vegas.

text:
When the oilfield men of Midland, Texas, finally pulled Baby Jessica out of the ground, they hung a sign on their drilling rig.

It said, "Thank You, America."

On October 14, 1987, 18-month-old Jessica McClure fell into an abandoned well in her aunt's backyard.

The pipe was eight inches wide. She was stuck 22 feet down, one leg pushed up beside her head.

Firemen and police came first. Then the drillers came.

West Texas is oil country. When a little girl is stuck in a hole, the town knows exactly who to call.

The plan sounded simple. Drill a second shaft about five feet away, then dig a tunnel sideways to her.

It was not simple. The rock was so hard it dulled diamond-tipped bits, and dozens of bits broke.

Men took turns lying in the rescue shaft, hammering sideways.

"It drains you a lot because you have to work on your knees," said David Perry, a construction worker.

"Just getting through to her, that's all that's on your mind," he said. "You get tired, you think about her."

While they drilled, they could hear her down there.

She was singing "Winnie the Pooh."

A roofing contractor named Ron Short offered to go down. He was born without collarbones and could fold his shoulders to fit through tight holes.

The team considered it. Special water jet drilling equipment was flown in from Houston to cut the last of the rock.

In the end, paramedic Robert O'Donnell was the one who crawled through the tunnel to her.

"I found out her nickname was Juicy, and she responded to me every time I used it," he said.

They covered her in Vaseline and slid her out feet first.

"She was very alert, very bright-eyed," said Police Sgt. Jeff Haile.

At 7:55 p.m., paramedic Steve Forbes rode up the shaft with her strapped to a backboard.

The whole country was watching live on television.

"We knew we would get her out," said driller Ribble Boler. "I saw her face and it felt real good."

"I don't usually cry, but who cares," said Police Sgt. Andy Glasscock, tears running down his cheeks.

Bruce Peeler had been on the rope line that pulled her up.

"When she reached up and wiped her little eye, it was all worth it."

President Reagan said everybody in America had become her godmothers and godfathers.

Jessica lost one toe. She grew up, got married, and had two kids of her own.

Then the drillers gathered in a circle for cheers and tears.

Above them, the sign on the rig still said three words.

text:
🗞️16 November 2026 | Daily Edition: First Hour

The Open Bought the Dip, the First Hour Sold It

A weak factory print lifted Bitcoin back over its weekly close for minutes, then the Nasdaq slide took it away, while Strategy, Coinbase, ICE and Zelle kept building underneath.

Prepared around 10:40 AM EST on Monday 16 November. This edition picks up from this morning's Pre-Market, prepared at 5:50 AM EST, and covers how crypto took the 8:30 AM EST data and the 9:30 AM EST stock open, plus the crypto stories that landed since. Crypto prices are live prints as of about 10:35 AM EST, and stock, Treasury, oil, dollar and gold figures are live mid-morning prints.

1⃣ Bitcoin reclaimed the weekly close at the bell and lost it within minutes

Bitcoin kept sliding after this morning's edition and made its session low of about $63,830 at 7:30 AM EST, just above Sunday's $63,725 early low. It held near $64,000 to $64,400 through the 8:30 AM EST data, then jumped about 1.9% in the first ten minutes of the stock open, from about $64,420 to $65,630 at 9:35 AM EST. That cleared both the $65,315 weekly close and the $65,480 overnight high, but only briefly: by 9:40 AM EST it was back under the weekly close, and the 10:00 AM EST leg lower in the Nasdaq took it to about $64,035 by 10:15 AM EST. It trades near $64,100, about 0.7% below this morning's edition and about 0.8% lower over 24 hours.

🖊️ Market significance: The open produced a clean test of the level I flagged this morning, and sellers took it back within ten minutes. A round trip of about 2.4% from high to low in under an hour is a liquidity event, not a trend change.

🗨️ My viewpoint: A reclaim has to hold on a closing basis to count. This one did not, so $65,315 stays resistance, and the morning low at $63,830 is now the line that matters.

2⃣ Ether ran harder on the squeeze and gave back more

Ether broke under this morning's $1,790 low at 7:30 AM EST, touching about $1,785, then rallied about 4.5% to $1,865 at 9:35 AM EST, above the $1,842 overnight high. It has since fallen about 3.3% from that peak and trades near $1,804, roughly flat on this morning's edition. Solana is near $70.05 and XRP near $0.944, both slightly below their early levels and lower on the day.

🖊️ Market significance: Ether's bigger swing in both directions tells me the move was driven by short positioning rather than spot demand, since Ether funding had been negative on most venues going into the open.

🗨️ My viewpoint: Ether keeps printing higher bounces off $1,785 to $1,790, which is constructive, but every bounce has failed below the weekly close near $1,835. I need a close above that before I take the relative strength seriously.

3⃣ Shorts covered into the open, and longs are paying again

Open interest fell while price spiked, the signature of short covering. Bitcoin open interest on the largest on-chain perps venue slipped about 0.7% since this morning to roughly 36,220 BTC, and on a large offshore exchange it fell about 3.0% to about 31,710 BTC. Ether open interest dropped about 4.1% on the on-chain venue and about 1.6% offshore. At the same time, Bitcoin funding moved from flat to positive, at about +0.005% to +0.008% per eight hours on the big offshore venues, while Ether funding is mixed around zero.

🖊️ Market significance: The squeeze removed short positions, and the fade back to $64,100 has left longs paying a small premium again at the same price where shorts were being added overnight.

🗨️ My viewpoint: Positive funding at the lows is not the washed-out positioning a durable bottom usually needs. If open interest rebuilds on the long side from here, the next flush has fresh fuel below $63,800.

4⃣ Crypto stocks caught down to the weekend in one session

US-listed crypto equities and funds opened Monday pricing in the weekend slide, since Friday's 4:00 PM EST stock close came with Bitcoin near $68,840, about 7% above where it trades now. By about 10:30 AM EST, Strategy was down about 7.6%, Coinbase about 7.5%, MARA about 7.2% to 7.5%, Circle about 7.0% and Robinhood about 5.6%. BlackRock's IBIT was down about 6.8% and its Ether fund ETHA about 7.3%. Monday's spot ETF flows, the first since last week's $1.065 billion of Bitcoin fund outflows, arrive after this evening's close.

🖊️ Market significance: The equity wrapper is where weekend crypto losses finally hit traditional portfolios, which is why the first ETF flow print after a red weekend carries extra weight.

🗨️ My viewpoint: A 7% gap down in IBIT on a Monday is the kind of print that triggers rebalancing and risk-limit selling. I expect tonight's flow number to be red, and I will treat anything close to flat as a positive surprise.

5⃣ Strategy bought only 485 BTC and spent nearly seven times more retiring STRC

Strategy's Monday filing shows it bought 485 BTC for $33.4 million at an average of $68,887 between 9 and 15 November, taking its holdings to 850,849 BTC at an average cost of $75,452. The bigger number was elsewhere: it repurchased 2,282,510 shares of its STRC preferred stock for $228.1 million, about $99.93 a share, funding $206.3 million of that from common stock sales and $21.8 million from interest on its cash. It has $332.2 million left under its preferred buyback program and reports $4.9 billion of US dollar assets. At $64,100, its Bitcoin is worth about $54.5 billion, roughly 15% below cost.

🖊️ Market significance: The flagship Bitcoin treasury company used most of last week's equity raise to shrink a 12% funding obligation, not to buy Bitcoin.

🗨️ My viewpoint: That is the rational move when your cost of capital is 12% and your asset is in a six-week downtrend, but it also removes the steadiest corporate bid from the market. Treasury buying is now a trickle, not a floor.

6⃣ Strive and Bitmine kept buying, and Tom Lee blamed the IPO calendar

Strive bought 251 BTC for $17.5 million at an average of $69,853, taking its holdings to 43,404 BTC, with $10 million raised through its SATS share program and preferred dividend coverage of 133 months. Bitmine added 7,653 ETH last week and now holds 6,077,745 ETH, about 4.97% of supply, with 5,227,037 ETH, about 86%, staked. Its combined crypto, cash and investments fell to $11.8 billion from $14.5 billion at the start of the month. Chairman Tom Lee called Ether's slide a "waterfall decline in price" that is "not consistent" with the tokenization news flow, and pinned part of it on margin selling in Asia tied to Nvidia and on investors raising cash ahead of Anthropic's planned 18 November pricing.

🖊️ Market significance: Two of the biggest followers of the treasury model are still accumulating, but at a pace that is small next to ETF outflows.

🗨️ My viewpoint: The IPO cash-raise argument is plausible and testable. If Anthropic prices on Wednesday and crypto does not stabilize by the end of the week, that excuse is gone.

7⃣ The Supreme Court ended Custodia's fight for a Fed account

The Supreme Court on Monday morning denied Custodia Bank's petition in its case against the Federal Reserve Board, with no explanation and no noted dissent. That leaves standing the Tenth Circuit's 2 to 1 ruling that regional Fed banks have discretion to refuse master accounts, even to legally eligible institutions. The Wyoming crypto bank applied in October 2020 and was denied by the Kansas City Fed in January 2023. Since then the Fed has floated a narrower "skinny" account, and Kraken's banking unit received a limited-purpose account from the Kansas City Fed.

🖊️ Market significance: Direct access to Fed payment rails for crypto-focused banks now depends on the Fed's discretion and its limited-purpose accounts, not on a legal right.

🗨️ My viewpoint: This closes the litigation path for good. Any future access will come through policy or legislation, and that keeps crypto banks reliant on correspondent banks.

8⃣ Nine senators told the CFTC to back off, the Hyperliquid policy arm backed it

Nine Democratic senators, including Adam Schiff, Amy Klobuchar and Elissa Slotkin, wrote to CFTC Chairman Michael Selig on Monday morning demanding that the agency reverse its 5 November interpretation, which gives prediction market exchanges 30 days to stop blocking traders by state. "Your unilateral decision directly conflicts with active court orders, undermines state and tribal law, and must be reversed," they wrote. At 8:00 AM EST the Hyperliquid Policy Center went the other way, filing comment letters supporting the CFTC's two proposed rules separating federally regulated event contracts from state-regulated gambling. Louisiana's restraining order runs to 22 November, with a hearing on 30 November.

🖊️ Market significance: The fight over who regulates prediction markets is now a three-way contest between the CFTC, the states and Congress, and the crypto industry has picked the federal side.

🗨️ My viewpoint: A letter does not change the rule, but it puts nine senators on record against the agency. For platforms, the 30-day clock and the state court orders now point in opposite directions.

9⃣ Coinbase and Broadridge proposed a standard for tokenized shareholder rights

At 7:00 AM EST, Coinbase and Broadridge published a jointly developed open standard for delivering shareholder communications, such as dividends, splits, tender offers and meeting notices, directly to wallets that hold tokenized shares, and submitted it as an Ethereum Improvement Proposal. Broadridge also launched a data oracle so participating firms can show, in aggregate, that notices were distributed. The first phase covers announcements and corporate actions only; on-chain proxy voting is the next step.

🖊️ Market significance: A core piece of US proxy and shareholder-communications plumbing is helping write the on-chain version, which addresses the biggest gap in tokenized equities: holders get price exposure but not shareholder rights.

🗨️ My viewpoint: This is plumbing, and plumbing is what turns tokenized stocks from a trading product into an ownership product. The choice of an Ethereum standard also matters for where issuers build.

1⃣0⃣ ICE said the NYSE's trading venue is ready for Solana tokens

On stage at Breakpoint, Hester Serafini, president of ICE Clear Europe, said the New York Stock Exchange's alternative trading system is ready to accept tokens minted on Solana, that ICE's digital trust unit already supports Solana, and that ICE is considering running a Solana validator. "There's a number of things we're already working on, and we're quite keen to explore more things going forward," she said.

🖊️ Market significance: The parent of the world's largest stock exchange is now talking openly about connecting its venues and possibly its infrastructure to a public chain.

🗨️ My viewpoint: Considering a validator is not running one, so I treat this as intent. Still, on the day Solana dropped its beta label, an exchange operator saying its venue is ready is the most useful endorsement it could get.

1⃣1⃣ Zelle hid a $1.25 million stablecoin payment on Solana, Solflare added cash pickup

Zelle, the bank-owned payments network, demonstrated a $1.25 million ZelleUSD transfer on Solana's test network at Breakpoint, moving funds from Anchorage Digital through two test banks with the amount encrypted, so it was hidden from the public but still verifiable. It was a demonstration, not a launch. Separately, the Solflare wallet launched USDC cash withdrawals at MoneyGram locations in more than 170 countries and territories, with fees waived until 31 December.

🖊️ Market significance: The two ends of the payments stack moved in one morning: a bank network testing confidential stablecoin settlement, and a wallet turning USDC into street cash worldwide.

🗨️ My viewpoint: Confidential amounts are the feature banks need before they settle real payments on a public chain. If Zelle ships this to production, it would be one of the largest US payment networks settling on a public chain.

1⃣2⃣ Stablecoin supply shrank by about $4 billion in a week

Total stablecoin supply fell to about $287.05 billion from about $291.22 billion a week earlier, a drop of about $4.17 billion. USDT is near $175.3 billion and USDC near $69.0 billion to $69.4 billion. At 9:07 AM EST, about 100.5 million PYUSD was burned at the Paxos treasury, after a matching transfer from Paxos about half an hour earlier.

🖊️ Market significance: Stablecoins are the cash pile that funds crypto buying, and the pile is shrinking at the same time as ETF outflows, so neither on-chain nor off-chain money is coming in.

🗨️ My viewpoint: This is the single most important number for a bottom call. I want to see supply stop falling, then start growing, before I trust any rally.

1⃣3⃣ A Safe wallet lost $6.45 million through its own permissions

A Safe multisignature wallet lost about $6.45 million on Monday, including about $4.3 million in USDC and $1.7 million in syrupUSDC, Maple's yield-bearing dollar token. An on-chain analyst traced the drain to permissions set up in the wallet's Zodiac Roles module, which lets chosen addresses act without fresh owner signatures, and another analyst said the setup failed to restrict who received tokens, so this looks like a configuration failure rather than a contract bug. The attacker swapped most of the haul into ether and moved over $1 million into Monero, including about $813,000 bought on Hyperliquid. About $236,000 was still sitting in USDC that Circle can freeze.

🖊️ Market significance: The weak point was a permissions add-on, not the core wallet code, the same kind of module that a flaw in June used to take about $1.5 million from Gnosis Pay users.

🗨️ My viewpoint: Every module that removes a signature from the approval path is an attack surface. Treasuries using role modules should audit who can trigger what this week.

1⃣4⃣ Russia opens Bitcoin, Ether and USDT to retail investors on Tuesday

From Tuesday 17 November, the Bank of Russia's list of cryptocurrencies for non-qualified investors takes effect. Retail buyers can purchase Bitcoin, Ether and USDT through licensed intermediaries, capped at 300,000 rubles a year per intermediary, after passing a mandatory test. Exchanges may begin organized crypto trading from 22 November once their rules are approved, the Moscow Exchange plans to start on 1 December, and direct peer-to-peer trading will be banned from 1 July 2027.

🖊️ Market significance: A G20 economy is moving crypto from informal channels to regulated brokers, and USDT made the approved list alongside the two largest coins.

🗨️ My viewpoint: The cap keeps the retail flow small. The more important part is the peer-to-peer ban in 2027, which pushes Russian volume onto domestic venues the state can monitor.

1⃣5⃣ A factory miss, a Nasdaq slide and Washington's Nvidia turn

The New York Fed's Empire State manufacturing index fell to 7.8 in November at 8:30 AM EST, far below the 18.0 forecast and down from 25.5. By about 10:30 AM EST, the Nasdaq Composite was down about 2.0%, the S&P 500 about 1.3% and the Dow about 0.6%, with Nvidia off about 2.1% near $159.40. The Commerce Department moved to close a route that let Chinese firms rent Nvidia computing power through data centers in other countries, while President Trump said Jensen Huang did not put national security at risk and, asked about Nvidia reinstating him, said "I would certainly not mind seeing that." Fed Chair Kevin Warsh speaks at 12:00 PM EST, and Nvidia reports after Tuesday's close.

🖊️ Market significance: The data miss was the first sign of cooling in a week dominated by hike talk, but tech selling overwhelmed it within the first half hour.

🗨️ My viewpoint: Bitcoin's 9:35 AM EST high came in the first minutes of the open, before the Nasdaq extended lower. Once it did, crypto followed. Equities, not the Fed, are setting the tone today.

1⃣6⃣ Oil fell 3%, yields eased, the dollar held

Brent is near $93.00, about 3.0% below Friday's $95.84 settle, and WTI near $86.50, about 2.3% lower. The 10-year Treasury yield is near 5.11% to 5.12%, about 3 to 4 basis points lower after the Empire miss. The dollar index is near 103.5, up about 0.1%, and gold is near $3,870, down about 0.4%.

🖊️ Market significance: Lower oil and lower yields are the two inputs crypto most needs, and both moved the right way this morning without lifting crypto for long.

🗨️ My viewpoint: The 10-year is still above 5%. I want it back under 5% before macro becomes a tailwind rather than just a smaller headwind.

🗨️ My Overall Viewpoint:
The first hour gave a clean read of where buyers and sellers stand. A weak factory print and lower yields sparked a short squeeze that pushed Bitcoin back above its $65,315 weekly close at the open, but the reclaim failed within ten minutes, and the Nasdaq's slide to a 2% loss pulled Bitcoin back to the $64,000 area. Open interest fell into the spike, which tells me shorts covered rather than new buyers arrived, and Bitcoin funding has turned positive again at the lows. Crypto stocks absorbed the weekend in one session with drops of about 5% to 8%, and stablecoin supply shrank by about $4 billion last week. The building continued: Coinbase and Broadridge proposed tokenized shareholder rights, ICE said the NYSE's venue is ready for Solana tokens and Zelle tested confidential stablecoin payments. But the treasury bid is thin, with Strategy spending most of its raise on buying back preferred stock.

For the rest of the US session, my Bitcoin support is $64,035, the post-open low, then $63,830, this morning's low, $63,725, Sunday's early low, and $61,950, Saturday night's low. Resistance is $64,420, the 9:30 AM EST opening print, then $65,315, the weekly close, and $65,630, today's high, with $66,100 above that. A close back above $65,315 would turn the open's spike into a reclaim, while a break of $63,725 opens the way back to $62,000. For Ether, support is $1,800, then $1,785, this morning's low, then $1,772 and $1,709. Resistance is $1,823, then $1,835, the weekly close, and $1,865, today's high. I stay defensive. I watch Warsh at 12:00 PM EST, whether the Nasdaq stabilizes into the close and Monday's ETF flows this evening. These are my analytical levels, not forecasts, and nothing here is financial advice.

🧭 A DAY OF CONQUEST, RECKONING & NEW HORIZONS

════════════════ ❧ ════════════════

ANNALS OF THE DAY 🪔

════════════════ ❧ ════════════════

A HISTORICAL CHRONICLE • NOVEMBER 16 EDITION

──────────────── ❧ ────────────────

⏱️ READING TIME: APPROXIMATELY 9–11 MINUTES

──────────────── ❧ ────────────────

🪔 EPIGRAPH

“We carry yesterday like a lantern—not to light the road behind us, but to see how far we’ve already come, and how much farther we need to go.” — Hodgepodgery, 2026

──────────────── ❧ ────────────────

🧭 CALENDAR OVERVIEW ♏️

November 16 is the 320th day of 2026 (≈87.67% completed), with 45 days remaining (≈12.33%). Today is Monday, in ISO week 47. The United Nations observes the International Day for Tolerance, reminding the world that respect and understanding are essential to peaceful coexistence. 🌍

──────────────── ❧ ────────────────

📑 TABLE OF CONTENTS

🪔 Epigraph — A thought to frame the day.

🧭 Calendar Overview — The date, its place in the year, and its observances.

🔎 Intro — The stories and contradictions behind November 16.

🏛️ Major Historical Events — Five consequential moments that changed the course of events.

🔬 Scientific, Technological & Cultural Milestones — Discoveries and innovations that changed how we see the world.

🎂 Famous Birthdays — Notable people born on this date.

🥀 Memoriam — Remembering those whose lives ended on November 16.

🏟️ Sports Highlights — Records, milestones, and extraordinary sporting moments.

❓ History Quiz — A question to test your historical instincts.

🌎 Closing — A final reflection on the lessons of the past.

📣 There's More History Waiting! — Today's publication schedule.

🦉 The Stoic Mind — One thought from the Stoic tradition.

✅ Quiz Answer — The answer and its historical explanation.

──────────────── ❧ ────────────────

🔎 INTRO

November 16 brings conquest, political reversals, institutional beginnings, and scientific ambition. From the capture of the Inca emperor to a Revolutionary War defeat, the date reveals how power can shift—and how far-reaching the consequences can be. It also marks the opening of the Federal Reserve Banks and a message sent from Earth toward the stars.

──────────────── ❧ ────────────────

🏛️ MAJOR HISTORICAL EVENTS

November 16 marks turning points in conquest, war, statehood, and finance.

—— ❦ ——

1532 — Pizarro Captures the Inca Emperor Atahualpa 🇵🇪

On November 16, 1532, Spanish conquistador Francisco Pizarro captured Atahualpa, ruler of the Inca Empire, at Cajamarca in present-day Peru. Pizarro's force numbered fewer than 200 Spaniards, while Atahualpa commanded a vastly larger army.

Atahualpa entered the town with a retinue of several thousand men. Pizarro's soldiers had concealed themselves around the plaza. When negotiations collapsed, the Spaniards attacked, killing many of the emperor's unarmed attendants and taking Atahualpa prisoner.

But captivity did not immediately strip Atahualpa of his power. For months, he retained his royal attendants, held councils with his advisers, received the customary homage due an Inca ruler, and continued issuing orders through messengers to officials and military commanders across the empire. His Spanish captors maintained the outward appearance of his authority while exploiting his position for their own purposes.

Atahualpa later offered an enormous ransom of gold and silver for his release. Although the treasure was delivered, the Spaniards executed him in July 1533. His capture opened the way for Spain's conquest of the Inca heartland.

🧩 TRIVIA: Atahualpa offered to fill a room with gold as high as he could reach and fill two additional rooms with silver in exchange for his freedom.

🐶 SPOT: Pizarro's tiny force did not succeed through numbers alone. The Inca Empire was already weakened by a civil war between Atahualpa and his half-brother Huáscar, divisions the Spanish exploited.

🎯 TAKEAWAY: Empires can be vulnerable not only to outside enemies, but also to divisions within their own walls.

—— ❦ ——

1776 — British Forces Capture Fort Washington 🇺🇸

On November 16, 1776, British and Hessian forces captured Fort Washington on Manhattan Island. A coordinated assault overwhelmed one of the last major American positions in New York City; more than 2,800 American soldiers were captured with artillery and supplies.

Following the earlier defeat at Long Island, the loss forced George Washington's army to retreat across New Jersey. It was a severe setback, but not the end of the American cause.

🧩 TRIVIA: The British capture of Fort Washington was followed just days later by the loss of Fort Lee, across the Hudson River in New Jersey.

⚠️ IRONY: The fort had been named in honor of George Washington, yet its capture became one of the darkest setbacks of his early command.

🎯 TAKEAWAY: A serious defeat can threaten a cause without determining its final outcome.

—— ❦ ——

1907 — Oklahoma Becomes the 46th State 🇺🇸

On November 16, 1907, President Theodore Roosevelt issued the proclamation admitting Oklahoma to the United States as its 46th state.

The new state was formed by combining Oklahoma Territory and Indian Territory. The process followed decades of federal policies that had forcibly displaced Native American nations and reshaped the region through land allotment and settlement.

Oklahoma's admission completed a major chapter in the expansion of the continental United States, but its path to statehood was inseparable from the dispossession of Indigenous peoples.

🧩 TRIVIA: Oklahoma's name comes from two Choctaw words: okla, meaning people, and humma, meaning red.

🐶 SPOT: The statehood proclamation was issued by President Roosevelt while he was in Washington, D.C.; Oklahoma's residents had voted in favor of the proposed state constitution two months earlier.

🎯 TAKEAWAY: The creation of a state can represent opportunity for some while carrying the consequences of injustice for others.

—— ❦ ——

1914 — The Twelve Federal Reserve Banks Open for Business 🏦

On November 16, 1914, the twelve regional Federal Reserve Banks opened, putting a central part of the system created by the Federal Reserve Act of 1913 into operation. The system was designed to address banking panics and create a more stable currency and credit structure.

The regional banks distributed operations across the country. Their opening came as World War I disrupted international commerce and finance.

🧩 TRIVIA: The twelve original Federal Reserve Bank cities were Boston, New York, Philadelphia, Cleveland, Richmond, Atlanta, Chicago, St. Louis, Minneapolis, Kansas City, Dallas, and San Francisco.

🌀 OBSCURE: Some banks opened with remarkably modest facilities. The Federal Reserve Bank of Minneapolis initially operated from temporary quarters inside an existing financial institution.

🎯 TAKEAWAY: Lasting institutions are often built not in a single dramatic moment, but through practical decisions that make a new system work.

—— ❦ ——

1973 — Nixon Signs the Trans-Alaska Pipeline Authorization Act 🛢️

On November 16, 1973, President Richard Nixon signed legislation authorizing the Trans-Alaska Pipeline System. The roughly 800-mile route would carry oil from the North Slope to the ice-free port of Valdez.

The energy crisis and Arab oil embargo heightened urgency, while environmental concerns, engineering challenges, and legal disputes continued to shape the project.

🧩 TRIVIA: The pipeline's route crosses three mountain ranges, more than 800 rivers and streams, and hundreds of miles of permafrost.

🐶 SPOT: The pipeline was designed with elevated sections in areas where warm oil could otherwise thaw the frozen ground beneath it.

🎯 TAKEAWAY: Major infrastructure projects must balance economic needs with environmental realities and long-term consequences.

The pages of history turn. The lessons remain. 📜

──────────────── ❧ ────────────────

🔬 SCIENTIFIC, TECHNOLOGICAL & CULTURAL MILESTONES

The date also marks advances in energy, culture, spaceflight, and international cooperation.

—— ❦ ——

1896 — Niagara Power Reaches Buffalo ⚡

On November 16, 1896, electricity generated at Niagara Falls reached Buffalo, New York, demonstrating that alternating current could transmit power over distance. The project sent hydroelectricity roughly 20 miles to the city, helping establish water power as a practical energy source for industry and urban life.

🧩 TRIVIA: The project used alternating current, a system that made it possible to transmit electricity over much greater distances than earlier direct-current systems.

🌪️ TWIST: A natural wonder famous for its beauty became an industrial powerhouse, helping demonstrate how rivers and waterfalls could help electrify modern life.

🎯 TAKEAWAY: A breakthrough becomes transformative when it can move beyond the laboratory and serve an entire community.

—— ❦ ——

1945 — UNESCO's Constitution Is Signed 🌐

On November 16, 1945, representatives of 37 countries signed UNESCO's constitution in London. Founded after World War II, the organization advanced education, science, culture, and the exchange of ideas as foundations for international understanding. It formally came into existence in 1946 after ratification.

🧩 TRIVIA: UNESCO's full name is the United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization.

🐶 SPOT: Its constitution opens with the memorable principle that wars begin in the minds of people—and that the defenses of peace must therefore be constructed in those same minds.

🎯 TAKEAWAY: Peace is not sustained by treaties alone; it also depends on what societies teach, preserve, and share.

—— ❦ ——

1959 — The Sound of Music Opens on Broadway 🎭

On November 16, 1959, The Sound of Music, the musical by Richard Rodgers and Oscar Hammerstein II, opened at the Lunt-Fontanne Theatre in New York City.

Inspired by the memoir of Maria von Trapp, the production told the story of a young woman who becomes governess to the children of an Austrian naval officer and eventually confronts the rise of Nazi Germany.

Mary Martin starred as Maria, with Theodore Bikel as Captain von Trapp. The musical became a major success and later inspired the celebrated 1965 film starring Julie Andrews.

🧩 TRIVIA: The original Broadway production ran for 1,443 performances and won five Tony Awards, including Best Musical.

🌀 OBSCURE: The real Maria von Trapp's memoir was titled The Story of the Trapp Family Singers and provided the foundation for the stage adaptation.

🎯 TAKEAWAY: Stories rooted in personal experience can become cultural touchstones when music and drama give them a wider voice.

—— ❦ ——

1973 — Skylab 4 Launches into Orbit 🚀

On November 16, 1973, NASA launched Skylab 4, the third and final crewed mission to America's first space station.

Astronauts Gerald Carr, William Pogue, and Edward Gibson spent 84 days aboard Skylab, conducting scientific experiments, observing the Sun, and studying Earth.

Their mission extended the limits of human endurance in space and helped researchers understand the physical and psychological demands of long-duration spaceflight.

🧩 TRIVIA: Skylab 4's 84-day mission set a new record for the longest time humans had spent in space during a single mission at that point.

🐶 SPOT: The crew carried out extensive observations of the Sun, including studies of solar flares that could help scientists understand the activity of our nearest star.

🎯 TAKEAWAY: Exploration is not only about reaching a destination; it is also about learning how humans can live and work there.

—— ❦ ——

1974 — The Arecibo Message Is Sent into Space 📡

On November 16, 1974, scientists transmitted a powerful radio message from the Arecibo Observatory in Puerto Rico toward the globular star cluster Messier 13.

The binary message encoded information about humanity, including numbers, chemical elements, DNA, the human figure, Earth's population, and the Arecibo telescope itself.

The transmission was primarily a symbolic demonstration of the observatory's capabilities rather than a practical attempt to begin a conversation with extraterrestrial life. Because M13 is about 25,000 light-years away, any reply would take an extraordinary length of time to arrive.

🧩 TRIVIA: The message contained 1,679 binary digits, a number chosen because it is the product of two prime numbers: 23 and 73.

🐶 SPOT: When arranged into a rectangle of 23 columns and 73 rows, the binary sequence forms a graphic image containing the message's encoded information.

🎯 TAKEAWAY: Curiosity can inspire humanity to send questions into the universe even when the answers may lie far beyond our own lifetimes.

—— ❦ ——

2001 — Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone Opens in U.S. Theaters 🪄

On November 16, 2001, Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone, directed by Chris Columbus, opened in U.S. theaters. Daniel Radcliffe, Rupert Grint, and Emma Watson made their debuts as Harry, Ron, and Hermione. The hit launched an eight-film franchise.

🧩 TRIVIA: The film was released in the United Kingdom as Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone, retaining the original title of Rowling's first novel.

🌪️ TWIST: The same story carried two different titles across the Atlantic: the American publisher had changed Philosopher's Stone to Sorcerer's Stone before the film adopted the U.S. title.

🎯 TAKEAWAY: A story can travel across cultures while being adapted to the language and expectations of different audiences.

Here's to curious minds, bold ideas, and discoveries that move humanity forward. 🚀

──────────────── ❧ ────────────────

🎂 FAMOUS BIRTHDAYS

November 16 birthdays span politics, literature, entertainment, and music.

—— ❦ ——

42 BC — Tiberius 🏛️

Tiberius was the second Roman emperor, succeeding Augustus in AD 14. His reign expanded the administrative stability of the empire, though his later years became associated with political suspicion and repression. He was born in Rome.

🧩 TRIVIA: Tiberius was the stepson of Augustus and became emperor after a long and complicated succession process.

—— ❦ ——

1907 — Burgess Meredith 🎭

Burgess Meredith was an American actor whose career spanned stage, film, and television. He became widely remembered as the Penguin in the 1960s Batman television series and as Mickey Goldmill, Rocky Balboa's trainer, in the Rocky films. He was born in Cleveland, Ohio.

🧩 TRIVIA: Meredith received two Academy Award nominations, including one for his performance in The Day of the Locust.

—— ❦ ——

1922 — José Saramago 📚

José Saramago was a Portuguese novelist whose imaginative, often philosophical fiction explored power, morality, human nature, and society. His best-known works include Blindness and The Gospel According to Jesus Christ. He was born in Azinhaga, Portugal.

🧩 TRIVIA: Saramago became the first Portuguese-language writer to receive the Nobel Prize in Literature, winning it in 1998.

—— ❦ ——

1930 — Chinua Achebe ✍️

Chinua Achebe was a Nigerian novelist, poet, and critic whose writing transformed modern African literature. His landmark novel Things Fall Apart explored the disruption of Igbo society under colonial rule. He was born in Ogidi, Nigeria.

🧩 TRIVIA: Things Fall Apart, published in 1958, has been translated into dozens of languages and is widely regarded as one of the most influential African novels of the twentieth century.

—— ❦ ——

1952 — Shigeru Miyamoto (age 74) 🎮

Shigeru Miyamoto is a Japanese video game designer whose creations helped shape the modern video game industry. His work includes Super Mario Bros., The Legend of Zelda, and Donkey Kong. He was born in Sonobe, Kyoto, Japan.

🧩 TRIVIA: Donkey Kong introduced the character Jumpman, who would later become known worldwide as Mario.

—— ❦ ——

1964 — Diana Krall (age 62) 🎹

Diana Krall is a Canadian jazz pianist and singer known for her warm contralto voice and elegant interpretations of jazz standards. Her recordings have earned international acclaim and multiple Grammy Awards. She was born in Nanaimo, British Columbia.

🧩 TRIVIA: Krall is the only jazz singer to have had eight albums debut at the top of the Billboard Jazz Albums chart.

—— ❦ ——

1993 — Pete Davidson (age 33) 🎤

Pete Davidson is an American comedian and actor who became widely known as a cast member on Saturday Night Live. His stand-up comedy and screen work have made him a prominent figure in contemporary American entertainment. He was born in Staten Island, New York.

🧩 TRIVIA: Davidson joined Saturday Night Live in 2014 at age 20, becoming one of the show's youngest cast members.

—— ❦ ——

Happy birthday to all those born on November 16! 🎂

──────────────── ❧ ────────────────

🥀 MEMORIAM

Today we remember notable individuals whose lives ended on November 16. Their work and ideas continue to shape the world.

—— ❦ ——

1960 — Clark Gable (aged 59) 🎬

Clark Gable was an American film actor known as the “King of Hollywood.” His performances in It Happened One Night and Gone with the Wind made him one of the most celebrated stars of his era. He died in Los Angeles, California, following a heart attack.

🧩 TRIVIA: Gable won the Academy Award for Best Actor for It Happened One Night in 1935.

—— ❦ ——

2006 — Milton Friedman (aged 94) 📊

Milton Friedman was an American economist and Nobel laureate whose work profoundly influenced modern economic policy. A leading advocate of monetarism and free-market economics, he argued that monetary policy played a central role in economic stability. He died in San Francisco, California.

🧩 TRIVIA: Friedman received the 1976 Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences for his contributions to consumption analysis, monetary history, and the theory of stabilization policy.

—— ❦ ——

2023 — A. S. Byatt (aged 87) 📖

A. S. Byatt was a British novelist, poet, and critic whose intricate fiction often blended literature, history, mythology, and intellectual debate. Her novel Possession won the Booker Prize in 1990. She died in London, England.

🧩 TRIVIA: Possession was subtitled A Romance and follows two modern scholars investigating the hidden relationship between Victorian poets.

—— ❦ ——

In fond remembrance of them all. 🕯️

──────────────── ❧ ────────────────

🏟️ SPORTS HIGHLIGHTS

November 16 has brought landmark moments in hockey, football, and soccer.

—— ❦ ——

1926 — The New York Rangers Win Their First NHL Game 🏒

On November 16, 1926, the New York Rangers played their first National Hockey League game, defeating the defending Stanley Cup champion Montreal Maroons by a score of 1–0.

More than 13,000 fans attended the game at Madison Square Garden. Bill “The Original Ranger" Cook scored the first goal in Rangers history, while goaltender Hal Winkler recorded a shutout.

🧩 TRIVIA: The Rangers became the second NHL team based in New York City, following the New York Americans, who had joined the league the previous season.

🐶 SPOT: Winkler's shutout made him the first goaltender to record a shutout in his NHL debut.

🎯 TAKEAWAY: A great sporting tradition can begin with one night, one goal, and one remarkable performance.

—— ❦ ——

1957 — Notre Dame Ends Oklahoma's 47-Game Winning Streak 🏈

On November 16, 1957, Notre Dame defeated Oklahoma 7–0 in Norman, ending the Sooners' extraordinary 47-game winning streak.

Oklahoma entered the game as the nation's No. 2 team and a heavy favorite. Notre Dame's defense held firm, while Dick Lynch scored the game's only touchdown late in the fourth quarter.

The victory became one of college football's most famous upsets and ended a winning streak that had stood as an NCAA record.

🧩 TRIVIA: Oklahoma's 47 consecutive victories remain one of the longest winning streaks in major college football history.

🌪️ TWIST: Notre Dame was also the team that had handed Oklahoma its previous defeat, back in 1953.

🎯 TAKEAWAY: Even the most imposing streak can end when preparation, belief, and opportunity meet.

—— ❦ ——

2005 — Australia Qualifies for the World Cup After a 32-Year Wait ⚽

On November 16, 2005, Australia defeated Uruguay in a dramatic penalty shootout in Sydney to qualify for the 2006 FIFA World Cup.

The two teams had finished their two-leg playoff tied 1–1 on aggregate. After extra time failed to produce a winner, Australia prevailed 4–2 on penalties.

The result sent Australia to its first World Cup since 1974 and ended a 32-year absence from the tournament.

🧩 TRIVIA: Goalkeeper Mark "Schwarzy" Schwarzer saved two penalties in the shootout, helping Australia secure qualification.

🐶 SPOT: The victory made Australia the first team to qualify for a World Cup through a penalty shootout.

🎯 TAKEAWAY: Sometimes the road back to the world's biggest stage is decided by a single moment of nerve.

November 16 has given sports fans moments of firsts, endings, and extraordinary comebacks. 🏆

──────────────── ❧ ────────────────

❓ HISTORY QUIZ OF THE DAY

On November 16, 1974, scientists transmitted a binary message from the Arecibo Observatory in Puerto Rico toward a distant star cluster.

What was the name of the cluster targeted by the message?

[A] Andromeda

[B] Messier 13

[C] Pleiades

[D] Omega Centauri

Think it over before scrolling down to the answer. 👀

──────────────── ❧ ────────────────

🌎 CLOSING

November 16 shows how power can shift—and how its consequences endure. At Cajamarca, the capture of Atahualpa exposed the danger of internal division; at Fort Washington, a major Revolutionary War defeat failed to end the American cause. Oklahoma's admission expanded the Union while carrying the legacy of Indigenous dispossession.

The Federal Reserve's opening showed the value of durable institutions. The Trans-Alaska Pipeline reflected the demands of energy security, while the Arecibo message expressed humanity's wish to reach beyond Earth. UNESCO, The Sound of Music, and Skylab 4 each reveal different ways knowledge and culture can cross boundaries.

History advances through choices, conflict, invention, and failure. Its challenge is to learn before repeating the mistakes.

History has had its turn. Now go make yours.  🌟

──────────────── ❧ ────────────────

💋 SEND-OFF

If today's stories made you think or see the past differently, share them with someone who loves history—or someone who has yet to discover it.

──────────────── ❧ ────────────────

📣 THERE'S MORE HISTORY WAITING!

Today's publication schedule:

🤯 10:00 AM — THE WEIRDEST EVENTS IN HISTORY: Stranger Than Fiction

🪔 12:00 PM — ANNALS OF THE DAY: A Historical Chronicle

🎭 2:00 PM — CULTURAL DEBUTS: A Cultural Time Capsule

🎙️ 3:00 PM — HARVEY'S CORNER: A Closer Look at One Remarkable Figure

—— ❦ ——

Four journeys through the past. Stay curious—another story is waiting.

──────────────── ❧ ────────────────

🦉 THE STOIC MIND

“Men are disturbed not by things, but by the views which they take of things.” — Epictetus, Enchiridion, 5

──────────────── ❧ ────────────────

✅ QUIZ ANSWER: [B] — Messier 13.

The Arecibo message was transmitted on November 16, 1974, toward Messier 13, a globular cluster in the constellation Hercules, approximately 25,000 light-years from Earth.

The message contained 1,679 binary digits. When arranged in a grid of 23 columns and 73 rows, the sequence formed a graphic representation of several pieces of information about humanity and our planet.

The transmission was created as a demonstration of the Arecibo Observatory's capabilities and as a symbolic attempt to communicate with possible extraterrestrial intelligence. It was not expected to produce a quick response: even a reply traveling at the speed of light would take tens of thousands of years to reach Earth.

The message remains a remarkable expression of human curiosity—a small signal sent from one planet into an enormous universe.

NUCLEAR SHELTER anyone ?

'The Big Picture. Doomsday Suite'

In the new episode, we explore how luxury shelters designed for nuclear war are built and what they can actually protect people from.

Amid growing international tensions, the threat of a global catastrophe no longer seems like something out of a science fiction film. 

Fear of a possible apocalypse is spreading, and billionaires are willing to spend fortunes to ensure their own survival. An entire industry has emerged around these fears, with companies selling luxury underground bunkers that promise safety and familiar comforts even after the apocalypse.

A former missile silo in Kansas has been converted into a shelter complete with a swimming pool, a cinema and even gardens for growing vegetables. Meanwhile, the developers of a private shelter near Prague claim it has enough resources to sustain its occupants for ten years without outside support.

The show's host spoke with Alexey Isaev, Candidate of Historical Sciences, and historian Dmitry Yurkov, co-founder of the Underground Moscow bunker museum.

 The experts explained which threats underground shelters can actually protect against, why even the most expensive bunker can turn into a death trap, and when an organised evacuation offers a better chance of survival.

text:
Miss Aloha Wanderwell reaches Barcelona during her attempt to set an endurance record by driving a motor car around the world. She set off from Atlanta in September 1919...

Aloha Wanderwell (born Idris Galcia Hall) was a pioneering Canadian explorer, filmmaker, and aviator who became the first woman to drive around the world in an automobile. She traveled across roughly 75 countries and 380,000 miles over a five-year period (1922–1927), primarily driving and filming using Ford Model T cars. During the trek, she served as the expedition's driver, mechanic, translator, and cinematographer, capturing rare footage of cultures around the globe. Her travels and films are preserved and recognized through resources like the Academy Museum of Motion Pictures and chronicled in historical profiles by Time Magazine.

. . . 

In 1922, a newspaper in France ran a job ad that sounds completely made up: "Brains, Beauty & Breeches. World Tour Offer For Lucky Young Woman."

A 16-year-old Canadian schoolgirl named Idris Hall answered it.

She was already a girl who felt she belonged nowhere. Her stepfather was killed at Ypres in 1917, and his will revealed a secret no one had told her: he was not her real father. So when the open road offered her a way out, she took it, with her mother's permission.

The man behind the ad was "Captain" Walter Wanderwell, a self-styled adventurer whose real name was Valerian Johannes Pieczynski. He was still married. He hired her as secretary and driver, handed her a brand new name, and Idris Hall became Aloha Wanderwell.

She did not ride in the passenger seat. She drove a Ford Model T over deserts, mountains and roads that barely existed. She was the crew's mechanic, translator and filmmaker. When the car needed grease, she reportedly crushed bananas into the differential and kept going.

Between December 1922 and January 1927, she became the first woman to drive around the world. She posed on the rim of an active volcano in Hawaii, and in 1924 she filmed the aviators attempting the first flight around the globe.

She and Walter married in 1925 and had two children. Then in 1930 and 1931 she flew into Brazil's Mato Grosso. When her plane ran out of fuel, she landed on a remote river and spent about six weeks living among the Bororo people. Her footage is the earliest film record of them.

Then came a twist no screenwriter would dare. In December 1932, Walter was killed aboard their yacht in Long Beach, California. Aloha was not on board. A suspect went to trial and was acquitted. The case was never solved.

She refused to fade. She kept traveling, filming and lecturing for decades, covering hundreds of thousands of miles across about 80 countries. She died in 1996 at 89, and her films still survive.

In 1922, most girls her age were being prepared for marriage. Aloha was learning to fix an engine with fruit.

text:
Dwayne Johnson's family was evicted over $280 a month in rent. He was 15, and his mom was crying at the door. He says that moment is why he still works the way he does.
In 2019 he made $89.4 million in one year.

In the video below, he explains how being evicted, and seeing his mom cry, became the reason behind everything he's done since.

They had a little apartment in Hawaii. They had a week to get out, or the police would come.

"I saw my mom crying. I'm a mama's boy, and that kind of pain really impacted me."

"I want to make sure we never get evicted like this again, and make sure that she is never this upset again."

He says he was arrested multiple times by the time he was 16.

He got a football scholarship to the University of Miami. Then a future Hall of Famer took his spot. No NFL. No combine invite.

He ended up in Canada, making $250 a week. Then they cut him too.

His dad drove through the night to pick him up. He opened his wallet. A five, a one and some change.

"I got seven bucks in my pocket. Where do I go now?"

His father, a pro wrestler, told him he didn't think he had anything to offer in wrestling.

He went anyway. In 1996 he signed with WWE for $150,000 a year, paying for his own hotels and travel.

Arenas chanted "Rocky sucks." So he became the bad guy, and then The Rock.

In Hollywood they told him to lose weight and stop calling himself The Rock. He did, for a few years. Then he stopped.

"Hollywood conformed to me when I became authentic."

He named his company Seven Bucks.

Is it the pain that makes people like him, or would he have made it anyway?

text:
Low vs. High Impedance Guitar Pickups

Pickup impedance affects how a guitar interacts with cables, pedals, and amplifier inputs. Active low-output-impedance systems reduce sensitivity to cable capacitance, while passive pickups interact more strongly with cable loading, influencing resonance and high-frequency response.

The objective is impedance bridging: the amplifier’s input impedance should be higher than the guitar’s output impedance. Equal impedance values are neither necessary nor desirable.

Low impedance - Active pickups

1. Fender Stratocaster - EMG DG20 + Roland JC-120 Jazz Chorus

The DG20 combines three active EMG SA single-coil pickups with EXG bass/treble enhancement and SPC midrange boost circuitry. Powered by a 9V battery, its electronics provide a buffered output that reduces cable-loading effects. The system offers adjustable frequency shaping beyond conventional passive Stratocaster wiring.

The Roland JC-120 is a 120-watt stereo solid-state combo with two 12-inch speakers, clean headroom, and stereo chorus. Its 680 kΩ instrument input accepts the active signal. The combination suits clean amplification, modulation effects, and consistent frequency response without a matching transformer.

2. ESP LTD M-1000 - EMG 81/85 + Mesa/Boogie Dual Rectifier

An M-1000 equipped with an EMG 81 bridge and EMG 85 neck uses active humbuckers with onboard preamplifiers and 9V power. Both pickups have a specified 10 kΩ output impedance. Their buffered outputs reduce sensitivity to cable capacitance.

The Mesa/Boogie Dual Rectifier provides multiple gain stages, substantial distortion capability, and a conventional high-impedance guitar input. It accepts the EMG output directly. The active electronics maintain signal consistency, while the amplifier determines gain, distortion characteristics, and dynamic response.

High impedance - Passive pickups

3. Fender Telecaster + Fender Deluxe Reverb

A traditional Telecaster uses two passive single-coil pickups without onboard preamplifiers. Pickup inductance, winding resistance, cable capacitance, and amplifier loading determine electrical resonance and frequency response.

The 22-watt Fender Deluxe Reverb provides a nominal 1 MΩ instrument input, appropriate for passive pickups. Its tube circuitry delivers clean response at moderate levels and progressive overdrive as volume increases. The combination preserves the Telecaster’s pickup resonance while providing responsive amplification.

4. Gibson Les Paul Standard + Marshall 1959 Super Lead

A traditional Les Paul Standard uses two passive PAF-style humbuckers. Their dual-coil construction reduces electromagnetic hum. Pickup inductance, winding configuration, magnets, and external loading influence resonance and frequency response.

The 100-watt Marshall 1959 Super Lead uses high-impedance instrument inputs. Its high-sensitivity input provides suitable loading for passive humbuckers, while its tube circuitry produces characteristic gain and overdrive. The Les Paul’s humbuckers drive the amplifier directly without impedance-matching electronics.

The essential distinction

Low-output-impedance active pickups reduce cable-loading effects and provide a stable electrical interface. High-impedance passive pickups are more sensitive to cable capacitance and amplifier loading, contributing to their frequency response.

All four amplifiers accept their paired guitars directly. None requires an external matching transformer.

Low-Z output into High-Z input: compatible.

Passive High-Z output into a suitably High-Z guitar input: compatible.

The correct amplifier is selected for electrical compatibility, gain structure, headroom, and desired sound - not by matching equal impedance values.

Re-Elect Illinois Chicago Mayor Brandon Johnson
 
Black Churches and Others Who Supported the Campaigns to get rid of the Trump Agenda should do the same to Re-Elect Mayor Brandon Johnson. We, as black and brown people, need to let Mayor Brandon finish the work he has started. The other black candidates should support one agenda and get behind Mayor Brandon Johnson.
 
This kind of support is what I offered to Congressman Danny K Davis' Second Chance Act (SCA) Advisory Committee members in 2007 before the Second Chance Act was adopted and signed into law by President Bush in 2008. I am a member of the SCA Advisory Committee. The committee was made up of various organizations in Illinois. It was about 30 representatives sitting at the table working with Congressman Davis on the framework for the SCA. I suggested to the SCA Advisory Committee members to form groups of 3, then elect a person or organization from the the group to apply as the primary for the first SCA grant, and the next grant one of the others in the group apply as the primary. They would not or could not agree. I, Dr. Fred L Nance Jr., applied and was one of the first SCA grant recipients in Illinois (2010). No other organization in our SCA Advisory Committee got one of the first SCA grants.
 
This White Paper emphasizes Black Americans' historical capacity for unity through cooperative institutions and resistance but discusses enduring divisions rooted in slavery and racial hierarchy. It stresses evidence-based accountability in politics, highlights disparities in wealth, housing, and employment, and advocates for sustained civic engagement, community-based organizations, and legal frameworks to advance racial equity. Long-term leadership and nuanced policy evaluation are key.

Eugene Debs’s Life Speaks to Today’s Socialist Movement
by Nelson Lichtenstein
“Shawn Gude’s splendid new biography of Gilded Age Socialist Eugene V. Debs could hardly have arrived at a more propitious moment. 

Perhaps as many as half of all young people tell pollsters they prefer socialism to capitalism. Gude, a member of the 130,000-strong Democratic Socialists of America (DSA), calls that organization, whose activism and endorsements have put eight self-professed socialists in the new Congress, the “institutional descendant” of Debs’s Socialist Party of America. In his victory speech right after winning the New York city mayoral election in 2025, Zohran Mamdani, an unapologetic DSAer, quoted Debs: “I can see the dawn of a better day for humanity.” 

And when Bernie Sanders and Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez made their “Fighting Oligarchy” tour in the months after Donald Trump’s 2026 election, their critique of the billionaire class echoed Debs’s blistering denunciations of Gilded Age wealth when the barnstorming five-time presidential candidate denounced the Rockefellers, Morgans, and Carnegies of his day. Gude has written a Debs biography for our time. 

He emphasizes the rootedness of the Indiana railroad fireman in middle-American culture and Christianity, downplays more than other historians the ideological divisions endemic to the early twentieth century Socialist Party, and emphasizes the degree to which Debs, like Bernie Sanders and some of his contemporary comrades, could appeal to such a remarkably wide variety of constituencies. 

Gude’s biography also offers a full-bodied sense of Debs as a fragile and contradictory personality in which his constant travel, the crowd’s applause, and the opportunities thereby created for liaisons with the opposite sex, may well have compensated for a childless and increasingly distant marriage, as well as a distaste for the conflicts, political and personal, attendant upon leadership in any mass organization.”

Or....
Canadian's can look at this through a different lens, geopolitical strategic deception strategy.

Viewing Mark Carney’s engagement with Beijing through the reverse lens—a hypothetical "double-game" or counter-deception strategy designed to protect the Crown, NATO, and North American security—recasts his outreach to Xi Jinping as a calculated delaying and containment operation aimed at neutralizing China’s Belt and Road Initiative (BRI) footprint on Canada’s Pacific coast. 

In this strategic framework, Ottawa is not naively walking into a trap, nor is it genuinely pivoting away from Washington and London. 

Instead, Carney is leveraging his background in global finance and institutional statecraft to feign accommodation while boxing Beijing in.

1. Tactical Appeasement to Buy Time for Allied Re-Industrialization

• The Surface Move. Carney offers Beijing expanded access to Canadian conventional energy (oil, gas, coal) and lowered tariffs on a capped quota of Chinese EVs in exchange for agricultural relief and clean-tech imports.

• The Counter-Deception. Western nations, including NATO allies and the U.S., currently lack the immediate refining, battery, and green-tech manufacturing capacity to decouple overnight without triggering severe economic shock. 

By keeping 🇨🇦 raw commodities flowing eastward while importing cheap Chinese solar and wind hardware, Ottawa uses China’s own state-subsidized overcapacity to subsidize Canada’s energy transition—buying critical years for North American and 🇪🇺 supply chains to scale up independently.

2. Neutralizing Belt and Road (BRI) Footholds via "Poison Pill" Guardrails

• The Surface Move. Ottawa invites Chinese firms to invest in Canadian manufacturing and clean energy under "clear guardrails" and domestic content rules.

• The Counter-Deception. China’s BRI relies on acquiring strategic port infrastructure, logistics hubs, and debt-leveraged assets—a major security threat on British Columbia’s coast, which serves as North America's Pacific gateway and hosts critical naval and NORAD/NATO logistics nodes. 

By channeling 🇨🇳 capital strictly into heavily regulated, onshore joint ventures subject to strict Canadian labour, environmental, and national security screening (such as the Investment Canada Act), Ottawa ties up 🇨🇳 state capital in bureaucratic red tape while keeping Beijing completely locked out of West Coast ports, telecommunications, and Arctic maritime corridors.

3. Signaling "Strategic Autonomy" to Gain Leverage in Washington

• The Surface Move. Carney speaks of building a "new international order" with middle powers and China to hedge against U.S. trade protectionism.

• The Counter-Deception. Rather than genuinely abandoning the Anglo-American alliance or NATO, Ottawa uses the optics of a Beijing rapprochement as diplomatic leverage against Washington. 

Facing aggressive U.S. tariffs, demonstrating that Canada has alternative buyers for its Trans Mountain oil and critical minerals forces Washington to treat Canada as an indispensable North American partner rather than a captive supplier—ultimately strengthening the continental defense and economic perimeter on better terms for Ottawa.

4. Intelligence Gathering and Containment at the Top

• The Surface Move. Carney engages in direct, high-level leader dialogue with Xi Jinping at forums like APEC, framing Canada as a constructive middle-power interlocutor.

• The Counter-Deception. In classic British and Commonwealth statecraft, keeping a rival close at the negotiating table yields far better intelligence and strategic visibility than total diplomatic isolation. Direct engagement allows Ottawa—working in tandem with Five Eyes and NATO intelligence partners—to map Beijing’s economic pressure points, monitor state-linked corporate networks operating in North America, and maintain open crisis-communication channels while quietly hardening domestic counter-interference laws and Arctic defenses.
