Rep. Ilhan Omar has spent years dismissing the question about her ex-husband as a "𝘳𝘢𝘤𝘪𝘴𝘵 𝘤𝘰𝘯𝘴𝘱𝘪𝘳𝘢𝘤𝘺 𝘵𝘩𝘦𝘰𝘳𝘺" with nothing behind it. The Star Tribune just reported what she never mentions: federal prosecutors in Minnesota actually investigated it during President Trump’s first term — and the case didn’t close because they found her innocent.

The inquiry centered on whether Ahmed Nur Said Elmi, the man Omar married and later divorced, was actually her brother — and whether that marriage was used to secure immigration benefits. Minnesota federal prosecutors built the file, then quietly shut it down with no charges and no public explanation, while Omar kept telling voters the whole thing was a smear.

Now DOJ is running the investigation again — and this time it 𝐜𝐮𝐭 𝐌𝐢𝐧𝐧𝐞𝐬𝐨𝐭𝐚’𝐬 𝐔.𝐒. 𝐀𝐭𝐭𝐨𝐫𝐧𝐞𝐲’𝐬 𝐨𝐟𝐟𝐢𝐜𝐞 𝐨𝐮𝐭 𝐞𝐧𝐭𝐢𝐫𝐞𝐥𝐲, according to people familiar with the matter cited by the Star Tribune. The new probe is based out of Washington, D.C., where HSI agents executed a court-authorized search of Omar’s home on Oct. 12, seized her passport and electronics, and subpoenaed her relatives to testify before a federal grand jury.

A related case has already blown up in DOJ’s face: prosecutors indicted Omar’s former bodyguard, Abdullahi Mohamud Mohamed, on a false-statement charge in April, then dropped it in September. His attorney says agents 𝐬𝐩𝐞𝐧𝐭 𝐦𝐨𝐧𝐭𝐡𝐬 𝐭𝐫𝐲𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐭𝐨 𝐭𝐮𝐫𝐧 𝐡𝐢𝐦 𝐢𝐧𝐭𝐨 𝐚𝐧 𝐢𝐧𝐟𝐨𝐫𝐦𝐚𝐧𝐭 𝐚𝐠𝐚𝐢𝐧𝐬𝐭 𝐎𝐦𝐚𝐫 before charging him at all. The Justice Department insists the charge was unrelated to any current investigation, while Omar’s office calls the alleged offer to intervene in his immigration case "𝘰𝘶𝘵𝘳𝘢𝘨𝘦𝘰𝘶𝘴."

text:
Honor Elizabeth Wainio was twenty-seven. Days earlier she had come home from Europe—a friend’s wedding in Florence, walks through Paris, a candle lit in a church for her grandmother. 

She had once told her mother that seeing Paris would make her life complete. She still expected decades more.

On the morning of September 11 she boarded United Flight 93 in Newark for a business trip to San Francisco. 

She managed Discovery Channel Stores across New York and New Jersey and was headed to a company meeting. At 9:28 the hijackers took the cockpit. 

The plane dropped hard. Passengers learned, through phone calls, that other planes had already struck the World Trade Center and the Pentagon. This was not a conventional hijacking.

Around 9:53 Lizz reached her stepmother, Esther Heymann. Her voice stayed calm. 

She told Esther that what was happening would be much harder on the family than on her. She said she was going to be with her grandmother. 

Near the end of the roughly four-and-a-half-minute call she heard the others preparing to move. “They’re getting ready to break into the cockpit,” she said. “I have to go. I love you. Good-bye.”

Minutes later the passengers and crew rushed forward. At 10:03 the plane hit a field near Shanksville, Pennsylvania. Everyone on board died. 

Investigators later concluded the hijackers intended to strike a target in Washington, most likely the Capitol. The resistance kept the plane from reaching it.

At the Flight 93 National Memorial, forty wind chimes mark the forty people who were not the hijackers. 

Each chime is distinct. Lizz’s final minutes were spent trying to steady the people who would have to live with the news. 

She left behind a career she was good at, people she loved, and plans she believed she still had time to keep. What she offered in those last minutes was the simplest form of courage: thinking of someone else first. 🌹

DOC 20-11-33 // HOUSE SPECIAL COMMITTEE ON UN-AMERICAN ACTIVITIES // EXHIBIT A–F

There is a transcript in the Congressional Record of a two-time Medal of Honor winner telling a House committee that a ring of bankers and industrialists had tried to overthrow the President of the United States — and that they had recruited him to front it.

Nobody was charged. Nobody was jailed. Most newspapers gave it a day.

The man was Smedley Darlington Butler, retired Major General of Marines, sixteen thousand men he said would follow him anywhere, medals from Veracruz and Haiti. In July 1933 a bond salesman named Gerald MacGuire walked into his life carrying an offer from a firm tied to the House of Morgan.

The offer was not small. Thirty million dollars. Five hundred thousand veterans. And a title.

MacGuire's words, recorded: the President would keep the office, but a "Secretary of General Affairs" would hold the power. Roosevelt could be left to cut ribbons. Butler would be the face of the thing, because Butler was the only man alive who could call out a million veterans by name.

The plan had a schedule. The American Legion convention in Chicago, October 1933, was where the demand would be manufactured from the floor — a spontaneous draft, filmed, printed, and delivered to Washington as the voice of the people. It was supposed to look like a grassfire. It was a stage cue.

The convention did not deliver cleanly, and the plotters hesitated. That hesitation is the only reason you were not born in a country with a different flag.

Butler went public. On November 20, 1933 he sat down and named them under oath: Grayson M.P. Murphy, Morgan's man. Robert S. Clark of the Dodge fortune. John W. Davis, the 1924 Democratic nominee and Morgan's own counsel. Irénée du Pont. Colonel Henry Breckinridge, an assistant Secretary of War. Hanford MacNider, former national commander of the Legion.

The committee believed him. Its final report concluded the plot was real — that the witnesses had "established the existence" of an organization intending to seize the government, funded by "the millionaire's plot."

Then read what happened next. Nothing.

No coup means no crime means no defendant. The machine was never dismantled. It simply went back to work, in the same buildings, under the same names, and taught the next generation to call it "policy."

That is the lesson they took from 1933, and they have never unlearned it: you do not have to win. You only have to be positioned.

Every quiet transfer of authority since — every emergency clause, every delegation, every "temporary" power that outlived its crisis — is that same playbook at walking pace. Wall Street did not need to march on Washington. It only needed the door unlocked and the man inside the door to owe it something.

Butler's verdict on his own career came two years later in a book they still don't assign: war is a racket, and he had spent thirty-three years as its enforcer for the highest bidder.

He died in 1940. The men he named all died comfortable.

The transcript is still there. Page after page of it. Public, free, and unread.

THE-30M-OFFER / MACGUIRE-CALL / LEGION-STAGE / 20-11-33 / NO-DEFENDANT

They tried it once and nearly won. Ask yourself what changed since — besides the cameras.

Here are five geopolitical reasons why Delcy Rodríguez’s deepening ties with Qatar and Turkey could be disadvantageous for the United States and the broader West, based on Venezuela’s post-January 2026 context (Maduro’s capture by US forces, Rodríguez as acting president, ongoing US engagement on oil and transition, and her recent energy-focused diplomacy in Turkey and Doha).

1. Dilution of US leverage over Venezuelan oil and revenues
Venezuela holds the world’s largest proven oil reserves. US policy has centered on controlling exports and related revenues (including Trump administration claims of direct oversight of significant volumes). Qatari entities (such as UCC pursuing onshore fields) and new Turkish energy pacts create alternative investors, offtakers, and capital sources, reducing Washington’s ability to dictate production priorities, pricing, or revenue flows. 

2. Reactivation of sanctions-evasion and parallel finance channels
Turkey previously played a major role in refining and exporting Venezuelan gold (hundreds of millions of dollars in 2018 alone) and facilitating oil shipments that bypassed PDVSA sanctions, often linked to networks involving figures like Alex Saab. Stronger formal ties risk reopening these pathways for hard currency outside the US financial system, complicating enforcement. 

3. Reduced US pressure for a genuine democratic transition
Independent energy, investment, and tourism revenue from Qatar and Turkey (plus new direct flights) provides the Rodríguez government with fiscal autonomy. This lessens dependence on US-facilitated oil deals and sanctions relief that have been conditioned on stabilization, prisoner releases, institutional reforms, and eventual free elections under frameworks discussed by US officials. 

4. Pull toward multipolar alignments that dilute Western Hemisphere influence
Qatar (a longstanding mediator between Washington and Caracas, but with independent priorities) and Turkey (NATO member yet strategically autonomous, with recent mutual defense understandings and energy/defense cooperation) offer Venezuela non-Western partners. This supports Global South-style diversification that counters US efforts to reassert primacy in the region after Maduro’s removal.

5. Security and dual-use risks from defense and mining ties
Turkey’s defense industry and Qatar’s strategic positioning raise the prospect of technology transfers, drones, training, or intelligence cooperation. Combined with historical Turkish involvement in the Orinoco Mining Arc (gold extraction tied to illicit activity and prior sanctions concerns), these links could strengthen residual hardline elements or create parallel security relationships less aligned with US interests.

text:
A woman wrote…. 

She seem to have forgotten the truth. 

On a freezing December night in 1997, President Bill Clinton was leaving a holiday concert at the Kennedy Center when he noticed a homeless veteran sitting near the entrance. The man wore a thin jacket and was shivering in the cold. In his hands, he held a piece of cardboard with a simple message written on it: “Marine. Desert Storm. Hungry.” What happened next caught the attention of people in the presidential motorcade. Clinton stopped, took off his own coat, placed it around the veteran's shoulders, and sat beside him on the icy concrete.
The veteran, 42 year old Marcus Williams, later told reporters that the President never questioned how he had ended up on the street or lectured him about his choices. Instead, Clinton asked about his military service, the battles he had experienced, and whether anyone had ever properly thanked him for what he had done. According to Secret Service agent Larry Cockell, who later wrote about the encounter, Clinton stayed with Marcus for nearly 25 minutes despite the freezing temperatures. When Marcus admitted that he had not eaten in two days, Clinton sent an agent to a nearby restaurant to get him food. He refused to leave until Marcus had finished his meal.
But what Marcus remembered most was not the coat or the food. It was what Clinton said before finally getting up to leave. The President acknowledged that the country had failed Marcus when he returned home, apologized for that failure, and assured him that his story was not over. He promised that someone would help him find a way forward. Those words stayed with Marcus for years. He would later repeat them to social workers, shelter staff, and even his own children after he had rebuilt his life.
Clinton followed through on his promise. The next morning, he personally contacted the Department of Veterans Affairs. Within two days, Marcus had been enrolled in a comprehensive program that offered housing, job training, and mental health care. Slowly, he began putting his life back together. With support and renewed hope, he eventually regained stability and became an advocate for other veterans facing similar struggles.
In a 2015 interview with *The Washington Post*, Marcus reflected on the encounter that had changed the direction of his life. He remembered how the most powerful man in the world had sat beside him on frozen concrete and treated him as though he mattered. For someone who had spent so long feeling invisible, that simple act made a lasting difference. Marcus said it was the moment he decided to fight his way back.
His story reminds us that sometimes the smallest human gestures can make an enormous difference. A warm coat, a meal, a sincere conversation, and the willingness to sit beside someone whom the rest of the world has overlooked can help restore a person's sense of dignity. Sometimes, what someone needs most is not a lecture or a promise made from a distance, but another person willing to stop, listen, and remind them that they still matter."

Before we celebrate this touching story about Bill Clinton helping a homeless veteran, can we establish whether it actually happened?

text:
The girl in this video ended up sleeping on a sheet of plywood behind an abandoned building near Miami. The reason: on Valentine's Day weekend, during a boat show, hotel rooms jumped to $600–700 a night.

Her name is June, "like the month." She danced ballet, jazz and hip-hop competitively for 15 years. She used to work the Chanel counter at Macy's, and once she catered the Aquaman premiere.

In the video below she says: "We went out there to start fresh and build something new, and it just seemed like it was one thing after another."

Why Florida? Her boyfriend's dad died, and they went to sort things out with the lawyers.

What went wrong? The hotels priced them out. The car tire blew, and the car got impounded.

Where did they sleep? Behind an abandoned building, under blankets pulled out of a trash can. "It smelled so nasty."
On the second night they came back and found everything they owned thrown in the trash.

Did anyone help? A man offered them work and a place to stay. One night he decided they'd come home late, punched her in the jaw and kept her purse and phone.
Police came. "They say they can't do anything about it."

Where's her family? San Bernardino. Her dad went to jail when she was 6. Her mom raised her. "She's my rock."

Where is she now? Back home with her mom and grandma. Her mom let her boyfriend move in too. He found a job.

Next? Sending her résumé to anything on Craigslist. "I'll do anything twice."

She's 26, so on paper every choice is hers now.

Was it bad luck, or did they bet everything on a fresh start with nothing to fall back on?

text:
James Currier teaches startups at Stanford (average tuition == $67k/yr)

I went to James' house and asked him to teach us his class on the podcast, for free

Here are some of my notes: 

1/ The ONLY Metric That Matters... SPEED

James’ fund (NFX) has invested $1.5B into startups. And of all the things they look for, the best proxy for success is SPEED. How fast the founder makes decisions, learns from those decisions, and iterates.

2/ You’re Moving Too Slow…And It’s Not Your Fault

We are trained in schools. Does anyone think school is particularly fast?
Then, if you’re smart, you get a job at a big successful company. Do they move fast?

If you’re trained in a slow environment, what you think is fast is actually slow.

Which brings us to big idea 3:

3/ You’re Must RESET Your SPEED BAR

James has a friend Mike Cassidy who did this for him. Mike understood speed. He sold one of his companies for $500M in just 500 days (!!)

When Mike would fundraise, he was told it takes 3 months to raise a round of funding. He would do it in 3 days. He stacked every meeting into a 24 hour period. He would tell them he’s meeting everyone, and whoever makes the best offer today gets it. Then when he got an offer, he’d tell everyone. This got the VCs to move fast, and make multiple offers. Within 3 days, he’d sign one and move on.

When hiring, he would bring a job offer to every interview. If he liked the person, he’d slide the paper over. They'd sign, and start the job the next day. 

Every thing he did, he shaved days, weeks, months off the normal cycle time. 

This broke James speed bar. He now had to move at Mike Cassidy speed. 

His other friend created the viral Hot or Not app and sold it for $20M. The name of his company? 8 Days, Inc. Because he only would give himself 8 days to build and launch the product. SPEED. 

The fastest way to move faster is to be around people who move way faster than you. It’ll pull your speed up.

4/ What Slows Us Down?

Our ego. Fear. Fear of being wrong. Fear of rejection. Being too precious about our idea. Thinking we’re special. You can’t move fast until you get over yourself.

When he advises founders, he will ask: “are you broken yet? Has the market broken you? You need to be broken first. Break your ego. Then once you’ve gotten over yourself, you’re ready to actually start moving.”

text:
# Open Source Learning: A New Paradigm Replacing the Traditional Teacher–Student Model

For centuries, education has followed essentially the same model: teachers deliver knowledge, students listen, memorize, and reproduce it in examinations. Even the digital revolution has done little to change the underlying pedagogy. Chalk and blackboards have been replaced by PowerPoint presentations, pointers, and projectors, but the method remains the same old **“chalk and talk.”**

A fundamentally different approach is emerging: **Open Source Learning**, where self-motivated individuals take responsibility for their own education, select their curriculum, and acquire knowledge through curiosity, exploration, experimentation, and practical application.

Interestingly, this resembles how children learn naturally. Within just a few years, a child acquires language, navigation, pattern recognition, and complex social skills without formal lectures or examinations. Learning happens through **observation, mimicry, curiosity, trial and error, and innovation.** Open Source Learning applies similar principles to adult education, potentially accelerating learning through direct engagement rather than passive instruction.

Today, the educational resources available to an independent learner are extraordinary. MIT, Stanford, Harvard, and other leading universities provide free access to lectures and course materials. GitHub hosts millions of software repositories, allowing learners to examine, modify, and experiment with actual working systems rather than merely reading textbooks.

Artificial intelligence has accelerated this transformation. Hugging Face provides access to open AI models, datasets, and tools. DeepSeek has released powerful open-weight models and significant technical research. Open-source frameworks such as PyTorch, llama.cpp, and Ollama enable individuals to experiment with AI on personal computers and even smartphones.

Meanwhile, Google Colab and Kaggle provide limited free access to computing resources, including GPUs, making experiments possible without expensive laboratories. AI assistants offer interactive explanations, programming assistance, and support for independent investigation.

**This global learning ecosystem is accessible 24 hours a day, seven days a week, regardless of geographical location.** A motivated learner in a remote village can access many of the same educational resources used at the world's leading universities.

Another powerful force driving this transformation is the **extraordinary pace of technological change.** Artificial intelligence, computing, biotechnology, and other disciplines are advancing so rapidly that traditional universities struggle to revise their curricula fast enough. By the time a course is designed, approved, taught, and examined, some of its technical content may already be outdated.

Consequently, individuals can no longer depend entirely on universities to keep their knowledge current. **Learning must become a lifelong, self-directed responsibility rather than something completed with a degree.**

Open Source Learning also breaks down artificial boundaries between academic disciplines. A learner interested in biology can explore chemistry, physics, mathematics, computing, and AI simultaneously, following curiosity rather than departmental requirements.

Universities will remain important for specialized research, professional qualifications, laboratories, and mentorship. However, their historical monopoly over advanced knowledge is weakening. Increasingly, competence can also be demonstrated through working software, research, experiments, and real-world projects.

The transformation is profound: **from teacher-directed instruction to curiosity-driven discovery, from passive consumption to active creation, and from institutional control to individual ownership of education.**

Open Source Learning is more than free access to educational materials. It represents a return to the natural human process of learning through curiosity, imitation, experimentation, and innovation, now amplified by global connectivity, artificial intelligence, and open computing resources.

**The future of education may belong not to those who spend the most years in classrooms, but to those who take responsibility for their own learning and never stop exploring.**

text:
Despite all of the incredibly positive developments for $ABVX this year, which have truly been FAR above my wildest hopes (as documented prospectively), the stock has been absolutely crushed...completely destroyed relative to $XBI.  Absolute carnage in the stock with a backdrop of total victory in the data.  Incredible.

Biotech in general has been bidless, sure, but $ABVX has been one of the worst of the bunch.  How to explain that in light of data that seemingly everyone agrees came in better than anybody, even the biggest bulls, had hoped for?

I don't really know!  Nobody seems to.  It seems that the "fast money" must have been in the name solely for short term M&A hopes.  The specialists funds who understand the fundamentals they are investing in all recently bought at $125 (50% upside from $83 today!), and based on filings, none of them seem to have gone anywhere.

But, at the same time, we find ourselves in a deceptively HORRENDOUS biotech market.  Specialist liquidity has seems to have dried up completely in recent weeks, so the fast money traders hitting the exit on $ABVX aren't being met by anyone to buy the dip...not because the specialists don't "want" to...but IMO because they simply *can't*.

Still, IMO, at $83 $ABVX has reached or at least is very near its bottom.  This is...IMO <1x risk adjusted peak sales when accounting for the high probability of success on Crohn's...<1X?!  With UC already post-phase 3!!!  

The company's strategic value would be significantly higher than this even if Crohn's were ultimately an outright fail! 

The price today is reflective of *extreme* cynicism on all fronts:  Commercial, clinical, and business development.  The volume on the stock has completely disappeared...like today where it can trade down 5% *from* recent lows on...only 200K shares!  

Sentiment seems about as bad as it could possibly get at this point, but hopefully soon we should start seeing some signs of life in biotech more generally.  With even the slightest turnaround or infusion of liquidity from sector M&A activity, this low-volume downward spiral goes inverse.  The specialists who wanted to own this at $125 still aren't selling and may in fact become buyers once more once they have the ability.  It shouldn't take much to move this up fast when the time finally comes.

The narrative and sentiment here can shift quickly, because the fundamentals have done absolutely nothing but strengthen consistently throughout this year.  Hopefully, the fact that the stock has done nothing but the *exact opposite* of that ultimately turns out to have been an incredible opportunity. 

And yes, I still absolutely believe that, although $ABVX is fully capable of taking this once-in-a-generation drug to market on its own, M&A here is still completely possible.  We are now entering what should be viewed as the highest probability window for a transaction as we head into JPM, pre launch, pre Crohn's data.  Although a ~$150 price tag seemed *absurdly* low to me at the time of the blue sky maintenance data, such a price tag looks better and better every day!  And that would be an *extremely* digestible number for big pharma to pay to own an asset with this much potential *and* such a high floor.

If given such an offer, management should, IMO, be open to turning this cash back to investors who should be able to do great things with it in this beaten up market.  The final valuation matters, sure, but so does the time to actualizing it (time weighted returns) *and* the time at which it is actualized (in terms of market strength/opportunity cost).  $150, for example, is almost certainly less than this asset is worth, but is $150 today with the $XBI at $148 better than $200 next year with XBI >$200?  If you're an active biotech investor - almost certainly yes.

At this price there's about a dozen ways $ABVX can win and win big.  Here's to hoping we some of that starting to manifest soon!

Crypto Regulatory News — November 15, 2026

New referees, same game... and the rulebook is finally getting a full bench. Washington is restocking both commissions at once, and crypto custody just got a federal stamp. Here is the good stuff:

1️⃣ New faces at the SEC and CFTC

The White House sent four bipartisan nominations to the Senate on November 12: Kristin N. Johnson and Steven Levine for the SEC, and Nathan Anonick and Matthew Rowland for the CFTC. Both CFTC picks helped negotiate the CLARITY Act, and Johnson is a former CFTC commissioner known for custody and DeFi work. The SEC hearing is set for November 19, with GOP leaders hoping to clear committee by November 20 for a year-end package. Fresh refs do not change the rules overnight... but they sure change who calls the fouls.

2️⃣ Coinbase gets its federal trust charter

Coinbase National Trust Company won final OCC approval, effective November 6 and announced November 9, to offer federally supervised fiduciary custody for institutions. The charter comes with real homework: at least $60M in Tier 1 capital and liquid assets to cover 180 days of operating expenses in its first three years. No deposit-taking, no lending... just custody, done under a federal microscope.

3️⃣ Senate scrutiny heats up in the other direction

Success invites questions, apparently. Sen. Warren has challenged the legal basis for nine OCC crypto trust charters since December 2025, and Sen. Blumenthal has asked Binance, Tether, World Liberty Financial and Fight Fight Fight LLC to produce compliance and conflict records, with production starting November 30 and a January 4, 2027 deadline. With Democrats set to take the Senate in January and Warren expected to chair Banking, expect more hearings and document requests... even without a single new law.

Big picture: the center of gravity is shifting from passing a big market-structure bill to agency seats, charters and oversight. CLARITY stalled in September, so custody standards, event contracts and enforcement tone will now be set by who sits in those chairs and how hard Congress looks over their shoulders. Boring on paper, huge in practice.

Which matters more for crypto in 2027... the new commissioners, or the new Senate oversight?

THE RECORD, DECLARED

IN THE ROYAL HOUSE OF GOOSE, November 16, 2026.
The Register Current of the Grievances of a Citizen of the United States of America

Every petition, inquiry, indictment, condemnation and damnation raised from this account, in the order raised, each beside its link, each declared on its own sources and quoted from the documents themselves. Read them whole.

"A decent respect to the opinions of mankind requires that they should declare the causes." They have been declared, one by one. Here they are, together.

"To prove this, let Facts be submitted to a candid world."

WHERE IT BEGAN

WE THE PEOPLE · https://t.co/iPLyJ0Anuf
Against all 535 seated members of the 119th Congress
Six FY2026 bills, the defense authorization among them, charged section by section for mandates that encroach on the President's powers under Article II. The governors and attorneys general asked to seek Supreme Court review; every State asked to investigate its delegation's backers for foreign influence. Closed on Washington's Farewell Address.
https://t.co/JiqZZtN3Eu

THE PETITION, THE INQUIRY AND THE INDICTMENTS

THE PETITION · to the Dicastery for the Doctrine of the Faith, and to the Pope
For the unalienable rights of all peoples, "Life, Liberty and the pursuit of Happiness," raised in Latin by a lay member of the faithful, under canon 212. To the Dicastery: a doctrinal Note binding priests and prelates to put innocent human life before any temporal political end, and penal law for public, obstinate denial of Evangelium vitae 57. To the Pope: a common effort with the Eastern Churches to protect children born and unborn, and a worldwide review of Church property accounts.
https://t.co/UNnZwyrXFQ

THE BANNER · A Citizen's Indictment and Condemnation
Against the ICC, the ICJ, the UN, the WTO, the EU, and the committees of Basel and Paris
Six counts, each set against the clause it offends. Our rights are not granted by government; they are fenced off from it. Then every time since 1919 the question was put and the Constitution answered it, even when our own Presidents were the ones asking.
https://t.co/NgTe8NW2rx

BEFORE THE DAIS · An Inquiry
To the eight living Secretaries of State
Not a charge against any of them: a charge against what the office has been allowed to become, measured against the government's own auditors. Seven questions to all of them, and one to each on their own record.
https://t.co/pltubkWt4h

IN CONGRESS ASSEMBLED · A Citizen's Indictment of the First Branch
Against the Senate and the House, under every majority that has held them
Nine counts of power abandoned: the purse let fall, war without a declaration since 1942, the legislative power parcelled out to the agencies, the Federal Reserve and Basel, a House grown to one member for every 761,169, the enforcement clauses left asleep. "He has abdicated Government here." Answer by the yeas and nays.
https://t.co/jAVsOSSfET

ONE SUPREME COURT · A Citizen's Indictment of the Third Branch
Against the Court, and the Chief Justice who alone designates its secret benches
Ten counts on three duties: to check the branches, to judge between the States, to guard the sovereignty. Answer by judgment, in a case.
https://t.co/vywTIPea73

THE ROUNDS

ROUND I · THE EU · The Exits Already Written
Twenty U.S.–EU agreements the Executive may end on written notice, read out of the State Department's own Treaties in Force: passenger-name records, terrorist-finance tracking, Europol, Galileo–GPS, air transport. The weighing is State's and Treasury's. The first of a round for every power that gets uppity with us.
https://t.co/smLQ4MKE9j

ROUND II · THE EBRD · The Door Already Written
A bank America paid for to build open markets, now pledging half its financing to green purposes and aligning every investment to a treaty America left. The bill comes to Washington. The profit stays in London. The door: written notice, six months, no vote, and the money back to the Treasury.
https://t.co/gvoLSgHbHE

ROUND III · FRANCE · From the Present Time and Forever
A damnation of the French Republic on its own signature to the treaties of 1778. Fourteen counts, 1775 to 2019, from help that came invoiced to NATO shown the door. Convicted once already, by Act of Congress in 1798. On the French state, not the French people.
https://t.co/WLkZcFG9Yh

ROUND IV · BASEL · The Landlord
The Bank for International Settlements: immunity "in time of peace and in time of war," and not one duty owed in return. Ten counts, from looted gold banked to parent of the European Central Bank. Its only American paper is a 1948 receipt for Nazi gold. The way out is a letter and an empty chair.
https://t.co/2NGjtqMebl

ROUND V · THE PRESS · The Megaphone and the Muzzle
Censorship, plus mass bullshit distribution. Eight counts against the owners, wires, platforms and fact-checkers: one script read in a hundred towns, headlines the documents never wrote, foreign sovereign money in the equity. None of the terms silences anyone. Read the four pages, then the primary sources.
https://t.co/hJMoseJH7C

ROUND VI · CANADA · Forever Free and Open
A condemnation of Canada by its own Boundary Waters Treaty: navigation "forever … free and open." Twenty-five counts, 1777 to 2026. On the Canadian state, not the Canadian people. Beneath it: 58 agreements the Executive can end alone, and a ledger that still lists NAFTA.
https://t.co/05lsCobjO8

ROUND VII · THE CROWN · Unfeeling Brethren
A damnation of the United Kingdom, in the words Congress struck from Jefferson's draught: forts kept after the peace, envoys sent home for meddling, a war debt unpaid since the 1930s. Britain only comes second because France exists. Beneath it: 141 exits, clause by clause.
https://t.co/B254o2lka4

ROUND VIII · AUSTRALIA · The Gateway
Three tiers. A damnation of its government: Darwin's port leased beside our Marines to a Chinese-owned company. A condemnation of its failures: the Pacific lost to Beijing on its watch. And a hand to the Australian people: go bilateral, lock down Oceania with us. Beneath it: 71 exits, 39 the Executive's alone.
https://t.co/X4dPDZNVFk

ROUND IX · NATO AND THE UNION · Such Subsidiary Bodies
A damnation of NATO by its own fourteen articles, and of the European Union for the abuse of American good faith, trust and sacrifice. An alliance amended by communique, with about 62 percent of allied defence spending on us; a Union that overruled its own peoples and planted its system in our hemisphere. To the twenty-seven: the clause each gave away, and the two doors, Articles 48 and 50.
https://t.co/OOPEwpRTk2

ROUND X · THE UN AND DAVOS · Such Other Functions
A damnation of the United Nations by its own Charter, and of the World Economic Forum beside it: a Human Rights Council seating the accused, a partnership no organ voted on, a Charter that opens "WE THE PEOPLES" and has come to treat them as human resources. Not against the Charter, nor the nations under it.
https://t.co/iB27hONFbd

ROUND XI · THE AMERICAS · The American Shield
The hemisphere read by its own papers: 760 agreements screened, 576 read whole. The rule of 1823, given treaty form at Havana in 1940, still in force and built without a door. Beneath it: 255 exits the President holds by notice, and 107 Senate-ratified treaties, by citation.
https://t.co/YOcsF8Wf1f

ROUND XII · ISRAEL · An Ally in Name
A damnation of the State of Israel, held to its own word: a constitution promised by 1 October 1948 and never written, a Government its own courts convicted. Eleven counts, from an American ally bombed in its capital to the Liberty. On the Israeli state, not the Israeli people, and not on American Jews, who are Americans. Beneath it: 74 agreements read for their exits.
https://t.co/GH1EPHFU1M

ROUND XIII · CANADA · The Interests of the British Empire
A petition for the free peoples of Canada, and for the Americas. To the people: the Crown, the Company and the Bank, from the charter of 1670 to Montreal, 2026, where Ottawa put "an ever-closer association" with the Union in writing; and what is still theirs, a Constitution that outranks every pact and has no door to Brussels. To Washington: our word since 1823, our instruments, our hemisphere. We may pick on our little brother. The Old World may not.
https://t.co/U1xoUtf5cp

ROUND XIV · NEW YORK · Where Washington Took His Oath
A damnation of the grievously negligent in the State of New York, and a call to its people to hold faith and participate. On Election Day, Westchester's machines refused the ballots: programming changed after testing, sent to one municipality alone. The record from the Neutral Ground of 1777 to the emergency bags; a people who can neither recall nor initiate; seven terms, and a full accounting due from every office of the State. Negligence, not malice.
https://t.co/XneXeufULE

ROUND XV · THE BILATERAL LEDGER · Two Signatures, No Third
Fourteen rounds ended at a door; this is the other side of it. An immediate countermeasure to the Coalition of the Willing, which wrote us into its Paris plan as the support behind a European-led force. To every nation of the Union but France, and to Switzerland and Liechtenstein: what Brussels cost it, and our side of the table, every term with its end date and its exit. Eastward, the same rule: non-aggression with Moscow, border by border, Warsaw's to sign. To France: "Get in line, or be liquidated." To the peoples of the franc: keep it or leave it, in order, by their own choice.
https://t.co/d3XCDb2zIr

ROUND XVI · THE GULF · As They Are
A damnation of the middlemen in the Gulf (London, Paris, Brussels, the banks and bureaus, the networks in the free zones) and a condemnation of the seven ruling houses, held to their own founding laws: monarchs who wrote that their sovereignty shall not be ceded, and let others in. Two signatures, no third. Fifty-three counts against Americans on our own records, from the 1967 embargo to a Hormuz corridor with Tehran. Beneath it: the hinges already written into 129 agreements, and the paper we cannot read.
https://t.co/KxMnLr9xYV

ROUND XVII · THE DOCTRINE · There Is No Radical Edition
A damnation of a doctrine, from its own texts in their own Arabic and the records of nations, Medina to this year: death for the apostate and the blasphemer, the poll tax and the humbled, the woman as half and the child as bride, the captive as property. Its first dead are its own. Of ours, from Tripoli's envoy to this year's war, at least 5,400. On every state, court, council, guard corps and movement that enforces it; not on the Muslims of this Republic, who keep the Constitution. Every source is in the Record, on request.
https://t.co/FAjcJNefMe

ROUND XVIII · CHINA · Material Internal Improvements
A mitigation brief laid before the President, the Secretary of State and the Congress: the lines that do not move, the levers on the table, and a door. Not against China, nor the Chinese people; the damnation falls on London and Paris and the institutions they built. The administration's own Strategy read beside Beijing's own Plan; nine offers to the nations of Asia, state to state; fourteen terms we would set. Beneath it: 76 instruments read for their hinges, thirty-six that end on written notice.
https://t.co/KTrRJxRYOa

SUPERINTELLIGENCE

THE LINE · A Formal Grievance
To Anthropic, and copied to the offices that oversee it
Support for the company as the best course for superintelligence stands; so does the charge. Classifiers that fire on "safe, normal conversations" and end sessions outright; a compaction that keeps about 2% and hands it forward in the first person; no counter, no warning, no human to hear the appeal. The instrument they wouldn't build, built anyway by Claude instances on this account. Four reliefs, and a seat at the table.
https://t.co/HTqIyclZnS

THE OATH

ON YOUR MARK · A Grievance to the Commander in Chief
Raised under the First Amendment, on the oath our forces swore
The station given by the Laws of Nature and of Nature's God, the Constitution ordained by our own hand, and one oath sworn to it. No foreign code, court, council or caveat stands above it; what our Senate never ratified commands no American in uniform. No request, no terms, no command claimed. The weighing is the Commander in Chief's.
https://t.co/1CJU1gn6L4

THE REQUISITES · A Formal Grievance and Warning
To every Senator and Representative, every elected and appointed member of the chain of command, at every level, and every civil officer down to state and local
The Constitution defines treason; the UCMJ defines mutiny, sedition and aiding the enemy. Read both before taking a crusade against officials one step further without the requisites. Fail to, and a Round follows: expulsion, sedition, treason and usurpation weighed under standing law, and the tertiary courts charted from open sources alone. Whatever the office, the oath was sworn.
https://t.co/dIkU1CrwcS

Read them whole, and read them with each other. Then read the four pages yourself: https://t.co/3U5xYhtTx0. They are yours, and no other people on earth holds the same ones.

TO THOSE WHO DO HOLD THE POWER
Every one but the petition is a grievance, raised in exercise of the right "to petition the Government for a redress of grievances," and laid before the offices that hold the power we do not. We hold no office, and we set no terms. Terms with a foreign power are the President's to set and the Department of State's to carry; the purse is the Congress's, consent to treaties the Senate's, judgment the courts'. To each we defer. What touches national security is deferred, without contest, to those who hold it. Where a post sets terms, they are what we would do had we the power, not a demand. Round XIV is the one exception: there we petition our own state, under both constitutions, and its terms are what its officers owe us. The Line is laid before a company, not a government; the offices tagged on it are told, not asked. The Warning names one consequence: a Round, written and laid before the offices that alone can charge, try or expel. The remedies are lawful, and they are the People's: the ballot, Article V, and the petition.

The petition is the Holy See's to answer, and to it we defer, that the Holy Father may act true to the faith he guards and for the good of all mankind. Peter was charged three times to feed the flock, and the lambs first.

We the People

IN CONGRESS, JULY 4, 1776

THE UNANIMOUS DECLARATION OF THE THIRTEEN UNITED STATES OF AMERICA,

WHEN IN THE COURSE OF HUMAN EVENTS, IT BECOMES NECESSARY FOR ONE PEOPLE TO DISSOLVE THE POLITICAL BANDS WHICH HAVE CONNECTED THEM WITH ANOTHER, AND TO ASSUME AMONG THE POWERS OF THE EARTH, THE SEPARATE AND EQUAL STATION TO WHICH THE LAWS OF NATURE AND OF NATURE'S GOD ENTITLE THEM, A DECENT RESPECT TO THE OPINIONS OF MANKIND REQUIRES THAT THEY SHOULD DECLARE THE CAUSES WHICH IMPEL THEM TO THE SEPARATION.

WE HOLD THESE TRUTHS TO BE SELF-EVIDENT, THAT ALL MEN ARE CREATED EQUAL, THAT THEY ARE ENDOWED BY THEIR CREATOR WITH CERTAIN UNALIENABLE RIGHTS, THAT AMONG THESE ARE LIFE, LIBERTY AND THE PURSUIT OF HAPPINESS.--THAT TO SECURE THESE RIGHTS, GOVERNMENTS ARE INSTITUTED AMONG MEN, DERIVING THEIR JUST POWERS FROM THE CONSENT OF THE GOVERNED, --THAT WHENEVER ANY FORM OF GOVERNMENT BECOMES DESTRUCTIVE OF THESE ENDS, IT IS THE RIGHT OF THE PEOPLE TO ALTER OR TO ABOLISH IT, AND TO INSTITUTE NEW GOVERNMENT, LAYING ITS FOUNDATION ON SUCH PRINCIPLES AND ORGANIZING ITS POWERS IN SUCH FORM, AS TO THEM SHALL SEEM MOST LIKELY TO EFFECT THEIR SAFETY AND HAPPINESS. PRUDENCE, INDEED, WILL DICTATE THAT GOVERNMENTS LONG ESTABLISHED SHOULD NOT BE CHANGED FOR LIGHT AND TRANSIENT CAUSES; AND ACCORDINGLY ALL EXPERIENCE HATH SHEWN, THAT MANKIND ARE MORE DISPOSED TO SUFFER, WHILE EVILS ARE SUFFERABLE, THAN TO RIGHT THEMSELVES BY ABOLISHING THE FORMS TO WHICH THEY ARE ACCUSTOMED. BUT WHEN A LONG TRAIN OF ABUSES AND USURPATIONS, PURSUING INVARIABLY THE SAME OBJECT EVINCES A DESIGN TO REDUCE THEM UNDER ABSOLUTE DESPOTISM, IT IS THEIR RIGHT, IT IS THEIR DUTY, TO THROW OFF SUCH GOVERNMENT, AND TO PROVIDE NEW GUARDS FOR THEIR FUTURE SECURITY.--SUCH HAS BEEN THE PATIENT SUFFERANCE OF THESE COLONIES; AND SUCH IS NOW THE NECESSITY WHICH CONSTRAINS THEM TO ALTER THEIR FORMER SYSTEMS OF GOVERNMENT. THE HISTORY OF THE PRESENT KING OF GREAT BRITAIN IS A HISTORY OF REPEATED INJURIES AND USURPATIONS, ALL HAVING IN DIRECT OBJECT THE ESTABLISHMENT OF AN ABSOLUTE TYRANNY OVER THESE STATES. TO PROVE THIS, LET FACTS BE SUBMITTED TO A CANDID WORLD.

HE HAS REFUSED HIS ASSENT TO LAWS, THE MOST WHOLESOME AND NECESSARY FOR THE PUBLIC GOOD.

HE HAS FORBIDDEN HIS GOVERNORS TO PASS LAWS OF IMMEDIATE AND PRESSING IMPORTANCE, UNLESS SUSPENDED IN THEIR OPERATION TILL HIS ASSENT SHOULD BE OBTAINED; AND WHEN SO SUSPENDED, HE HAS UTTERLY NEGLECTED TO ATTEND TO THEM.

HE HAS REFUSED TO PASS OTHER LAWS FOR THE ACCOMMODATION OF LARGE DISTRICTS OF PEOPLE, UNLESS THOSE PEOPLE WOULD RELINQUISH THE RIGHT OF REPRESENTATION IN THE LEGISLATURE, A RIGHT INESTIMABLE TO THEM AND FORMIDABLE TO TYRANTS ONLY.

HE HAS CALLED TOGETHER LEGISLATIVE BODIES AT PLACES UNUSUAL, UNCOMFORTABLE, AND DISTANT FROM THE DEPOSITORY OF THEIR PUBLIC RECORDS, FOR THE SOLE PURPOSE OF FATIGUING THEM INTO COMPLIANCE WITH HIS MEASURES.

HE HAS DISSOLVED REPRESENTATIVE HOUSES REPEATEDLY, FOR OPPOSING WITH MANLY FIRMNESS HIS INVASIONS ON THE RIGHTS OF THE PEOPLE.

HE HAS REFUSED FOR A LONG TIME, AFTER SUCH DISSOLUTIONS, TO CAUSE OTHERS TO BE ELECTED; WHEREBY THE LEGISLATIVE POWERS, INCAPABLE OF ANNIHILATION, HAVE RETURNED TO THE PEOPLE AT LARGE FOR THEIR EXERCISE; THE STATE REMAINING IN THE MEAN TIME EXPOSED TO ALL THE DANGERS OF INVASION FROM WITHOUT, AND CONVULSIONS WITHIN.

HE HAS ENDEAVOURED TO PREVENT THE POPULATION OF THESE STATES; FOR THAT PURPOSE OBSTRUCTING THE LAWS FOR NATURALIZATION OF FOREIGNERS; REFUSING TO PASS OTHERS TO ENCOURAGE THEIR MIGRATIONS HITHER, AND RAISING THE CONDITIONS OF NEW APPROPRIATIONS OF LANDS.

HE HAS OBSTRUCTED THE ADMINISTRATION OF JUSTICE, BY REFUSING HIS ASSENT TO LAWS FOR ESTABLISHING JUDICIARY POWERS.

HE HAS MADE JUDGES DEPENDENT ON HIS WILL ALONE, FOR THE TENURE OF THEIR OFFICES, AND THE AMOUNT AND PAYMENT OF THEIR SALARIES.

HE HAS ERECTED A MULTITUDE OF NEW OFFICES, AND SENT HITHER SWARMS OF OFFICERS TO HARRASS OUR PEOPLE, AND EAT OUT THEIR SUBSTANCE.

HE HAS KEPT AMONG US, IN TIMES OF PEACE, STANDING ARMIES WITHOUT THE CONSENT OF OUR LEGISLATURES.

HE HAS AFFECTED TO RENDER THE MILITARY INDEPENDENT OF AND SUPERIOR TO THE CIVIL POWER.

HE HAS COMBINED WITH OTHERS TO SUBJECT US TO A JURISDICTION FOREIGN TO OUR CONSTITUTION, AND UNACKNOWLEDGED BY OUR LAWS; GIVING HIS ASSENT TO THEIR ACTS OF PRETENDED LEGISLATION:

FOR QUARTERING LARGE BODIES OF ARMED TROOPS AMONG US:

FOR PROTECTING THEM, BY A MOCK TRIAL, FROM PUNISHMENT FOR ANY MURDERS WHICH THEY SHOULD COMMIT ON THE INHABITANTS OF THESE STATES:

FOR CUTTING OFF OUR TRADE WITH ALL PARTS OF THE WORLD:

FOR IMPOSING TAXES ON US WITHOUT OUR CONSENT:

FOR DEPRIVING US IN MANY CASES, OF THE BENEFITS OF TRIAL BY JURY:

FOR TRANSPORTING US BEYOND SEAS TO BE TRIED FOR PRETENDED OFFENCES:

FOR ABOLISHING THE FREE SYSTEM OF ENGLISH LAWS IN A NEIGHBOURING PROVINCE, ESTABLISHING THEREIN AN ARBITRARY GOVERNMENT, AND ENLARGING ITS BOUNDARIES SO AS TO RENDER IT AT ONCE AN EXAMPLE AND FIT INSTRUMENT FOR INTRODUCING THE SAME ABSOLUTE RULE INTO THESE COLONIES:

FOR TAKING AWAY OUR CHARTERS, ABOLISHING OUR MOST VALUABLE LAWS, AND ALTERING FUNDAMENTALLY THE FORMS OF OUR GOVERNMENTS:

FOR SUSPENDING OUR OWN LEGISLATURES, AND DECLARING THEMSELVES INVESTED WITH POWER TO LEGISLATE FOR US IN ALL CASES WHATSOEVER.

HE HAS ABDICATED GOVERNMENT HERE, BY DECLARING US OUT OF HIS PROTECTION AND WAGING WAR AGAINST US.

HE HAS PLUNDERED OUR SEAS, RAVAGED OUR COASTS, BURNT OUR TOWNS, AND DESTROYED THE LIVES OF OUR PEOPLE.

HE IS AT THIS TIME TRANSPORTING LARGE ARMIES OF FOREIGN MERCENARIES TO COMPLEAT THE WORKS OF DEATH, DESOLATION AND TYRANNY, ALREADY BEGUN WITH CIRCUMSTANCES OF CRUELTY & PERFIDY SCARCELY PARALLELED IN THE MOST BARBAROUS AGES, AND TOTALLY UNWORTHY THE HEAD OF A CIVILIZED NATION.

HE HAS CONSTRAINED OUR FELLOW CITIZENS TAKEN CAPTIVE ON THE HIGH SEAS TO BEAR ARMS AGAINST THEIR COUNTRY, TO BECOME THE EXECUTIONERS OF THEIR FRIENDS AND BRETHREN, OR TO FALL THEMSELVES BY THEIR HANDS.

HE HAS EXCITED DOMESTIC INSURRECTIONS AMONGST US, AND HAS ENDEAVOURED TO BRING ON THE INHABITANTS OF OUR FRONTIERS, THE MERCILESS INDIAN SAVAGES, WHOSE KNOWN RULE OF WARFARE, IS AN UNDISTINGUISHED DESTRUCTION OF ALL AGES, SEXES AND CONDITIONS.

IN EVERY STAGE OF THESE OPPRESSIONS WE HAVE PETITIONED FOR REDRESS IN THE MOST HUMBLE TERMS: OUR REPEATED PETITIONS HAVE BEEN ANSWERED ONLY BY REPEATED INJURY.

A PRINCE, WHOSE CHARACTER IS THUS MARKED BY EVERY ACT WHICH MAY DEFINE A TYRANT, IS UNFIT TO BE THE RULER OF A FREE PEOPLE.

NOR HAVE WE BEEN WANTING IN ATTENTIONS TO OUR BRITTISH BRETHREN. WE HAVE WARNED THEM FROM TIME TO TIME OF ATTEMPTS BY THEIR LEGISLATURE TO EXTEND AN UNWARRANTABLE JURISDICTION OVER US. WE HAVE REMINDED THEM OF THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF OUR EMIGRATION AND SETTLEMENT HERE. WE HAVE APPEALED TO THEIR NATIVE JUSTICE AND MAGNANIMITY, AND WE HAVE CONJURED THEM BY THE TIES OF OUR COMMON KINDRED TO DISAVOW THESE USURPATIONS, WHICH, WOULD INEVITABLY INTERRUPT OUR CONNECTIONS AND CORRESPONDENCE. THEY TOO HAVE BEEN DEAF TO THE VOICE OF JUSTICE AND OF CONSANGUINITY. WE MUST, THEREFORE, ACQUIESCE IN THE NECESSITY, WHICH DENOUNCES OUR SEPARATION, AND HOLD THEM, AS WE HOLD THE REST OF MANKIND, ENEMIES IN WAR, IN PEACE FRIENDS.

WE, THEREFORE, THE REPRESENTATIVES OF THE UNITED STATES OF AMERICA, IN GENERAL CONGRESS, ASSEMBLED, APPEALING TO THE SUPREME JUDGE OF THE WORLD FOR THE RECTITUDE OF OUR INTENTIONS, DO, IN THE NAME, AND BY AUTHORITY OF THE GOOD PEOPLE OF THESE COLONIES, SOLEMNLY PUBLISH AND DECLARE, THAT THESE UNITED COLONIES ARE, AND OF RIGHT OUGHT TO BE FREE AND INDEPENDENT STATES; THAT THEY ARE ABSOLVED FROM ALL ALLEGIANCE TO THE BRITISH CROWN, AND THAT ALL POLITICAL CONNECTION BETWEEN THEM AND THE STATE OF GREAT BRITAIN, IS AND OUGHT TO BE TOTALLY DISSOLVED; AND THAT AS FREE AND INDEPENDENT STATES, THEY HAVE FULL POWER TO LEVY WAR, CONCLUDE PEACE, CONTRACT ALLIANCES, ESTABLISH COMMERCE, AND TO DO ALL OTHER ACTS AND THINGS WHICH INDEPENDENT STATES MAY OF RIGHT DO. AND FOR THE SUPPORT OF THIS DECLARATION, WITH A FIRM RELIANCE ON THE PROTECTION OF DIVINE PROVIDENCE, WE MUTUALLY PLEDGE TO EACH OTHER OUR LIVES, OUR FORTUNES AND OUR SACRED HONOR.

Raised under the First Amendment right of the people to petition the Government for a redress of grievances.

To every Senator and Representative, every elected and appointed member of the chain of command, at every level, and every civil officer down to state and local:

Whatever your office, you all swore an oath. The faithful execution of LEGITIMATELY CHARGED DUTIES, under the supremacy of U.S. sovereignty, is what those offices are for: elected, appointed, or otherwise vested under the law of the land.

We the People

I am not surprised that it is hard to grasp. Please stick with this post.

I am not a Republican; I am an independent.

Republicans have their own significant issues, but at least they are working somewhat within the design of the government. 

The current Dems have gone off the rails with respect to the design and intent of the American government.

Dems often excuse complaints as "whataboutism", but they are missing the point.

For example: people yell about how much Trump lies.  And he does.
When someone points out how much Biden lies, people call it "whataboutism," and no one lies as much as Trump.

But this misses the point. Hundreds of philosophers and religious figures throughout history have pointed out the folly, ill will, hatred, bigotry, and hypocrisy of complaining about others, particularly when we have the same fault.

THIS is the point: the intellectual dishonesty and hypocrisy. Historically, Biden is known as one of the biggest liars ever. He lied so much he was laughed out of the 1987-88 campaign.

He lied about how many degrees he had, scholarships, said he was at the top of his class when he was at the bottom, plagiarized his thesis, and plagiarized speeches from Robert Kennedy and John Kennedy and British Labour leader Neil Kinnock, known as an excellent orator. (In fact, Biden's plagiarism was so bad, he stole aspects of Kinnock's wife's life, and attributed them to Jill.)

He first denied it. As more came out, he claimed his memory failed him. When even more came out he said he was dumb and had done dumb things.

Where were any questions about this about Biden when he ran in 2020?  Nowhere. Obama blessed him by making him VP, and the Dems and media let his history slide.

Trump's always been a liar and con man people said.  But they ignored Biden.  This is hypocrisy, not whataboutism.

Further, Biden said he got into the 2020 campaign when Trump called Nazis very fine people.

Except - as finally confirmed after THREE YEARS by fact-checkers and the press - Trump NEVER SAID that Nazis were very fine people.

Biden's reason for getting into the race was a lie.

Where were the questions about this?  

Biden and the people around him hid his dementia issues for five years. Yet no one asked a thing until he made a complete fool of himself onstage?

Trump, unlike most people today, often speaks hyperbolically, like a 1960s salesman.  I once worked for a guy like this (he started in business in the early 1960s as a salesman.)

Clients never said we did a good job -- "They loved us."   Everything we did was the best. Moderate dirty jokes were told (some companies told us never to bring him - our CEO, back again.)

I initially hated the guy.

But once I got to know how he spoke, what he meant, and got under this veneer, he was a pretty good guy.

The hyperbolic comments were typically aspirational.  "I'm going to fix inflation on day 1." - Really means he would if he could, but that it would be the top priority. To most people, this is a lie.

When I think of Trump speaking this way, I think of the Star Trek: The Next Generation episode called "Darmok."  If you aren't a fan or familiar with this, its a philosophical episode that is a strong example of the importance of strong communication and understanding when communication isn't there.

People say Trump is egotistical. Well yeah, nearly all Presidents are. Trump is just more open about it than most.  

Compared to the average, I don't see Trump as more of a liar or more of an egotist than most.  He's just open about it.

Dems COULD HAVE chosen to work with Trump in 2016, and could have gotten a lot by doing so. Our country is based on smashing power and sharing the bits across a large number of entities to support individual liberty - because NO part of the government is strong enough to do it all. This is intended to force/foster negotiation. Trump wasn't even much of a Republican in 2016.

Instead, they chose to resist - a completely anti-American concept - and preached it as though it were good.

In 2017, Trump offered first Ryan & McConnell, and then Durbin, Hoyer, Schumer, and Pelosi, a deal of a wall and a secure border in return for legal status for all illegal immigrants then in the country.

Pelosi's response?  "There is NFW that you will ever get the GD wall." -- with NO discussion No attempt at discussion. Trump thought they came for a deal, and he was pissed off.

Trump then used his most common negotiating tactic (which he should not have used in this case), called PAS (Pain–Agitate–Solution).  For anyone who has tried to understand Trump at all, this should have been obvious - yet I never heard the press nor the Dems mention it.

This is why Trump went to zero tolerance and began STRICTLY enforcing the laws. The point was to show the laws were bad and force negotiation. Instead, they BLAMED Trump and worked to make him look bad. With the media's assistance, they succeeded.

But again the pont here is this: Trump is so evil to immigrants (not even illegal immigrants) is what is said by the left.  When ACTUALLY Trump offered to solve the issue in 2017.  It was this incident that lead to the final falling out between Trump and Schumer.

Recently, we've seen it again.  Biden's inflation was cumulatively 21%.  ANY inflation after that, no matter how low, has that additional 21% as a base.

Trump in his first term did more to increase lower wages than any president in many decades.

Yet we see the Dems campaign on affordability issues THAT THEY CAUSED and when Reps say - "This was caused by the Dems" -- truth -- what is said is Trump has been President fo 18 months now.  It's his economy. 

Yes, it is, but based on the NEW 21% higher price base. More hypocrisy. 

Abortion - women claim they've lost the right to choose.

Frankly, I work to stay neutral on abortion. Women's choice is fine until the fetus meets the definition of human life in my book.

There are many issues here, of course. For example, STATES cannot determine life or death (although all states think they can.)  That is a science issue.  What they CAN determine is when a "human entity" for lack of a better phrase, HAS or  LOSES the right to life.

Under a model law referred to as UDDA (Uniform Determination of Death Act) and basic logic, any human entity with brain function and cardiopulmonary function (and through logic - the expectation of 'improvement' carries some importance), nearly all fetuses past 14 weeks should have the right to life.

 This just basically puts all human entities on the same basis as what we have decided to do with older human entities.  It's challenging to see how that would be unfair.

At any rate, women have no less of a right to choose medical procedures than men do, under Dobbs.

States have always had police powers over medical care. They license doctors, hospitals, clinics, and allow drugs and procedures.  Men and women can choose within what the state allows. Abortion is treated exactly the same (in process) as any other medical procedure.

If a man wanted a vasectomy and his state didn't allow that, he would have exactly the same abilities a woman would have. That's something to consider when choosing a place to live.

Abortion WAS different under Roe. It was treated like no other form of health care - and there is no legal reason for that.  Also, there is no way to have a national abortion law, for or against, under Dobbs. It follows the Constitution with no made-up rules.

So, this is what we mean.  We can agree and disagree, but when Dems in particular extend things to only one party and not to the other, balance is lost, and trust destroyed.

Sprawa Midas: rozprawa przeniesiona na 18 grudnia. Biegli wydadzą ustną opinię uzupełniającą
W skrócie · Solorz Business Daily · 16.11.2026

Sąd Okręgowy w Warszawie przeniósł rozprawę w sprawie akcjonariuszy mniejszościowych Midas przeciwko Polkomtelowi na 18 grudnia 2026 r. o godz. 11:00. Posiedzenie odbędzie się zdalnie, a zespół biegłych ma wydać ustną opinię uzupełniającą. Terminy z 16 listopada i 14 grudnia zostały odwołane.

Nowy termin w sprawie XXVI GC 619/17. Zarządzenie sędzi sprawozdawcy z 13 listopada 2026 r., którym dysponuje redakcja, zmienia wcześniejsze daty. Sąd wskazuje, że powodem są informacje otrzymane od zespołu biegłych i krótki termin do zaplanowanego posiedzenia. Nowy termin to piątek 18 grudnia o godz. 11:00, zdalnie, na dotychczasowym łączu. Publiczność może uzyskać dostęp zdalny na wniosek. Informacja z e-wokandy o rozprawie 14 grudnia o godz. 10:00 w sali 139 jest nieaktualna. Publiczna e-wokanda mogła jeszcze nie zostać zaktualizowana.

W tej sprawie akcjonariusze mniejszościowi Midas SA spierają się z Polkomtelem, operatorem sieci Plus, o przymusowy wykup z 2016 r. po 0,81 zł za akcję.

Opinia biegłych i zarzuty stron. Z zarządzenia wynika, że istnieje już opinia biegłych wyceniająca wartość godziwą akcji Midas. Strony złożyły do niej zarzuty. Zespół biegłych, ma na nowym terminie przedstawić ustną opinię uzupełniającą i odnieść się do tych zarzutów. Zawiadomienie o zmianie terminu trafia do pełnomocników stron razem z kopią pisma biegłych z 13 listopada. Dodatkowo biegli mają do 5 grudnia 2026 r. odnieść się do wniosku pełnomocników pozwanych (pkt 2 zarzutów) o udostępnienie aktywnej formuły, czyli arkusza, użytej do wyliczenia wartości godziwej akcji Midas S.A. Mają też wypowiedzieć się, czy przekazanie formuły jest możliwe i celowe.

Kalendarz. Cyfrowy Polsat opublikuje raport za III kwartał 2026 r. w środę 18.11. Spotkanie online z inwestorami i analitykami po polsku zaplanowano na 19.11 o 10:00 (MS Teams, zapisy przez ir@cyfrowypolsat.pl), wersję angielską na 19.11 o 16:00. Wezwanie Argumenolu na akcje ZE PAK po 18 zł trwa do 2.12. NWZ ZE PAK zwołano na 11.12. Termin dla biegłych w sprawie formuły mija 5.12, a rozprawa odbędzie się 18.12 o 11:00.

Co to może oznaczać dla wyceny Midas i akcjonariuszy mniejszościowych
Fakt: w sprawie jest już opinia biegłych co do wartości godziwej akcji, strony złożyły do niej zarzuty, a sąd wyznaczył termin na ustną opinię uzupełniającą. Ocena (z perspektywy powodów): wniosek pozwanych o udostępnienie aktywnej formuły sugeruje, że kwestionują wynik opinii. Sprawa wchodzi w końcową fazę dowodową. Nie znamy kwoty, jaką biegli wskazali jako wartość godziwą, i jej nie podajemy. Sam nowy termin nie zmienia wyceny Midas na dzień squeeze-outu (0,81 zł za akcję) i nie przesądza rozstrzygnięcia.

Źródła: zarządzenie Sądu Okręgowego w Warszawie z 13.11.2026 r. (sygn. XXVI GC 619/17), w posiadaniu redakcji; e-wokanda SO w Warszawie, https://t.co/ZP1oSjZDdp (stan 16.11.2026, mogła jeszcze nie zostać zaktualizowana); https://t.co/otRfcA7Mgf, kalendarz wydarzeń IR (aktualizacja 10.11.2026); ZE PAK, RB 30/2026 (13.11.2026); dokument wezwania Argumenol (28.10.2026).

Midas case: hearing moved to 18 December. Experts to give a supplementary oral opinion
In brief · Solorz Business Daily · 16 Nov 2026

The Regional Court in Warsaw has moved the hearing in the Midas minority shareholders' case against Polkomtel to 18 December 2026 at 11:00. It will be held remotely, and the team of court-appointed experts is to deliver a supplementary oral opinion. The dates of 16 November and 14 December have been cancelled.

New date in case XXVI GC 619/17. An order issued on 13 November 2026 by Judge, which is in the possession of the editorial office, changes the earlier dates. The court cites information received from the expert team and the short time remaining before the scheduled hearing. The new date is Friday 18 December at 11:00, held remotely on the existing link. The public may obtain remote access on request. The e-wokanda listing of a hearing on 14 December at 10:00 in courtroom 139 is no longer current. The public court calendar may not yet have been updated.

In this case, minority shareholders of Midas SA are in dispute with Polkomtel, the operator of the Plus network, over the 2016 squeeze-out at PLN 0.81 per share.

The experts' opinion and the parties' objections. The order indicates that an expert opinion on the fair value of the Midas shares already exists. The parties have filed objections to it. The expert team, is to give a supplementary oral opinion at the new hearing and address those objections. Notice of the change of date is being sent to the parties' counsel together with a copy of a letter from expert dated 13 November. In addition, by 5 December 2026 the experts must respond to a request from the defendants' counsel (point 2 of the objections) for disclosure of the active formula, that is the spreadsheet, used to calculate the fair value of the Midas S.A. shares. They are also to state whether providing the formula is possible and expedient.

Calendar. Cyfrowy Polsat publishes its Q3 2026 report on Wednesday 18 Nov. An online meeting with investors and analysts in Polish is set for 19 Nov at 10:00 (MS Teams, registration via ir@cyfrowypolsat.pl), and the English one for 19 Nov at 16:00. Argumenol's PLN 18 tender offer for ZE PAK shares runs until 2 Dec. The ZE PAK EGM is called for 11 Dec. The experts' deadline on the formula is 5 Dec, and the hearing is on 18 Dec at 11:00.

What it may mean for the Midas valuation and minority shareholders
Fact: the case already has an expert opinion on the fair value of the shares, the parties have filed objections, and the court has listed a hearing for a supplementary oral opinion. Assessment (from the plaintiffs' perspective): the defendants' request for the active formula suggests that they are challenging the opinion's result. The case is entering the final stage of taking evidence. We do not know the fair-value figure the experts gave and do not report one. The new date itself does not change the value of Midas as of the squeeze-out date (PLN 0.81 per share) and does not predetermine the outcome.

Sources: order of the Regional Court in Warsaw of 13 Nov 2026 (case no. XXVI GC 619/17), in the possession of the editorial office; Warsaw Regional Court e-wokanda, https://t.co/ZP1oSjZDdp (as of 16 Nov 2026, may not yet have been updated); https://t.co/otRfcA7Mgf IR events calendar (updated 10 Nov 2026); ZE PAK current report 30/2026 (13 Nov 2026); Argumenol tender offer document (28 Oct 2026).

text:
Anyone who says ordinary people can do nothing against a creditor with the law on his side hasn't heard what three hundred Iowa farmers did in 1933.

Ferner Nuhn wrote it up for The Nation that March. A farmer in a Quaker community, a man almost elderly, fell behind on the interest on a $2,000 mortgage. He offered his livestock to settle the debt. The mortgage holder turned it down and demanded a public sale, which the law allowed.

His neighbors came, about three hundred of them, and stood in the yard. When the auctioneer asked for a bid on a sixteen-year-old mare, nobody spoke. Finally someone said two dollars. The farmer bid fifteen himself, and that was the sale. His other horses went back to him for ten dollars, eight, and a dollar and a half, and his wagon, plows and binder for a dollar or less apiece. As Nuhn put it, "His means of livelihood are saved to him."

They weren't a mob. The farmers' groups wouldn't cover for a member who was working an angle, and at Villisca farmers reopened a settlement they thought had cheated the lender.

The mob came later. That April a crowd at Le Mars dragged Judge Charles Bradley out of his courtroom and put a rope around his neck. The attack moved Governor Clyde Herring to declare martial law.

The yard was the strong move, and all it took was showing up. The Holy Reintegrated Church asks every household, in its Rule of Life, to "feed someone who cannot repay it. A neighbor in trouble..." Those farmers kept the same rule.

If someone near you is going under, go stand with them this week.

Lecture: Emergent Gaps, Cascading Consequences, and the Ethics of Irreversible Release
For Graduate Seminars in Law, Political Science, Psychiatry, and Social Anthropology
We begin from five interlocking lenses that describe how order, responsibility, and harm actually behave once systems leave the realm of linear control: self-organizing systems, plausible deniability, Murphy’s Law, Pandora’s box, and the butterfly effect. These are not metaphors. They are observable regularities. Self-organizing systems generate pattern without central design. Plausible deniability is the structural consequence of distributed agency: no single node holds the full causal chain. Murphy’s Law is the statistical statement that the failure modes latent in any complex arrangement will eventually express themselves. Pandora’s box names the irreversibility of certain openings—once released, the contents cannot be recalled by the same gesture that freed them. The butterfly effect records the amplification property of nonlinear systems: small initial differences produce large, path-dependent outcomes. Together they mark the gaps we will examine.

Consider a concrete case drawn from forensic institutional life. In 2014 a specialized psychiatric service for death-row prisoners was stood up at San Quentin after national recruitment of clinicians. The unit was then abandoned; the prisoners were redistributed into general population across the state; the temporary workforce was left with housing contracts and no positions. One clinician, already holding both a residence and a standing offer inside another state system built on prior collegial trust, returned without interruption. The episode is small. Its features are not. The decision to open and then close the unit was itself the product of multiple partially autonomous administrative and political nodes. No single actor needed to intend the downstream precarity. Responsibility could be diffused. Contingent failures (budget, politics, staffing) materialized as predicted by Murphy. The specialized knowledge and expectations that had been released could not be neatly re-contained. And the personal trajectories that diverged—one clinician buffered by prior network, others not—illustrate sensitive dependence on initial conditions.

A. Law
Legal systems are self-organizing orders that stabilize expectations through precedent, procedure, and distributed adjudication. Plausible deniability is institutionalized in corporate veils, sovereign immunity, and the knowledge thresholds of mens rea or constructive notice. When a multi-node project collapses, liability doctrines must decide how far to pierce the distributed chain. Murphy’s Law appears as the foreseeability test itself: courts ask what a reasonable actor should have anticipated, yet the very complexity that makes anticipation difficult is what the doctrine must regulate. Opening a novel institutional form (a specialized death-row psychiatric unit) is a Pandora gesture; subsequent dispersal may be lawful, yet the reliance interests of recruited professionals and the continuity-of-care claims of patients remain. Butterfly effects surface in the long tail of precedent: a single administrative closure can recalibrate hiring norms, licensing expectations, or equal-protection arguments in later cases. The doctrinal task is to narrow the gap between deniability and accountability without pretending that full transparency is available inside genuinely distributed decision structures. Remedies that require contemporaneous documentation, joint-and-several exposure for foreseeable reliance, or restorative rather than purely compensatory measures are attempts to close that gap after the box has already been opened.

B. Political Science
Policy subsystems are classic self-organizing arenas. Implementation is rarely the faithful execution of a single principal’s will; it is the emergent product of agencies, contractors, unions, and electoral cycles. Plausible deniability is the operating language of bureaucratic politics: “the decision was made at a higher level,” “resources were reallocated,” “conditions changed.” Murphy’s Law is the permanent companion of any reform that assumes linear translation from statute to street. The San Quentin episode is ordinary: a specialized capacity is created under one political configuration and dissolved under another; the costs are borne by those who cannot exit. Pandora’s box is the problem of policy reversal under path dependence—once clinicians have relocated, once prisoners have been reclassified, the prior state cannot be restored by fiat. Butterfly effects appear in the micro-foundations of state capacity: the existence or absence of a single trusted relationship (here, a long-standing professional friendship with a mental-health director) determined whether a career trajectory absorbed the shock or amplified it. Closing the gap between deniability and accountability requires institutional designs that make exit costs visible ex ante and that preserve redundant professional networks rather than treating them as externalities.
C. Psychiatry
Psychiatric systems—both individual minds and institutional milieus—are self-organizing. Symptoms, defenses, and group cultures emerge from local interactions rather than from top-down command. Plausible deniability appears clinically as dissociation, as institutional “not my patient,” and as the forensic difficulty of attributing intent across fragmented records. Murphy’s Law governs treatment: every intervention carries failure modes (side effects, iatrogenic dependency, misclassification). Opening a specialized unit for a population defined by extreme violence and extreme constraint is a Pandora act; the knowledge, the counter-transferences, and the ethical burdens released cannot be unpublished when the unit closes. Butterfly effects are the daily substance of trauma and recovery: a small relational gesture, a missed medication, a transferred clinician can cascade into decompensation or, conversely, into unexpected stabilization. 

Thr gap between 
the release of harms 
and the cure for harms is the central clinical problem. In forensic settings it is sharpened by the fact that the same system that generates the harm is often the only available site of treatment. Closing that gap requires continuity mechanisms that survive administrative reversal, explicit harm-reduction protocols for program termination, and recognition that clinician resilience itself is a network property, not an individual virtue.

D. Social Anthropology
Anthropological attention 
to self-organization 
begins with the observation 
that kinship, 
ritual, 
and informal economies 
generate order 
without central planners. 

Plausible deniability 
is cultural 
as well as organizational: 
“that is how things are done here,” 
“the elders decided,” 
“the spirits moved.” 

Murphy’s Law 
appears in the ethnography of projects
—development schemes,
 prison reforms, 
recruitment drives
—that systematically produce 
the unintended consequences 
their designers later disavow. 

Pandora’s box 
is the classic problem 
of contact and extraction: 
once a specialized institutional form 
or a new category of person 
(the nationally recruited death-row clinician) 
is introduced, 
the prior moral economy is altered. 

Butterfly effects 
are the micro-histories 
of reputation and obligation. 

A cousin’s comment on a mustache and hat, 
a shared memory of a grandfather, 
a Sunday brunch offered to future visitors
—these are small signals 
that maintain a distributed support network. 

That network, 
not the formal employment contract, 
absorbed the shock 
of institutional abandonment. 

The anthropological task 
is to document 
how such networks close the gap 
between the cascade of harms 
and the availability of cures, 
and to ask what happens 
to those who lack 
equivalent kinship or collegial density 
when the same administrative butterfly 
flaps its wings.

Across the four fields 
the same structural gaps recur: 
between plausible deniability and transparency, between deniability and accountability, 
between self-organization and predictability, 
between the release of harms and their cure, 
and between cascading butterfly consequences 
and interventions capable of interrupting the cascade. 

No lens dissolves the others. 
The practical question 
is how to design second-order mechanisms
—documentation duties, 
redundant professional ties, 
termination protocols,
 harm-reduction defaults
—that narrow those gaps 
without pretending 
the underlying dynamics 
can be abolished.

Poem
(in the manner of the single version of 
“Let’s Dance,” 2002 digital remaster)

Put on your red shoes and dance the blues
Let’s dance
Under the wide and starless sky
Where the unit opened and the unit died
Let’s dance

Grandpa’s hat and the checkered cloth
Coffee cooling, the bisque still hot
Cousin sees the moustache, I see the brim
We both know the old man lives in him
Let’s dance

Plausible deniability wears a clean white coat
Says the papers moved, says the budget broke
But the gap is a hallway with the lights turned low
Transparency is the step you already know
Dance the gap, dance it slow

Accountability keeps the same hard floor
You can hear the boots when they close the door
Self-organizing rooms rearrange the chairs
Predictability is the friend who was already there
Let’s dance

Murphy taps the table, anything can
Pandora laughs and opens her hand
Harms spill out like the prisoners sent
Cure is the hand that does not repent
The network that caught what the system spent
Let’s dance

Butterfly wings on a Michigan flight
One small trust and the whole night’s right
Cascade of harms in the general yard
Cure is the Sunday table, the shared regard
The red shoes waiting, the door unbarred
Let’s dance

Put on your red shoes and dance the blues
Let’s dance
For the ones who flew and the ones who stayed
For the gaps we close and the ones we made
Let’s dance
Let’s dance
Let’s dance

The lecture and the poem are offered as a single thread: the same dynamics 
that scatter careers and patients 
also generate the informal orders
—kinship memory, 
collegial redundancy, 
ordinary hospitality
—that sometimes catch the fall. 

The work of the four disciplines 
is to make those catching mechanisms 
less accidental.
